items.desc: Your Mission As Research Scientist / Engineer — Large-scale Training , you will develop the architectures and training methods that make UMA’s robotic foundation models more capable and more efficient to train . You will investigate how model design, optimization, and hardware-aware implementation work together to deliver better humanoid robot performance within a given compute budget. Your primary focus will be pretraining , with work extending into mid-training and post-training . You will explore efficient multimodal architectures, faster training recipes, and compute-efficient scaling strategies, using controlled experiments to determine which improvements translate into stronger capabilities on real robots. We already have a working training stack and a strong team behind it. Working closely with AI researchers and Training Infrastructure engineers, you will take ideas from architectural changes and kernel-level prototypes through training experiments to larger-scale validation. Your findings will shape what we train, how we train it, and how we allocate compute . Key responsibilities: Research efficient model architectures for robotic foundation models, including attention mechanisms, multimodal fusion, visual and action tokenization, sequence compression, and dense versus sparse or mixture-of-experts designs. Optimize training recipes and convergence through choices of optimizers, learning-rate schedules, initialization, normalization, batch sizes, and numerical precision. Measure improvements in time and compute required to reach a target capability. Co-design architectures and compute kernels: identify expensive operations, explore hardware-friendly alternatives, and prototype fused or custom kernels using tools such as Triton or CUDA where useful. Investigate efficient attention and sequence processing, reducing the cost of learning from video, temporal context, and action sequences while preserving useful information. Develop scaling laws and compute-allocation studies to understand how performance changes with model size, training data, and compute. Use smaller experiments to guide larger runs, and validate where those predictions hold. Research training acceleration techniques, such as progressive increases in resolution or context length, selective freezing, parameter sharing, and lower-precision computation, evaluating their effects on stability and final performance. Run controlled ablations and performance benchmarks that distinguish faster execution from better learning efficiency, tracking wall-clock time, compute, memory, convergence, and downstream capability. Diagnose training dynamics and numerical instabilities, including gradient behavior, sensitivity to precision, loss spikes, and changes that emerge as models or batch sizes scale. Evaluate how pretraining improvements transfer through mid-training and post-training to real-robot success, generalization, robustness, and adaptation efficiency. Work with Training Infrastructure engineers to integrate validated methods into scalable, reproducible training systems, and with Data researchers to study interactions between model capacity, data mixtures, and training duration. What You Bring To The Table Previous experience in training large-scale frontier foundation models such as LLMs, Video Generation Or Vision Encoders Strong experience in deep learning research, efficient model training, foundation models, or ML systems, demonstrated through research projects, publications, deployed systems, or open-source work. Strong Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience implementing architectures and running substantial training experiments. A deep understanding of model architectures, optimization, and training dynamics, and the ability to explain why a change affects convergence, stability, or computational cost. Experience improving training efficiency, whether through architecture design, optimization methods, numerical precision, or hardware-aware implementation. The ability to reason about compute, memory bandwidth, tensor shapes, and GPU execution, and connect profiling results to research decisions. Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, fair compute comparisons, reproducible results, and careful interpretation of scaling trends. Interest in connecting efficient training research to multimodal learning and real-world robot capabilities. Thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced startup: autonomous, rigorous, collaborative, and comfortable moving between research and implementation. Bonus: Triton, CUDA, fused kernels, efficient attention, or compiler-based optimization. Bonus: scaling laws, compute-optimal training, mixture-of-experts models, or large-scale multimodal pretraining. Bonus: distributed training, low-precision training, vision-language-action models, or robot learning. Bonus: open-source contributions, reproducible research implementations, or technical writing. We value deep expertise in one or more of these areas , …

items.desc:
This role sits at the intersection of numerical physics / simulation, physics-informed ML, and surrogate modeling with a strong pull toward high‑impact industrial domains such as aeronautics, automotive, and non‑destructive testing (NDT).
 We are open in how we frame the position (Research Scientist vs Applied Scientist): what matters is a profile that can do serious research while keeping a clear path to deployment and operational impact, including collaborations with labs and industrial partners when relevant.
 What you’ll work on 
 Physics-informed & surrogate modeling (PINNs / Neural Operators / Neural PDEs) 
 Build fast, accurate surrogates to emulate expensive simulations or physical processes (e.g., PDE-driven systems, complex boundary conditions, multi-physics settings).
 Explore approaches such as Fourier Neural Operators, operator learning, PINNs, and hybrid ML+numerics methods.
 Computational / numerical physics meets foundation models 
 Help us extend “foundation model thinking” to physical domains: pretraining, adaptation, and evaluation for scientific/industrial data (fields, meshes, sensor arrays, tomography/ultrasound-like signals, etc.).
 Develop strategies that work under scarce, noisy, irregular, or biased physical datasets.
 Architecture, inductive biases, and messy reality 
 Design architectures that respect physical structure: invariances/equivariance, geometry, irregular spatial/temporal grids, mesh-based data, multimodal measurement pipelines.
 Investigate failure modes: when deep learning breaks in physics settings, why it breaks, and what to do about it.
 From research to demonstrators 
 Own projects end-to-end: hypotheses → experiments → training on GPU infrastructure → robust evaluation → prototype integration.
 Define evaluation protocols aligned with constraints like calibration/uncertainty, robustness, traceability, and cost of error.

items.desc: Here at Humanoid, we believe in a future where robots amplify human potential. That’s why we’ve set out on a mission to build the world’s most capable, commercially-scalable, and safe humanoid robots. We’re bringing that mission to life with HMND‑01 - our rapidly developed humanoid platform being deployed in real industrial environments - and we’re growing the team to take it even further. Our Mission At Humanoid we strive to create the world's leading, commercially scalable, safe, and advanced humanoid robots that seamlessly integrate into daily life and amplify human capacity. About The Role As a Research Engineer on the World Models team, you will build action-conditioned generative models that predict how the world evolves around our robots — future video, proprioception, contacts, and outcomes — from past observations and actions. World models serve four purposes in our stack: a pretrained, physics-aware prior for our VLA policies; an engine for rare data collection, cross-platform transfer, and sim-to-real transfer; a testbed for policy evaluation and testing before hardware; and a future-prediction rollout engine that surfaces what our policies intend to do, for safety and planning. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you will design architectures, run large training jobs, and validate your models against real fleet data from industrial deployments. What You'll Do Design and train multimodal world models — video, state, action, and language — using diffusion-based and transformer architectures. Build action-conditioned video prediction and dynamics models that stay physically consistent over long horizons, including contact-rich manipulation, and serve as pretrained priors for VLA policies. Develop learned-simulator evaluation: score candidate policies offline, predict real-world success rates before deployment, and roll out policy futures to expose intended behaviour for safety review and planning. Generate synthetic rollouts and counterfactual experience — including rare events, cross-platform transfer, and sim-to-real transfer — to augment policy training, and measure their effect on downstream task performance. Establish fidelity metrics and calibration protocols that quantify where the world model can be trusted and where it diverges from reality. Build data pipelines that turn fleet telemetry, teleoperation logs, and internet-scale video into training corpora for world models. Run scaling and ablation studies on architecture, data mixture, and context length; communicate findings crisply. Collaborate with pretraining, RL, and manipulation teams to integrate world models into policy training and evaluation loops. What We're Looking For A track record of training large generative models — video, world, or multimodal — with shipped models or published artifacts to show for it. Deep hands-on experience with modern generative architectures: diffusion models, autoregressive transformers, latent-variable models, or video prediction. Experience with large-scale distributed training: streaming datasets, checkpointing and state management, debugging numerics and training instabilities. Strong Python + PyTorch/JAX; you can profile kernels, optimize data loaders, and write maintainable research code. Empirical rigor: you design careful evaluations, run honest baselines, and document experiments clearly. Excitement about grounding generative models in physical reality rather than pixels alone. Nice to have Experience with world models for robotics or autonomous driving (e.g., action-conditioned video models, learned simulators, model-based RL). Familiarity with robotics simulators (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) and sim-to-real considerations. Experience using world models for policy evaluation or synthetic data generation at scale. Publications at top-tier deep learning conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, CVPR) or equivalent open-source contributions. Experience optimizing generative models for fast inference. What We Offer Competitive equity: stock options with meaningful upside as we scale. 30+ paid days off, including 23 days of annual leave, all UK bank holidays, and additional company closure days (including Christmas–New Year shutdown). Private healthcare, including virtual and in-person care. Pension scheme with 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings. Free daily breakfast, catered lunch, and snacks in-office. Work at the frontier - collaborate daily with world-class engineers, researchers, and product experts building the next generation of AI and humanoid robotics. Real ownership - direct access to founding leadership, meaningful input on product direction, and the ability to drive key initiatives from day one.

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




THE ROLE

As a Research Engineer on the Latency & Throughput team, you will push the frontier of LLM inference by researching and prototyping techniques that reduce latency and increase throughput — from speculative decoding and quantization to KV compression and new attention variants. The team sits at the intersection of research and production: you will take ideas from recent literature, form hypotheses, run experiments, and ship the techniques that prove out into our serving stack.

This role sits between our inference engineers, who own the production serving stack, and our research scientists, who focus on paper-level contributions. You will be more science-focused than a pure engineer: you are expected to generate new ideas, keep up with the state of the art, and implement proof-of-concepts that bridge the gap between academic results and production impact. Some techniques you explore will be lossy or require integration into training — retraining models, tuning architectures, or training auxiliary models to improve inference.

You will work closely with the Inference Foundation and Kernels teams, who turn your validated techniques into production recipes, and with pretraining and RL teams when your work touches model training. Success is measured by demonstrated latency or throughput gains, first at small scale, then adopted in production.



What You Will Do

 - Research and prototype inference techniques — speculative decoding, quantization, KV compression, watermarking, and new model architectures — by reading recent literature and forming testable hypotheses.

 - Design and run experiments to validate or refute ideas, iterating quickly on small-scale setups before proposing production integration. Demonstrate clear latency or throughput gains without unacceptable quality loss.

 - Collaborate with the Inference Foundation team to integrate validated techniques into the vLLM-based serving stack.

 - Partner with pretraining and RL teams when techniques require co-training, retraining, or training auxiliary models to improve inference.

Build the right tooling and validation platforms to facilitate AI-driven inference research.



What We're Looking For

 - A strong ML background with solid knowledge of LLM training techniques — architecture, tokenization, fine-tuning, and evaluation.

 - Hands-on experience with Python and PyTorch; you write clean, experimental code and iterate fast. JAX is acceptable with strong Python proficiency. C++ and Rust are not required, CUDA and GPU knowledge is expected but hands-on experience is not required.

 - Research experience of some form: a thesis, publications, a dedicated research project, or efficiency-oriented work in a lab or industry research setting. A PhD is not required, but we are looking for genuine research depth.

 - A track record of conducting experiments: forming hypotheses, designing controlled comparisons, and drawing clear conclusions from results.

 - Familiarity with the state of the art in LLM inference — you know what has been tried, what works, and where the open problems are.

 - Self-starter, low-ego, and collaborative. You are comfortable with ambiguity, negative results, and are eager to take matters into your own hands.

 - Inference or serving experience is a plus, not a requirement. Prior work with vLLM, production LLM deployments, or serving systems will help you ramp up faster.



Location and Remote

The Role As a Research Engineer on the Latency & Throughput team, you will push the frontier of LLM inference by researching and prototyping techniques that reduce latency and increase throughput — from speculative decoding and quantization to KV compression and new attention variants. The team sits at the intersection of research and production: you will take ideas from recent literature, form hypotheses, run experiments, and ship the techniques that prove out into our serving stack. This role sits between our inference engineers, who own the production serving stack, and our research scientists, who focus on paper-level contributions. You will be more science-focused than a pure engineer: you are expected to generate new ideas, keep up with the state of the art, and implement proof-of-concepts that bridge the gap between academic results and production impact. Some techniques you explore will be lossy or require integration into training — retraining models, tuning architectures, or training auxiliary models to improve inference. You will work closely with the Inference Foundation and Kernels teams, who turn your validated techniques into production recipes, and with pretraining and RL teams when your work touches model training. Success is measured by demonstrated latency or throughput gains, first at small scale, then adopted in production. What You Will Do Research and prototype inference techniques — speculative decoding, quantization, KV compression, watermarking, and new model architectures — by reading recent literature and forming testable hypotheses. Design and run experiments to validate or refute ideas, iterating quickly on small-scale setups before proposing production integration. Demonstrate clear latency or throughput gains without unacceptable quality loss. Collaborate with the Inference Foundation team to integrate validated techniques into the vLLM-based serving stack. Partner with pretraining and RL teams when techniques require co-training, retraining, or training auxiliary models to improve inference. Build the right tooling and validation platforms to facilitate AI-driven inference research. What We're Looking For A strong ML background with solid knowledge of LLM training techniques — architecture, tokenization, fine-tuning, and evaluation. Hands-on experience with Python and PyTorch; you write clean, experimental code and iterate fast. JAX is acceptable with strong Python proficiency. C++ and Rust are not required, CUDA and GPU knowledge is expected but hands-on experience is not required. Research experience of some form: a thesis, publications, a dedicated research project, or efficiency-oriented work in a lab or industry research setting. A PhD is not required, but we are looking for genuine research depth. A track record of conducting experiments: forming hypotheses, designing controlled comparisons, and drawing clear conclusions from results. Familiarity with the state of the art in LLM inference — you know what has been tried, what works, and where the open problems are. Self-starter, low-ego, and collaborative. You are comfortable with ambiguity, negative results, and are eager to take matters into your own hands. Inference or serving experience is a plus, not a requirement. items.desc: Your Mission As AI Infra / Engineer — Large-scale Training , you will build the systems that make UMA’s humanoid robot learning fast, scalable, and reliable . You will turn experimental training code into robust execution pipelines that scale across thousands of GPUs and support rapid iteration. You will work directly with AI researchers, shaping the software used to train our robotic foundation models across pretraining, mid-training, and post-training on large-scale multimodal data . You will own the engineering challenges of distributed execution: choosing parallelism strategies, optimizing memory and communication, accelerating critical operations, and keeping long-running jobs reliable.. We already have a working training stack and a strong team behind it. You will build on that foundation, with room to rethink components where needed. Working closely with AI researchers, you will scale pretraining across GPUs and nodes , optimize compute, memory, and communication , and make long-running training jobs reliable. The goal is to reduce training time and increase experiment throughput , enabling larger models and faster research iteration within our compute budget. Debugging here goes beyond keeping jobs running. You will understand enough of the learning process to recognize when a numerical issue or distributed implementation bug appears in a loss curve, and work with researchers to resolve it. The systems you build will also support mid-training and post-training as our models evolve. Key responsibilities: Build distributed pretraining systems across multiple GPUs and nodes, selecting appropriate strategies such as DDP, FSDP, and tensor, pipeline, or expert parallelism as workloads require. Develop RL and post-training execution infrastructure, including distributed rollouts, actor–learner coordination, policy synchronization, replay buffers, and efficient batching. Maximize MFU and eliminate bottlenecks: Profile the complete training loop—data loading, decoding, CPU-GPU memory transfers, and compute kernels—eliminating bottlenecks to keep MFU high and ensure accelerators operate at peak efficiency. Integrate and benchmark accelerated kernels and execution techniques, such as FlashAttention, fused operations, mixed precision, and compilation; develop custom optimizations where they provide clear value. Build efficient training-time data movement and buffering, including out-of-core storage, caching, prefetching, and asynchronous transfers, in partnership with the Data Infrastructure team. Turn research prototypes into maintainable training systems, with reusable components that support evolving architectures and experimental workflows. Diagnose distributed and numerical failures, including deadlocks, memory leaks, gradient anomalies, precision issues, and inconsistencies between single-device and distributed runs. Deep numerical debugging and run determinism: Diagnose complex issues across the stack—from distributed deadlocks and memory leaks to training instabilities and gradient anomalies—while enforcing numerical determinism so that training runs, evaluations, and experiments are strictly reproducible. Build reliable checkpointing and fault-tolerant resumption, preserving model, optimizer, and relevant execution state so interrupted jobs can recover correctly. Strengthen observability and reproducibility through configuration tracking, profiling, run diagnostics, and deterministic execution where practical. What You Bring To The Table Solid experience building ML training infrastructure, distributed systems, or high-performance ML software. Strong Python and PyTorch, with hands-on knowledge of distributed training tools such as DDP, FSDP, or Megatron. Experience with multiprocessing, asynchronous execution, and GPU memory management, and an understanding of how communication and synchronization affect scaling. Practical knowledge of losses, optimizers, gradients, and numerical precision, sufficient to debug training behavior alongside researchers. Experience profiling accelerator workloads with tools such as PyTorch Profiler or Nsight Systems, and translating findings into measurable improvements. A pragmatic engineering mindset: you can turn experimental code into reliable, scalable systems while keeping research iteration fast. Clear communication and a collaborative approach to working with researchers whose requirements evolve quickly. Bonus: RL infrastructure, distributed rollouts, replay buffers, or actor–learner architectures. Bonus: C++, CUDA, Triton, custom kernels, or compiler-based optimization. Bonus: Slurm or Kubernetes, GPU networking such as InfiniBand/RoCE, or storage caching. Bonus: contributions to open-source training tools or technical writing. UMA is an inclusive workplace that values exceptional builders over perfect pedigrees . Whatever your background, identity, or journey, if you don’t meet every criterion but believe you can have an outsized impact here, we strongly …

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




THE ROLE

Mistral AI is seeking Applied Scientists and Research Engineers focused on formal methods. You will design, train, and deploy SOTA large language models and apply them to diverse use cases. 

You'll work cross-functionally with internal and external science, engineering, and product teams to deliver high-impact AI solutions.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Run pre-training, post-training and deploy state of the art models on large clusters.

 - Generate and curate datasets for theorem proving and software verification, and build evaluators and benchmarks for formal reasoning.

 - Develop the necessary tools and frameworks to facilitate data generation, model training, evaluation and deployment.

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to tackle complex use cases.

 - Manage research projects and communications with client research teams.
   
    


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Fluent in English with excellent communication skills — at ease explaining complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Expert with PyTorch or JAX.

 - Not afraid of contributing to a big codebase; finds their way around independently with little guidance.

 - Writes clean, readable, high-performance, fault-tolerant Python code.

 - Doesn’t need roadmaps: moves independently and navigates uncertainty with confidence.

 - Low-ego, collaborative and eager to learn.

 - Track record of success through personal projects, professional projects or academia.




NICE TO HAVE

 - PhD / Master in a relevant field (Computer Science, Mathematics, Machine Learning).

 - Experience with autoformalization, proof automation, or verified code generation.

 - Experience with reinforcement learning using verifiable rewards, ideally from Lean or other proof assistants.

 - Contributions to a large open-source or industry codebase.

 - Publications in top academic journals or conferences.

 - Enjoys improving existing code: typing, tests, CI pipelines.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.desc: ABOUT CFM Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients. We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions. YOUR ROLE We’re hiring for a Machine learning researcher: a role that blends modern ML research, GPU-heavy experimentation, quantitative modelling, and production-quality engineering. You’ll join a newly formed quant research team whose goal is to build AI-based alpha models that are predictive, reliable and efficient. You will work at the intersection of research and engineering to design, implement, and scale the AI models and algorithms that power our predictive signals. You’ll collaborate closely with data teams, the ML platform team, portfolio teams, and quant researchers across the firm. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES • You’ll be engaged as a core contributor to our AI-based alpha models, working across research and engineering. • Research: Iterate on data pipelines, target definitions, model architectures, and training recipes (optimization strategies and hyperparameters). You’ll be responsible for both getting things to work, and developing a deeper understanding, which we can bring to the next problem. • Engineering: Develop, optimize, and scale distributed training and evaluation workflows for large-scale foundation models, working closely with the ML platform team to efficiently leverage multi-GPU infrastructure. • Keep up with the latest DL research and collaborate with diverse teams, including other quant researchers, software engineers, and hardware architects. • Attend conferences and communicate research results to the rest of the firm. Where possible, there will be the opportunity to publish your research. YOUR SKILLS Required: • Proficiency in Python and at least one deep learning framework such as PyTorch. • PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning or other quantitative domains preferred. Open also to candidates with 2/3 years experience in a AI research role. • Experience with end-to-end model development, spanning dataset construction, training, evaluation, profiling, and monitoring. • Familiarity with modern model architectures, e.g. MoEs, long-context transformers, vision-language models, efficient attention mechanisms (e.g. GQA/MQA), and new techniques such as multi-token prediction. • Experience training and scaling models using distributed training frameworks such as PyTorch Distributed, DeepSpeed, FSDP, or Megatron-LM. • Strong engineering skills, ability to contribute performant & maintainable code, profile bottlenecks, debug training failures, and work with large codebases. • Initiative and appetite for helping shape the direction of a newly formed team. Preferred (we encourage you to apply even if you don’t satisfy all of the below): • Experience optimizing LLM inference (e.g. KV-cache management, continuous batching, quantization, speculative decoding) • Familiarity with distributed execution and orchestration tools such as Ray or Kubernetes. • Experience with RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, or reward modeling. • Experience with CUDA, including developing custom kernels or other GPU performance optimizations. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT We are continuously striving to be an equal opportunity employer and we prohibit any discrimination based on sex, disability, origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, or religion. We believe that our diversity, breadth of experience, and multiple points of view are among the leading factors in our success. CFM is a signatory of the Women Empowerment Principles. FOLLOW US Follow us on Twitter or LinkedIn or visit our website to find out more about CFM.

Our Computer Vision and Machine Learning algorithms detect every player, the ball and the referees, locate them on the field, track them frame by frame and recognize who is who. Since 2016, we have grown into a global leader in our field. We cover more than 150 men’s and women’s competitions, hold over 100 billion data points on more than 100,000 professional players, and are trusted by more than 350 football, basketball and American football teams. Clubs, federations and agencies use our data to rethink how they analyze performance, scout and recruit. We are a team of about 150 people around the world, with our tech team based mostly in Paris. The Computer Vision team, 16 people strong, sits at the heart of our mission: it uses state-of-the-art deep learning to deliver precise, high-quality tracking data, at scale and in production. The role We are looking for a Computer Vision Scientist to join our Computer Vision team. You will bring solid experience in deep learning applied to computer vision to the models that power our tracking data, from detection and tracking to re-identification and recognition. You will own key models: designing and training architectures, building training and evaluation pipelines, and pushing performance to production-grade quality. You will work with tools like PyTorch/TensorFlow, OpenCV and deep learning architectures (CNNs, Transformers, etc.). You will make technical decisions with real downstream impact and help raise the research and engineering standards of the team. This role sits where applied research meets production. Your work will go from experiment to live deployment, used by professional sports teams and organizations around the world. items.desc: Your Mission As Research Scientist / Engineer — Data , you will develop the methods that efficiently turn diverse data into better humanoid robot policies at UMA. You will investigate which data improves robot learning , how to make it useful, and when to introduce it during training. You will work with on-robot teleoperation, simulation, and off-robot data —including egocentric human recordings and UMI-style demonstrations—across pretraining, mid-training, and post-training . Your research will help answer central questions: what should we collect next? How can human demonstrations transfer to robots? Which data mixtures, representations, and supervision signals produce the greatest gains in real-world performance? We already have a working data and training stack and a strong team behind it. Working closely with our AI, Robotics, and Data Infrastructure teams, you will take ideas from dataset design and research prototypes through controlled training experiments to validation on humanoid robots . Your findings will directly shape our data collection and acquisition strategy , helping us improve robot capabilities while making the best and most efficient use of collection effort and compute. Key responsibilities: Develop methods to make off-robot data useful for robot learning, including action inference, retargeting, and alignment across viewpoints and embodiments, drawing on camera and hand pose estimation or object tracking where useful. Research data composition across training stages: broad pretraining, mid-training, and post-training using demonstrations, simulation, and deployment experience. Design data curation tools and selection methods for filtering, segmentation, annotation, quality scoring, and identifying informative examples. Study source mixtures, sampling strategies, curricula, supervision signals, re-annotation and data ingestion strategies, and implement these ideas in training experiments. Run controlled ablations and scaling studies to isolate the effects of data quantity, quality, diversity, and source under realistic compute budgets. Measure impact on real-robot success, generalization, robustness, and adaptation efficiency, including how much additional robot data is needed to learn new tasks. Shape collection and acquisition priorities based on evidence: which tasks, environments, embodiments, data types, failures, and recoveries are worth capturing, and at what cost. Work with data engineers to turn validated research methods into reproducible processing and training workflows. What You Bring To The Table Strong experience in data-centric research, robot learning, computer vision, or multimodal learning, demonstrated through research projects, deployed systems, publications, or open-source work. Strong Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience implementing research ideas and training or fine-tuning models. A solid understanding of machine learning and experimental design: meaningful baselines, controlled comparisons, reproducibility, and evaluation beyond training loss. Experience investigating how data quality, coverage, mixtures, and distribution shifts affect downstream model behavior. Experience with multimodal or sequential data, such as video, motion, sensor streams, or action trajectories. The ability to connect research findings to practical decisions about data collection, training, and robot evaluation. Experience in working with large-scale multimodal data. Thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced startup: autonomous, rigorous, collaborative, and curious about robotics and learning. Bonus: egocentric data, robot teleoperation, UMI-style demonstrations, simulation, or autonomous-vehicle datasets. Bonus: 3D geometry, pose estimation, retargeting, cross-embodiment learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or sim-to-real transfer. Bonus: active data selection, public datasets, open-source contributions, or technical writing. Bonus: Optimizing data ingestion pipelines during training. UMA is an inclusive workplace that values exceptional researchers and builders over perfect resumes . If you enjoy discovering what makes data useful and turning those findings into better robot capabilities, we strongly encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box.

items.desc: Develop the Next Generation of AI for Computational Life Sciences At JIJ, we develop advanced computational technologies for solving complex scientific and industrial problems. Our R&D spans machine learning, mathematical optimisation, network science, quantum and quantum-inspired computing, with a strong emphasis on translating fundamental research into practical scientific impact. We are expanding our interdisciplinary life-sciences research team to develop advanced computational approaches for challenging problems in microbiology, bioinformatics, genetics, microbiome science, and biological network modelling . Example problems include understanding how microbial communities change over time, how microorganisms interact, how biological perturbations propagate through these communities, and which mechanisms determine recovery or loss of resilience. This is not a role focused simply on applying standard machine-learning pipelines to biological datasets. It is particularly suited to researchers interested in developing new computational methodology and translating research ideas into reproducible scientific technology. The Opportunity We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer with expertise spanning computational biology and machine learning to develop next-generation models of longitudinal microbiome systems. You will work with high-dimensional biological datasets including microbial abundance, genomic and functional information, environmental or intervention metadata, and potentially metabolomic and other multi-omics measurements. A central research direction will be representing biological systems as dynamic graphs , where microorganisms, genes, metabolites, pathways, or host factors form interacting networks whose topology and state evolve over time. You will investigate state-of-the-art approaches including: Graph machine learning : GNNs, message passing, graph attention, graph transformers, and heterogeneous or knowledge-graph models. Temporal and dynamic modelling : evolving interaction networks and continuous-time or state-space approaches. Biologically informed learning : combining pathway, phylogenetic, metabolic, and genomic priors with data-driven models. Representation and multi-omics learning : self-supervised methods, foundation-model representations, and multimodal integration. Causal, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware modelling for perturbation analysis, biological discovery, and robust prediction. Where scientifically justified, you may also investigate quantum or quantum-inspired approaches (e.g. quantum machine learning, quantum kernels, tensor networks, Ising/QUBO formulations). These are complementary research directions rather than mandatory components of every project. What You'll Do Computational Biology & Biological Representation Develop computational models for microbiome dynamics, perturbation, recovery, resilience, and broader biological network problems. Build biologically meaningful graph and multi-omics representations that integrate microbial, genomic, metabolic, pathway, phylogenetic, and host information. Formulate biologically meaningful questions and translate them into rigorous computational experiments. Graph, Temporal & Interpretable Learning Design and evaluate GNN, graph-transformer, temporal, causal, and interpretable learning methods. Address microbiome-specific challenges such as compositionality, sparsity, batch effects, confounding, and irregular sampling. Establish strong classical and statistical baselines and distinguish statistical associations from biologically plausible mechanisms. Research to Impact Translate state-of-the-art research into reproducible experiments, research software, technical reports, and peer-reviewed publications. Collaborate across computational and experimental teams and with academic, scientific, and industry partners. Develop reusable methods and technologies rather than one-off analyses wherever possible. Qualifications We are looking for engineers and researchers who can move comfortably between biology, mathematics, and machine learning . You may be an excellent fit if you have: A PhD, or a research-intensive MSc with significant experience, in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Microbiology, Genetics, Genomics, Systems Biology, or a closely related discipline. A strong background in statistics and machine learning, with the ability to design, train, validate, and rigorously benchmark predictive models for complex scientific datasets. Practical experience developing models in Python using PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or an equivalent framework. Experience with graph machine learning or biological network modelling (GNNs, graph attention or transformers, heterogeneous graphs, knowledge graphs, or temporal graph models). Strong working knowledge of microbiology, microbial ecosystems, genetics, molecular biology, or bioinformatics, enabling effective communication with biological …

items.desc: London, UK · Full-time · £120k–£300k base salary + 1.2–3% equity About us At Archemind (currently stealth), we’re tackling one of artificial intelligence's fundamental challenges: making AI systems genuinely adaptive. Foundation models have made extraordinary progress, yet they still struggle to adapt to new tasks, environments and changing requirements. We believe the next major advances in AI will come not only from making models more capable, but from enabling them to learn, adapt and improve through experience. Our research combines foundation models, reinforcement learning, post-training and adaptive learning, with the ambition of developing new approaches to machine intelligence with broad real-world impact. Our founding team brings together experience from Google DeepMind and Oxford , with deep expertise in machine learning, reinforcement learning, foundation models, adaptation and personalisation. At DeepMind, our team members worked on Gemini and led research on user adaptation, evaluation and model behaviour. Our scientific advisors are internationally recognised researchers in artificial intelligence: Michal Valko , co-founder of DeepMind’s Paris office and Professor Philip Torr , University of Oxford. We also collaborate with the University of Cambridge on computational models of cognition and human states. We’ve received early backing from venture capital investors and angels, and are now preparing for our first institutional funding round. The Opportunity You’ll join Archemind at a formative stage and help shape the research direction, core technology and engineering foundations of a new AI company. You’ll have substantial autonomy to identify important problems, develop novel methods, lead research initiatives and turn promising results into real-world systems. As the company grows, you’ll help shape its technical culture and strategy, and can take on research or engineering leadership. Depending on your expertise and interests, you'll contribute to areas including: Adaptive intelligence: new approaches that let AI systems adapt to changing tasks, environments and requirements. Reinforcement learning and post-training: algorithms that improve the capabilities, adaptability and behaviour of foundation models. Learning from experience: methods that let AI systems learn from interactions, feedback and outcomes. Evaluation and generalisation: rigorous methods for measuring adaptation, learning, robustness and generalisation. New learning paradigms: architectures, algorithms and training approaches built for continual adaptation. Research to production: turning fundamental research into scalable, real-world AI systems. Who We're Looking For We're particularly interested in people who combine strong machine learning expertise with an entrepreneurial mindset , and who thrive on difficult, open-ended problems. You should have: Excellent foundations in modern machine learning, with a strong understanding of model architectures, training methods and evaluation; Strong hands-on programming skills, particularly in Python and PyTorch, JAX or equivalent frameworks; Experience conducting ML research, building sophisticated ML systems, or both; The ability to work independently and solve difficult problems with limited direction; Scientific rigour and a willingness to challenge existing approaches; A genuine interest in building a company, not just contributing to an isolated research project; 2+ years of experience at a frontier AI lab or high-impact startup. Particularly relevant experience: LLM post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling or preference optimisation; Personalisation, recommendation systems, user modelling or long-term memory; AI agents, adaptive systems or human–AI interaction; Scalable ML infrastructure, distributed training or inference systems; Strong open-source contributions, publications at leading ML conferences; PhD in a relevant field from a top lab. Location & Compensation Location: London, King's Cross, UK Type: Full-time Base salary: £120,000–£300,000 Equity: 1.2–3% Both depending on experience and responsibilities. We're looking for people excited to help build a new AI company and want their work to have a lasting impact. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

items.card: The Role The video understanding pipeline—from multi-object tracking and re-identification to action recognition—is yours to own and scale. items.desc: The Role The video understanding pipeline—from multi-object tracking and re-identification to action recognition—is yours to own and scale. The technical challenge lies in balancing high-throughput, low-latency GPU inference with cutting-edge detection accuracy across massive streams of sports footage. You will establish rigorous benchmark suites and decide which vision foundation models make it into production. About the Product The platform ingests live and recorded sports video to automatically extract real-time metadata, temporal key moments, player statistics, and scene-boundary events. Operating across multiple sports leagues, it relies on frame-accurate video parsing to power downstream broadcast automation, search, and analytics tooling. Technology Stack: The core ML pipeline is built in Python using PyTorch for model training and fine-tuning. Production GPU inference is optimized for cost and latency using TensorRT and ONNX Runtime within Dockerized, queue-driven microservices. FFmpeg handles large-scale video decoding, while Azure (Service Bus, Blob Storage) underpins the asynchronous messaging infrastructure. What You’ll Be Doing Own and improve the vision services Own the video understanding pipeline, including object detection, multi-object tracking, player re-identification, jersey-number recognition and on-screen text recognition (OCR). Own event and action recognition, including temporal localisation of key moments, shot and scene-boundary detection, replay detection and camera-view classification. Optimise GPU inference for throughput and cost through batching, precision tuning and compilation. Monitor production quality and latency, and investigate failures and regressions. Evaluate and test new models Build and maintain labelled sports benchmarks, split by sport, league and content type. Define and track key metrics, including mAP, F1, precision, recall, IoU, latency and GPU cost. Run systematic bake-offs comparing new detection, tracking, segmentation, re-identification and video foundation models. Reproduce published results on our data. Write decision memos with clear recommendations, trade-offs and licensing considerations. Own the regression suite and shadow or A/B testing pipelines, ensuring every model or configuration change is validated before deployment. Track new papers, model releases and leaderboards, and identify which developments warrant further evaluation. What We Expect Must have 3–5+ years of experience shipping production ML systems, including 2+ years in computer vision, ideally working with video. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, including hands-on experience profiling and optimising GPU inference using TensorRT and ONNX Runtime. Hands-on experience in at least two of the following areas: object detection and segmentation (YOLO, DETR-family, SAM), OCR and scene-text recognition, or video action recognition and temporal localisation. Experience building test sets, calculating evaluation metrics such as mAP, F1 and temporal IoU, and running rigorous model comparisons. Ability to critically evaluate new research papers and model cards, and reproduce published results. Production deployment experience with Docker, queue-driven services and cloud GPU infrastructure. Experience with video processing at scale, including FFmpeg, video decoding pipelines and frame sampling. Strong written communication skills, with the ability to document technical trade-offs and make clear recommendations. Nice to have Experience with Azure (Service Bus, Blob Storage) and message-driven architectures. Experience with vision-language models and multimodal understanding across video, audio and text. Experience fine-tuning or adapting vision models to specific domains, particularly sports video. Experience with self-supervised learning or synthetic data generation to reduce labelling costs. Familiarity with annotation tools such as CVAT and Label Studio, and experience working with labelling teams. Experience with shadow deployments and A/B testing. Familiarity with commercial model licensing. Why This Role Is Worth Your Time Direct, unconstrained ownership of the full ML lifecycle—from paper replication and benchmark creation to live GPU optimization. Production impact at scale, where your model optimization directly lowers real-world infrastructure costs and improves latency on high-volume video data. High-rigor, evidence-driven engineering environment that prioritizes A/B testing, shadow paths, and statistical validation over hype. Category Machine Learning · Сomputer Vision Type Location hybrid · Poland · Warsaw

items.desc: Here at Humanoid, we believe in a future where robots amplify human potential. That’s why we’ve set out on a mission to build the world’s most capable, commercially-scalable, and safe humanoid robots. We’re bringing that mission to life with HMND‑01 - our rapidly developed humanoid platform being deployed in real industrial environments - and we’re growing the team to take it even further. About The Role We're hiring a strong Robotics Learning Engineer to join our Manipulation team based in London. In this role, you will work on teaching our robots to manipulate the world around them. This is a role at the intersection of applied deep learning and robotics, and to be set up for success you need both experience of working with real robot hardware (e.g. identifying issues in control or teleop), and applied deep learning (you don’t have to be an expert on cutting edge neural network techniques, but you should be perfectly capable of curating data, fine-tuning a policy on that data and hypothesising potential mitigations when something doesn’t work). What You’ll Do Post-train manipulation policies via behaviour cloning and RL; own the full loop from data to deployment. Come up with data preprocessing strategies to improve the quality of collected data. Work with the simulation team to set up RL training using digital twin, and then iterate on reward and simulation quality to ensure successful transfer to the real world. Partner with the data collection organization to drive data collection activities for a specific capability: specify what good data looks like, ensure diversity and coverage, and iterate on instructions. Expand observation and action spaces with new components required to support novel capabilities, and work with the Teleoperations team to expose these components to robot operators. Partner with Teleoperations and Controls teams to improve motion smoothness and teleoperation experience. Interface with hardware design team to ensure that manipulation team findings regarding the current generation of hardware are reflected in future designs. What We're Looking For 3+ years working on robots (industry or research) with shipped artifacts to show for it. A good understanding of modern teleoperation and low-level control stack. Experience with neural network post-training. Familiarity with deep learning infrastructure: streaming datasets, checkpointing & state management, distributed training, PyTorch or JAX. Ability to profile & debug numerics and write maintainable research code. Good familiarity with modern software engineering practices. Ability to document experiments clearly and communicate trade‑offs crisply. Nice To Have Experience training VLA models for manipulation (autoregressive, diffusion or flow-matching based). Familiarity with OpenVLA, Physical Intelligence (π) models, or similar open VLA frameworks. Experience applying RL to robotics problems. Publications at top-tier robotics or deep learning conferences or equivalent open‑source contributions. What We Offer Competitive equity: stock options with meaningful upside as we scale. 30+ paid days off, including 23 days of annual leave, all UK bank holidays, and additional company closure days (including Christmas–New Year shutdown). Private healthcare, including virtual and in-person care. Pension scheme with 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings. Free daily breakfast, catered lunch, and snacks in-office. Work at the frontier - collaborate daily with world-class engineers, researchers, and product experts building the next generation of AI and humanoid robotics. Real ownership - direct access to founding leadership, meaningful input on product direction, and the ability to drive key initiatives from day one.

items.desc:
RIVR, an Amazon company, is building Physical AI by deploying autonomous robots for real-world doorstep delivery. Operating daily in diverse urban environments, RIVR's robots continuously learn from and navigate the millions of scenarios encountered during deliveries. By owning the full stack from software.
Our fleet of delivery robots operates globally today, generating vast amounts of robotic real-world data. By utilizing state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, large-scale generalist models (like Transformers), generative AI, and similar methods, we can leverage this pool of data to significantly enhance its autonomy, navigation, and manipulation skills. In this role, you will develop multi-modal models that enable robots to autonomously generate actions from demonstrations, real-time sensor data, and natural language commands. We are seeking an expert in VLA models, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques with a deep knowledge of supervised, and self-supervised learning algorithms. If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of AI we invite you to join us in shaping the future of intelligent robotics. 
Key job responsibilities
Develop and implement Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, generalist robot transformers, and imitation learning algorithms (e.g., diffusion policies) to enable robots to autonomously execute complex tasks.
Design, test, and refine your algorithms to meet the demands of complex real-world autonomy and navigation tasks, with a focus on spatial reasoning and generalization.
Streamline the data collection and training workflow to efficiently expand model capabilities with new tasks and data sources.
Collaborate with the reinforcement learning team to innovate methods that leverage both simulated and real-world data.
Optimize and distill networks for real-time deployment on the edge (e.g. Nvidia Jetson Thor).
Build, lead and mentor an exceptional team of software engineers.
Provide expert guidance to product managers and executives for strategic decision-making.
Create and maintain documentation, guidelines, and best practices to streamline knowledge sharing.
About the team
Our team is focused on applying scientific research to solve meaningful customer problems at Amazon scale. We bring together scientists and engineers who are passionate about translating ideas from the latest academic literature into production systems that make a real difference. We value collaboration, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to rigorous, reproducible science. As we continue to grow, you will have the opportunity to shape new solutions, contribute to published research, and develop your career alongside some of the most talented minds in the industry.
- Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning.
- At least three years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable.
- Strong deep learning fundamentals including supervised learning, self-supervised learning, Transformer-based architectures, policy optimization algorithms, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques (including Diffusion Models).
- Proven experience in developing Vision-Language-Action models or large-scale generalist robot models (e.g., RT-2, Octo).
- Strong background in robotics including autonomy, navigation.
- Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms.
- Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python (Pytorch)
- PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience.
- Publications at top-tier conferences.
- Experience in managing a software team.
- Ability to write production-level code in modern C++

The UCL Cancer Institute is a world-leading centre for cancer research, bringing together more than 400 scientists and clinicians who work collaboratively to understand cancer and translate discoveries into improved diagnostics, treatments and patient outcomes. Professor Attard’s research group utilises bioinformatic analysis, computational modelling, and digital histopathology to interrogate treatment resistance in prostate cancer, and he leads several of the world leading trials in prostate cancer, including STAMPEDE, that have changed clinical practice multiple times. Dr. Chakraborty’s research group TRAIL is a computational lab that develops state of the art explainable and trustable AI/ML methods applied to grand challenges in personalised healthcare and precision biomedicine, particularly multimodal computational cancer problems. UCL Medical Physics & Biomedical Engineering is a world-leading multidisciplinary department that develops innovative technologies spanning medical imaging, biomedical engineering, healthcare technologies, artificial intelligence and computational medicine. Cancer is a complex, multi-scale disease involving interacting processes across the molecular, cellular, tissue and organ levels. At the same time, advances in genomics, molecular profiling, pathology, imaging and clinical data collection have generated unprecedented volumes of multimodal cancer data. A major challenge is to integrate these diverse data sources into coherent computational frameworks that can generate biological insights, support clinical decision-making and accelerate therapeutic discovery. We are seeking a highly motivated and talented Data Scientist (Grade 7) in AI for computational cancer to join an ambitious and multidisciplinary research programme focused on constructing and validating transparent, interpretable, and biologically grounded models directly from multimodal cancer datasets. About the role The successful candidate will lead the research, generation, and exploration of novel multi-modal AI models, intended to deepen our understanding the underlying relationships between different forms of computational cancer data - including digital histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and genomics - generated from tissue samples collected as part of prostate cancer clinical trials. The researcher will contribute to fundamental advances in our understanding of cancer biology while supporting the development of innovative approaches for patient stratification, therapeutic target discovery, treatment optimisation and precision oncology. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to publish in leading journals, present their work at major international conferences and contribute to the development of transformative AI technologies with significant scientific and clinical impact. This is an exceptional opportunity for an ambitious AI researcher to develop and apply cutting-edge AI technologies to challenging real-world problems in biomedicine. For more details about the Attard Group, please visit: Treatment Resistance | Faculty of Medical Sciences This post is funded for 1 year in the first instance, with potential of extension subject to availability of funds. Applications should include a CV and a Cover Letter: In the Cover Letter, please provide evidence of the essential and desirable criteria in the Person Specification part of the Job Description. You will possess excellent programming skills, particularly in Python and modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and have experience in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing or multimodal AI. items.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. Description of the Research Group At the research group “Hypertension and Cardiovascular Disease” within the Department of Clinical Sciences, Malmö (IKVM), research is conducted in the field of cardiometabolic disease prevention. For several years, the group has been at the forefront of this research area and has identified novel hormonal systems that influence the risk of cardiometabolic diseases. The group is led by Professor Olle Melander and consists of both research and technical staff. The activities are based at the Clinical Research Centre (CRC) in Malmö. A positive and supportive work environment is a priority within our research group. items.desc: « Rejoignez le CEA pour donner du sens à votre activité, mener ou soutenir des projets de R&D nationaux et internationaux, cultiver et faire vivre votre esprit de curiosité. » EN SYNTHESE, QU’EST-CE QUE NOUS VOUS PROPOSONS ? Nous cherchons un(e) Ingénieur(e)-chercheur(se) en IA embarquée pour le CND et le SHM pour le laboratoire « Instrumentation Intelligente, Distribuée et Embarquée » (LIIDE). Ce poste de cadre en CDI est basé sur le site du CEA Paris-Saclay, Essonne (91). Ce poste est à pourvoir dès que possible. QU’ATTENDONS-NOUS DE VOUS ? En tant qu’ingénieur-chercheur en IA embarquée, vous renforcez une équipe multidisciplinaire spécialisée en intelligence artificielle et en micro-électronique dont la mission est de développer une plateforme mixte, matérielle et logicielle, pour concevoir les fonctionnalités de l’instrumentation du futur pour le Contrôle non destructif (CND) et la surveillance des structures et des systèmes (SHM – Structural Health Monitoring). Vous aurez pour missions de : Développer des algorithmes d’IA et de Machine Learning pour l’analyse de données issues de systèmes de CND et de SHM : signaux temporels/fréquentiels, images et données multimodales ; Adapter et optimiser les modèles pour leur déploiement sur des architectures embarquées contraintes développées au CEA (Orchestra, Aidge, etc.) ; Implémenter et évaluer les solutions sur différentes cibles matérielles : microcontrôleurs, processeurs embarqués, GPU/NPU ou FPGA ; Contribuer à l’intégration et à la validation expérimentale des solutions développées sur des démonstrateurs en collaboration avec l’équipe de micro-électronique et les contributeurs des projets utilisant ces outils ; Participer au montage et à la réalisation de projets de R&D collaboratifs ou industriels ; Contribuer au suivi technique et au reporting des projets, en lien avec le chef de laboratoire ; Valoriser les travaux de R&D par des publications, communications scientifiques et dépôts de brevets. Profil du candidat Ingénieur.e /docteur.e en méthodes IA / sciences des données / technologies de l’information, vous disposez de compétences solides dans plusieurs des domaines suivants : Machine Learning et Deep Learning ; Mathématiques appliquées, méthodes statistiques ; Traitement du signal embarqué ; Architectures de réseaux de neurones : CNN, RNN, LSTM, Transformers ; IA embarquée / Edge AI et optimisation de modèles pour des architectures à ressources contraintes (compression, etc.); Programmation Python/C++ et maîtrise de frameworks de Deep Learning tels que PyTorch ou TensorFlow. Des connaissances en microélectronique, architectures matérielles et systèmes embarqués constitueraient un plus. VOUS AVEZ ENCORE UN DOUTE ? Les à-côtés de votre mission principale peuvent vous intéresser : Un écosystème de recherche à la pointe, unique en son genre et dédié à des thématiques à fort enjeu sociétal, qui donne du sens à votre mission Des formations pour renforcer vos compétences, en acquérir de nouvelles et booster votre mission Un équilibre vie privée / vie professionnelle reconnu par nos collaborateurs La possibilité de télétravailler pour équilibrer les temps de transport et contribuer à votre qualité de vie Un CE riche en avantages et en activités sociales, culturelles et sportives Un lieu de travail au cœur d’un plateau dynamique, entouré d’écoles et d’entreprises de la tech Un restaurant d’entreprise subventionné à proximité Un plan d’épargne entreprise avec abondement employeur Des frais de transports en commun couverts à 75% Cela vous tente ? Postulez, ce poste est fait pour vous ! Conformément aux engagements pris par le CEA en faveur de l'intégration des personnes en situation de handicap, cet emploi est ouvert à toutes et à tous Localisation du poste Site Saclay Localisation du poste France, Ile-de-France, Essonne (91) Ville Saclay Demandeur Disponibilité du poste 01/10/2026

La risorsa sarà coinvolta nelle seguenti attività: sviluppo di algoritmi di Computer Vision multispettrale RGB + IR
items.desc: Siamo alla ricerca di una persona talentuosa e appassionata da inserire nel team che sviluppa sistemi di monitoraggio e controllo qualità di processo basati su visione multispettrale RGB + IR e su altri sensori , con elaborazione a bordo su hardware embedded per applicazioni industriali e aerospace . La risorsa sarà coinvolta nelle seguenti attività: sviluppo di algoritmi di Computer Vision multispettrale RGB + IR (termografia) per il monitoraggio di processi e componenti industriali: registrazione e fusione delle immagini, calibrazione radiometrica, gestione dell'emissività; progettazione e training di modelli di anomaly detection non supervisionati o semi-supervisionati (ad esempio autoencoder, modelli one-class, metodi basati su feature) per rilevare anomalie termiche e visive, difetti e derive di processo; analisi dell'andamento dei segnali nel tempo e fusione con altri sensori (ottici, acustici, vibrazionali); ottimizzazione e implementazione dei modelli su piattaforme edge (es. NVIDIA Jetson) con vincoli di latenza, memoria e consumo energetico: quantizzazione, pruning, ONNX/TensorRT; sviluppo della pipeline di acquisizione ed elaborazione real-time in C++ e Python, e trasmissione dei risultati verso i sistemi di supervisione; pianificazione ed esecuzione di campagne sperimentali su banco prova e in campo, costruzione dei dataset e validazione delle prestazioni; collaborazione con team multidisciplinari per l'integrazione del sistema. Chi stiamo cercando Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Informatica, Elettronica, dell'Automazione, Fisica o discipline affini; Solida esperienza in Computer Vision e deep learning (OpenCV, PyTorch e/o TensorFlow); 2+ anni di esperienza con immagini termiche IR o multispettrali e con tecniche di anomaly detection; Ottima conoscenza di Python e C++; Esperienza nell'ottimizzazione e nel deploy di modelli su piattaforme embedded o edge (NVIDIA Jetson, ONNX, TensorRT o equivalenti); Familiarità con ambienti Linux embedded e con l'acquisizione real-time da sensori e camere. Costituiscono un plus: esperienza in condition monitoring, controllo qualità o diagnostica di processo (analisi termica, vibrazionale, acustica); conoscenza di CUDA, GStreamer o ROS 2; esperienza con microcontrollori (ARM Cortex, STM32) e sistemi operativi real-time; conoscenza di MATLAB/Simulink; esperienza in contesti aerospace o con standard di qualifica di settore L'attività si svolge in un contesto internazionale: per questo è richiesta una buona conoscenza della lingua italiana e inglese. Entrando in Modelway troverai: progetti innovativi e tecnologicamente sfidanti; flessibilità organizzativa, con possibilità di smart working e autonomia nella gestione delle attività; percorsi di formazione tecnica e trasversale; programma di mentoring dedicato alla crescita professionale; sede strategica nel centro di Torino; buoni pasto da 10 € per ogni giornata lavorata in presenza. La retribuzione sarà commisurata all'esperienza; per le figure più junior prevediamo una RAL compresa tra €26.000 e €35.000 . I dettagli economici saranno approfonditi durante il processo di selezione per assicurare un accordo in linea con le aspettative di entrambe le parti. Se la posizione ti interessa, devi sapere che: In Modelway sviluppiamo soluzioni tecnologiche avanzate per supportare i nostri clienti nella realizzazione di prodotti e servizi innovativi. Siamo specializzati in modellazione, simulazione e automazione, progettiamo sistemi ad alto contenuto tecnologico per settori complessi e strategici come Automotive, Aerospace & Defence. Attraverso competenze multidisciplinari e l’utilizzo di tecnologie all’avanguardia, accompagniamo i nostri clienti lungo l’intero ciclo di sviluppo, contribuendo alla trasformazione di idee innovative in soluzioni concrete. Retribuzione: €26.000,00 - €35.000,00 all'anno Benefit: Assistenza sanitaria integrativa Bevande gratis Buoni pasto Cellulare aziendale Computer aziendale Congedo parentale Supporto allo sviluppo professionale Sede di lavoro: In presenza

items.desc: Junior AI Evaluation / Trustworthy AI Scientist Job Title: Junior AI Evaluation / Trustworthy AI Scientist Job Ref: AICOS_Jobs_2026_04 Job Type: Full-time contract Job Salary: €1.807,85 Job Location: Porto, Portugal Job Description: Fraunhofer Portugal AICOS is seeking an AI Evaluation / Trustworthy AI to join our dynamic and multidisciplinary team within the Intelligent Systems Group. It is expected that you will contribute to the business area of Digital Health and Digital Futures. As a researcher at AICOS you will work at the forefront of AI innovation, creating purposeful technologies that positively transform industries, promoting social well-being and improving quality of life. Specifically, in this job you will participate in the research and development of components for an evaluation framework to apply in the context of LLMs, agentic AI and physiological time-series data, namely in the dimensions of robustness and uncertainty, and bias/fairness, towards transparent and responsible AI practices. Your role: - Research and develop Responsible AI methodologies related to the evaluation of LLM-based and agentic AI systems, namely: o Investigate robustness, uncertainty, and reliability, including sensitivity to input variations, distribution shifts, and potential failure modes; o Develop and apply methodologies to assess bias, fairness, and performance variability across relevant population subgroups; o Design and implement reproducible evaluation pipelines, systematically analyzing model and system behavior, limitations, and potential risks; - Provide methodological guidance for evaluating AI models based on physiological time-series data, addressing aspects such as data quality, robustness, uncertainty, and performance variability across populations and acquisition conditions; - Contribute to reproducible evaluation reporting and AI model documentation, including model cards, and support the evolution of related internal tooling where relevant. Your profile: - Mandatory Requirements: o Academic Qualifications : Master’s degree or equivalent academic qualifications in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering or similar. o Professional Experience : Minimum of 1 year of relevant work experience in industry, applied research institutions, or universities. - Technical Skills: o Experience with NLP and LLM-based systems; o Experience with time-series analysis, physiological signal processing, or machine learning for biosignals; o Programming proficiency in Python and experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow; o Knowledge of trustworthy and responsible AI, particularly robustness testing, uncertainty estimation, and bias/fairness assessment. - Other Skills: o Excellent English communication skills (technical and general audiences); o Capacity to translate research findings into actionable insights for real-world applications. We value: - Experience evaluating LLM-based applications or agentic AI systems, including their reliability and behavior across different scenarios; - Experience in time-series analysis, physiological signal processing, or machine learning applied to biosignals; - Commitment to clear and honest communication of data, model and component limitations using established reporting standards and tools; - Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and cross-functional teams; - Autonomous, dependable, proactive, and critical-thinking team player. Why should you join Fraunhofer Portugal: - Innovative Environment: Be part of a people-centric workplace that fosters creativity and out-of-the-box thinking. We encourage the development of new ideas and ensure that every voice is heard; - Research with Impact: Engage in projects that sit at the intersection of research and real-world applications, contributing to technology that makes a tangible difference in society; - Multidisciplinary Teams: Collaborate with professionals from diverse backgrounds, enhancing your learning and professional growth; - Professional Excellence: Work within a culture that upholds professional standards and best practices, promoting continuous improvement and excellence in research; - Flexible Work Arrangements: Benefit from flexible working hours and hybrid work opportunities, supporting a healthy work-life balance; - Comprehensive Benefits: Benefit from a partially funded health insurance plan, and a variety of additional perks; - Supportive Culture: Join a team with an excellent spirit, where collaboration, mutual support, and team achievements are celebrated. Application Process: Applications are open from the 19th to the 30th of October 2026. The selected candidate is expected to start working on December 1st, 2026. Applications must be made via Fraunhofer Portugal Website and contain: - Curriculum Vitae – mandatory; - Motivation Letter – mandatory; - Qualifications Certificate – optional.
