items.desc: Mission: As a Forward-Deployed AI Engineer, you will bring the full range of Data & AI expertise - data engineering, data analytics, data science and machine learning - directly into a UAV platform team. You will sit with the engineers and operators who design, test and fly our aircraft in Caldas da Rainha, understand their problems first-hand, and turn them into working data and AI solutions, fast. You will work with flight logs, telemetry, video and mission data; analyse them to answer engineering questions; build models where they add value; and package the results as internal tools, dashboards and integrations with our mission and ground control software. You will be the bridge between the platform team and Data & AI: bringing in Data & AI's platforms, models and specialists, and feeding the team's needs and domain knowledge back into Data & AI's roadmap. You will work AI-first, using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude to prototype quickly, validate with users, and harden what proves useful. We are looking for a deeply technical generalist - a data scientist, ML engineer or data engineer with strong software skills - who enjoys working close to the product and the people using it, and who would rather ship a useful solution this week than a perfect one next quarter. What will be your responsibilities: Data Analytics & Data Science: Analyse flight logs, telemetry and mission data to answer engineering questions - e.g. flight performance, anomaly detection, post-flight review, test and validation analysis; Machine Learning: Identify where ML adds value for the team, then build, evaluate and iterate on models - from quick baselines to production candidates - together with Data & AI's data science and ML engineering teams; Data Engineering: Help make the team's data easy to collect, find and trust - ingestion of logs and video, consistent mission identifiers, documented and queryable datasets; Internal Tooling: Design, build and maintain internal tools - scripts, CLIs, small web apps, dashboards and automations that remove manual work from engineering, testing and flight operations; Rapid Prototyping: Use AI-assisted development workflows (e.g. Claude, Claude Code or similar) to go from a problem to a working prototype in days, test it with users, then iterate or harden it; Systems Understanding & Integration: Build a working knowledge of how our software fits together - mission and ground control software, onboard and ground data flows - so you can integrate with it, debug across it and explain it to others; Bridge to Data & AI: Be the platform team's day-to-day point of contact for Data & AI. Translate needs into clear, scoped requirements, bring in the right Data & AI teams, and help the platform team adopt their products; Field & Test Support: Support ground and flight tests when needed, making sure tools, models and data pipelines work in real-world conditions; Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document analyses, tools and data flows, and share AI-assisted ways of working with the team; Agile Delivery: Work within the team's agile rituals, keep work visible in Jira and Confluence, and prioritise with the platform team's Product Owner. Profile and requirements: Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Aerospace or Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years of hands-on experience delivering data, analytics or ML solutions end to end, in a data science, ML engineering, data engineering or similar role - ideally including time spent working directly with end users or customers. Strong skills in exploratory data analysis, statistics and visualisation, especially on time-series, logs or sensor data. Strong SQL and Python data stack (pandas/Polars, NumPy, Jupyter). Hands-on experience training, evaluating and iterating on ML models (e.g. scikit-learn, PyTorch), including choosing the right metrics and validation approach. Good judgement on when a model is the right answer and when a simpler analysis or rule is enough. Strong Python; experience with at least one of C#, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript is a plus. Experience building internal tools end to end: scripts and CLIs, dashboards or simple web apps (e.g. Streamlit, Dash, React), REST APIs. Ability to read, understand and integrate with existing systems you did not write - APIs, file formats, message buses, databases. Comfortable with Git, Linux, Docker and basic CI/CD. AI-Assisted Development (essential): Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants and agents (e.g. Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to prototype and ship quickly, with the judgement to review, test and verify what they produce. Additional training can be provided in-house, but affinity, some form of experience and strong openness to these new ways of working are essential. Domain Affinity: Interest in aviation, UAVs or robotics. Experience with flight data, telemetry, ground control software, autopilots …

items.desc: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. As an ML Research Engineer in the Visual Navigation team , you will join us at an early stage to heavily influence our technical direction. Operating out of Paris, Lausanne or Zurich, you will focus on developing Machine Learning models to enable our drones to navigate on the battlefield, with responsibilities ranging from data curation and model architecture definition to onboard inference on our drones. Responsibilities DL Algorithm Development: Design deep learning models to analyze a drone's environment in multiple modalities and enable its localization through time and space. Edge AI Optimization: Embed models on heterogeneous platforms with limited shared compute. Optimize trade-offs between model speed and accuracy to minimize pipeline latency. Validation & Field Testing: Actively participate in real-world flight tests. Analyze in-field failures to continuously iterate and improve deployed models. Experience with MLOps and edge deployment optimization. Professional Attributes: Highly structured, analytical, and research-oriented. Excellent communicator able to translate complex algorithmic benchmarking to downstream users and stakeholders. Thrives in a fast-paced environment with a hands-on, “no-task-is-too-small” mentality. Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission, vision, and growth plans, ready to go the extra mile for operational excellence. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. The team InterDigital Video Lab brings together a team of highly motivated, fast-paced, and highly skilled researchers with strong backgrounds in video compression, video processing, machine learning, and standardization. We actively contribute to leading video standards organizations, including ISO/IEC MPEG, ITU-T SG16, JVET, IETF, SMPTE, ITU-R SG6, 3GPP, DVB, and ATSC, alongside mid- to long-term incubation activities. The Media Services research group at the InterDigital Video Lab has broad experience in energy efficient technologies in video streaming and high dynamic range imaging. The research group is dedicated to improving video industry technologies, creating authentic, energy-efficient, and high-quality streaming solutions. Energy-Aware Media project in the Media Services group is dedicated to making the entire video delivery chain more energy-efficient, from content creation through end-user display, while preserving the authentic, high-quality experience users expect. The team develops technologies, tools, and standards that reduce the energy footprint of streaming video at scale. What you'll work on This position focuses on the streaming segment of the energy-aware delivery pipeline. You will design algorithms and systems that make video streaming more energy-efficient end-to-end, including adaptive bitrate (ABR) ladder design, CDN and edge delivery strategies, network-adaptive streaming, and live streaming workflows. Concrete examples of problems you might tackle include energy-aware encoding ladder optimization, CDN cache and routing strategies that reduce end-to-end energy cost, and low-power live streaming architectures based on latest live streaming protocols. Job Summary InterDigital Research & Innovation seeks a qualified candidate to join the Video Lab as a Research Scientist focused on energy-aware video streaming. The candidate will join the Energy-Aware Media project and contribute to designing innovative algorithms, methods, and standards that improve the energy efficiency of video streaming workflows, with a particular emphasis on the streaming layer. The role spans both conventional and learning-based approaches and offers a clear path to taking ownership of dedicated research workstreams as the candidate grows into the role. Responsibilities Identify research opportunities in video streaming with a focus on energy efficiency, including ABR ladders, CDN and edge delivery, network adaptation, and live streaming. Research, develop, and implement new algorithms and prototypes in the identified areas. Contribute to existing research tracks within the team and grow into leadership of dedicated workstreams over time. Disseminate results through invention disclosures and technology reference implementations, tradeshows and exhibitions, and publications in peer-reviewed conferences and journals. Promote the team's research in standards organizations such as MPEG and 3GPP, as well as SVTA, DVB or ATSC Establish and maintain collaborations with external industrial partners and academic groups. Help supervise non-permanent team members, including interns, PhD candidates, and post-doctoral researchers. Expertise in conventional and learning-based algorithm development applied to video streaming, image processing, signal processing, or networking. Publications in peer-reviewed conferences or journals in a related area. Software development skills in Python and C/C++. Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset for working across the team and with external partners. Curious, creative, and motivated personality. Professional working proficiency in English, written and spoken. Nice to have Hands-on …

items.desc: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About The Role You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems. The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model. What You'll Do Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data. 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP. Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production. Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling. Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems. Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate. What You'll Bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience. Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area. Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion. The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy). Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines. …

Job Description Snapshot AI is reshaping our world. Now you get to shape AI. This large and ambitious project aims to develop a groundbreaking family of advanced, multilingual, open source foundation models based on solid research on model architecture, data quality, scaling, generalizability, finetuning, and safety. It combines the unique expertise of AI companies and top academic labs to create models with stronger generalization and finetuning capabilities, as well as enhanced transparency and safety. This will be an inclusive, community-driven project designed to and foster a new wave of innovation and scientific advancement. The team This position is hosted by the research group on Advanced Models by Open Research & Engineering (AMOR/e), providing an ideal environment for advanced AI research and collaboration. We are a team of scientists and engineers who aim to deeply understand, explain, and build AI systems. In addition to producing highly-cited research published at top academic venues, we build models and systems that are widely used by people every day. This work is also part of the OpenEuroLLM project, a large and talented team with world-class labs and experts across Europe, supported by well-known companies with advanced knowledge of LLM development. In this role, you will design and build cutting-edge tools and software that will shape the future of foundation models, used by millions of people worldwide. We appreciate a strong empirical and theoretical understanding of deep learning. Key Responsibilities Contribute to one or more of the following tasks: Develop and implement scalable, efficient model architectures and fine-tuning techniques. Build robust data processing pipelines to enhance learning and generalization. Design and implement benchmarks and evaluation tools. Optimize (pre)training processes and contribute to the development of innovative LLM systems with real-world applications. Create tools for continuous evaluation, monitoring, and visualization of training progress. Collaborate with a team of researchers to tackle challenging technical problems and publish in top venues. What We’re Looking For A motivated and skilled software engineer passionate about open source development and building high-quality, highly scalable AI systems as part of a team. Experience with machine learning, MLOps, foundation models, or LLMs is a strong plus. Impact This is your chance to make a real-world impact by advancing open-source foundation models while collaborating with leading AI researchers and innovative AI companies. Gain invaluable new skills as you help democratize AI, develop cutting-edge models, and create more efficient fine-tuning techniques that empower responsible innovation and drive scientific progress. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in Computer Science or a related field. Strong programming skills in languages like Python and experience with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow). A pragmatic, hands-on approach to creating efficient, scalable, and reliable software systems. Ability to communicate technical ideas effectively, e.g. through discussions, whiteboard sessions, written documentation. Proven experience with open source development and tools is a plus. A true passion for AI! Conditions of Employment An exciting position within an international yet personal university. You are right in the middle of the students, on a green campus within walking distance of the central station. items.desc: Mission As a Forward-Deployed AI Engineer, you will bring the full range of Data & AI expertise - data engineering, data analytics, data science and machine learning - directly into a UAV platform team. You will sit with the engineers and operators who design, test and fly our aircraft in Caldas da Rainha, understand their problems first-hand, and turn them into working data and AI solutions, fast. You will work with flight logs, telemetry, video and mission data; analyse them to answer engineering questions; build models where they add value; and package the results as internal tools, dashboards and integrations with our mission and ground control software. You will be the bridge between the platform team and Data & AI: bringing in Data & AI's platforms, models and specialists, and feeding the team's needs and domain knowledge back into Data & AI's roadmap. You will work AI-first, using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude to prototype quickly, validate with users, and harden what proves useful. We are looking for a deeply technical generalist - a data scientist, ML engineer or data engineer with strong software skills - who enjoys working close to the product and the people using it, and who would rather ship a useful solution this week than a perfect one next quarter. What Will Be Your Responsibilities Data Analytics & Data Science: Analyse flight logs, telemetry and mission data to answer engineering questions - e.g. flight performance, anomaly detection, post-flight review, test and validation analysis; Machine Learning: Identify where ML adds value for the team, then build, evaluate and iterate on models - from quick baselines to production candidates - together with Data & AI's data science and ML engineering teams; Data Engineering: Help make the team's data easy to collect, find and trust - ingestion of logs and video, consistent mission identifiers, documented and queryable datasets; Internal Tooling: Design, build and maintain internal tools - scripts, CLIs, small web apps, dashboards and automations that remove manual work from engineering, testing and flight operations; Rapid Prototyping: Use AI-assisted development workflows (e.g. Claude, Claude Code or similar) to go from a problem to a working prototype in days, test it with users, then iterate or harden it; Systems Understanding & Integration: Build a working knowledge of how our software fits together - mission and ground control software, onboard and ground data flows - so you can integrate with it, debug across it and explain it to others; Bridge to Data & AI: Be the platform team's day-to-day point of contact for Data & AI. Translate needs into clear, scoped requirements, bring in the right Data & AI teams, and help the platform team adopt their products; Field & Test Support: Support ground and flight tests when needed, making sure tools, models and data pipelines work in real-world conditions; Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document analyses, tools and data flows, and share AI-assisted ways of working with the team; Agile Delivery: Work within the team's agile rituals, keep work visible in Jira and Confluence, and prioritise with the platform team's Product Owner. Profile And Requirements Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Aerospace or Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years of hands-on experience delivering data, analytics or ML solutions end to end, in a data science, ML engineering, data engineering or similar role - ideally including time spent working directly with end users or customers. Strong skills in exploratory data analysis, statistics and visualisation, especially on time-series, logs or sensor data. Strong SQL and Python data stack (pandas/Polars, NumPy, Jupyter). Hands-on experience training, evaluating and iterating on ML models (e.g. scikit-learn, PyTorch), including choosing the right metrics and validation approach. Good judgement on when a model is the right answer and when a simpler analysis or rule is enough. Strong Python; experience with at least one of C#, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript is a plus. Experience building internal tools end to end: scripts and CLIs, dashboards or simple web apps (e.g. Streamlit, Dash, React), REST APIs. Ability to read, understand and integrate with existing systems you did not write - APIs, file formats, message buses, databases. Comfortable with Git, Linux, Docker and basic CI/CD. AI-Assisted Development (essential): Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants and agents (e.g. Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to prototype and ship quickly, with the judgement to review, test and verify what they produce. Additional training can be provided in-house, but affinity, some form of experience and strong openness to these new ways of working are essential. items.desc: Et si votre prochain défi s’écrivait chez Parrot ? Du Bluetooth dans l’automobile aux drones grand public, jusqu’aux drones professionnels : depuis 1994, nous avons fait de l’innovation notre culture . Année après année, nous transformons notre savoir-faire technologique en solutions toujours plus intelligentes, performantes et ambitieuses . Trois décennies d’innovations nous ont permis de construire une expertise unique et de nous imposer sur des marchés en constante évolution. Et cette dynamique se traduit aussi dans nos chiffres : le Groupe a réalisé près de 80 M€ de chiffre d’affaires en 2025, dont 87 % à l’international . À Paris, 180 ingénieur·e·s R&D imaginent et développent les prochaines générations de drones. De la conception aux essais, les équipes interviennent sur l’ensemble de la chaîne technologique dans un environnement international et multiculturel propice à l’autonomie et à la prise d’initiative . Des projets qui évoluent vite, des cycles courts et des défis technologiques qui se renouvellent en permanence. Votre terrain de jeu : apprendre à un drone à voir, à comprendre son environnement et à s’y repérer en temps réel. Au sein de l’équipe Computer Vision – Deep Learning, votre cœur de métier sera de concevoir et développer les réseaux de neurones qui répondent à un problème de perception concret (détection, segmentation, tracking, estimation de profondeur…), puis de les intégrer, les tester et les fiabiliser jusqu’à ce qu’ils tournent à bord de nos drones. Données, formulation du problème et contrainte embarquée se pensent d’un bloc : exploiter nos données de façon créative en mettant les foundation models les plus récents au service de nos datasets , choisir le paradigme d’apprentissage adapté, et concevoir une architecture taillée pour le NPU embarqué. Vous travaillerez aux côtés d’ingénieur·e·s spécialisé·e·s dans la conception et l’intégration de réseaux de neurones embarqués , en lien étroit avec les autres métiers du drone. Vous développerez votre expertise sur trois fronts : avant tout le deep learning , de la conception des architectures à leur entraînement ; la computer vision , important pour concevoir les réseaux et tout ce qui les entoure ; et l’intégration embarquée (C++, optimisation, tests, debug). Pour progresser sur ces trois fronts, vous pourrez compter sur la veille active de l’équipe, qui suit de près l’état de l’art en deep learning pour le transformer en solutions réalistes sur des cibles contraintes. Vous aimez autant lire un article de recherche récent que traquer un bug sur cible ? La robotique et l'IA embarquée vous passionnent, et la rigueur comme la persévérance qu'exigent l'intégration et les tests ne vous font pas peur ? Ce poste est fait pour vous. VOS MISSIONS : Concevoir : poser le problème de perception, choisir le paradigme d’apprentissage adapté et définir l’architecture du réseau en intégrant d’emblée les contraintes du NPU embarqué, en vous appuyant sur l’état de l’art. Valoriser les données : imaginer des solutions créatives pour exploiter nos données dans les apprentissages, notamment à base de foundation models (auto-annotation, pseudo-labels, curation et constitution de datasets ciblés). Entraîner et itérer : piloter les apprentissages sous PyTorch avec des stratégies d’entraînement en plusieurs étapes, et faire évoluer conjointement données, formulation et architecture, notamment pour la rendre quantization-friendly, jusqu’à la solution la plus performante sur cible. Embarquer : compresser et optimiser le réseau et le code pour la cible (quantification, profiling de latence sur NPU), implémenter la librairie C++ et l’intégrer au firmware, en lien étroit avec les autres métiers du drone. Valider : construire les outils de test et de validation de la fonction embarquée et des briques de computer vision qui entourent le réseau, et mener des benchmarks précision/latence rigoureux et reproductibles, représentatifs de l’usage opérationnel. Voler : éprouver vos algorithmes en conditions réelles, lors de tests avec nos drones. VOTRE PROFIL : Vous êtes diplômé·e d'une école d'ingénieur avec spécialisation en computer vision et deep learning ou disposez d'une expérience équivalente. Vous justifiez de plus de 3 ans d'expérience en industrie . Vous maîtrisez la conception et l'entrainement de réseaux de neurones pour la perception, en Python / PyTorch et avez une forte connaissance de l'état de l'art . Des connaissances en compression de modèles, déploiement sur NPU, en foundation models et modèles multimodaux en C++, outils de test et de débug embarqué et en MLOps seraient un plus. Vous êtes passionné de robotique et IA embarquée , vous êtes curieux et faite de la veille sur l'état de l'art. Vous êtes reconnu·e pour votre rigueur et persévérance, votre prise d'initiative et votre esprit d'équipe. Vous êtes à l'aise en français et anglais pour des échanges réguliers écrits et oraux. items.desc: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future. Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform. We are looking for a Data / Machine Learning Engineer to join our team. This job is for you if you like turning large, messy, heterogeneous experimental data into clean, labelled, trustworthy datasets. You have done this with scientific or industrial sensor data. Familiarity with fusion is a plus but not a strict requirement. Responsibilities Build, maintain and run pipelines that bring experimental fusion data into high quality, consistent, documented, versioned datasets. Develop ML-assisted labelling and event detection (e.g. disruptions, MHD activity, diagnostic faults), using weak supervision, active learning and anomaly detection. Own data quality and provisioning: provenance, calibration metadata, automated validation. Manage and facilitate access for the rest of the team. Work with physicists validating the datasets & labels. Work with our computational scientists and control engineers, who build models and controllers on these datasets, and with customers to understand and integrate their data. Requirements Hands-on experience building data pipelines for large scientific or industrial time-series data formats (e.g. HDF5, Parquet, Zarr). Proficiency in designing, querying and optimizing SQL and noSQL database systems and familiarity with Time Series databases such as TimescaleDB, InfluxDB. Experience in applying ML techniques to time series in Python (PyTorch or JAX): sequence models, anomaly and event detection, semi- or weakly-supervised labelling. Solid software engineering habits: testing, reproducibility, data versioning are second nature to you. Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD thesis and/or published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. You should be comfortable designing data architectures independently from day 1. The following are an advantage but not strictly required: Human-in-the-loop labelling tools and workflows. Pipeline Orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Airflow, Prefect) and data versioning (e.g. DVC, lakeFS). Data from large physics experiments: fusion, accelerators, astronomy, or exposure to fusion data systems (MDSplus, IMAS). What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. Build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation, matched to level of seniority, and benefits including immigration assistance.

You will hold or be close to completion of a PhD/DPhil in health data science. You will have demonstrated the ability to manage your own academic research and associated activities. A strong track record of advanced statistical skills and machine learning with health data is required. Applications for this vacancy are to be made online and require a supporting statement and CV. The supporting statement must address the selection criteria for the post using examples of your skills and experience. Further particulars, including details of how to apply, can be obtained from the document below. Applications for this vacancy should be made online and you will be required to upload a CV and supporting statement as part of your application. Only applications received by 12.00 midday on 29th October will be considered.

items.title: Research Scientist in AI for Robotics F/M
items.card: Responsibilities Conduct research on machine learning approaches for robotics. Develop new models and algorithms in robotics, perception (computer vision) and sequential decision taking. Design and implement prototypes and proof-of-concept systems to evaluate new ideas and algorithmic approaches. Run and analyze large-scale experiments both in simulation and on real robotics platforms with a hands-on approach.
items.desc: About NAVER LABS Europe NAVER LABS Europe is part of the R&D division of NAVER, Korea’s leading Internet portal and a global tech company with a range of services that include search, commerce, content, fintech, robotics and cloud. About The Team The Spatial AI team at NAVER LABS Europe conducts research on AI for robotics and spatially aware agents. Our work is motivated by challenging real-world robotics problems and we are currently building the next generation of agents capable of robust high-level reasoning in complex real-world environments. One of the team’s research directions focuses on AI for manipulation and mobile manipulation. We develop systems that learn through interaction, acquiring diverse, whole-body, contact-rich skills to tackle complex long-horizon tasks. We combine a passion for robotics and its unique problems with an understanding of (and experience in) large-scale machine learning, deep learning and generalization. Through close collaborations with computer vision and robotics teams across NAVER LABS, researchers have the opportunity to connect fundamental research questions with real operational problems. This creates a unique environment to pursue ambitious research directions, publish in leading conferences, and contribute to emerging AI-driven robotics services. The position We encourage early-career researchers and recent PhD graduates to apply. Responsibilities Conduct research on machine learning approaches for robotics. Develop new models and algorithms in robotics, perception (computer vision) and sequential decision taking. Design and implement prototypes and proof-of-concept systems to evaluate new ideas and algorithmic approaches. Run and analyze large-scale experiments both in simulation and on real robotics platforms with a hands-on approach. Contribute to publications in leading conferences and journals in machine learning, artificial intelligence, computer vision and robotics. Required Qualifications What we're looking for PhD in machine learning, robotics, computer vision, or a related field. Strong background in machine learning and AI for robotics. Excellent programming skills in Python and experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch. Experience in designing, implementing, and evaluating machine learning models, especially policies for robotics tasks (manipulation, navigation, mobile manipulation, etc.). Experience with large-scale experiments, simulation environments, or real-world robotics environments. Strong interest in research problems and, importantly, their application to real life industrial scenarios. Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary research environments. Publications in leading conferences in machine learning, artificial intelligence, computer vision or robotics (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV/ECCV, IROS, ICRA). Preferred Qualifications Experience with deep reinforcement learning. A solid background in the fundamentals of robotics (e.g. kinematics and dynamics, control, path planning and physics simulation). Team Publications Reasoning in visual navigation of end-to-end trained agents (CVPR 2025) End-to-End Image goal navigation (ICLR 2025) DOCIR: Disentangled Object-Centric Image Representation for Robotic Manipulation (IROS 2025) Kinaema: a recurrent sequence model for memory and pose in motion (NeuRIPS 2025) What we offer We foster a collaborative environment dedicated to ambitious, multidisciplinary projects that translate advanced research into impactful, real-world solutions, supported by 30+ years of experience in AI and related fields. Flexible work/life balance. We are an equal opportunity employer that hires based on skills, experience, and merit. We foster an inclusive and diverse workplace where all qualified candidates are considered fairly, regardless of background. We’re based in Meylan, close to Grenoble, a city that offers the perfect balance of urban life, cutting-edge research and technology, and spectacular mountain landscapes that provide countless opportunities to relax, recharge, and enjoy the outdoors. All applications will be carefully considered, even if not all required skills are met. We value diverse backgrounds and the potential of each candidate, and we offer training to support the development of necessary skills. NAVER LABS, co-located in Korea and France, is the organization dedicated to preparing NAVER’s future. Scientists at NAVER LABS Europe are empowered to pursue long-term research problems that, if successful, can have significant impact and transform NAVER. We take our ideas as far as research can to create the best technology of its kind. Active participation in the academic community and collaborations with world-class public research groups are, among others, important ways to achieve these goals. Teamwork, focus and persistence are important values for us. When applying for this position online, please don't forget to upload your CV and cover letter. Incomplete …

items.title: Research Scientist – AI-Driven Power Electronics Development
items.card: In this role, you will focus on accelerating design, simulation, control, and validation processes of complex power electronics systems using AI-driven tools and methodologies. As a part of Hitachi Energy’s global research organization, you will join a dynamic, motivated, and multidisciplinary team where you will contribute to the development of AI-enabled methods and software workflows that improve how complex
items.desc: The opportunity For our research centre in Kraków, Poland, we are looking for a Research Scientist with expertise in Artificial Intelligence (AI) applied to power electronics development. In this role, you will focus on accelerating design, simulation, control, and validation processes of complex power electronics systems using AI-driven tools and methodologies. As a part of Hitachi Energy’s global research organization, you will join a dynamic, motivated, and multidisciplinary team where you will contribute to the development of AI-enabled methods and software workflows that improve how complex power electronics systems such as HVDC, STATCOM, SVC, and grid-connected converter platforms are designed, optimized, and validated. You will be based onsite at our Research Center in Kraków, Poland. Strong local ecosystem in the field, combined with global research and business unit interfaces, enables rapid ideation, prototyping, and validation of AI-driven engineering solutions with real-world impact. How You Will Make An Impact Develop AI-enabled software workflows and engineering methods that enhance power electronics design, simulation, and validation processes. Drive applied research in design automation using AI/ML, optimization algorithms, surrogate modelling, and data-driven methods. Develop and validate approaches for design space exploration, performance prediction, reliability assessment, and system-level optimization of power electronic converters. Build AI-assisted simulation pipelines to accelerate engineering workflows (e.g., automated parameter tuning, model calibration, model order reduction, anomaly/fault detection), integrating ML frameworks with MATLAB/Simulink, PSCAD, and/or PLECS. Support component selection, reliability assessment, and scalability improvements for power electronic systems Partner with local Power Electronics teams in Kraków to ground AI solutions in practical converter and controller design challenges, and with local ML/AI teams to scale robust, reusable methods. Collaborate with global research teams and business units to identify high-impact opportunities and translate engineering pain points into user-focused tools and scalable workflows. Work with external partners (universities, research institutes, startups, and industry consortia) to advance joint research initiatives and validate novel approaches. Disseminate results through technical reports, patent applications, and scientific publications. Ensure compliance with applicable external and internal regulations, procedures, and guidelines. Your Background Ph.D. (preferred) or M.Sc. with strong relevant industrial research experience in Electrical Engineering with focus on Power Electronics, Control Systems, Computer Science, or a related field. Solid foundation in power electronics and control (e.g., MMCs, grid-connected converters) and familiarity with system-level performance and validation considerations. Hands-on experience applying AI/ML techniques (e.g., supervised/unsupervised learning, optimization, surrogate modelling, reinforcement learning, Bayesian methods) to engineering or physical system problems. Proficiency in Python and familiarity with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and scientific computing libraries. Experience with simulation and modelling tools used in power electronics such as MATLAB/Simulink, PSCAD, and/or PLECS, and an ability to connect data-driven methods with physics-based models. Demonstrated ability to bridge theory and practice through prototyping and validation in simulation and/or lab environments. Excellent communication skills in English, with the ability to convey complex technical ideas to both specialists and non-specialists. Strong analytical problem-solving mindset and enthusiasm for multidisciplinary, collaborative R&D. More About Us At Hitachi Energy, we recognize that our people are at the heart of our success. We are committed to providing a supportive and inclusive workplace, competitive rewards, and opportunities for professional and personal growth. Our benefits package is designed to help employees thrive both at work and in their personal lives. Our Benefits Offering For This Role Generally Includes Private medical care and life insurance Access to fitness and wellness programs Access to benefits platform with discounts and perks Employee Capital Plans (PPK) Equipment for working from home or allowances for setting up a workplace at home Spectacles and contact lenses allowance Company events and team‑building activities Psychological support program Free parking available Add if applicable: additional benefits may apply depending on the role, grade, and business requirements. You will receive more specific information during the recruitment process. Publication date : 2026-07-09

items.desc: About Us Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI. The Role As an Applied Machine Learning Engineer, you are the technical owner of a customer engagement. This is what is globally known as the Forward Deployed Engineer role; at Fireworks in EMEA it carries the AMLE title. You embed with a small number of accounts, work in their environment, and own whatever stands between them and production on Fireworks: the model, the serving path, the integration, the performance. You scope the work before signature and deliver what you scoped. Depth over breadth: few accounts, owned end to end. What we value most is first principles thinking: reasoning about unfamiliar problems from the ground up rather than from playbooks. You will be evaluated on this directly in the interview process, and strength here can outweigh gaps elsewhere in your background. Four Spikes Software engineering. You ship production systems and are comfortable dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or a customer environment with a deadline. Backend and systems depth, strong Python plus at least one systems language, and fluency with AI-assisted and agentic engineering as a core part of how you build. Machine learning. You take open models and make them better on a customer's task: SFT, LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods, reinforcement learning (RLHF, RLVR), distillation. Just as important, you design evaluations that reflect the real task and let them drive training decisions, and you know when fine-tuning is not the answer. Infrastructure and performance. You know your GPUs: memory bandwidth, kernels, parallelism, what utilization numbers actually mean. Serving and inference optimization: quantization, speculative decoding, batching, KV cache behavior, latency vs throughput tradeoffs, multi-GPU and multi-node serving, capacity planning. You can take a deployment that works and make it fast and economical, and reason about where the bottleneck is before touching a profiler. Customer engagement. You want to be in the room. The point of this role is creating specialized intelligence for each customer: the best model for their task, their data, their constraints. That takes real interest in the customer's problem, not just the technical one. Exceptional here looks like founder energy with customers; the floor is genuine appetite to embed, explain, and own outcomes with them. Key Responsibilities Own Engagements: Take customer deployments from scoping through production, as the single accountable technical owner. Embed: Work directly inside customer teams; understand their domain, data, and constraints well enough to make decisions they trust. Train and Tune: Run fine-tuning and post-training work where the engagement needs it, from data to evaluation to a model serving in production. Optimize: Drive serving performance and cost on Fireworks: model choice, deployment shape, and inference optimization. Scope Honestly: Assess what is achievable before we commit, and inherit what you scope. Product Signal: Feed what customers need back to product and engineering, with enough precision to be actionable. Minimum Qualifications Spikes in two or all three areas. For the ML spike: formal training (PhD, PhD in progress, or a strong MSc) and experience post-training LLMs specifically. For the infrastructure spike: experience with GPU infrastructure, distributed serving, or inference engines. Founder or founding engineer experience. Experience in a startup or fast-paced environment. Why Fireworks? Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving. Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally. Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results. Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation. Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

items.desc: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future. Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform. We are looking for a Data / Machine Learning Engineer to join our team. This job is for you if you like turning large, messy, heterogeneous experimental data into clean, labelled, trustworthy datasets. You have done this with scientific or industrial sensor data. Familiarity with fusion is a plus but not a strict requirement. Responsibilities Build, maintain and run pipelines that bring experimental fusion data into high quality, consistent, documented, versioned datasets. Develop ML-assisted labelling and event detection (e.g. disruptions, MHD activity, diagnostic faults), using weak supervision, active learning and anomaly detection. Own data quality and provisioning: provenance, calibration metadata, automated validation. Manage and facilitate access for the rest of the team. Work with physicists validating the datasets & labels. Work with our computational scientists and control engineers, who build models and controllers on these datasets, and with customers to understand and integrate their data. Requirements Hands-on experience building data pipelines for large scientific or industrial time-series data formats (e.g. HDF5, Parquet, Zarr). Proficiency in designing, querying and optimizing SQL and noSQL database systems and familiarity with Time Series databases such as TimescaleDB, InfluxDB. Experience in applying ML techniques to time series in Python (PyTorch or JAX): sequence models, anomaly and event detection, semi- or weakly-supervised labelling. Solid software engineering habits: testing, reproducibility, data versioning are second nature to you. Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD thesis and/or published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. You should be comfortable designing data architectures independently from day 1. The following are an advantage but not strictly required: Human-in-the-loop labelling tools and workflows. Pipeline Orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Airflow, Prefect) and data versioning (e.g. DVC, lakeFS). Data from large physics experiments: fusion, accelerators, astronomy, or exposure to fusion data systems (MDSplus, IMAS). What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. Build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation, matched to level of seniority, and benefits including immigration assistance.

Founded in 2014, KIEFER has delivered 600MW+ of energy projects and is now developing sovereign AI infrastructure, enterprise AI products and physical AI systems for Greece and Southeast Europe. About the role We are looking for an ML Engineer to develop capabilities that work on physical robots. You will take ideas from model and data experiments through robotics integration and evaluation on real hardware. Our fleet includes Unitree Go2, G1, H1, and B2 robots using NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor compute. Current areas of focus include navigation, learned policies, vision-language-action models, and robotics data. What you will do Develop, train, adapt, and evaluate models for navigation, perception, planning, and robot behavior. Apply suitable methods such as imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or vision-language-action approaches. Build data collection and evaluation pipelines using real-world and simulated robotics data. Integrate models with robotics software, sensors, actuators, and control systems. Test on physical robots, measuring task success, sim-to-real performance, on-device latency, and failure modes. Work with ML, Engineering, robotics specialists, and Product to improve reliability and move prototypes toward repeatable deployment. What you will need 3+ years of relevant ML or robotics engineering experience, or equivalent impact taking research into real-world systems. Hands-on experience developing and evaluating ML-enabled systems on physical robots. Strong Python and production software engineering skills, including experience with ROS or a comparable robotics framework. A strong ML background in robot learning, perception, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, multimodal models, or a related area. Experience with robotics data, simulation, experiment design, and evaluation on real hardware. Practical understanding of sensors, actuators, control loops, latency, and hardware debugging. Why Marvel Fusion By joining us, you will be: Solving one of the most complex technological challenges known to humanity, harnessing Fusion on Earth Part of a highly purpose-driven team working on providing the world with clean, safe and abundant energy Working alongside world-leading scientists and entrepreneurs in the field of Fusion Part of a start-up where growth on a company and individual level is the default The impact you will make As part of our multidisciplinary research and engineering team, you will shape how we tackle computational challenges in fusion research. You will combine your software expertise with the team's knowledge of physics and engineering to develop new approaches, make technical decisions and turn ideas into reliable scientific software. From advancing numerical performance to enabling shared GPU computing on NVIDIA servers or AWS, you will own meaningful technical challenges and contribute directly to our scientific progress. Your responsibilities Develop and maintain scientific Python software, turning research requirements into reusable, tested features and clear interfaces. Work with scientists to define acceptance criteria and verify numerical results against reference cases and agreed accuracy requirements. Use profiling to identify bottlenecks; compare algorithms, code translations and CPU/GPU implementations through reproducible benchmarks. Prepare and deploy scientific workloads on NVIDIA GPU servers or AWS using reproducible environments and automated execution workflows. Work with IT to support multiple users through appropriate access controls, job scheduling, resource allocation, monitoring and result storage. Connect computational services to internal applications through stable APIs for job submission, status tracking and result retrieval. Improve testing, continuous integration, packaging and documentation, and independently carry agreed development tasks through to delivery. What you bring A degree in Computer Science, Physics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong Python software engineering skills and a track record of independently delivering maintainable software within an existing codebase. Experience with scientific or numerical computing, including testing numerical accuracy and collaborating with domain experts. Practical experience profiling computational workloads and using GPU computing frameworks such as CuPy, PyTorch, JAX or CUDA. Hands-on experience deploying scientific Python or GPU workloads on remote Linux servers or cloud infrastructure, including reproducible environments, job execution and data handling. A structured approach to debugging, version control, automated testing and documentation, with the ability to make pragmatic engineering decisions. A self-driven, collaborative working style and excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Nice to have Direct experience with AWS GPU services or shared NVIDIA GPU infrastructure, including containers, workload scheduling or monitoring. Expertise in CUDA, multi-GPU computing, high-performance computing or performance-portable numerical software. Experience integrating scientific applications with compute services, or a background in optics, photonics or experimental data analysis. Experience evaluating AI-based acceleration of scientific workloads against accuracy and runtime benchmarks. What we offer Our mission is motivation enough for many. But we also support our team with benefits that foster wellbeing and growth: Public Transport Subsidy Employee Incentive Program Phone Bill Reimbursement Wellpass or Complimentary Private Health Insurance Professional Learning & Development Budget Relocation Support Company Pension Plan 30 Days of Vacation plus additional half day on 24. & 31.Dec. items.desc: Over Terramira Terramira is een nieuwe kracht in Earth Intelligence, ontstaan uit de gecombineerde expertise van NEO, eLEAF en 52impact. Wij zetten satelliet- en sensordata om in bruikbare informatie voor uitdagingen als klimaatverandering, waterschaarste, biodiversiteit en infrastructuur. Onze klanten – van agro-ondernemingen en waterautoriteiten tot internationale organisaties en overheden – hebben behoefte aan inzichten die betere beslissingen mogelijk maken. Dat is precies wat wij leveren. Bij Terramira geloven we dat impact begint met helder zien. We maken impact zichtbaar. En we brengen deze binnen bereik. Wij zijn een groeiende organisatie met korte lijnen, een open cultuur en een oprechte drive om werk te doen dat ertoe doet. Over de functie Als AI Data Scientist ontwikkel je AI-modellen die geospatiale data omzetten in bruikbare intelligence. Je werkt met satelliet- en luchtbeelden, tijdreeksen en sensordata om veranderingen in water, natuur, landbouw en infrastructuur zichtbaar en meetbaar te maken. Je combineert diepgaande kennis van machine learning met gevoel voor de geospatiale en ruimtelijke context van onze data — en zorgt dat de uitkomsten betrouwbaar zijn, waar en wanneer ze ook worden toegepast. Wat ga je doen? Je traint en evalueert machine-learning- en deep-learning-modellen, en past computer vision toe op satelliet- en luchtbeelden om veranderingen in water, natuur, landbouw en infrastructuur zichtbaar te maken. Daarnaast ontwikkel je time-series- en spatiotemporele modellen en werk je met Earth Observation foundation models, die je waar nodig fine-tuned voor onze specifieke toepassingen. Concreet houdt dat onder andere in dat je: Veranderingen detecteert in water, natuur, landbouw of infrastructuur; Natuurlijke-taalvragen vertaalt naar concrete ruimtelijke en temporele analyses; Modelresultaten valideert over verschillende locaties, seizoenen en databronnen, zodat klanten kunnen vertrouwen op wat we opleveren. Wat zoeken we? Je hebt ruime ervaring met machine learning, deep learning en computer vision, en weet je weg met time-series- en spatiotemporele modellering. Je hebt eerder gewerkt met foundation models, model training, fine-tuning en model-evaluatie, en je hebt affiniteit met uncertainty estimation en explainable AI, zodat je resultaten niet alleen accuraat maar ook uitlegbaar zijn. Daarnaast breng je mee: Kennis van remote sensing, GIS, raster- en vectordata, satellietbeelden, SAR, multispectrale data en/of LiDAR; Begrip van coördinatensystemen en spatial statistics; Goede Python-vaardigheden en ervaring met databases zoals PostgreSQL; Ervaring met reproduceerbare analyses, feature engineering, data preparation, experiment tracking en model pipelines. Ervaring met Parquet, parallelisatieframeworks zoals Ray, orchestratiekaders zoals Dagster, MLflow of FastAPI is niet vereist, maar wel een mooie pre. Je beheerst de Engelse taal; kennis van het Nederlands is een pre. Je communiceert gemakkelijk met collega's en werkt net zo goed zelfstandig als in teamverband. Wat bieden wij? Een veelzijdige functie binnen een groeiend en duurzaam bedrijf voor 32 tot 40 uur per week; Flexibele werktijden; Hybride werken, waaronder twee dagen per week op kantoor; Een kantoor nabij het treinstation en op loopafstand van het bruisende centrum van Amersfoort; Een dynamisch team van collega's die gedreven zijn om de wereld een betere en veiligere plek te maken; Een informele werkomgeving met veel ruimte voor initiatief en persoonlijke ontwikkeling; 25 feestdagen, met de mogelijkheid om een extra week te kopen; Een salaris dat overeenkomt met je ervaring en achtergrond. Ben je klaar om impact te maken? Wil jij AI-modellen bouwen die daadwerkelijk laten zien wat er met onze planeet gebeurt? Solliciteer dan snel! Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Nieuwsgierig naar onze coole initiatieven? Klik hier om meer te lezen over onze customer use cases.

From renewable energy infrastructure and AI systems to robotics and enterprise applications, we connect the technologies that power Europe's intelligent future. Founded in 2014, KIEFER has delivered 600MW+ of energy projects and is now developing sovereign AI infrastructure, enterprise AI products and physical AI systems for Greece and Southeast Europe. About The Role We are looking for an ML Engineer to develop capabilities that work on physical robots. You will take ideas from model and data experiments through robotics integration and evaluation on real hardware. Our fleet includes Unitree Go2, G1, H1, and B2 robots using NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor compute. Current areas of focus include navigation, learned policies, vision-language-action models, and robotics data. What You Will Need 3+ years of relevant ML or robotics engineering experience, or equivalent impact taking research into real-world systems. Hands-on experience developing and evaluating ML-enabled systems on physical robots. Strong Python and production software engineering skills, including experience with ROS or a comparable robotics framework. A strong ML background in robot learning, perception, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, multimodal models, or a related area. Sim-to-real transfer, teleoperation, human demonstration data, or large-scale robotics data collection. C++, low-level control, tactile or force sensing, or real-time systems. What Is There For You Compensation: Competitive package aligned with talent benchmarks. Impact: Hands-on work shaping AI capabilities for Kiefer Tech’s products and real-world applications. AI-native environment: Real challenges across model development, evaluation, and production AI systems. Culture: Engineering-first, high autonomy, low bureaucracy, and space to shape meaningful AI products.

items.desc: A Little Bit About Us At Recycleye we are revolutionising recycling. Our ground-breaking AI-powered robots and optical sorters are making waste sorting faster, cleaner and more profitable. With our advanced tech, the previously unsortable can now be sorted efficiently and effectively. Founded in 2019, we have grown rapidly ever since, with installations at leading waste management companies across Europe and the US. We are on a mission to help our clients produce higher quality outputs – turning the world’s waste into valuable resource. And our work has never been needed more. Worldwide only 9% of plastic waste is being recycled – every day, we are proud to work on making a meaningful difference towards a sustainable future. Be part of it – come and join us! Why choose to work at Recycleye? Our team works together to grow and succeed, driven by our shared values of ambition, curiosity, customer centricity, integrity and respectful ideation. We offer great benefits, built-in upskilling and unlimited holiday. We know that our mission will be achieved by having the most passionate, driven, talented, and all-around best people on our team. So come and help us shape the future! What You'll Work On Our team develops new features across Recycleye’s waste sorting and plant monitoring products, improving the end-to-end performance of our systems. That might mean evaluating and deploying new model architectures, adapting ideas from ML papers to our use cases, implementing novel object tracking algorithms, diving deep into camera optics and calibration, or making our DeepStream pipelines more efficient. Everything we build runs in production on real sorting lines, so we look for the solution that works best for the problem, which might mean stepping back and choosing a better camera rather than chasing a cool new model. You will be a core member of a small, high-impact ML R&D team. Building new features and developing better ways to measure how well our products perform, whether that’s sorting a waste stream or understanding what’s in it, and how real site conditions affect that performance. You will work closely with our data team, who train models day to day for client projects and rely on the tools we build, and with colleagues developing a new plant monitoring product. You will also help support our deployed systems and spend time on site, getting hands-on with the waste they sort. As the team develops, you will help shape how we work, from code review to testing, and take on more responsibility for planning and decision-making. Along the way you will build a deep understanding of our products and the waste sorting industry, keep up with advances in computer vision, and share what we learn across the company. We work mostly in Python, with some Go, deploying models and algorithms to NVIDIA Jetson devices running DeepStream pipelines, supported by Docker, GitHub Actions and Azure. What Success Looks Like Your work regularly reaches production and makes a measurable difference to how our products perform. You bring new ideas to the table, test them, and help shape what we build next. You grow into owning technical areas of our systems, and become a trusted reviewer and planning partner for the team. Teams across the company, from data to install and support, know to come to you, and you help them get the best from our systems. Our ways of working and measuring performance keep improving, so that our systems get better with every deployment. What You'll Bring We’re looking for someone who is proactive, driven and practical, comfortable with change, and keen to learn. We don’t expect you to be an expert in everything on day one. Hands-on computer vision experience, with a background in ML, physics, maths, engineering or computer science. Around 3-5 years’ experience writing production-quality code, primarily in Python, and promoting good engineering practice. A track record of shipping ML into production in a commercial setting, ideally including computer vision on edge devices. Solid software engineering fundamentals: tested code, version control and code review. Clear communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues, and a collaborative approach. Comfort working independently and as part of a small team. Creative, practical problem solving. A love of seeing your work in the real world. You’ll spend time on site and at our demo centre, testing in challenging environments and getting hands-on with the waste our systems sort. It’s the best way to understand the problem you’re solving. items.desc: At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution. We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints. With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge? Research questions you could initially work on Learning dynamics from operational data. How can we identify useful models of a plant from noisy, partially observed data collected during closed-loop control? Optimising under uncertainty. How can Bayesian optimisation improve plant performance when experiments are expensive, samples are noisy, and operating constraints must be respected? Learning while controlling. How can we use dual control and active learning to choose actions that improve performance while gathering information about uncertain dynamics? Learning across plants. Which parts of a model or control strategy can transfer between plants, and how can we adapt them efficiently to a new site? These are meant as examples rather than an exhaustive list. We’re looking for someone who can bring depth to a relevant area, identify promising connections, and help us decide which problems to tackle next. Your main responsibilities As a Research Scientist, you’ll: Help shape our research and development agenda, turning challenges from live plants into well-defined research problems. Develop and implement methods for modelling, identification, optimisation and control of complex physical systems. Design rigorous experiments, establish strong baselines and understand when and why a method works. Work with process engineers to incorporate plant physics, operating knowledge and constraints into models and algorithms. Work with machine learning and deployment engineers to evaluate promising methods and bring them into production. Follow deployed performance, investigate failures, and use what you learn to guide further research. Communicate your findings clearly and contribute to the team’s scientific understanding. What a great fit looks like A PhD in control, machine learning, applied mathematics, engineering, physics or a related field, or equivalent research experience. A strong research background in one or more of control theory, data-driven control, system identification, Bayesian optimisation, probabilistic modelling, physics-informed machine learning, imitation learning or model-based reinforcement learning. Evidence that you can formulate a research question, develop a method and evaluate it carefully, through publications, open-source work or applied research. Strong Python skills and experience implementing machine learning models using tools such as Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch. An interest in working closely with engineers and taking responsibility for how your methods perform in practice. Practical experience deploying machine learning and control algorithms. A strong interest in climate mitigation. You don’t need to know about cement. You do need to get excited about the physics, willing to learn from operators and process engineers, and keen to understand why a plant behaves the way it does. We don’t expect you to tick every box. If you bring depth in a relevant area and these problems excite you, we’d like to hear from you. In return for your hard work, we’ll give you 📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside. 🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team. 🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge 🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one. Our Operating Principles ↗️ Go Gig or Go Home : High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires. 🏭 Concrete Honesty : Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture. 🦾 Autonomous Ownership : High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it. 😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun : Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still …

items.desc: At Marso, as an AI Engineer , you will own the full lifecycle of the robot’s embedded AI models: data quality, training, production reliability, and tooling that speeds up the path from development to deployment. Responsibilities Contribute to the development, training, and evaluation of embedded models that control the Marso robot. Make sure models stay reliable through every deployment stage: PoCs, field tests, and production rollout in general. Help define and assess data quality. Automate dataset extraction for model training. Cut the time-to-value between AI model development and production deployment. Build internal tools to visualize and debug data and model performance. Profile 3 to 5 years of experience in AI/ML engineering, ideally with an embedded or robotics component. Strong command of Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or equivalent). Hands-on experience deploying models to production, including under hardware constraints (edge, quantization, optimization). Solid understanding of data pipelines: collection, cleaning, labeling, and quality measurement. Rigorous and autonomous, and you enjoy testing in real-world conditions, not just in simulation. Nice to have: experience with mobile robotics, ROS/ROS2, computer vision, or sensors (lidar, cameras, IMU). We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of background. Chez Marso, en tant qu’ AI Engineer , vous prendrez en charge le cycle complet des modèles d'IA embarqués du robot : qualité de la donnée, entraînement, fiabilité en production et outillage pour accélérer le passage du développement à la mise en service. Missions Participer au développement, à l'entraînement et à l'évaluation de modèles embarqués pour le pilotage du robot Marso. Garantir la fiabilité des modèles lors des déploiements : PoC, tests terrain et, plus généralement, mise en production. Participer à la définition et à l'évaluation de la qualité de la donnée. Automatiser l'extraction de datasets pour l'entraînement des modèles. Réduire le time-to-value entre le développement des modèles d'IA et leur mise en production. Développer des outils internes de visualisation et de debugging des performances des données et des modèles. Profil 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en ingénierie IA/ML, idéalement avec une composante embarquée ou robotique. Maîtrise de Python et des frameworks de deep learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow ou équivalent). Expérience concrète du déploiement de modèles en production, y compris sous contraintes hardware (edge, quantization, optimisation). Bonne compréhension des pipelines de données : collecte, nettoyage, labellisation, mesure de qualité. Rigueur, autonomie et goût pour le test en conditions réelles, au-delà du travail en simulation. Un plus : expérience en robotique mobile, ROS/ROS2, vision par ordinateur, ou capteurs (lidar, caméras, IMU). Nous sommes engagés dans la construction d’une équipe diverse et inclusive. Toutes les candidatures qualifiées sont les bienvenues et nous accordons une attention particulière aux compétences, à l’impact et à la capacité à contribuer au projet.
