items.desc: Welcome to the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS! As the largest institute within the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, we have been conducting research for over 30 years in diverse fields such as artificial intelligence, microelectronics, sensor systems, data acquisition, signal processing, and signal transmission. Talented individuals from various engineering and natural science disciplines will find a wide range of exciting research topics under one roof. A few highlights that reflect our innovative strength include 5G/6G mobile communication technologies, generative AI in speech and signal processing, neuromorphic computing and X-ray imaging for e-mobility that’s just the beginning! What sustainable solution will you find with us? Be part of change The group »AI-Based Communication Systems« within the Wireless Systems and Standardization (WSS) department in the Communication Systems division at Erlangen focuses on research, implementation and demonstrations of AI-enabled wireless communication systems. The group investigates machine learning and mathematical optimization techniques for sensing and communication applications to optimize radio link, end-to-end network performance, and edge inference across terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Our activities span a wide range of methodologies, from link/system-level simulation and data-driven experimentation to real-time evaluation with hardware-aware training and deployment. Concept & Demonstration: Design, develop, and demonstrate proof-of-concept systems for AI-enabled autonomous communication systems with integrated sensing. Industrialization: Transfer research prototypes into robust demonstration platforms for industrial partners, customer engagements, and technology showcases. Embedded Intelligence: Develop, implement, and optimize AI/ML models on embedded platforms and hardware accelerators. Wireless Algorithms: Implement and optimize communication and signal processing algorithms for real-time wireless and sensing systems. Performance Validation: Evaluate system performance through simulations, laboratory experiments, and hardware-based testing. Project Support: Contribute to technical documentation, proposal preparation, and customer demonstrations. What You Contribute A Master's degree (preferably with a Ph.D.) in electrical engineering, telecommunications, computer engineering, robotics, or a related field. Experience in wireless communications, embedded AI, robotics, or signal processing. Hands-on experience in developing prototypes and technical demonstrations. Strong programming skills in Python and C/C++, as well as experience with common AI frameworks. A solid technical background in signal processing and communication systems. Fluency in English, both written and spoken; German language skills are a plus. What We Offer Top of the line infrastructure at your workplace: With our state-of-the-art technologies, we develop solutions to meet the challenges of today and tomorrow. We value personal contact: With our structured onboarding process, you will quickly become familiar with our institute and be able to extend your network successfully. We take your needs seriously: We support your work-life balance by offering flexible working hours and hybrid work. Your goals and interests are important to us: We offer ongoing professional and personal seminars, coaching, and language classes. We offer complimentary parking spaces, charging stations for electric cars, covered bicycle parking, and showers at the institute. The position can also be filled part-time, but as close to full-time as possible. The position is initially limited to 2 years with the aim to extend it subsequently. Appointment, remuneration and social security benefits are based on the public-sector collective wage agreement (TVöD). In addition, Fraunhofer may grant performance- and success-based variable compensation components. We value and promote the diversity of our employees' skills and therefore welcome all applications - regardless of age, gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, ideology, disability, sexual orientation and identity. Severely disabled persons are given preference in the event of equal suitability. Around 30 000 employees work with an annual research budget of 3.4 billion euros. The Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS, located in Erlangen, is the largest institute of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft with more than 1 200 employees. items.card: The Role As a Computational Chemist, you will play a central role in shaping the scientific foundations of the venture's technology, helping develop the computational methods and workflows that underpin its end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving
items.desc: This an Atlantic portfolio venture. About the Venture This early-stage venture is building a discovery engine for chemistry, comprising a platform for running end-to-end simulations of chemical reaction systems, and a world model + agent stack that uses the simulation platform to discover new chemistry. Their goal is to build backend scientific data infrastructure to meet the demands of AI systems that can truly accelerate and automate the discovery layer of chemistry. Both founders hold PhDs in Chemistry from the University of Oxford, and the venture has already secured pre-seed funding. They are now building out their founding team. The Role As a Computational Chemist, you will play a central role in shaping the scientific foundations of the venture's technology, helping develop the computational methods and workflows that underpin its end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving progress towards the venture's strategic and scientific objectives. You’ll take ownership of developing, validating and optimising the computational chemistry components of the platform, with a particular focus on reaction mechanisms, reaction kinetics, molecular dynamics and the modelling of complex chemical environments. You will design, implement and refine scalable scientific workflows for generating, processing and analysing chemical reaction data, improving the accuracy, reliability and computational efficiency of simulations. Beyond your core scientific responsibilities, the team is looking for someone who can contribute to strategic research decisions, bring strong independent scientific judgement, and help shape the interdisciplinary research culture of the company at an early stage. What You'll Work On Foundation models for chemical reactivity: The team is building and training foundation models for chemical reactivity with a variety of data modalities. You'll help curate this foundational data corpus by developing cheminformatics and computational chemistry workflows for generating data from combinatorial enumeration, as well as robust data filtering, clustering and validation routines. Computational methods: The team is working on efficient computational methods from which foundational data is generated and the platform is validated. You'll be responsible for developing protocols for estimating solvation and entropy factors in chemical reaction steps. This involves keeping up to date with published literature for ideas and inspiration. Generative models: The venture is expanding its foundational data corpus beyond combinatorial workflows. You'll help design, validate and benchmark the generative model architectures that accomplish this. Chemical reaction simulation: The team is building out an end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You'll be involved in designing the architecture and assembling the platform, as well as developing benchmarks and validation protocols against computational and experimental methods. World models and agents: The venture will be developing an agent + world model stack that operates on the simulation platform. You'll be responsible for formulating the action space in which the world model is trained and the agent explores new chemical reaction space. What They're Looking For The team is looking for someone who enjoys being given a blank canvas and the chance to create something spectacular with it. In particular, someone who brings: A PhD in Computational Chemistry, Machine Learning, or a related field. Intellectual curiosity: Someone who enjoys venturing outside their comfort zone, exploring new ideas and applying their knowledge and experience to unfamiliar domains. An entrepreneurial mindset: Someone who thrives in an early-stage environment, enjoys building things from scratch and is excited to grow beyond the traditional boundaries of their role. Independent thinking and scientific judgement: Someone who can take ownership of complex challenges, contribute new ideas and help shape the scientific direction of the venture. A collaborative approach: Someone who can build strong relationships across the team and actively contribute to shaping and nurturing the company culture as it grows. An instinct for building great working environments: Someone who understands the importance of the right tools, systems and ways of working to help themselves and the wider team do their best work.

Job Description Summary 
As AI Data Engineer (f/m/d) in GE HealthCare's Advanced Imaging Solutions business, you will develop reusable tools, operate shared data infrastructure, and evaluate platforms for ultrasound teams worldwide.
At GE HealthCare, our machines, our software, our solutions, our services, and our people make a genuine difference to medical professionals and patients all over the world. That’s because we never lose sight of what healthcare really needs—the human touch. 
This position is hired in Zipf, Austia in hybrid work (min. 3 days per week in office). 
 Job Description 
 AI Data Engineer (f/m/d) 
 As AI Data Engineer in GE HealthCare's Advanced Imaging Solutions business, you will develop reusable tools, operate shared data infrastructure, and evaluate platforms for ultrasound teams worldwide.
 GE HealthCare develops medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and digital solutions that help clinicians make informed decisions and improve patient outcomes. With more than a century of healthcare experience, we pursue a world where healthcare has no limits and embrace respect, transparency, integrity, and diversity.
 Job Description 
 Working with local teams and infrastructure owners, you will turn requirements into tested solutions and help teams adopt and operate common tools.
 In this role you will:
 Work with AI technical leaders to translate cross-team requirements, reference architectures, and priorities into working solutions and operational procedures.
 Design and run reproducible experiments, proofs of concept, and benchmarks on third-party and internal data management and AI development platforms using representative ultrasound team workflows.
 Assess functional fit, interoperability, performance, scalability, usability, integration effort, and operating cost against agreed requirements. Document methods, results, limitations, and recommendations to inform platform selection.
 Collaborate with individual teams to extend internally developed tools for use across the ultrasound organization. Refactor team-specific assumptions into configurable modules and standardize interfaces to increase reuse.
 Develop and maintain shared libraries, services, and connectors, with automated tests, versioned packages, and deployment workflows that make adoption and maintenance easier for other teams.
 Build and operate data ingestion, transformation, and validation pipelines supporting data curation, annotation, dataset preparation, and AI development.
 Carry out day-to-day operation of agreed shared tools and environments, including configuration, updates, job monitoring, troubleshooting, and performance tuning, in coordination with platform owners.
 Support teams with platform onboarding, tool integration, and data or workflow migrations, and provide practical feedback on gaps in shared infrastructure.
 Implement data quality checks, logging, and traceability, and automate approved data access, de-identification, and retention workflows with guidance from the responsible specialists.
 Investigate pipeline and platform failures, reproduce issues, and work with internal platform teams or external vendors to resolve root causes and prevent recurrence.
 Create user guides, integration examples, and operational runbooks; provide training and technical support so teams can adopt, operate, and contribute to shared tools.
 Qualifications

 Master's degree in computer science, data engineering, software engineering, information systems, AI, or a related technical field.

 Awareness of security, privacy, and traceability requirements when handling healthcare data.
 Fluent English and the ability to collaborate with globally distributed engineering, data science, and infrastructure teams.

items.desc:
Join our Team
 About the opportunity 
Join Ericsson Research and help shape the future of connectivity. AI is central to Ericsson’s 6G vision, enabling intelligent, sustainable, and secure networks for people and industries in the 2030s and beyond. Our work combines machine learning, advanced reasoning, and real network systems, with access to live network data and opportunities to influence global standards and technologies used worldwide. 
This early-career role suits a recent master’s graduate or someone with a few years of experience in AI/ML. You’ll take on meaningful research from day one, collaborate with global, cross-disciplinary teams, and learn from experienced mentors. A telecom degree or prior radio expertise isn’t required: you can build domain knowledge through hands-on work with radio specialists. We value diverse perspectives and offer an inclusive environment, flexible ways of working, wellbeing support, benefits, and growth opportunities. You don’t need to meet every preferred qualification; curiosity and motivation matter. 
 What you will do 
• Research, design, and evaluate AI/ML concepts for future radio access networks and AI-native systems, including autonomous, large-scale telecom networks. 
• Develop algorithms, models, and simulation frameworks. Explore AI applications in radio access networks. 
• Use modern AI-assisted development tools to prototype and iterate quickly. 
• Collaborate with experts in radio systems, networking, and hardware, connecting research ideas with practical needs such as performance, scalability, robustness, automation and energy efficiency. 
• Turn research into prototypes, publications, patents, and contributions to future standards. Share findings, build your research profile, and keep learning with support from senior researchers. 
 Skills you bring 
• An MSc in AI, data science, computer science, engineering physics, robotics, or a closely related field is preferred. Candidates with an MSc and strong AI research experience are also encouraged to apply. 
• A strong foundation in modern AI, such as deep, reinforcement, or distributed learning; generative AI; probabilistic modelling; stochastic optimization; or graph-based methods. 
• Python programming skills and familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow. 
• Some experience designing, training, or validating ML-driven systems through studies, internships, or personal projects. Familiarity with simulation-based evaluation is valuable. 
• Interest in AI coding assistants and openness to new tools. Experience with Docker or Kubernetes is a plus. 
• Interest in telecommunications, networking, or signal processing. Telecom expertise can be learned on the job. 
• A curious, self-directed approach: you generate and test ideas, learn independently, ask questions, seek expert input, and work through uncertainty. You bring analytical problem-solving, ownership, and collaborative skills, and can communicate clearly, including explaining AI concepts to non-specialists.

items.desc: Your Impact at LILA We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems. As scientific AI systems become more capable and autonomous, their safety assessment and safeguards must develop alongside them. At Lila Sciences, you will help build the research methods and tools that make this possible, so that more and more decision-enablers can be automated safely. This will move us closer to the vision of a safety and security apparatus that is robust to a fully autonomous scientific engine. Your initial focus will be misuse: developing flexible and automated red-teaming approaches that test safety-relevant scientific capabilities and the robustness of safeguards. You will also contribute to safety automation beyond red teaming, helping the team evaluate, monitor and respond to risks across increasingly autonomous scientific workflows. You will own reusable research methods and assessment tools, working with mitigation engineers who implement protective mechanisms. We welcome Research Scientists and Research Engineers; responsibilities can span or evolve between the two profiles. What You'll Be Building Develop and run capability evaluations of scientific models, agents and tool-mediated workflows (including simulated lab environments), working with domain experts to make tests scientifically meaningful. Create methods or systems that explore diverse failure modes, adapt tests as evidence emerges and support systematic investigation beyond fixed benchmarks. Build reproducible experiments and evaluation tools that capture relevant behavior, outcomes and the evidence needed to interpret findings. Measure the quality and coverage of automated assessments, including failure cases in the evaluators themselves. Develop broader safety automation, across threat model management, evidence triage, regression testing, monitoring workflows or tools that help researchers assess and respond to risks. Collaborate with risk researchers and mitigation engineers to translate findings into improved assessments and safeguards, and verify whether those changes work. What You'll Need to Succeed Strong empirical judgment, practical programming ability and experience working with modern AI systems. The ability to investigate ambiguous failures, design informative comparisons and communicate limitations clearly. An interest in scientific misuse risks and the ability to collaborate productively with domain specialists. For the Research Scientist profile: evidence of selecting valuable research questions, developing or adapting methods, and designing experiments that yield defensible conclusions. You should be able to prototype and test your ideas. For the Research Engineer profile: evidence of building reliable research software, evaluation infrastructure or agent systems that enable reproducible experiments and efficient iteration. You should be able to contribute to experimental design and interpretation. Bonus Points For Automated red teaming, adversarial testing or evaluation-method research. Scientific AI, tool-using agents, laboratory automation or other complex environments. Experience with safety monitoring, model-based evaluators or scalable experimental infrastructure. About LILA Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves. LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai. Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply. items.desc: Project Tricorder — Clinical Infrastructure for Field Operations We're looking for a hands-on engineer to build two foundations of the Tricorder product: the evaluation harness and training data pipeline behind our AI models, and a clinical knowledge base grounded in tactical combat care, SNOMED CT and ICD-10. About Project Tricorder - https://www.tricorder-systems.com/ Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. Care increasingly happens somewhere else - in the field, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward. Tricorder builds the deployable clinical infrastructure for that world: a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It is a dual-use venture serving defence medical and civilian pre-hospital care. Our prototype product is already in user testing. Edge AI sits at the core: multimodal language models that turn video, sensor data and clinical notes into patient records, drive predictions and inform data-driven learnings across deployments. To trust those models in the field, we need rigorous data and evaluation - that's where you come in. What you'll do You'll own two workstreams, working day to day with the founder and the FF build team. 1. Data pipeline and evaluation harness Build the data foundations that tell us whether our models are good enough for clinical use. Data labelling: design labelling schemas and guidelines, set up tooling, and run labelling with clinical input, including quality checks and inter-annotator agreement. Data processing: build reproducible pipelines to ingest, clean, de-identify and transform multimodal data (video, sensor streams, text). Video data organisation: structure, version and catalogue video datasets so clips, annotations and metadata stay searchable and traceable. Training dataset preparation: assemble balanced, well-documented train, validation and test splits, with clear lineage from raw data to model input. Eval harness: build an automated harness that benchmarks vision-language and NLP models against clinically meaningful metrics, tracks regressions and supports build-vs-buy model decisions. 2. Clinical knowledge base Build the structured clinical knowledge base that turns unstructured input into coded, interoperable records. Database design: design the schema and stand up the data store for clinical concepts and their relationships. Clinical terminologies: ingest and map TC3, SNOMED CT, ICD-10 and related NHS standards, including cross-mappings between them. Natural language processing: extract entities and relationships from clinical text and link them to coded concepts. Document handling: parse and structure clinical documents (PDFs, notes, forms) into the database. Clinical knowledge: work with clinicians to make sure the database reflects real-world clinical reasoning and pre-hospital workflows. By the end of the first 3 months, we'd expect a working eval harness in use for model decisions, a labelled and versioned core dataset, and a first version of the knowledge base linked to the product. What we're looking for We don't expect one person to be expert in everything below. Strong candidates will be deep in one workstream and credible in the other. Must-haves Strong Python and data engineering skills, with a track record of shipping production data or ML pipelines, not just research notebooks. Hands-on experience building ML evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or test harnesses, ideally for vision, video or language models. Experience running data labelling and training-data preparation, including annotation tooling and quality control. Working knowledge of databases and data modelling. Practical NLP experience: entity extraction, entity linking or document parsing. Comfort handling sensitive data under data protection and clinical safety constraints. Pragmatism and speed: you can work with ambiguity, make good build-vs-buy calls and ship in weeks, not quarters. Nice to have Experience with SNOMED CT, ICD-10, dm+d or other NHS clinical terminologies and coding. A background in health-tech, clinical informatics or another regulated domain such as defence. Experience with video data at scale (frame sampling, temporal annotation, multimodal datasets). Familiarity with FHIR or HL7 interoperability standards. Experience working with LLMs and VLMs, including edge or on-device deployment. Early-stage startup experience, especially as a founding or early engineer. Probably not the right fit if You need detailed specs and a large team around you to be effective. You prefer pure research over building tools people use every day. items.desc: Job number ENG04085 Faculties Faculty of Engineering Departments Department of Computing Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 22 Nov 2026 About the role We are looking for a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA/PostDoc) to join the Safety&Alignment lab at Imperial College London, led by Dr. Oana-Maria Camburu in a fully funded research role. The position is fully funded in the context of Dr. Oana-Maria Camburu’s grant on the project Detecting Unverbalized Dangerous Capabilities in Frontier Models . The project focuses on the detection of frontier model’s dangerous capabilities that are not verbalized in their Chain-of-Thoughts (CoTs). Externalized reasoning oversight is a safety paradigm focusing on monitoring the CoTs of large language models (LLMs). As frontier models learn that they are monitored, they can become incentivized to hide their dangerous capabilities from their CoTs. Moreover, as these models become increasingly capable, their obfuscation capabilities also increase, allowing them to bypass monitors. This project investigates ways to detect and defend against such emerging scenarios. The post is based in the Department of Computing at Imperial College London at the South Kensington Campus. The Department of Computing is a leading department of Computer Science in the UK and worldwide and has consistently been awarded the highest research rating. In the previous REF assessment, the Department was ranked third (1st in the Research Intensity table published by The Times Higher) and was rated as "Excellent" in the previous national assessment of teaching quality. What you would be doing We strive in publishing in top-tier conferences and journals. Some of the areas you will work on are: Designing and developing novel algorithms for detecting and defending against unverbalized dangerous capabilities in frontier models. Conducting independent and collaborative research within the group. Publishing results in top-tier conferences and journals (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, AIJ, TACL, etc). Contributing to research projects involving frontier models. Contributing to the life and development of the Safety & Alignment lab, such weekly meetings, presentations, etc. Mentoring PhD and MSc students. items.desc: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future. Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform. We are looking for a Computational Scientist specialized in Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) to join our team. This job is for you if you know how to write numerical solvers that are fast, correct and differentiable end to end, and want to see them run against real plasma data and inside real control systems. We are looking for a PhD-level or senior computational researcher for this role. Responsibilities Design, implement and validate differentiable solvers in JAX for plasma physics problems such as free-boundary equilibrium, transport and state estimation. Make them robust and fast enough for production use via advanced numerical techniques for differential equation time stepping, as well as optimization of GPU/TPU performance. Using automatic differentiation for model calibration against experimental data, parameter estimation and controller design and optimization, working with our data and control engineers. Code ownership: quality, testing, verification against reference solutions, packaging and documentation. Requirements Substantial code written in a differentiable framework. Our stack is in JAX, Julia or PyTorch experts are very welcome if they’re happy to switch. Strong background in numerical methods for ODEs and PDEs: discretisation, stiff and implicit solvers, nonlinear and sparse linear solvers. Demonstrated ability to operate at the frontier of SciML, Universal Differential Equations, Neural ODEs, and other emerging hybrid data-driven/mechanistic paradigms. Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD or thesis, published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. Experience in the following fields an advantage but not strictly required: The JAX ecosystem: Diffrax, Equinox, Optax, Lineax. Plasma, fluid, electromagnetic, or other multiphysics simulation. Having led the design of a scientific codebase used by others. What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. Build cutting-edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance.

items.desc: *** FOR APPLICATION please apply by emailing CV and cover letter to info@spliceor.com *** Research Scientist — RNA Therapeutics Spliceor · Babraham Research Campus, Cambridge Full time, Permanent · On site · Start: January 2027 · Closing date: November 15 th About Spliceor Spliceor is a University of Cambridge spin-out, backed by venture funding. We are building a next-generation programmable RNA technology to treat cancer and inflammatory conditions in new ways. One of the biggest challenges in building programmable RNA technologies is control. A treatment delivered to the chosen destination, can also end up in non-target tissues and cells. We build that control into the medicine itself, so it only acts inside the cells it is meant to treat, avoiding off-target effects, and enabling multi-dosing. We are a small team, where everyone inputs into experimental design, execution and interpretation. Being a start-up, we have the agility to make decisions quickly, keeping the gap between having an idea and testing it to a minimum. The role We are looking for a scientist to join the laboratory and take ownership of experimental work on our core RNA constructs. This is primarily a hands-on laboratory-based role. You will design and build vectors, run experiments in mammalian cells, and generate data that moves the programme forward. You will work closely with the rest of the team, and you will be encouraged to contribute your ideas, not just conduct experiments. What you will do Design and build gene expression constructs and RNA vectors. Run mammalian cell culture and transfection experiments. Analyse and interpret data and present it to the team. Build assays from the ground up, troubleshooting them along the way. Keep clear, reproducible records of what you did and what you found. Contribute to grant reports, patent filings and publications. The impact you can have In a startup of this size, one piece of data can change the direction of the science. This is a great opportunity to have real impact in a growing company, with personal visibility, and take on a stimulating, varied role. What we are looking for Ideally you will bring: A doctorate in RNA biology, gene expression, molecular biology, synthetic biology, or a closely related subject. Strong hands-on experience of mammalian cell culture and of the molecular biology behind gene expression studies. Skill in designing gene expression vectors, and experience of advanced molecular cloning (for example Gibson assembly or Golden Gate). A proven ability to design, run, troubleshoot and interpret your own experiments, and to keep clear records of them. Clear communication, and a genuinely collaborative way of working. Also useful, though not essential: A deep understanding of RNA biology: how RNA is processed, how stable it is, how it is translated, and how all of that is regulated. Experience of in vitro transcription of RNA. Experience of qPCR, Western blotting, and plate-based assays such as ELISA and luminescence readouts. A publication record, or an industry track record, in RNA biology or a related field. Experience of flow cytometry workflows and/or quantitative cell imaging methods. What we offer Salary and pension, with level dependent on experience A cross-functional team: you will work directly with people who have run businesses in pharma and biotech, and with people who have spent careers doing the science in industry. A supportive working environment, where you will be given all appropriate training and guidance to thrive in the role. Broad learning. You will see the commercial side of a company and understand how decisions are made as well as having the opportunity to expand your laboratory skills and experience You will be eligible to participate in our employee share option scheme Where you will work Our laboratory and offices are in the Live Labs institute space on the Babraham Research Campus, just south of Cambridge. The campus is one of the largest clusters of early-stage life science companies in the United Kingdom, with shared scientific facilities, a regular seminar programme, and a substantial research community on site. There is free parking, a regular bus service from Cambridge city centre and the railway station, and cafés and a gym on site. How to apply Send a CV and a covering letter to info@spliceor.com We read applications as they arrive, and we will close the advert once we have found the right person. Early applications are encouraged. We aim to have sent invites for interview to prospective candidates by Wednesday 4 th November. We are a small company and we are unfortunately not able to reply and give application feedback to everyone. If you have not heard from us by mid November, please assume we have not taken your application forward on this occasion. We are sorry to do it that way, and we are grateful for the time it takes to apply. Spliceor is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from every background, …

items.desc: AI/ML Engineer – Applied Research & Systems Design The Opportunity We're looking for an experienced AI/ML Engineer to help design and build a shared AI/ML platform supporting multiple engineering and research teams. This is a hands-on engineering role with a strong applied research component. You'll tackle complex technical problems, design targeted experiments and evaluate different systems and architectures to determine the most effective solutions. The focus isn't on developing new AI models, but on designing or selecting the systems and infrastructure that enable machine learning at scale. What You'll Do Translate ambiguous technical challenges into clearly defined problems, hypotheses and targeted experiments. Evaluate different systems, technologies and architectural approaches through prototyping, benchmarking and experimentation. Design scalable, reliable infrastructure supporting both traditional ML and emerging AI workloads. Work closely with engineering and research teams to understand requirements and identify shared platform needs. Turn experimental findings into technical designs and hands-on engineering projects. Assess architectural trade-offs across performance, scalability, reliability and efficiency. What We're Looking For Strong software engineering background, particularly Python and systems design. Solid understanding of traditional machine learning, including algorithms, model training, validation and evaluation. Experience designing distributed systems, ML infrastructure or large-scale data processing platforms. A scientific approach to problem-solving, with experience designing experiments, testing hypotheses and making evidence-based technical decisions. Ability to move from technical discovery and experimentation through to architecture and implementation. Strong communication skills and experience collaborating with technical stakeholders. Particularly Relevant Experience Building shared ML platforms or research infrastructure. ML experimentation, benchmarking and evaluation frameworks. Distributed computing, high-performance systems or large-scale ML workloads. Experience combining traditional ML and modern AI technologies. The ideal candidate is a strong AI/ML engineer or software engineer with deep ML knowledge, excellent systems design skills and a scientific mindset. Someone who enjoys figuring out which approach works best, why it works and how to turn that understanding into a scalable engineering solution. If interested in learning more, apply or contact James@atlanticsearch.com directly with your CV to arrange a call. Thanks, James

items.desc: Do you love turning demanding optical setups into robust hardware that others can rely on? Are you at home in the lab with lasers and optics, and comfortable working across electronics, control software, mechanics, and automation? Would you like to help build a deep-tech startup—not only by developing technology, but by turning it into products for real customers? The Institute of Physics (IoP) is looking for a hands-on Research Engineer to work with the Ultracold Strontium Gases group and its spin-off OpticsFoundry B.V. Working at the UvA Join Us! OpticsFoundry is developing technology for the robotic manufacture of compact, stable optical circuits for quantum technology and other demanding applications. Our optical circuit boards are already used in the AQuRA optical lattice clock; the next challenge is to broaden the platform to lasers, optical cavities, frequency references, and other active systems. Working at the boundary between the University of Amsterdam and OpticsFoundry, and in collaboration with the Nonlinear Nanophotonics group at the University of Twente, you will help turn advanced laboratory optics into repeatable, manufacturable products. This is an opportunity to join at an early stage, shape both the technology and the way we build it, and—if there is a strong mutual fit—progressively move from UvA into a core engineering role at OpticsFoundry over the course of the project. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do You will take ownership of challenging engineering problems from first idea to tested hardware. In a small, fast-moving team, you will design experiments, build prototypes, measure performance, find failure modes, and iterate until a system is robust enough for production and customer use. Your work will include: designing and building compact optical circuits that incorporate gain media, piezo and motorized actuators, optical cavities, spectroscopy cells, photonic integrated circuits, and related components; developing robotic methods to place, align, bond, and integrate optical components reproducibly; building and benchmarking complete systems, such as laser sources and laser-frequency locks; designing or integrating the electronics, instrumentation, and control software needed to operate and test those systems; translating prototypes into scalable production processes, fixtures, test procedures, and clear technical documentation; and working directly with researchers and early customers to understand requirements and deliver practical, reliable hardware. The role offers substantial freedom and responsibility. You will be encouraged to propose solutions, make design decisions, and develop new technical capabilities—not simply execute a predefined research plan. items.desc: Junior AI/ML Engineer - Applied Computer Vision The Role We’re looking for a motivated Junior AI/ML Engineer to join a growing engineering team working on advanced computer vision and machine learning technologies. You’ll work with CNNs, Vision Transformers and emerging deep learning architectures, contributing to projects from early experimentation through to production deployment. You’ll learn from experienced engineers and researchers, developing your technical skills while taking on increasing responsibility. This is a hands-on engineering role where you’ll write code, run experiments, evaluate models and help turn cutting-edge research into reliable software for demanding applications. What You’ll Do Develop and test computer vision algorithms using CNNs, Vision Transformers and other deep learning architectures. Run experiments and evaluate model performance, including training strategies, loss functions and evaluation metrics. Help translate research into robust, production-ready software. Contribute to scalable model training, evaluation and inference pipelines. Support model optimisation for accuracy, speed and deployment across edge and cloud platforms. Explore emerging AI architectures and contribute to the development of new machine learning solutions. Work alongside experienced engineers, researchers and technical leadership on customer projects. Take part in technical discussions and develop your understanding of software engineering best practice. Essential Skills and Experience Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, gained through a degree, personal projects, internships or professional experience. Hands-on experience with PyTorch. TensorFlow experience is also welcome. Good understanding of CNNs and Vision Transformers, with an interest in current computer vision research. Strong Python programming skills. Familiarity with software engineering practices, including version control, testing and code reviews. Comfortable working in Linux and/or Windows environments. Good analytical and problem-solving skills. Clear communication skills and a willingness to learn, ask questions and collaborate with others. Desirable Skills Experience with object detection, tracking, image segmentation or pose estimation. Exposure to aerial, satellite or intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) imagery. Interest in edge deployment, real-time AI or GPU optimisation. Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, Kubeflow or other MLOps tools. Experience with synthetic data or simulation platforms, such as Unreal Engine or NVIDIA Omniverse. Experience working alongside researchers. An interest in defence, government or national security applications. Education An MSc or PhD in Computer Vision, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics or a related discipline would be beneficial. Equivalent practical experience and demonstrable project work are equally welcome. Security Requirements Candidates must be eligible to obtain UK security clearance. The ability to achieve Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required, with Security Check (SC) clearance or higher desirable. What’s on Offer? The opportunity to work on advanced AI and computer vision technologies. Mentoring and technical development from experienced engineers and researchers. Exposure to both research-led development and production engineering. The chance to contribute to systems used in demanding operational environments. Opportunities to develop your skills, take on greater responsibility and progress your career within a highly technical team.

items.desc: Imagine working on Denmark's most critical systems, turning unique customer data into real value through applied machine learning. As our new Data Scientist, you will play a key role in analysing customer data and training models within our established product. Ready to make an impact? The job You will be responsible for generating value from customer data within our established product, which underpins national security and critical infrastructure domains. Our customers are classified and cannot be disclosed, so your work will take place in secure environments, often in collaboration with Product teams, security teams and onsite at customer locations. As this is a newly established position, you will have the opportunity to help shape this role as it grows. In short, you can look forward to: Analysing and preparing customer data for use in our established product Training, evaluating and refining machine learning models on customer data Integrating models and data-driven features that generate measurable value Exploring customer data to identify new opportunities for value creation Collaborating with security teams to ensure compliance with national classifications and profiles Joining the team You will join an organisation where you will be associated with multiple teams, part of our NSI business unit. We develop and maintain military-grade solutions that support a nation's most critical systems. The organisation is highly collaborative, organised around Products that make a difference. If you are located in Aarhus, we are open to discussing a hybrid arrangement, but you should expect regular presence in Copenhagen (6–8 days per month). Your Qualifications We are looking for a data scientist with hands-on experience applying machine learning to real-world data in production settings, who can work confidently in high-stakes, security-classified environments. Relevant technical education, Bachelor's or Master's, in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics or equivalent experience Documented experience with applied machine learning on real-world data Some hands-on experience with data science and machine learning in production settings Strong knowledge of Python, machine learning frameworks (scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow), SQL and data processing tools Fluent Danish and English skills A strong security mindset and ability to work in high-stakes environments Alongside this, we value: A collaborative and proactive work style Comfortable working independently and navigating ambiguity, particularly as this is a newly established role Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving abilities Comfortable working onsite at customer environments when needed Expect travel activity to our HQ in Aarhus and to customer sites, primarily in Copenhagen. Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here. Welcome to Systematic Copenhagen When you join us in Copenhagen, you're not just getting a desk at one of the city's best locations - you are stepping into a workplace where community matters. Our Employees Club keeps things lively with monthly social events, and our office catering makes sure you are always well taken care of. Whether you are into casual games or just good company, you will find both at our foosball table or during our relaxed Friday bar gatherings. Never stop developing Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong. Start your development here We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Kasper Bach Klokker, Associate Director, NSI Operations. Get in touch Tobias Falck Jensen Talent Acquisition Partner

You will complete tasks at the intersection of ML and biological data analysis - including model development, pipeline construction, and research tasks applied to real genomic, transcriptomic, or multi-omics datasets. items.desc: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring. This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. Job description The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere. You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species. Your profile Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics. Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage. Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication. Who we are The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. What we offer The successful candidate is offered: Access to a well-developed research infrastructure Office space and shared equipment a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance Place of work and area of employment The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Visant à approfondir les connaissances en IA tout en gardant l'être humain au centre de ses préoccupations, la Région Ile-de-France ambitionne de jouer un rôle majeur dans ce secteur d'avenir, par son excellence scientifique et son écosystème incomparable et souhaite de faire de ce dernier un acteur incontournable de la construction d'une Intelligence Artificielle (IA) frugale, fiable, efficace , amenée à cohabiter avec l'être humain et à l'assister dans ses décisions. A cet effet, DIM AI4IDF lance périodiquement des appels à projets de recherche doctorale. Cette thèse s'inscrit dans cet cadre et établit un partenariat entre les clusters Hi!Paris et PRAIRIE, très précisément entre Telecom ParisTech et Inria Centre de Paris. L’ objectif de cette thèse est de mener des recherches commune sur la persistance dans les modèles génératifs de monde pour la robotique et de développer des algorithmes capables d'intégrer les concepts physiques lors de la génération d'images en particulier. Le projet développera des méthodes pour imposer la persistance dans les modèles génératifs du monde, avec des contributions incluant une définition formelle de la persistance, des méthodes d’apprentissage à l’échelle de la trajectoire, et une validation empirique en prédiction et contrôle robotiques. Des déplacements réguliers sont prévus pour ce poste , notamment à des fins de dissémination, de formation scientifique et de participation à des réunions de projet et de collaboration . items.desc: Build the science that shapes the future of human health. Application closing date: 11.11.2026 Join a place where ambitious science thrives Human Technopole (Milan) is a rapidly expanding life science institute where international researchers and cutting-edge technologies converge to accelerate biomedical discovery. Our mission is to transform bold scientific ideas into advances that improve human health. Within this mission, the Casale Group in the Health Data Science Centre develops AI methods that transform population-scale human data into mechanistic models of disease. Our research integrates large-scale human genetics with molecular and clinical data to generate testable hypotheses that accelerate biological discovery and therapeutic innovation. We are recruiting an ambitious AI Scientist to build the reusable AI foundations and agentic scientific systems that power the group’s research across human genetics, multimodal biology, and disease. Your mission As AI Scientist, you will develop next-generation AI systems at the interface of ambitious biological research and frontier artificial intelligence, using population-scale genetics and multimodal biomedical data to uncover mechanisms of human disease. You will turn methods and models emerging from this research into robust, reusable AI capabilities—including foundation models, multimodal representation learning, agentic workflows, evaluation frameworks, and scalable research software—that can accelerate discovery across multiple projects. A longer-term goal is to develop AI systems that increasingly act as scientific collaborators: connecting evidence across biological scales, proposing testable hypotheses, identifying informative analyses, and working alongside researchers to accelerate iterative cycles of biological discovery. Your work will combine methodological innovation, biological discovery, and scientific software development at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computational biology, and human genetics. You will have substantial scientific and technical ownership, with the opportunity to help shape the group’s technical AI architecture while leading and contributing to high-impact scientific publications, open-source software, and reusable research capabilities. As part of Human Technopole’s interdisciplinary AI ecosystem, you will engage closely with the European AI community, including through collaborations with Helmholtz Munich and connections to the ELLIS network. Your work will benefit from interactions with computational, biological, and clinical groups across the institute, alongside opportunities for international collaboration, research exchanges, interdisciplinary training, and engagement with industry. You will also draw on the group’s established network across leading academic institutions and industry partners in Europe and North America, helping you build collaborations, broaden your expertise, and accelerate the impact of your research. Grow Your Skills You will enhance your scientific and professional skills by: Developing next-generation AI methods through ambitious biological research. Building foundation models, multimodal representation learning approaches, and agentic AI systems for scientific discovery. Turning scientific advances into robust, benchmarked, and reusable AI capabilities that accelerate discovery across multiple research projects. Building scalable research software and AI workflows for large and heterogeneous scientific datasets. Shaping the future of AI for science through high-impact publications, open-source software, international collaborations, and entrepreneurial initiatives. Human Technopole supports career development through training, mentoring and dedicated learning opportunities. With more than 20 million new cancer cases diagnosed globally each year , there is an urgent need for more effective and personalized treatment strategies to improve patient survival while reducing the costs associated with ineffective therapies. By advancing the ability to predict patients' responses to treatments , Rosetta Omics empowers physicians with deeper molecular insights to guide therapeutic decisions and deliver the most effective care to each patient as early as possible. The company's mission is to accelerate the transition toward a future where precision medicine becomes the standard of care for cancer patients worldwide . Rosetta Omics is a laureate of the France 2030 AI Pioneers program (2026) , recognizing its innovative approach at the intersection of biotechnology, artificial intelligence, and healthcare. Working closely with the Founder & CEO, scientific team, and clinical research partners , the successful candidate will play a central role in developing and implementing advanced bioinformatics and artificial intelligence solutions for precision oncology. The primary mission will be to analyze and integrate complex multiomics datasets, develop machine learning models to predict cancer treatment responses, and identify clinically relevant biomarkers . Ensure data quality, traceability, documentation, and reproducibility across computational workflows. 4. items.desc:
Research fellow in gas fermentation and sustainable bioprocesses - IT | Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia 
 Research fellow in gas fermentation and sustainable bioprocesses 
 Italy 
 Commitment & contract: collaboration contract, 13 months, Fellow position 
 Location: Center for Sustainable Future Technologies, Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia, Torino, Italy 
 Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! 
 At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds.
 We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential.
 THE ROLE 
 You will be working in a multicultural and multi-disciplinary group, where junior and senior scientists collaborate, each with their expertise, to carry out a scientific activity with a shared research goal.
 The Center for Sustainable Future Technologies (CSFT) is an interdisciplinary research center committed to addressing sustainability challenges through innovative solutions for the energy transition, circular economy, and valorization of renewable resources. The Center develops advanced materials, processes, and systems aimed at reducing environmental impact and promoting the conversion of waste streams and carbon-based feedstocks into valuable products.
 The Advanced Materials for Sustainable Future Technologies Research unit is coordinated by Prof. Candido Fabrizio Pirri. The research focuses on a combination of advanced materials science with microbial biotechnology, focusing on the development of innovative bioprocesses based on photosynthetic and gas-fermenting microorganisms for the sustainable production of chemicals, fuels, and other value-added products. This includes research activities carried out within the European project GoodByO (Multi-commodities microbial-driven Biorefinery based on food-processing industry wastes, biogenic CO₂ and bioprocess wastewaters). In particular, the development and optimization of microbial gas fermentation processes for the conversion of biogenic CO₂ and renewable hydrogen into bio-based chemicals, contributing to the advancement of sustainable biorefinery technologies.
 Within the research team, your main responsibilities will be:
 Maintain and cultivate anaerobic microbial strains, prepare culture media and inocula, and perform routine laboratory activities required for the operation of gas fermentation experiments.
 Operate and monitor anaerobic bioreactors and gas fermentation systems.
 Perform analytical characterization of fermentation products, with particular focus on bio-hexanol production.
 Analyze process performance and microbial growth data.
 Contribute to process optimization and scale-up activities.
 Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, scientific publications and project deliverables.
 ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS 
 Master's degree in Biotechnology, Industrial Biotechnology, Microbiology, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Biochemistry or related disciplines.
 Hands-on experience in microbial cultivation and lab-scale bioprocesses.
 Hands-on experience with gaseous flows control systems.
 Basic knowledge of molecular biology technologies.
 Basic knowledge of fermentation technologies and anaerobic microbiology.
 Good command of spoken and written English.
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 Knowledge of analytical techniques such as HPLC, GC and spectrophotometry
 Ability to work in a challenging and international environment
 Capacity to work autonomously and collaboratively in a highly interdisciplinary environment
 Possess Analytical Reasoning skills and a growth mindset
 COMPENSATION PACKAGE 
 A yearly gross salary of 21.000 euro
 Private health care coverage depending on your role and contract
 Candidates from abroad or Italian citizens who have carried scientific research activity permanently abroad and meet specific requirements, may be entitled to a deduction from taxable income of up to 90% from 6 to 13 years.
 This open position is financed by Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking (CBE JU) wihin the GoodByO – Multi-commodities microbial-driven BiOrefinery based on food-processing industry wastes, biogenic CO₂ and bioprocess wastewaters project (Grant Agreement No. 101156486 ).

You’ll challenge advanced language models on topics like computer architecture and hardware design, embedded systems and IoT, networking and distributed systems, hardware security, and systems software and operating systems—documenting every failure mode so we can harden model reasoning. Organization : Alignerr Position : Computer Engineering Expert - AI Content Specialist Type : Hourly Contract Compensation : $35–$60 /hour Location : Remote Commitment : 10–40 hours/week What You’ll Do Develop Complex Problems: Design advanced computer engineering challenges across domains like RISC-V/ARM architecture, FPGA development, memory management, and hardware-software co-design. Author Ground-Truth Solutions: Create rigorous, step-by-step technical solutions, including assembly code, hardware description language (HDL) snippets, and architectural diagrams that serve as "golden responses" for AI training. Technical Auditing: Evaluate AI-generated code (C/C++, Verilog, VHDL), logic gate designs, and operating system kernels for technical accuracy, efficiency, and adherence to industry standards. Refine Reasoning: Identify logical fallacies in AI reasoning—such as race conditions, memory leaks, or improper timing constraints—and provide structured feedback to improve the model's "thinking" process. Requirements Advanced Degree: Masters (pursuing or completed) or PhD in Computer Engineering, Computer Science with a hardware focus, or a closely related field. Domain Expertise: Strong foundational knowledge in core areas such as Computer Architecture, Embedded Systems, Digital Logic Design, or Operating Systems. Analytical Writing: The ability to communicate highly technical hardware concepts and low-level software logic clearly and concisely in written form. Attention to Detail: High level of precision when checking bit-level operations, clock-cycle timing, and technical documentation. No AI experience required Preferred Prior experience with data annotation, data quality, or evaluation systems Proficiency in engineering software concepts (e.g., SolidWorks, MATLAB, ANSYS) to evaluate AI-generated code or workflows. Why Join Us Competitive pay and flexible remote work. Collaborate with a team working on cutting-edge AI projects. Exposure to advanced LLMs and how they’re trained. Freelance perks: autonomy, flexibility, and global collaboration. Potential for contract extension. Application Process (Takes 15-20 min) Submit your resume Complete a short screening Project matching and onboarding PS: Our team reviews applications daily. items.desc:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Research Engineer to join the research team at ElevenLabs, focused on the data infrastructure that powers our frontier AI models. The quality of our models is bounded by the quality and scale of the data behind them, and you will own the systems that make world-class data possible. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy:

 

 - Building large-scale data pipelines for collecting, processing, filtering, and transforming datasets used to train state-of-the-art models.

 - Training models used in our data processing pipelines, such as classifiers, quality filters, and labeling models.

 - Designing data curation strategies such as deduplication, quality scoring, labeling, and augmentation that measurably improve model performance.

 - Creating tooling and infrastructure that lets researchers explore and train on massive datasets quickly and reliably.

 


REQUIREMENTS

We do not require any formal certifications or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or GitHub contributions. Ideally, you bring:

 

 - Experience building data-intensive systems, ideally in support of machine learning training pipelines.

 - Strong engineering skills in distributed data processing at scale (e.g., Kubernetes, or custom pipelines over large datasets).

 - The capacity to autonomously evaluate how data quality, composition, and curation affect model outcomes, and to build the tooling to measure it.

 

Bonus: Experience building or operating web crawlers.

 


LOCATION

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw.

 

#LI-Remote

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print

 The Biomedical Image Computing Group develops algorithmic solutions to enable automatic interpretation and forming of biomedical images, aiming to increase efficiency and accuracy in clinical practice and research.
 Project background
 The enhancement of endoscopic videos is a critical yet complex task. These videos are integral to various clinical interventions, where the clarity of imaging data is essential for procedural success. Due to challenging imaging conditions, the quality of endoscopic videos can be significantly compromised by a range of artifacts. This project seeks to develop the next generation of enhancement algorithms tailored for endoscopic videos, with a focus on applications in real-time interventions. Development efforts will prioritize both enhancement quality and computational efficiency, particularly with respect to latency. 
 The successful candidate will join the BMIC team at ETH Zurich and also be part of the Computer Vision Lab (CVL). The project is conducted in collaboration with an industrial implementation partner, who will provide support with hardware and software integration. 
 The position is open immediately and initially limited to 8 months. 
 Job description
 This position involves the implementation, optimization, and deployment of deep-learning image-enhancement models for real-time operation. Rather than focusing primarily on model training, the successful candidate will work on translating existing and new architectures into efficient real-time processing pipelines connected directly to an industrial camera system. Typical tasks will include profiling and optimizing models for low-latency inference, implementing and adapting neural-network architectures with real-time constraints in mind, integrating camera acquisition and preprocessing pipelines, and contributing to project deliverables and scientific manuscript preparation.

 Familiarity with neural-network-based image processing pipelines.

We're looking for Machine Learning Engineers to help train cutting-edge AI models by demonstrating expert-level problem-solving — step by step, in real time. This isn't a typical ML role. items.desc: Summary You will become part of the Incident Creator and AI Research team within the Technology Division in Bratislava.
