items.desc: Research Scientist – Optimisation Science About Us: At SLB our purpose is to create amazing technology that unlocks access to energy for the benefit of all. As innovators, that’s been our mission for 100 years. We are facing the world’s greatest balancing act - how to simultaneously reduce emissions while meeting the world’s growing energy demands. We’re working on that answer. Every day is a step closer. Our collective future depends on decarbonizing the fossil fuel industry while innovating across the entire energy landscape. It’s what drives us, ensuring progress for the people and the planet - on the journey to net zero and beyond. With a global footprint in more than 100 countries and employees representing almost twice as many nationalities, we work each day on decarbonizing industry, innovating in oil and gas, delivering digital at scale, and developing and scaling new energy systems that accelerate the energy transition. We’re looking for innovators to join our diverse community. If you share our passion for discovery we’d like you to apply. Location: Cambridge, UK SLB Cambridge Research (SCR) is part of SLB’s global network of research and engineering centres. SCR is a dynamic, multidisciplinary environment with state-of-the-art laboratory and computing facilities. We work on applied research projects in the physical sciences to meet the current and future challenges of the industry. At SCR, we strike a balance between academia and industry with projects from early-stage research all the way to solution development for real business challenges. SCR is a distinctive marquee-like structure dominating the High Cross site on the western outskirts of Cambridge, England. The centre provides extensive laboratory and office facilities and is home to more than 100 scientists, technicians and domain experts. Job Summary: We are seeking a creative and self-motivated Research Scientist with expertise in optimisation, particularly multi-objective optimisation, and decision science. The scientist will develop optimisation methods for complex engineering and operational systems involving multiple, often competing objectives, constraints, uncertainties, and decisions across different temporal and spatial scales. The successful candidate will work as part of a multidisciplinary research team, combining optimisation with experiments, physical and mathematical models, data-driven methods, and domain knowledge. The research will support the understanding, design, operation, and control of complex systems and the development of new technologies. Responsibilities: Develop and apply optimisation methods for complex engineering, process, and operational systems. Formulate and solve decision problems involving multiple objectives, constraints, uncertainties, and trade-offs. Develop and integrate optimisation approaches with physics-based, reduced-order, surrogate, and data-driven models. Develop computationally efficient methods for optimisation under uncertainty, including robustness and sensitivity analysis. Contribute to optimisation of system design, operating strategies, measurement selection, resource allocation, and control. Work collaboratively with experimental scientists, mathematical modellers, data scientists, and domain experts to translate scientific and engineering challenges into suitable optimisation problems. Communicate findings through technical reports, publications, conference presentations, patent applications, and engagement with internal and external collaborators. Qualifications: PhD in operational research, applied mathematics, optimisation, engineering, computer science, or a related discipline. Strong expertise in mathematical optimisation, including multi-objective optimisation and decision-making under uncertainty. Experience applying optimisation methods to complex engineering or scientific problems, including integration with simulation, surrogate, and data-driven models. Strong scientific programming skills and experience developing optimisation workflows. Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Experience in dynamic systems, process optimisation, optimal experimental design, resource allocation, decision support, or optimisation-based control would be advantageous. SLB is an equal employment opportunity employer. Qualified applicants are considered without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or other characteristics protected by law.

Basic Function: We wish to recruit a dynamic and suitably qualified research scientist to support the Grass-BÓ project with particular focus on modelling GHG emissions from grass silage biomethane production and assessing sustainability criteria for forage feedstocks. The Research Officer will have expertise in bioenergy, more specifically AD, and ideally will have undertaken a PhD on a similar topic. Furthermore, they should preferably have experience in environmental modelling and sustainability analysis. Background: Ireland has ambitious targets to reduce agricultural emissions by 25% and to expand anaerobic digestion (AD) to meet 10% of current national gas demand by 2030. This includes the development of both farm-level and grid-scale AD plants. However, several knowledge gaps exist relating to the optimal supply of farm sourced forage and slurry/manure to provide secure and sustainable AD feedstocks in line with Renewable Energy Directive (RED) sustainability criteria. Grass-BÓ will address knowledge gaps in relation to the seasonal, regional and farm-specific dynamics feedstocks for the AD sector including livestock slurry and grass-silage. The project will also explore whether adding legumes and diverse plant mixes to grasslands can boost the amount and quality of material available for renewable gas production. This project will provide a more detailed understanding of how much farm-based feedstock is truly available across different regions in the country throughout the year; along with how digestate (a by-product of AD) can be reused on farms in an environmentally friendly way. By filling these knowledge gaps, this project will create decision-making tools to help farmers and policymakers plan for the rollout of AD more effectively. Ultimately, it will support the growth of renewable energy in Ireland, reduce agricultural emissions, and strengthen Ireland’s leadership in sustainable energy research. Job Objectives Day-to-day management of the Grass-BÓ project. This successful candidate will be a key member of the project team and will support the partners in adhering to the work-programme, its constituent tasks, deliverables, and milestones. Du är i början av din karriär och har en relevant högskole- eller civilingenjörsutbildning inom exempelvis datateknik, elektroteknik, teknisk fysik eller motsvarande. Du kan vara nyexaminerad eller ha något års erfarenhet. Vi tror att du har: Kunskaper i Python och/eller C++. Grundläggande förståelse för bildbehandling, datorseende och maskininlärning. Arbetat med relevanta projekt under utbildningen, genom examensarbete eller på egen hand. Förmåga att kommunicera tekniska resonemang på engelska. Erfarenhet av OpenCV, PyTorch, TensorFlow, kamerakalibrering, 3D-geometri eller eventbaserade kameror är meriterande. items.desc: Summary You will become part of the Incident Creator and AI Research team within the Technology Division in Bratislava. Beyond that, you maintain and improve deployed models across their full lifecycle, from monitoring to continuous optimization. Build and evaluate prototypes, iterating on architectures and features until production-quality, on dedicated in-house GPU servers — enough compute to compete with the biggest players in the industry. Deploy models into production and integrate them with existing detection and incident-handling pipelines. Monitor, maintain, and optimize deployed models across their full lifecycle — from drift detection to retraining and performance tuning. When opportunities arise, explore novel architectures beyond applying existing models. Proficiency in Python and its AI/ML ecosystem. Experience with AI/ML lifecycle tooling and infrastructure for production model serving and lifecycle management. Ability to work independently and take full ownership of model development from start to finish. Strong drive for continuous learning and staying current with state-of-the-art research. Experience with Big Data technologies and cloud platforms (AWS). items.desc: The Faculty of Science and the Finnish Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM), HiLIFE at the University of Helsinki invite applications for a joint (50%:50%) position as RESEARCH FELLOW (UNIVERSITY RESEARCHER) IN AI FOR POPULATION HEALTH AND GENOMICS for a fixed-term appointment of maximum 4 years with starting date as soon as possible. Position Description The position relates to the Sustainable Wellbeing Across Lifespan (SWAN) ( https://www.swan-helsinkiuni.net/ ) research action that conducts cutting-edge research to promote health span by identifying individual risks and susceptibilities, aiming to clarify mechanisms of degeneration across the lifespan and exploring new approaches to detecting, monitoring and treating remodeled metabolism associated with ageing. The candidate is expected to develop an independent research program within this scope, focusing on methodological innovation and the application of modern AI approaches to large-scale biomedical data. Research topics may include foundation models for longitudinal electronic health records and genomics, multimodal learning integrating health records with molecular data, causal representation learning, in-context learning and amortized inference for healthcare decision-making, and AI-assisted scientific discovery workflows. The work will be done together with the Ganna Lab ( https://www.dsgelab.org/) at FIMM and the Probabilistic Machine Learning Lab ( https://www.helsinki.fi/en/researchgroups/probabilistic-machine-learning ; groups of Acerbi and Klami) at the Department of Computer Science, aligning with concurrent projects developing foundation models for healthcare. The groups are active members of the ELLIS Institute Finland ( https://www.ellisinstitute.fi/ ), providing opportunities for collaboration with leading researchers in artificial intelligence across Finland and Europe. The position offers access to globally unique research resources, including nationwide longitudinal health records from Finland covering more than five billion healthcare events, FinnGen with genomic data from over 500,000 participants, and extensive multi-omics datasets including proteomics and single-cell transcriptomics. Researchers also benefit from access to world-class computing infrastructure through CSC and LUMI, one of Europe's most powerful supercomputers. Responsibilities The appointed researcher is expected to pursue independent research on methodological innovation in developing and applying AI methods, in collaboration with existing research groups at the university, and will have the opportunity to be part of ELLIS Institute Finland activities. They will also participate in university-wide activities advancing the use of AI in scientific research, together with other researchers working in the intersection of AI and other scientific disciplines. The daily working activities of the appointed researcher will be split between the Faculty of Science and FIMM. Opportunities for contribution to teaching (up to 5-10% of annual working time) will be provided. Qualifications We require a doctoral degree and postdoctoral research experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computational statistics, with demonstrated interest in applications to population health and/or human genetics. Excellent communication skills in English are necessary. The candidate needs to have: A doctoral degree in a suitable field Research activity after PhD (typically 2-4 years of postdoctoral research), ideally with evidence of independent research contributions, ability to lead a research group, experience in research funding acquisition, and public engagement. Scientific competence in developing and/or applying artificial intelligence methods with proven publication record in scientific venues in the field. We expect publication record in top-tier venues in AI and machine learning (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or similar) and/or publications with clear AI contributions in leading biomedical journals (e.g. Nature Genetics, Nature Medicine, Nature Machine Intelligence or similar ). Personal research interest that relates to the scope and topic of the position and connects to existing research groups at the University of Helsinki. What We Offer University of Helsinki is an equal opportunity employer and offers an attractive and diverse workplace with a variety of development opportunities and benefits. The appointee’s monthly salary varies between 4800-6000€ depending on their previous experience and qualifications. The employment contract will include a probationary period of six months. Standard Finnish pension benefits and occupational health care are provided for university employees. Further information can be obtained online . items.desc: The opportunity For our research center in Krakow, Poland, we are seeking a Researcher with solid expertise in polymer materials – particularly epoxy resins, thermoplastics, and related composite systems – and their processing, mechanical behavior, and life-cycle performance. You will join a dynamic, motivated, and interdisciplinary team with broad experience across materials science, mechanics, and energy technologies. As part of our team, you will focus on the practical application and processing of modern polymer materials, ensuring their reliable and efficient use in existing and future products by developing manufacturing ‑ ready solutions that deliver consistent mechanical performance and meet durability and life ‑ cycle requirements. Your work will directly support the development of products and systems used in energy distribution and transmission, ensuring that polymer materials are selected, processed, and applied in ways that maximize mechanical integrity, safety, and long ‑ term reliability. How You'll Make An Impact Propose, contribute to, and lead research and development projects focused on polymer materials processing, mechanical behavior, and their application in energy technologies. Investigate how manufacturing processes and parameters (e.g., molding, curing, extrusion, forming, joining) influence material structure, quality, and mechanical performance. Develop and optimize manufacturing methods for polymer components to improve product consistency, robustness, and efficiency. Evaluate durability, mechanical degradation mechanisms, fracture behavior, creep, fatigue, and long‑term aging of polymer materials used in demanding environments. Assess environmental impacts and life‑cycle performance of polymer materials, contributing to sustainability‑oriented material and design decisions. Collaborate globally with researchers and engineers at Hitachi Energy to solve material‑ and mechanics‑related challenges and optimize product performance. Stay up to date on polymer technologies, mechanical testing methods, and sustainable solutions, identifying opportunities for industrial application. Engage with universities, research institutes, startups, and technology partners to advance knowledge in polymer mechanics and applications. Communicate research outcomes through technical reports, scientific papers, conferences, and patent applications. Your Background Master’s or higher degree in Materials Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Polymer Engineering, or related fields. Robust understanding of polymer mechanics, including stress–strain behavior, viscoelasticity, fracture mechanics, fatigue, and failure mechanisms of epoxy resins and thermoplastics. Minimum 2 years of experience with polymer processing technologies (e.g., molding, curing, extrusion, composite processing, additive manufacturing), with a clear understanding of how processing influences mechanical properties. Experience with mechanical characterization techniques, such as tensile testing, compression, impact, DMA, fracture toughness testing, creep, and fatigue testing. Experience with thermal and chemical characterization techniques (DSC, TGA, rheology) supporting the interpretation of mechanical behavior. Knowledge of material aging, environmental degradation, reliability, or life‑cycle assessment is highly valued. Experience with CAD/CAE, mechanical simulation, or modeling of polymer behavior is an advantage. Ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary and multicultural teams while continually learning new topics. Fluency in English, both written and spoken. In addition, the following skills would be beneficial for the role: Knowledge of power network business, green energy, respective requirements, and industry standards. Understanding of energy system products, power network components, and relevant industry standards. Familiarity with sustainability concepts, circular materials, polymer recycling, or environmental compliance. items.desc: Ship maintenance is broken. We're fixing it. Ceto is a fleet intelligence company. Our platform, Watchkeeper, takes the high-frequency sensor data ships already generate and predicts machinery failures before they happen — on one vessel we flagged a developing fuel-system issue three days before a critical failure, on a ship earning $48,000 a day. No new hardware, no rip-and-replace: if an owner is already capturing data, we can have a full fleet live in days. We're deployed across fleets owned by major global shipowners, and we sell directly to the ship owners and operators who feel every day of unplanned off-hire on their P&L. We're a small, senior team - our CEO spent eight years at sea as a marine engineer before founding the company; we’re backed by investors including Dynamo Ventures who led our $4.8m seed round, and we're compounding fast which is exactly why we need you. What we're doing We're reshaping maritime. It's an industry that's incredibly important and serves as the backbone of global trade, moving $14 trillion of cargo each year. Despite its significance, the industry remains one of the final frontiers of digitalisation. Ceto provides the operational intelligence layer that technical teams rely on for mission-critical decision making. By capturing and analysing high-frequency data from commercial ships, Ceto monitors the condition of the machinery onboard. Through anomaly detection and degradation forecasting we predict mechanical failures ahead of time and guide decision making for our customers. Our analytics are served as insights through our SaaS platform, preventing costly breakdowns, loss of hire events and reducing operational risk. The role You'll turn high-frequency sensor data from ships' machinery into analytics our customers act on: condition monitoring, performance baselines, degradation trends, anomaly detection. Some of this is machine learning; much of it is statistics, signal processing and a real understanding of the physical systems producing the data. You'll work closely with the engineering team to take problems end to end, from raw, messy sensor data through to a deployed, monitored output feeding our dashboard. Your responsibilities will include: Building time-series analytics on machinery sensor data: performance baselines, derived signals, trend and degradation detection Owning the data from the point it arrives: ingesting raw sensor feeds, cleaning, validating and resampling them, and building the checks that catch gaps, outliers, sensor faults and vendor tag differences before they reach any model or customer Exploring new ideas in predictive maintenance and condition monitoring, and turning them into reliable, production-ready features Applying ML, supervised or unsupervised, where the problem calls for it, including cases where failure examples are rare and labels are imperfect Building and maintaining analytics pipelines end to end (cleaning, feature engineering, model training and inference, output storage) using version control, testing, CI/CD and experiment tracking Working closely with the rest of the technical team to prioritise what's worth investigating and what isn't Using AI tools such as Claude Code to work faster and more effectively Two firm requirements: You have experience in an early-stage startup and are comfortable working at speed, context switching and turning ambiguous problems into delivered solutions You’re AI-native, using the modern tools to increase your productivity and you have a good feel for when to trust agents and when to do the work by hand You'll be perfect for this role if: You have strong Python skills and know its data/scientific libraries (pandas/numpy/scipy, scikit-learn, statsmodels) Experience with supervised and unsupervised ML (e.g. gradient boosting, clustering, hidden Markov models), and clear reasoning about when you'd use each You have a strong grasp of time-series analysis (trends, seasonality, filtering, changepoints, anomaly detection) and the judgement to pick the simplest method that works You've shipped analytics or models into production, not just notebooks, with exposure to CI/CD and DevOps practices You have a physics, engineering or other quantitative degree, and a genuine interest in the physical systems behind the data, not just the data itself You can explain why a method fits a physical problem, and you're sceptical by nature. Models can be wrong, intuition can be disproven, and correlations in data often have mundane explanations. items.desc:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
 The Position
 At Roche, we advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love. A healthier future. For a world where everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for the generations to come. For this, we believe the next breakthrough in medicine will be powered by the intersection of computational engineering and biology. We are building the infrastructure that transforms AI from an experimental concept into a reliable, high-impact utility for our researchers. 
 Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organizations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness this transformative power of data and AI to assist scientists to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide. 
 Within the CoE, the Data and Digital Catalyst (DDC) organisation drives the modernization of computational and data ecosystems and integration of digital technologies across Research & Early Development. The AI Enablement Engineering group sits at the heart of this mission. We aren't just training models; we are building scalable systems, data pipelines, and intelligent applications that enable our scientists to work smarter, not harder. From optimizing model performance to designing end-to-end agentic workflows, our goal is to put powerful AI tools directly into the hands of those driving drug discovery to power data-driven science and accelerate decision making. 
 We are a cross-functional, impact-driven team that values cognitive diversity and technical excellence. Here, you’ll partner with biologists, computational scientists, data experts, and researchers to architect a future where AI/ML is an essential component of every scientific discovery. If you’re an engineer who thrives on solving complex problems, spans the stack with curiosity, and wants to build tools that truly change lives, we want to hear from you.
 The Opportunity: 
 As a Machine Learning Engineer in AI Enablement, you will implement the systems that unlock the potential of our scientific data, accelerating the discovery of life-changing treatments. You won't just build models; you will design the infrastructure that makes AI an everyday utility for researchers. 
 You will partner with a diverse ecosystem of computational scientists, ML experts, product leaders, and DevOps engineers to architect and implement robust, scalable, and maintainable backend systems and applications. You will have the autonomy to own end-to-end features (from initial model evaluation to production deployment) within a team that prioritizes technical rigor, mentorship, and collective growth. We are looking for engineers who view engineering excellence and inclusive, cross-functional collaboration as fundamental to delivering high-impact scientific solutions. 
 Translate scientific and business needs into actionable technical design and hands-on implementation of agentic AI solutions. For this, you will be writing, testing, and shipping high-quality, maintainable production code and building scalable systems and data pipelines on a daily basis. 
 Contribute independently to defined projects by writing maintainable code and applying software engineering best practices (testing, CI/CD, documentation) alongside AI tooling and quantitative metrics to evaluate and scale ML systems. 
 Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and the evolution of our development processes. 
 Be willing to span the stack and contribute where needed, even outside of your core area of expertise. 
 Stay up-to-date with emerging technologies and industry best practices and adopt a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, and curiosity.
 Who You Are: 
 You are a practitioner of technical rigor: You hold a Master’s degree with 2+ years of professional experience or a PhD in Computer Science or a similar technical field. You value engineering best practices, such as testing, clean code, and documentation, as the foundation for scalable, high-impact systems.

items.desc:
WHY FACULTY? 


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.



We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.



Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.



AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.




ABOUT THE TEAM 



Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.

We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres and MedTech start-ups to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges, and help to democratise health for all.




ABOUT THE ROLE



Join us as a Machine Learning Engineer to deliver bespoke, impactful AI solutions for our diverse clients.

You will be instrumental in bringing machine learning out of the lab and into the real world, contributing to scalable software architecture and defining best practices. Working with clients, and cross-functional teams, you'll ensure technical feasibility and timely delivery of high-quality, production-grade ML systems. 




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:



 - Building and deploying production-grade ML software, tools, and infrastructure.

 - Creating reusable, scalable solutions that accelerate the delivery of ML systems.

 - Collaborating with engineers, data scientists, and commercial leads to solve critical client challenges.

 - Leading technical scoping and architectural decisions to ensure project feasibility and impact.

 - Defining and implementing Faculty’s standards for deploying machine learning at scale.

 - Acting as a technical advisor to customers and partners, translating complex ML concepts for stakeholders.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:



 - You understand the full machine learning lifecycle and have experience operationalising models built with frameworks like Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.

 - You possess strong Python skills and solid experience in software engineering best practices.

 - You bring hands-on experience with cloud platforms and infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including architecture and security.

 - You've worked with container and orchestration tools such at Docker & Kubernetes to build and manage applications at scale

 - You are comfortable with core ML concepts, including probability, statistics, and common learning techniques.

 - You're an excellent communicator, able to guide technical teams and confidently advise non-technical stakeholders.

 - You thrive in a fast-paced environment, and enjoy the autonomy to own scope, solve and delivery solutions




THE INTERVIEW PROCESS



 1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

 2. Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes) 

 3. System Design Interview (90 minutes) 

 4. Commercial Interview (60 minutes)




OUR RECRUITMENT ETHOS




We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.



If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. 



A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

Organisé sous forme de projets à durée limitée, la mission de cette task-force européenne distribuée consiste, en collaboration avec d’autres centres européens d'excellence, à travailler sur des actions transverses de support applicatif de haut niveau pour les communautés scientifiques développant des méthodes d’IA à l’échelle d’infrastructures de calcul nationales. Dans le projet MINERVA, l’IDRIS est en charge du développement et de la mise à jour du portefeuille de services et de la fourniture de ces services. Les services de MINERVA sont stratégiquement alignés sur le besoin européen de s'appuyer sur des modèles de fondation open source entièrement développés conformément aux réglementations sur l'IA éthique et responsable incluses dans la loi sur l'IA. Les services se concentrent sur les grands modèles d'IA, avec un accent particulier sur les modèles de fondation open source, y compris le support de pré-entrainement (le transfert et le prétraitement des données, la tokenisation, le parallélisme de modèles et de données), l'adaptation des LMM aux applications en aval et l'adaptation de la charge aux ressources HPC. Au sein de l’équipe « Support aux utilisateurs IA » de l’IDRIS, l’ingénieure/ingénieur mène des missions d’expertise à la convergence de l’IA et du HPC en collaboration avec les autres centres européens membres du programme MINERVA Son travail consistera à accompagner les communautés d’IA et de ML à maitriser les ressources d’un supercalculateur, de répondre aux questions des utilisateurs, à installer les piles logicielles adaptées, rédiger de la documentation en ligne, participer à des formations, faire de la veille technologique. Elle/il connaît le fonctionnement du centre de calcul et est capable de conseiller les utilisateurs sur l’optimisation de leurs usages des ressources matérielles et logicielles du centre. L'Activité Assurer un support technique en distanciel ou présentiel aux projets du programme MINERVA, organiser son travail sur une durée limitée afin d’atteindre les objectifs fixés, et communiquer régulièrement sur l’avancée du projet. Identifier et répondre aux besoins des projets européens sélectionnés par le programme MINERVA Assurer un accompagnement technique et scientifique dans le domaine de l'IA, aussi bien sur les aspects méthodologiques, algorithmiques que logiciels, à destination des utilisateurs du projet MINERVA Contribuer activement à l'activité de veille technologique avancée sur les évolutions dans le domaine de l'IA (architectures de modèle, méthodes de distribution, optimisation d’entraînement, logiciels, conteneurisation, accélérateurs, optimisations matérielles, etc) Organiser, définir, construire et dispenser de nouvelles formations et workshops à destination des utilisateurs IA du projet MINERVA Proposer, planifier, organiser et mettre en œuvre le déploiement, l'exploitation, les tests de fonctionnalité, de non régression et de performance des environnements spécifiques et des piles logicielles répondant aux besoins des utilisateurs et participer à leur maintenance sur le long terme Interagir avec les autres partenaires du projet, participer aux réunions d’avancement du projet et aux réflexions sur les activités ou réalisations à mettre en production. Gérer l’avancement de l’ensemble des partenaires sur le WP dont l’IDRIS est responsable, organiser la répartition du travail en fonction des engagements, faire respecter les délais et superviser la rédaction de l’ensemble des délivrables dont l’IDRIS a la charge. items.desc: Località: Pieve Emanuele, Milano, IT, 20072 Laboratory of Cellular and Humoral Innate Immunity Work location: Via Rita Levi Montalcini 4, Pieve Emanuele (MI) Contract type: Fellowship Why Humanitas Choosing Humanitas means joining an environment where quality of care is built every day through clinical expertise, innovation and teamwork, where everyone contributes to the patient care journey. Who we are Humanitas Research Hospital is a highly specialized research and university hospital, and the first in Italy to be certified as an Academic Hospital by the Joint Commission International. Research is driven daily by over 500 physicians, biologists, physicists, data scientists, and technologists working across hospital wards and 10,000 sqm of high-tech laboratories. Our mission is to transform discoveries into concrete cures, with a strategic focus on five key areas: cancer, immunology, neuroscience, gastrointestinal medicine, and molecular cardiology. The context The Laboratory of Cellular and Humoral Innate Immunity at IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital is seeking a motivated Predoctoral Research Fellow to join a research project funded by the Italian Ministry of Health (Ricerca Finalizzata 2024) . Our research aims to understand how soluble innate immune effectors (including PTX3 and the complement system ) regulate inflammation, antimicrobial immunity, and bone remodelling during bacterial osteomyelitis and periprosthetic joint infection . By integrating high-content information from experimental models and human clinical samples, we seek to identify novel molecular mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets. The position offers an opportunity to gain research experience and potentially progress to the PhD program in Molecular, Experimental and Computational Medicine (MECM) at Humanitas University , starting in November 2027, subject to successful admission The successful candidate will actively contribute to the experimental activities of the project, including: performing cell and molecular biology , microbiology , and biochemistry experiments; working with cellular models of bacterial infection and host-pathogen interactions; investigating pathways involving PTX3, complement, and other soluble innate immune effectors; generating, analyzing, and interpreting experimental data in collaboration with senior researchers; contributing to scientific publications and conference presentations. The candidate will also have the opportunity to participate in in vivo studies using mouse models of bacterial osteomyelitis . The person we are looking for We are looking for enthusiastic and curious graduates with a strong interest in experimental biomedical research. Applicants should have: basic laboratory experience in cell and molecular biology, microbiology, and/or biochemistry; familiarity with mammalian cell culture and standard molecular and biochemical techniques; a genuine interest in basic and translational biomedical research; motivation, scientific curiosity, and willingness to learn new experimental approaches; good communication skills and command of English. Experience with experimental animal models, particularly mice, will be considered an advantage. An MSc in Biotechnology, Biology, Chemistry and Pharmaceutical Technologies, or a related discipline is desirable but not essential. Motivation, commitment, and enthusiasm for experimental research will be the primary selection criteria. The position will be based in the Laboratory of Cellular and Humoral Innate Immunity under the scientific supervision of Prof. Antonio Inforzato (https://www.humanitas-research.com/researchers/antonio-inforzato/) . The successful candidate will work alongside senior postdoctoral researchers and experienced research technicians , receiving close scientific mentoring and hands-on training. The candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment bringing together expertise in innate immunity, microbiology, osteoimmunology, proteomics, computational biology, and clinical research What we offer a fully funded 1-year position, starting in January 2027, with a gross salary from 20.000 to 23.000 euro the possibility of progressing to a 3-year PhD program in Molecular, Experimental and Computational Medicine (MECM) at Humanitas University, starting in November 2027, subject to successful admission; close scientific supervision, hands-on training, and strong technical support; access to state-of-the-art experimental facilities; a collaborative and international research environment; opportunities for scientific publications, international conferences, and professional development. This offer is open to candidates in compliance with Legislative Decrees 198/2006, 215/2003 and 216/2003.

items.desc: Applied Research Engineer £50,000 GBP pa 15-MONTH FIXED TERM Counterfeiting in critical supply chains is a growing threat across high-consequence industries. Backed by recent deeptech seed funding, our initiative, Project INSIGNIA, aims to make the physical counterfeiting of critical components impossible. We do this by embedding micro-scale cryptographic signatures directly into the internal structure of 3D-printed metal parts. We are a small, focused team looking for our next colleague: an Applied Research Engineer to serve as the practical engine of Project INSIGNIA. You will work directly with the founders, taking digital models and established project milestones and turning them into working physical reality. This means taking full ownership of laboratory execution, from designing experimental architectures to validating physical cryptographic states. As an Applied Research Engineer on Project INSIGNIA, you will: Devise and build the experimental plans required to write and read physical cryptography in metal alloys. Work hands-on with materials characterisation, including metallographic sample preparation, optical microscopy, and coordinating external X-ray computed tomography (XCT) scans. Test and iterate on sensor setups for non-destructive evaluation (NDE), exploring techniques such as acoustic resonance, eddy current, or bespoke electrical interrogation rigs. Coordinate trials with national user facilities and academic partners to validate our cryptographic states. Own laboratory execution, maintaining rigorous standards of data integrity and laboratory safety while moving quickly. You will thrive in this role if you: Possess a solid core craft with a degree or hands-on background in Metallurgy, Materials Science, Physics, or Electrical Engineering. Default to high agency and autonomy, thriving in an R&D environment where the path forward is not always pre-charted. When an experimental setup fails, you diagnose the fault, redesign the experiment, and try again. Value pragmatism over pure theory, preferring robust, reproducible physical data over endless modelling. Have practical familiarity with non-destructive testing sensors, microstructural characterisation, metal additive manufacturing, or Python for experimental data capture (all valuable, though not all required). Working at Instruct3D Small team, high agency: No bureaucracy or management layers. You own your work from concept to physical test. Pragmatic flexibility: Core working hours built around getting hard technical work done in the lab, balanced with genuine respect for personal and family commitments outside work. Craft over hype: We care about physics, sound metallurgy, and building things that reliably work in the physical world. Compensation & Benefits We believe in transparent compensation, solid security, and treating team members properly. Salary: £50,000 per annum. Contract: 15-month fixed-term role for Project INSIGNIA, with the intention to transition into a permanent position subject to future funding and project milestones. Pension: 5% employer pension contribution on all earnings. Financial wellbeing: An annual one-to-one review meeting with an independent financial adviser, plus year-round access for any pension or planning queries. Healthcare: Comprehensive private medical insurance including full cancer cover, full outpatient cover, mental health & therapies. Annual leave: 28 days annual leave, plus UK bank holidays. Start date: Onboarding by January 2027 at the latest, accommodating standard industry notice periods. Right to work: You must currently hold the right to work in the UK. Due to the strict timelines of this grant, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship. Why Sheffield? Our lab and office space sits in Sheffield city centre. Sheffield consistently ranks among the most affordable and liveable technical hubs in the UK, offering an exceptional quality of life without the punishing living costs of London, Oxford, or Cambridge. Commutes are typically measured in minutes rather than hours, the local housing market remains genuinely accessible, and the Peak District National Park is just 20 minutes from the lab bench. It is an ideal base to build both a career and a life outside work. What to expect next: Stage 1 (30 minutes): An informal video chat with the founders to discuss background, project scope, and mutual fit. Stage 2 (60 to 90 minutes): A technical deep dive where you walk us through a previous technical challenge or experimental rig, discussing first-principles physics, trade-offs, and failure modes. Stage 3 (In-person): A visit to our Sheffield lab to meet the team, inspect the hardware, and ensure the environment suits you. Not the right role for you, but interested in what we do? We keep our core team lean, but we are always keen to hear from skilled engineers and scientists. Send a brief note and CV to join@instruct3d.io. items.desc: We are looking for an experienced and motivated Data Scientist to join our Research and Innovation (R&I) Division. This is an exciting opportunity to use advanced analytics, predictive modelling and data visualisation to help shape the future of clinical research at The Christie. Working across a complex research portfolio, you will turn data from systems including EDGE, Florence, Tableau and NIHR reporting platforms into clear, actionable intelligence. You will work closely with R&I leaders, operational teams and colleagues across the wider Trust to improve visibility of the clinical trial pipeline, forecast demand, identify risks and capacity pressures, and support evidence-based decisions about workforce, resources and service development. We are seeking someone who can combine strong technical expertise with curiosity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. Please note that this role is hybrid working, with 2 days on site per week required. The post holder will collect, link, analyse and interpret large and complex datasets from multiple sources, ensuring that outputs are accurate, timely and meaningful. They will develop and maintain dashboards, reports, forecasts and analytical products for audiences including the R&I Leadership Team, ERIG, Trust Board, senior committees and external stakeholders. Using statistical and machine-learning techniques, the post holder will model future trial activity and demand, identify trends, inequalities, risks and capacity constraints, and translate findings into practical recommendations. This will support research performance, workforce and resource planning, patient recruitment, the national 150-day site set-up target, and improved diversity and inclusivity in research participation. The successful candidate will have substantial experience of data science, statistics or business intelligence, including strong skills in R, Python, TSQL, data modelling and visualisation. They will work autonomously and collaboratively, manage complex projects, maintain clear technical documentation, support safe change management, and ensure solutions comply with NHS data, information governance, security and quality standards. The role also includes providing technical guidance and line management support to junior staff. The Christie is one of Europe’s leading cancer centres, looking after more than 64,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 25% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country. We are the largest radiotherapy provider in the NHS with one in 20 treatments delivered at The Christie. We have up to 15 linear accelerators operating across our network of sites. We operate the largest chemotherapy unit in the UK on our main site and treatments are also provided at 13 other networked sites, and in patients homes. And as a specialist tertiary surgical centre, we focus on rare cancers, complex procedures, and multidisciplinary approaches to cancer surgery, specialising in colorectal, peritoneal, gynaecological, urological and plastic surgery. We are also an international leader in research, with world first breakthroughs for over 100 years. We have been named by the UK’s National Institute for Health Research (NIHR), as one of the best hospitals providing opportunities for patients to participate in clinical research studies, with more than 800 studies open at any time, caring for over 3,000 patients. 1. Conducting predictive modelling using statistical and machine learning techniques in order to build, maintain, and improve on multiple real-time decision systems. 2. Developing, documenting and maintaining code using statistical and machine learning software languages. 5. Identifying novel uses of NHS data and implement solutions to deliver fresh insights. 6. Working effectively on your own and as part of the team - contributing innovative ideas and knowledge to your colleagues. 7. Communicating effectively to non-technical colleagues both inside and outside of the Trust in both written and verbal form. 8. A commitment to innovation and good design will form part of the ethos of this role the post holder will be expected to participate in a culture of active investigation into better ways of working and service provision. The post holder will be expected to research best practice, interpret the relevance of this to the Trust, and identify methodologies that could be implemented to achieve improvements; this may involve learning new skills as required and staying abreast of current technological developments. Join our Vehicle Science team as a Data Science Engineer , where your work will directly influence the development and performance of our Formula One car. Working with complex data from CFD, wind tunnel testing and the track, you'll help turn advanced analysis into better engineering decisions. Your work will range from targeted experiments on individual components to measurements of complete LLM serving systems. Working with workload, simulation and uncertainty specialists, you will investigate bottlenecks, explain performance variation
items.desc: About CommonAI CommonAI CIC is a non-profit organisation built around collaborative engineering and is backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. Our Scaling Inference Lab (SIL) is developing simulation grounded in real measurements to help the UK invest in promising AI infrastructure. We connect proposed hardware designs to realistic workloads, helping investors and engineers understand their potential, their limitations and the next experiment worth doing. The Opportunity Design and run experiments that reveal how AI infrastructure behaves, what limits its performance and how reliably that behaviour can be predicted. You will build measurement tools and turn observations of real hardware and software into evidence for SIL’s simulation platform and the investment decisions it supports. Your work will range from targeted experiments on individual components to measurements of complete LLM serving systems. Working with workload, simulation and uncertainty specialists, you will investigate bottlenecks, explain performance variation and identify the meaningful effects. We welcome deep expertise in one or more parts of the hardware and software stack. You will work with colleagues who bring complementary strengths, with scope to broaden your expertise as the team grows. What you will do Design and run reproducible experiments, from individual hardware or software components to complete LLM serving systems, covering relevant workloads, configurations and operating conditions. Develop reusable measurement tools and collect traces, profiles and counters to characterise latency, throughput, memory behaviour and, where reliable measurement is possible, power and energy. Investigate bottlenecks, performance variation and unexpected behaviour across the layers your expertise covers, working with colleagues to extend the investigation through the stack. Take responsibility for reproducible workload details, software versions, configuration and measurement methods so results can be reproduced, compared and used to calibrate simulator models. Work with simulation and uncertainty specialists to choose measurements that resolve important unknowns and undertake curation of calibration and validation data. Help define the controls needed for experiments and use the resulting cluster-control interfaces, coordinating access and changes with colleagues responsible for the hardware. An example early project would be to work with workload colleagues to establish a reproducible reference experiment and measurement dataset, investigating how performance changes under a selected configuration or load change. Requirements Experience investigating the performance of real computing systems and designing experiments that support rigorous conclusions. Depth in one or more relevant areas: accelerator profiling, inference runtimes, memory systems, distributed/HPC workloads, networking, or power and energy measurement. The ability to build maintainable automation and analysis tools in a suitable software language, and to learn unfamiliar profiling tools. Knowledge and care of experimental controls, repeatability, confounding effects and the limits of a measurement. Some experience using AI coding agents, alongside sound debugging and review habits. LLM serving experience and familiarity with tools such as Nsight, PyTorch Profiler or system/network profilers would be useful. These are examples, not a requirement to know every tool. Strong expertise in one part of the stack is welcome; we can shape the role and recruit complementary strengths around it. Why join us Help build UK AI capability and improve how investment and compute serve the public good. Build a network spanning UK hardware SMEs, major technology companies, venture and public investors, and leading universities. Shape a growing team with startup pace and close academic links. Use frontier models and coding agents with a substantial tooling budget. Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package, including pension and benefits Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential figures from across the tech sector and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes’ walk away from Cambridge train station Working with us Hybrid, with regular time in Cambridge agreed individually around hardware work and collaboration; applicants across the UK are welcome. We are open to permanent employment, part-time arrangements and consultancy. We would like you to start as soon as practical and can be flexible for the right person. We particularly welcome experienced engineers but will also consider earlier-career candidates with strong evidence of ability. Relevant postgraduate study is useful, but qualifications are secondary to experience and the quality of your work. CommonAI CIC …

We engineer and deliver battle proven capabilities across the world. Kirintec is owned by BAE Systems, who provides some of the world’s most advanced, technology-led defence, aerospace and security solutions and employs a skilled workforce of more than 93,000 people in around 40 countries. About the role For most of the concepts that we develop, the journey begins with creating a python simulation (or similar) to understand the proposed technique/algorithm. The concept is then matured to use real data with SDRs or from our own hardware. Finally, the technique is fully ported to our hardware, typically in OpenCPI (C++ and VHDL). For this role we are looking for a specialist in Machine Learning to assist in the above with main emphasis at the earlier stage. We are looking for the principal skillset in ML and secondary skillsets in DSP and algorithms. The primary duty will be to develop machine learning techniques for embedded Radio Frequency (RF) platforms and desktop systems used in Electronic Warfare. On a day-to-day basis the role will include developing offline with the usual libraries (e.g. tensorflow), then using techniques such as quantisation to show that it can run on target hardware. Duties will include; Delivery of concept demonstrators up to field trial level Help identifying new techniques that can advance the product Provide expertise in the area of ML and algorithms to the company Any other reasonable duties required to support the company in meeting its objectives Working to Kirintec’s ISO standards About you You will be able to; Demonstrate best practices around training and deploying ML models Showcase demonstrable history of using ML/algorithms/statistical techniques to solve real world problems (ideally on FPGA or embedded processors) Prove practical experience of DSP in RF comms domain (or similar domain) Demonstrate expert knowledge in python and libraries such as numpy, pytorch/tensorflow Show knowledge of key software development tools e.g. Git, Docker, Jenkins Prove experience with software-defined radio (SDR) systems What we Offer 25 days annual leave entitlement, rising with length of service. All applicants must as a minimum achieve Baseline Personnel Security Standard. Many roles also require higher levels of National Security Vetting where applicants must typically have a minimum of 5-year continuous residency in the UK, to allow for meaningful security vetting checks. items.desc: Company Overview Central Pharma is a pharmaceutical company focused on supporting the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries through quality-driven products and services. We are committed to maintaining high standards of quality, safety, and customer service while operating in a professional and collaborative environment. At Central Pharma, we recognise that our people are key to our success. We aim to foster teamwork, encourage continuous improvement, and provide an environment where employees can develop their skills and contribute to the company’s growth. Location: HD7 5QH Contract: Initial three-month temporary contract, with the opportunity to move into a permanent role Salary: £26,000–£30,000 per annum equivalent, depending on skills and experience Positions available: 2 About the role We are looking for curious, practical and detail-oriented graduates or early-career professionals to join our team as Junior Data & Systems Analysts. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of data, software, hardware and quality within a pharmaceutical environment. You will help ensure our data is accurate, our systems work as expected, and our software and processes are properly tested and documented. You do not need previous pharmaceutical or GMP experience. We are looking for people with a good technical foundation, hands-on coding experience and a willingness to learn how technology is used in a regulated environment. What you will do Data integrity and reconciliation: Compare and reconcile data across warehouse and RFID systems, ERP, finance and other platforms, investigating discrepancies and helping resolve their causes. Software testing and validation: Test our in-house software, write test scripts, record results, collect evidence and support software validation documentation. Data migration and due diligence: Check data and records as we migrate from our ERP to our own platform, identifying inconsistencies and helping ensure data is complete and accurate. Reporting and analytics: Build simple reports, dashboards and data checks to improve visibility and support day-to-day operations. Systems support: Help investigate data and software issues, troubleshoot problems and support routine system maintenance. Hardware and device testing: Assist with setting up and testing RFID handhelds, cameras and small computing devices, including Raspberry Pi and Jetson hardware. Quality and documentation: Maintain clear, accurate records and follow agreed procedures appropriate to a regulated pharmaceutical environment. Essential skills and experience A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, Engineering or a related quantitative or technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Working knowledge of Python and SQL, demonstrated through work experience, internships, university projects or a personal portfolio. Good Excel and spreadsheet skills, including data cleaning, comparison and reconciliation. Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to checking work. Logical problem-solving skills and an interest in debugging and investigating discrepancies. Clear written communication and the ability to document work accurately. A practical, hands-on attitude and willingness to learn new tools and systems. Desirable skills You do not need experience in all these areas. Exposure to any of the following would be an advantage: Databases and cloud platforms, such as PostgreSQL, Supabase, AWS or Firebase. Reporting and visualisation tools, such as Power BI, Dash or Metabase. Git and GitHub. Machine learning or computer vision, including TensorFlow or PyTorch. Hardware, electronics, RFID, cameras or IoT devices. Software testing, data validation, quality assurance or regulated environments such as pharmaceutical manufacturing, healthcare or GMP. Pay: From £26,000.00 per year Benefits: Casual dress Company pension Free parking On-site parking Work Location: In person

items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous models and hardware. Our team is developing the science that makes that possible: a principled, evidence-based method for building agentic systems automatically at unprecedented scale. Today, designing these systems is a craft. Decisions about memory management, task decomposition, tool use and inter-agent coordination are made on intuition and convention. The results work until they don't, and it is rarely clear in advance which failure comes next. The team tackles these problems on two fronts. We build the tools to analyse and evaluate agentic systems rigorously enough to say where and why they go wrong, and we use what we learn to design better ones. We are not simply building a better harness; the best harness will change with every new model, task and generation of silicon. We are building the layer beneath it, so that design decisions follow from evidence rather than taste. The mandate is broad, and most of the questions inside it are still unanswered. You will have wide latitude to choose problems, and your results will shape what the company builds in the future. What You'll Build Design and run experiments that isolate why agentic systems fail - across behaviour, traces and activations - and turn those findings into interventions that measurably move intelligence, cost and reliability Attack one or more of our core research themes: context and memory management; agent steering, task decomposition and specialisation; continual learning during deployment; and inter-agent communication Build agent analysis and evaluation infrastructure - observability, behaviour analysis, evaluation harnesses, auditing - as durable instruments the whole company works from, not one-off scripts Publish. Evaluation results, methods and discoveries, as both company assets and public evidence Work across team boundaries in both directions: take a vertical domain-specific application problem and design systems which run at unpreceding scale at lowest cost and latency; or invent novel model and agent architecture which exploit emerging unconventional silicons beyond GPU What You'll Bring Evidence that you can run research of your own: you take an open question, design the experiments that settle it, and produce results other people can build on. Where you learned to do that matters less to us than that you can Deep hands-on experience with LLMs in agentic settings: multi-step tasks, tool use, long horizons, and the specific ways all of it breaks Real experimental discipline. items.desc: Are you a hands-on research scientist with deep expertise in medical imaging and strong technical skills in programming, data analytics and AI? Do you enjoy combining scientific research with practical technical development, taking ownership and driving complex research collaborations towards successful outcomes? Collective Minds is looking for a Research Scientist to drive scientific and technical contributions in public and private research consortia. This is an opportunity to combine research, technology and project ownership in a growing international healthtech company. About Collective Minds Collective Minds is based in Stockholm/Danderyd and we operate globally across clinical trials and life sciences. We are an imaging platform for clinical trials that connects hospitals, experts, and industry - including CROs, pharma, biotech, medtech, and eClinical vendors - enabling trials with imaging endpoints and the generation of high-quality evidence faster and more efficiently. We are a fast-moving, commercially minded team focused on collaboration, accountability, and impact. By combining deep domain expertise in medical imaging with novel cloud technology, we help customers reduce risk, ensure compliance, accelerate and scale research. About the role As Research Scientist, you will combine scientific expertise in medical imaging with hands-on technical development and ownership of selected research consortia. Collective Minds currently participates in more than 10 public and private research consortia spanning medical imaging, big data, analytics and AI modeling and validation. These collaborations bring together academic hospitals, research organizations and industry partners across therapeutic areas such as oncology, immunology, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal research. Acting as a data manager and platform provider, Collective Minds plays a central role in these collaborations. You will be responsible for our contributions in two to three consortia, with the opportunity to apply your scientific and technical expertise, work independently and contribute to impactful research. Your main responsibilities: Lead Collective Minds' contributions in selected research consortia, ensuring delivery within agreed budgets, timelines and scope. Develop and implement technical solutions, including scripts, data pipelines, analytical tools, dashboards and AI-based applications. Make scientific and technical decisions across medical imaging, data analytics, AI modeling and validation. Ensure effective use of the Collective Minds platform, prioritizing standardized and scalable solutions over unnecessary custom development. Manage project scope and stakeholder expectations, clearly defining deliverables and commitments. Take ownership of work package delivery, reporting to consortium partners, coordinators and funders, and efficient project close-outs. Collaborate with internal teams and external research partners, coordinating additional resources when needed. Who are we looking for? We are looking for a scientifically experienced and technically skilled professional who combines deep expertise in medical imaging with the ability to independently develop solutions and deliver complex research projects. You are analytical, pragmatic and hands-on, with a proactive approach to problem-solving. You enjoy taking ownership, collaborating across disciplines and driving results in a fast-moving environment. We believe you have: A strong scientific background in life sciences, medicine, biomedical engineering or a related field, with deep expertise in medical imaging research. Strong hands-on technical skills in Python, SQL, DICOM and AI frameworks, with experience developing scripts, data tools and analytical solutions. Familiarity with dashboarding tools such as Superset or Metabase is a plus. Experience delivering work packages in research consortia or grant-funded projects, including grant execution, reporting and project close-outs. A proven ability to independently manage research projects within agreed budgets, timelines and scope, and make informed scientific and technical decisions. Experience coordinating work across academic, clinical and industry partners, with strong communication and stakeholder management skills. Fluent in English, both written and spoken. Willingness to travel internationally as required, typically approximately every two months. Ability to work regularly from our Stockholm/Danderyd office. Why join Collective Minds? At Collective Minds, you will join an innovative and ambitious company where technology, science and collaboration come together to make a meaningful difference in healthcare. You will be part of an entrepreneurial environment with short decision-making processes, engaged colleagues and the opportunity to influence how things are done. items.desc: The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university. We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special. Overview We are inviting applications for a Research Associate to support the University of Sheffield’s contribution to the SMART (Secure Motor AI-Responsive Technology) project funded by Innovate UK. The post will contribute to the development and validation of computationally efficient motor-twin models for permanent magnet synchronous machines. The work will focus on machine modelling, parameter and state estimation, plus preparing modelling outputs that can be shared with project’s partners. The successful candidate will work with academic and industrial project partners to generate simulation and experimental validation evidence, using available machine data, dynamometer testing and HIL methods. The role will also involve documenting methods and results for project deliverables, reports and publications. The post is suited to candidates with a PhD awarded in electrical machines, drives, control, real-time simulation, or a closely related engineering discipline, who is motivated to develop deployable motor-twin methods for intelligent motor drives. Main Duties And Responsibilities Develop and implement motor-twin models for BLDC/PMSM drives, including parameters and state estimation. Deliver reduced-order high-fidelity electrical machine modelling methods suitable for simulation, HIL and real-time controller. items.desc: Data Scientist (LLMs & Conversational AI) About the role We are building production conversational AI systems powered by large language models, speech AI, and real-time AI workflows. We’re hiring two Data Scientists to join our LLM team, helping design, improve, and evaluate the systems that power our Conversational AI products in production. The focus is on defining, interrogating and solving complex modelling and evaluation problems, and building the data and experimentation foundations that will generate systematic advances in conversational AI. You’ll work closely with researchers, engineers, and evaluation teams across areas such as LLM behaviour and reasoning, prompt optimisation, conversational quality, and model evaluation. We’re particularly interested in people from strong quantitative backgrounds including Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Computer Science, or related fields, who enjoy piecing together difficult problems, thinking rigorously, and working in environments driven by research and experimentation. What you’ll do Design and use datasets, experiments and evaluation methods to gain detailed and intimate knowledge of our conversational AI solutions. Identify opportunities to improve quality, reliability, and performance through research and experimentation Statistically investigate how changes to prompts, pipelines, models, or system logic impact real-world outcomes Think creatively about edge cases that might expose flaws in a system, and devise and test different ideas about how to handle those cases without harming global performance Develop tests and metrics that capture the many nuances of user requirements, rather than uncritically relying on industry-standard proxies that might obscure underlying issues Advance the building blocks behind LLM-powered systems, including classification, ranking, retrieval, scoring, and conversational workflows Collaborate with engineering and evaluation teams to turn product problems into measurable AI problems Stay up to date with the latest research and critically apply new ideas to production AI systems, separating out strong, flexible approaches from fragile hype What we’re looking for Degree, MSc, or PhD in Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Computer Science, or a similarly quantitative field Strong Python skills with experience using tools such as pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn Experience working with data science, experimentation, statistical analysis, or machine learning systems Curiosity around the finer details of LLMs, NLP, or conversational AI Ability to think critically about model behaviour and system performance rather than simply training models Sceptical mindset: you are uncomfortable with taking any assumption as given, and you examine new ideas with an open but critical mind Comfortable working in fast-moving, collaborative environments with ambiguous problems Why join us Work on real-world conversational AI systems used in production Solve difficult applied AI problems in a highly collaborative environment Join a research-driven team working across LLMs, speech AI, and evaluation Influence how AI systems are measured, improved, and deployed at scale

items.desc: THE ROLE The FAIR Programme at The Alan Turing Institute is an academic-industry collaboration developing an actionable framework for the trustworthy and reliable adoption of AI at scale within the financial services industry. Its research focuses on three key challenges: AI assurance, AI-powered financial crime detection, and trustworthy agentic workflows. We are looking for a talented Research Associate to join our FAIR Programme. Working alongside leading researchers, partner universities and industry, you will develop, implement and evaluate innovative methods, models or tools that address real-world challenges in responsible and trustworthy AI for financial services. ABOUT YOU The successful candidate will hold or be working toward a PhD in Mathematics, Computer Science or a closely related discipline, alongside a strong background in areas such as reinforcement learning, bandit methods, anomaly detection, privacy, robustness, uncertainty quantification or quantitative finance. You will bring experience developing research software using tools such as Python, Java, TensorFlow or PyTorch, and an understanding of the technical challenges involved in operationalising AI, including generative AI, within financial services.
