items.desc: Magnesium alloys offer exceptional lightweighting potential for aerospace and space applications, but their wider use in extreme environments is limited by challenges including microstructural instability, temperature fluctuations and irradiation-induced damage. At the same time, oxide inclusions formed during casting and manufacturing are conventionally regarded as detrimental to structural performance. This project seeks to turn these"liabilities into assets" by exploiting solid-state, friction-based manufacturing to create finely dispersed oxide nanoparticles in magnesium alloys, enabling the development of oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) magnesium alloys with enhanced thermal stability, high-temperature performance and radiation resistance. You will work within the research group led by Dr Dikai Guan at the University of Southampton on an NSF-EPSRC research project. The project brings together the University of Southampton, Baylor University, UK National Ion Beam Centre, integrating alloy processing, friction-based manufacturing, multiscale characterisation, modelling and extreme-environment testing. The position is offered until 31/05/2028 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for up to 1 further year. The Research Fellow will be a major contributor to the experimental research activities at the University of Southampton, including: Feedstock alloy development and characterisation Multiscale microstructure characterisation Cryogenic and thermal-cycling testing Radiation-resistance testing You will have a good track record in carrying out independent and original scientific research, and publication of research papers. You should have the ability to work and communicate efficiently with other members of the team (supervisors, students and postdocs), and collaborators outside the University. Regular reports of research progress are required, and research plans should be adjusted accordingly. Critical analysis of experimental results and problem solving skills are essential to this role. You will also be required to write research papers for publication in high impact research journals and attend/present at relevant conferences. There will be an opportunity to supervisor PhD and Master students as a secondary supervisor. You should hold a PhD (or near completion)/ relevant experience in materials science or a relevant discipline. Research experience in physical metallurgy, metallic materials and advanced microstructure characterisation is particularly relevant to this position. Experience with SEM/EDS and EBSD, together with TEM/STEM or related high-resolution characterisation techniques, is highly desirable. Experience in oxide-dispersion-strengthened materials, metal casting, friction-based processing, cryogenic testing, thermal cycling, ion irradiation, or other advanced characterisation methods would be advantageous. Equality, diversity and inclusion are central to the ethos in the School of Engineering. We give full consideration to applicants who wish to work flexibly including part-time and due consideration will be given to applicants who have taken a career break. The University has onsite childcare facilities and we foster a good work-life balance. We also offer a mentorship programme and the school runs a women-oriented network event on a bi-weekly basis. The University of Southampton is in the top 1% of world universities and the top 10 of the UK’s research-intensive universities. We are committed to sustainability and being a globally responsible university, with the principles of sustainability embedded into all aspects of our individual and collective work, in our business planning, policy-making, and professional activities. items.desc: ABOUT ZENITHON Zenithon is an applied frontier lab for extreme physics. We build foundation models that simulate plasmas, so engineers can explore far more of the design space before they build anything. THE ROLE Semiconductor plasma etch is a core part of Zenithon's business, and this role helps shape it. We're hiring a computational plasma physicist to own the physics behind our etch reactor models. You'll decide how our simulations are set up, which physics matters and where, and where the work goes next. You'll work with our ML researchers to make sure the models get it right. When engineers at the companies we work with ask whether to trust a result, you'll be the person who can answer. WHAT YOU'LL DO Own how we set up reactor-scale etch simulations: geometries, chemistry, boundary conditions and the operating ranges that matter. Set the direction of our simulation work: where fidelity matters, from sheaths to surface chemistry, and which campaigns we run next. Run simulation campaigns across wide ranges of reactor geometry, chemistry and operating conditions. Check model outputs against physics and measurements, and show clearly where the errors sit. Work with ML researchers on model inputs, outputs and tests. Talk with engineers at partner companies about their reactors, and turn what they need into what we build next. WHAT YOU'LL BRING A PhD in plasma physics, applied physics, or electrical, chemical or mechanical engineering, or a related field. Hands-on experience with HPEM, VizGlow, COMSOL or a similar reactor-scale plasma code. You've built geometries, set up chemistry and boundary conditions, and fixed runs that wouldn't converge. Strong grounding in low-temperature plasma physics: sheaths, electron energy distributions, ion energy and angle distributions, and plasma chemistry. Python and scientific computing. Clear communication with engineers who don't model. This role suits someone early in their career or a few years past their PhD. BONUS POINTS Experience at a semiconductor equipment maker or a fab. Etch chemistries, surface reactions or feature-scale profile models. PIC/MCC codes, or HPC and GPU experience. Comparing simulations with experiments. You've written or extended a solver, shipped open-source code, or worked at a startup. HOW WE WORK We're a small, in-person team in London and San Francisco that works hard, moves fast and holds a high bar. Two principles guide everything we do: intellectual ambition in what we attempt, and empirical precision in how we measure it. You'll own real problems from your first week, and your work will shape what the company becomes. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive salary and meaningful equity, set by location, plus relocation support. You can be based in San Francisco or London, on site with the team. You must be authorized to work in the US or the UK, depending on where you're based. HOW TO APPLY Send your CV and a few lines on a reactor simulation you set up: what it taught you, and where it disagreed with experiment. Zenithon is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background

items.desc: We are hiring a Scientific Manager to take ownership of the machine learning and experimental design pipelines behind our customer’s genomic target prediction work. Much of this currently lives in individual scripts maintained by individual scientists. Your job is to turn it into an automated, version-controlled and reproducible platform the whole team can rely on – and to keep it scientifically sound by working shoulder to shoulder with our customer’s wet-lab and computational biology colleagues. This is a hands-on engineering role in a scientific environment. You will spend more of your time building, automating and hardening pipelines than running individual analyses, so we are looking for someone who is as comfortable with Git, containers and workflow managers as with genomics data. A PhD in bioscience engineering, bioinformatics, computer science or machine learning engineering – or an MSc with 5+ years of equivalent experience. You can demonstrate this through peer-reviewed publications, contributions to public code repositories or relevant project work. • Strong Python, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can read, test and re-run. • Proven experience taking analysis code into production: version control with Git, code review, packaging, containerization (Docker, Singularity/Apptainer) and automated testing or CI/CD. • Hands-on experience with workflow orchestration – Nextflow, Snakemake or equivalent. • Experience running workloads on cloud infrastructure (AWS) and/or HPC clusters (e.g. SLURM). • Solid grounding in statistical modelling and machine learning applied to biological data, including model evaluation and experiment tracking. • The ability to translate between engineering and bench science, and to work with scientists who are not engineers. • You are eligible to live and work in Belgium. What will you do? • Automate and professionalize internal ML and experimental design pipelines for genomic target prediction. • Migrate existing scripts and notebooks into a production-ready, version-controlled codebase. • Reduce the manual input required for dataset preparation, settings configuration and pipeline execution. • Integrate pipelines into existing digital infrastructure, including AWS and HPC environments. • Implement version control, testing and reproducibility standards across ML workflows, and help the team adopt them. • Collaborate closely with wet-lab and computational biology colleagues to make sure pipelines meet real scientific requirements. • Run several projects in parallel, (re)assigning tasks as priorities shift, and present results concisely to stakeholders inside and outside your domain.

items.desc: About The Role We are looking for an experienced AI/LLM Engineer (Model Fine-Tuning & Conversational AI) to join a fast-growing international technology company developing AI-powered conversational products. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on training, fine-tuning and improving self-hosted, open-weight large language models (LLMs) that power personalised AI conversations. You will work directly with model training pipelines, datasets, evaluation frameworks and GPU infrastructure to improve conversational quality, personality consistency, contextual memory and multilingual capabilities. The position covers the full model improvement lifecycle, from identifying weaknesses and preparing training data to running experiments, measuring results and deploying improved models into production. You will collaborate closely with AI engineering, product, web development and DevOps teams to deliver measurable improvements in conversational performance and user experience. The ideal candidate has practical experience personally fine-tuning and deploying open-weight LLMs, strong Python and PyTorch skills, and a solid understanding of post-training techniques such as supervised fine-tuning, LoRA and QLoRA. This is a model engineering position rather than a prompt engineering, API integration or purely academic research role. Candidates must have direct experience working with model weights, training processes and production deployment. Key Responsibilities Train, fine-tune and optimise existing open-weight language models to improve conversational performance. Develop and maintain model post-training workflows using supervised fine-tuning and parameter-efficient training techniques. Prepare, clean, structure and improve training datasets to enhance response accuracy, naturalness and consistency. Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure model quality and identify opportunities for improvement. Improve conversational memory, contextual understanding and personality consistency across extended interactions. Develop and optimise multilingual conversational capabilities. Enhance interactions involving multiple AI characters and complex dialogue scenarios. Investigate model failures, inconsistent responses and behavioural issues. Optimise training data, prompting approaches and response filtering mechanisms based on evaluation findings. Conduct GPU-based model training experiments and troubleshoot performance, memory and training stability issues. Apply techniques such as SFT, LoRA and QLoRA, with exposure to preference optimisation approaches such as DPO or GRPO. Analyse experimental results and identify measurable improvements in model behaviour and conversational quality. Deploy improved models into production environments and monitor their performance. Continuously refine deployed models using evaluation data, user interaction patterns and performance insights. Collaborate with AI engineers, product teams, web developers and DevOps specialists on model integration and deployment. Research and evaluate relevant developments in open-weight language models and post-training methodologies. Requirements Proven hands-on experience personally fine-tuning open-weight LLMs and deploying improved models into production. Strong professional programming skills in Python. Practical experience using PyTorch and Hugging Face or comparable machine learning frameworks. Hands-on experience with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques such as LoRA and QLoRA. Familiarity with preference optimisation techniques, particularly DPO or GRPO. Experience independently preparing training datasets and building model evaluation frameworks. items.desc: ABOUT ZENITHON Zenithon is an applied frontier lab for extreme physics. We build foundation models that simulate plasmas, so engineers can explore far more of the design space before they build anything. THE ROLE Our models learn from simulations today, and next they will learn from real experiments. Getting experimental data from an instrument into a form a model can learn from is hard, slow work, and this role owns it. You'll take data from plasma diagnostics and from the datasets our partners bring, clean it, pull out what matters and build datasets our ML researchers can rely on. You'll decide how we do this across instruments and domains, and you'll automate as much of it as you can. WHAT YOU'LL DO Take in raw data from instruments such as optical emission spectrometers, laser diagnostics, Langmuir probes and mass spectrometers, and from partner datasets in whatever form they arrive. Clean and validate it: calibrations, baselines, artefacts, missing values, and streams recorded on different clocks. Extract the quantities that matter, with their uncertainties, working closely with our physicists and ML researchers. Build training-ready datasets in Zarr and similar formats, with clear schemas, metadata and versions. Automate the path from raw files to datasets so new data flows through without hand-holding, at terabyte scale and beyond. Help decide what gets recorded in experiments, and work with our ML engineers on how data feeds training. WHAT YOU'LL BRING A degree in physics, chemistry, astrophysics, engineering or another science. Many people in this role have a PhD, but it isn't required. Hands-on experience taking messy experimental data from an instrument to clean, analysed results, ideally data you or your lab collected. Strong Python and the scientific stack (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, xarray), with Git and automated tests. Experience with large datasets and the tools to handle them. Clear, fluent English, written and spoken, for working closely with physicists, engineers and ML researchers. You don't need years of industry experience. We care most about what you've built and how fast you learn. BONUS POINTS You've trained ML models on data you processed yourself, for example to classify images, segment scans or identify compounds in spectra. Terabyte- to petabyte-scale data from experiments such as the LHC, synchrotrons or sky surveys. Spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, laser diagnostics such as Thomson scattering, or imaging data. Zarr, HDF5, NetCDF or ROOT; Dask, Ray or Spark; workflow tools and cloud storage. Signal processing and fitting: baselines, peak fitting, deconvolution and uncertainty propagation. You've built tools others rely on, contributed to open source, or worked at a startup. HOW WE WORK We're a small team that works hard, moves fast and holds a high bar. Two principles guide everything we do: intellectual ambition in what we attempt, and empirical precision in how we measure it. You'll own real problems from your first week, and your work will shape what the company becomes. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive salary and meaningful equity. You'll work from our London office near St Paul's at least three days a week. You must have the right to work in the UK. Some projects may involve export-controlled data, which can require additional screening. HOW TO APPLY Send your CV and a few lines on the messiest dataset you've worked with: what was wrong with it, what you built, and how you knew the result was right. Zenithon is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background.

items.desc:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Knowledge Platform team builds the data and action layer that connects Perplexity's agents to the systems where enterprise work happens. Useful agents need more than access to APIs: they need to discover the right tools, understand an organization's data and terminology, and act reliably within its permissions. This team brings native connectors, MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools into a consistent platform, and builds the marketplace through which customers adopt integrations and partners extend the ecosystem.



This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from designing connector infrastructure and semantic models to shipping the experiences customers use to discover, connect, and activate integrations. You'll build the runtime that executes tool calls, the knowledge layer that makes enterprise context reusable across connectors, and the developer and marketplace foundations that help the ecosystem grow. Working with AI Research and Enterprise teams, you'll turn fragmented systems into reliable, permission-aware capabilities that agents can use to complete real work. The impact is direct: every improvement helps customers put their existing software and knowledge to work through Perplexity.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the connector runtime that registers, hosts, and executes native connectors, hosted MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools through a consistent agent-facing interface.

 - Build the semantic and knowledge layer, including tool and entity schemas, capability metadata, relationships, organization-specific terminology, and reusable corrections, while preserving provenance and source-system permissions.

 - Design discovery, search, and recommendation systems that help agents find relevant tools and context and help users and organizations choose integrations that fit their work.

 - Build the marketplace and activation experience end to end, from browsing and recommendations to installation, configuration, admin enablement, and ongoing adoption.

 - Make connector execution reliable and observable, with structured results, retries, idempotency, pagination, rate-limit handling, and recovery from partial failures. Own reliability targets, production monitoring, and incident response.

 - Implement connector authentication, credential isolation, and permission enforcement, partnering with Trust & Governance, Security, and Backend Platform on shared policies and tenant boundaries.

 - Build the onboarding and publishing path for internal teams and external partners, including schemas, test fixtures, validation, review, and versioning.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable platforms that integrate heterogeneous APIs and services with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Connector runtimes, API platforms, or MCP servers, including authentication and authorization.
   
   - Schema design, semantic modeling, or knowledge systems that capture relationships and organizational context.
   
   - Search, ranking, recommendation, or tool discovery systems.
   
   - Marketplaces, developer platforms, or enterprise onboarding and activation experiences.

 - Ability to work across backend infrastructure and customer-facing product experiences, translating complex integration requirements into clear APIs, developer tools, and intuitive workflows.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive, distributed systems, balancing credential isolation, permission correctness, and failure behavior with performance, usability, and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.



If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

items.desc: Job description Division of Heat and Power Technology at the Department of Energy Technology is seeking a Research Engineer to conduct research within the Vinnova-funded projects “Impact of INlet DIstortion on the AEROdynamic and AEROelastic characteristics of an axial compressor stage (INDIAERO)” and “AI Supported Adaptive Manufacturing (AISAM)”. The projects address two important aspects affecting the aerodynamic and aeromechanical performance of fan and compressor blades in aero-engines: blade erosion and inlet flow distortion. Leading-edge erosion can increase aerodynamic losses and consequently fuel consumption. At the same time, aero-engines are frequently exposed to non-uniform inlet flow conditions due to intake geometry and varying flight conditions. These distortions can affect both aerodynamic performance and aeroelastic stability, potentially leading to phenomena such as flutter and high-cycle fatigue. Reliable methods for assessing these effects are still under development and constitute an active area of international research. High-quality experimental data are essential for the development and validation of such methods. The work will include the development and design of experimental test setups, detailed aerodynamic measurements, and the analysis and comparison of experimental and numerical results. The position involves close collaboration with the industrial partners participating in the projects. items.desc: Time Series Representation Learning for Industrial Process Characterization (ref. BAP-2026-637) Laatst aangepast: 21/10/26 The M-Group at KU Leuven Bruges Campus is an interdisciplinary research team focusing on intelligent and dependable mechatronic systems, combining research expertise from the departments of Computer Science, Electrical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering. One of the key research tracks focusses on the application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in real-world industrial settings on the one hand. The objective of the proposed PhD position is to investigate how novel techniques for time series representation learning on sensor data origination from complex and dynamic industrial processes can be leveraged for process characterization across multiple time series data mining tasks, such as anomaly detection, anomaly diagnosis and root cause analysis. The successful candidate will be offered to opportunity to pursue a PhD in Computer Science at KU Leuven, and will also be embedded within the Declarative Languages and Artificial Intelligence (DTAI) lab (https://dtai.cs.kuleuven.be), which pursues excellence in an explicit and synergistic combination of fundamental and applied research on machine learning and artificial intelligence. Doctoral training is provided in the framework of the Leuven Arenberg Doctoral School (https://set.kuleuven.be/phd). The PhD will be supervised by Prof. Mathias Verbeke and Mr. Louis Carpentier. Project Context Industry 4.0 has equipped industrial processes with large numbers of sensors, enabling continuous monitoring of machine and process behaviour. The resulting data allow the process to be modelled, which in turn yields analytical insights for optimising the process or for detecting and preventing faults. However, industrial processes are becoming increasingly complex, with many interacting components, varying operating conditions, and hundreds of monitored variables, which makes modelling the process as a whole increasingly difficult. Existing approaches rely mostly on deep neural networks to learn representations of the data, which are then leveraged in downstream tasks. While effective in terms of predictive performance, these models provide little understanding of the process itself, which is crucial in real-world applications. Post-hoc explanations do not solve this issue, as they only approximate the model's reasoning and are not guaranteed to faithfully reflect its behaviour. Furthermore, deep neural networks typically require large datasets to learn complex behaviours, which are rarely available in real industrial applications. Project The central research challenge of this PhD position is to automatically learn explainable representations from high-dimensional industrial time series data, and to leverage these representations across multiple time series data mining tasks. Within this PhD research, you will leverage motifs, i.e., representative subsequences, which act as the building blocks of the explainable time series representations and thereby offer a holistic view of the industrial process. To this end, you will design new algorithms for mining motifs in multivariate time series and for learning relationships among the discovered motifs. These algorithms will focus on three aspects. First, they will balance scalability and representativeness, i.e., the computational cost of building the motif-based representation against the level of detail and accuracy with which the motifs describe the process. Second, they will incorporate weak supervision, so that domain experts can steer the algorithms, and hence the motif-based representation, without needing to provide exhaustive labels. Finally, they will be simple to use, requiring minimal configuration with few hyperparameters whose meaning is intuitive to domain experts. The resulting representations will be evaluated in downstream tasks such as anomaly detection, anomaly diagnosis, and root cause analysis. The PhD position is part of an industrial research project with the aim of acquiring foundational knowledge about complex industrial systems and generating analytical insights that can be used to improve the production process. This PhD is embedded in the methodological core of the project, and is responsible for developing the representation learning methods on which the downstream analyses are built. The methods developed throughout the PhD will be validated on real-world industrial use cases leveraging operational data provided by the industrial partner in the project. Profile Profile We are seeking a highly motivated, enthusiastic, and communicative researcher, with a proactive and creative attitude who is eager to explore innovative solutions. items.desc: On the 1 August 2026, the University of Greenwich and the University of Kent formed a pioneering new multi-university group called London and South-East (LASE) University Group. Should you join us, you will be employed by LASE but will work as part of the University of Greenwich academic division, contributing to its distinct strengths, community and identity while also being part of a wider group that brings together the scale, resilience and shared ambition of both universities. Through LASE we aim to deliver outstanding education, impactful research, and meaningful regional and global impact. The Natural Resources Institute is a specialist research, knowledge exchange and postgraduate training unit based at the University of Greenwich’s Medway Campus. We aspire to be a global leader in collaborative research, knowledge exchange and learning to co-create a just, healthy, and sustainable future for all. We do this through transforming lives through research, innovation, and learning. The NRI has an international footprint and is home to over 80 international scientists and social scientists. We have made award-winning discoveries collaborating with partners across sectors and disciplines to co-create environmental resilience, sustainable agriculture, health, and food security. NRI works towards a just world free from disease, hunger, poverty, and violence. We are an inclusive, collaborative, and flexible research and learning institute. The Institute has a strong history of innovative research to address global challenges related to agriculture and food security. The unique diversity of disciplines across NRI’s three departments provides opportunities for transdisciplinary and systems research relevant to tackling the complexity of contemporary and emerging global agriculture, biodiversity, food security, food system and one-health challenges. An opportunity has arisen for a research entomologist to join the Agriculture, Health and Environment department. The successful applicant will carry out behavioural bioassays and electrophysiological assays on arthropods as part of our work on beneficial insects and sustainable control of pests and diseases of crops, livestock, and people. The post-holder’s responsibilities will include carrying out bioassays with terrestrial arthropods to measure responses to chemical and other stimuli. This will include electrophysiological assays (electroantennography, single sensillum recording) and behavioural bioassays in olfactometers and wind tunnels. The post-holder will have the opportunity to use apparatus for automated 2D- and 3D- tracking of insect behaviour. They will also be expected to work with the technical team to maintain colonies of arthropods in our insectaries and to conduct field work in the UK and for short periods abroad. The post-holder will be expected to contribute to the preparation of research outputs including published papers, and applications for future funding to continue research. There will be opportunities for the post-holder to undertake teaching at postgraduate and undergraduate level. Candidates must have a good theoretical and practical background in behavioural entomology or arthropod chemical ecology as demonstrated through a relevant PhD. Specific training in use of bioassay equipment will be provided. items.desc: An exciting opportunity is available for a postdoctoral Research Associate to join a recently funded Leverhulme Trust project investigating air entrainment and bubble formation by plunging jets in complex fluids. The project is motivated by a recently observed and unexpected fluid-mechanical phenomenon involving plunging jets in non-Newtonian fluids. It aims to understand the physical mechanisms governing the interaction between the jet, the free surface and the entrained air, and how these are influenced by the rheological properties of the fluid. The research will combine numerical simulations with complementary experimental and theoretical investigations to develop a fundamental understanding of these flows. This project sits at the intersection of fluid mechanics, complex fluids and interfacial phenomena. It offers the chance to contribute to ambitious, curiosity-driven research aimed at understanding a phenomenon that has not previously been described in the scientific literature. The successful candidate will play a leading role in the project’s numerical programme, developing and deploying new algorithms, and carrying out simulations of jets, bubbles and air entrainment in complex fluids. The work will involve developing new algorithms for high-fidelity adaptive multiphase fluid simulations, deploying these in in-house and open-source code bases, conducting a campaign of numerical experiments, and contributing to publications and conference presentations. The post holder will work closely with other academic investigators and project partners, including researchers undertaking complementary experimental/theoretical studies. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in numerical method development for fluid mechanics who is excited by fundamental research and wants to help shape an emerging area of study from an early stage. Applicants should have, or be close to completing, a PhD (or equivalent) in fluid mechanics, physics, engineering, or a closely related discipline. Experience in developing, deploying and analysing new numerical methods and algorithms is essential. Experience in areas such as multiphase flows, rheology, non-Newtonian fluids, or mesh-free numerical methods would be an advantage, but we welcome applicants with a strong numerical background and enthusiasm to develop new skills. The School is committed to Athena SWAN principles to promote women in science; the School’s website documenting activity in this area can be found at: https://www.manchester.ac.uk/connect/jobs/equality-diversity-inclusion/awards/athena-swan/ The University of Manchester values a diverse workforce and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. items.desc: The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee. Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference. The role The Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) home of the 5G and 6G Innovation Centre (5GIC/6GIC) is looking to recruit Research Fellow in Analog Computing for Advanced Communication Systems . The successful candidate will be part of the Wireless Systems Lab group and will have the opportunity to work very close with our industrial partners as well as with academic partners all over the world. The post holder will undertake research into ultra-low-power analog and mixed-signal computing architectures for future communication systems, with particular emphasis on receiver processing and architectures that reduce or remove reliance on conventional high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion. The research will investigate how signal-processing operations traditionally implemented digitally can be reformulated and realised using analog, mixed-signal and in-memory computing technologies. Particular emphasis will be placed on the co-design of algorithms and hardware, circuit- and system-level modelling, and evaluation of the resulting architectures in terms of communication performance, power consumption, latency, precision and implementation complexity. The post holder will be expected to be able to set, define and work towards achieving targets, disseminate results and document work done. About You ICS is the largest academic research institute in Europe specialising in all aspects of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). It is home to over 200 researchers with expertise in all communication and broadcasting systems and has developed the best in class large scale testbeds for research and innovation and enjoys the state-of-the-art lab and computing facilities. Established in 2012, 5GIC is the world’s first dedicated centre in researching end-to-end aspects of 5G and works closely with national and international leading academic institutes and key industrial partners. In November 2020, 6GIC was officially launched with parallel research undertaken in both 5G+ and 6G for 2030+. The Post Holder Must Have Expertise In The Following Strong knowledge and research experience in analogue circuit design, particularly for low-power signal processing, computing or communication applications. Experience in circuit-level modelling and simulation, including the ability to evaluate power/energy consumption and relevant circuit non-idealities. Experience or strong knowledge of algorithm–hardware co-design, including the mapping of mathematical or signal-processing operations onto practical hardware subject to noise, precision, dynamic-range, variability and implementation constraints. Strong analytical, modelling and programming skills, including experience with MATLAB and/or Python, and the ability to communicate research findings effectively in written and oral form. It would be desirable but not essential for the post holder to also have: Experience with in-memory computing architectures, including memristive/ReRAM or other emerging-device technologies. Knowledge of signal processing and communication systems, particularly channel estimation, detection, decoding, optimisation or linear algebra. A track record of high-quality peer-reviewed publications in analog/mixed-signal circuits, in-memory/neuromorphic computing, signal processing, communications or related areas. For Informal Enquiries Please Contact k.nikitopoulos@surrey.ac.uk How To Apply To apply, please submit your application with a CV and Cover Letter online via the University of Surrey jobs portal.

Al menos 2 años de experiencia en desarrollo de software o de soluciones de IA. Haber llevado algún modelo más allá del notebook : desplegado, integrado en una aplicación o en uso por alguien. Buen nivel de Python y experiencia con PyTorch o TensorFlow. Soltura con Docker y Linux. Inglés técnico para leer documentación y trabajar en proyectos europeos. Salario competitivo, con incentivos variables en función de nuestros resultados. Posibilidad de retribución variable mediante seguro médico. Flexibilidad horaria: puedes escoger entre diferentes horquillas de entrada y salida. Jornada intensiva todos los viernes a lo largo del año y en verano todos los días. ¿Te interesa? Inscríbete a nuestra oferta y síguenos en nuestras redes sociales para enterarte de todas las novedades y procesos que publicamos. En ITECAM reconocemos el valor de contar con una plantilla diversa en materia de género, edad, origen étnico, discapacidad, orientación sexual, religión y cualquier otra característica. items.desc: About The Company At Zonneplan, we are committed to shaping a sustainable future by eliminating reliance on fossil fuels and promoting renewable energy sources. Our mission, known as plan Zero, aims to create a Netherlands without fossil energy by leveraging innovative solutions in energy trading, battery optimization, and AI-driven forecasting. We believe in making a tangible difference through technological advancements and dedicated teamwork. Our organization fosters a collaborative environment where expertise, innovation, and impact are at the forefront, enabling us to contribute significantly to a cleaner, greener energy landscape. About The Role As a Data Scientist within our Trading & Optimization team, you will operate at the intersection of energy and artificial intelligence. Your work will have a direct and measurable impact on the energy grid, enabling smarter energy trading and management. You will develop integrated models that combine probabilistic forecasting, optimization, and control systems, ensuring real-time decision-making and operational efficiency. The role requires close collaboration with data scientists, engineers, and traders in a flat organizational structure that encourages initiative and ownership. Your models will be deployed live, and you will be responsible for maintaining, optimizing, and troubleshooting them proactively. The position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to plan Zero by enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of energy consumption and distribution through advanced AI tools and innovative modeling techniques. Qualifications Minimum of 3 years of experience as a data scientist with a strong foundation in statistics and machine learning. Proven experience in forecasting or time series analysis. Proficiency in Python at a production level, including deploying and monitoring models in live environments. Experience with or interest in AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar. Ability to translate models into measurable business impact and financial outcomes. Ownership mentality with the capacity to manage models from development to operational deployment. Curiosity and proactive approach to following developments in AI and machine learning, translating innovations into practical experiments. Fluent in Dutch at a professional level, with excellent communication skills. Responsibilities Develop, deploy, and maintain probabilistic forecasting models for energy trading and grid management. Integrate forecasting, optimization, and control models to support real-time decision-making processes. Work closely with engineers and traders to ensure models are operationally effective and aligned with business goals. Monitor model performance, troubleshoot issues, and implement improvements proactively. Leverage AI tools such as Claude Code to accelerate development and enhance model capabilities. Contribute to the continuous improvement of forecasting accuracy and operational efficiency. Translate complex data insights into actionable recommendations for stakeholders. Participate in team discussions and initiatives to innovate and optimize energy trading strategies. Benefits Competitive salary ranging from €4,000 to €6,000 gross per month, based on experience and seniority. 25 vacation days with options to purchase additional days. Reiskostenvergoeding (travel allowance). Claude Code Max 20x subscription as a secondary benefit, usable for work and personal projects. Personalized keuzebudget for sports, groceries, or other personal needs. Investment in your professional growth through the Zonneplan Academy, with opportunities for career advancement to senior roles. Access to modern tools and a collaborative, no-nonsense work environment. Engagement in meaningful projects that contribute directly to sustainability and energy transition. Equal Opportunity At Zonneplan, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives and backgrounds enhances our innovation and effectiveness. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or other protected characteristics. Our hiring practices are designed to ensure equal opportunity and to promote a respectful, supportive environment for everyone.

items.desc: The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university. We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special. Overview The University of Sheffield ATLAS group has an exciting opportunity for a Research Fellow in Particle Physics to join our effort in the construction of silicon strip detector modules for the ATLAS Phase-II tracker upgrade, the commissioning of the new detector and the detector development for future experiments alongside conducting physics measurements at the High Energy Frontier within the Sheffield ATLAS group remit (Higgs, Standard Model). You will supervise the work of a technician as well as graduate students in the project. We are looking for an enthusiastic candidate that is keen to develop and contribute to a sustainable research programme within the group and take over related responsibilities and leadership. There is the expectation to be involved in funding applications which could lead to the opportunity to (co-)supervise research associates / post-doctoral researchers. As such you will need a PhD in particle physics or a related field with relevant experience in software (e.g. C++, python, Root, Athena, GEANT4) and a track record of successful work within particle physics collaborations. You should have a track-record of contributing and leading publications regarding your research. You will be based in Sheffield, with frequent travel to CERN and other laboratories required. The Sheffield ATLAS group consists of five academics and has played a key role in the successful construction, commissioning and operation of the ATLAS SCT detector. Our particular strengths lie in searches for SUSY particles, measurements of SM diboson processes sensitive to new physics and of the Higgs boson and related performance studies. Main Duties And Responsibilities Strong Involvement in the day-to-day silicon module production and organisation. This includes: Performing reception and metrology tests on raw components for silicon detector modules and on the finished module Wire-bonding silicon detector modules Performing standardised tests on completed silicon detector modules using a data acquisition system Taking on leadership responsibilities in ITk module production and subsequent installation on the ATLAS-UK or ATLAS-wide level Leading the group’s participation in the R&D programme for the next generation of detectors (DRD3 and DRD8) International leadership in early ITk detector commissioning and alignment using cosmic-ray muons and the first Run-4 collision data using a Kalman filter techniques Leading contributions to physics analysis within ATLAS, for example H → μμ, diboson or di-Higgs measurements. Determine research objectives and initiate and implement a programme of research. This may include managing time, materials, finance and equipment. Disseminate research findings / results through the production of papers for high quality journals and presentations Identify and generate appropriate sources of funding and prepare research proposals for funding bodies Apply for, manage or co-manage external research funding over a period of grant(s). Prepare at least one grant application with Research Associate staffing and one without over the period of the post. Utilise research grants, report research budget management across relevant projects Provide support to senior colleagues for research proposals and funding applications Involvement in professional activities such as refereeing papers, editing journals, refereeing research grants, external examining, organising conferences, committee membership and involvement with professional bodies on accreditation. Supervise or co-supervise undergraduate / postgraduate project students and/or PhD students. Manage Research Assistant(s) and/or Research Associate(s) if requested. Delegate and monitor the work of research students. Deal with reactive requests relating to supervising research staff and students. Participate in consortium meetings and seminars Plan several months in advance to meet deadlines for journal publications and to prepare presentations and papers for collaboration meetings and conferences. As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever possible. items.desc: Vi tror på ett samhälle format av framgångsrika företag där entreprenörskap och samhällsnytta går hand i hand. Att vara en del av Fortnox är att vara en del av en ständig förändring - en förändring där du själv bestämmer hur långt du vill nå. Vårt största fokus är att ge dig rätt förutsättningar att få leva din passion tillsammans med oss. Var du kommer ifrån är inte relevant - det är vart du är på väg som är intressant för oss. Precis som vi igår inte kunde drömma om det Fortnox som finns idag, så kan du vara med och forma vilka vi är imorgon. Om tjänsten I vårt produktområde Inköp utvecklar vi några av Fortnox centrala SaaS-produkter, vilka utgör kärnan i vårt erbjudande. Här skapar vi smarta, skalbara och användarvänliga lösningar som dagligen används av hundratusentals företag i Sverige. Bland våra kunder finns en stor variation, från enskilda företagare till redovisningsbyråer. Vårt ansvar sträcker sig över produkter som bokföring, hantering av leverantörsfakturor, transaktioner, tolkning av både fakturor och kvitton och mycket mer – allt det som utgör grunden i kundernas vardag. Vi blickar mot en framtid där allt förväntas förändras, en stor del av denna förändring möjliggörs av en hög automatiseringsgrad. På Fortnox jobbar vi nu på att ta fram nästa generation av våra tolkar för allt ifrån kvitton, leverantörsfakturor och inkommande dokument. Med digitala “agenter” i olika former som stöttepelare möjliggör denna teknik att vi kan erbjuda våra kunder en upplevelse där de behöver lägga minimal tid på att hantera olika former av inkommande underlag och istället lägga sin tid på att driva sitt företag. items.desc: On this page you find: About the Science Traineeship: Context What Does the Science Traineeship Look Like? What Do We Offer? What Do We Ask? Science Trainee Testimony About Rewire Recruitment Process: Timeline The opportunity of the Science Traineeship Our Science Traineeship is meant for ambitious and high-potential master’s students who want to do things differently. In collaboration with the University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG), you are offered the opportunity to write your master thesis in the medical field. The goal is to employ the power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to better understand complex diseases, like various forms of cancer, and to advance medical science. Simultaneously, you get to work on transformative AI projects at Rewire. After graduation, you may have the opportunity to turn your research into a scientific publication, transforming your thesis work into tangible societal impact. The Science Traineeship is part of the collaboration between the UMCG and Rewire . Since the start, over than six years ago, we have already worked on more than 10 different research streams with many enthusiastic colleagues involved from both Rewire and the UMCG. Will you be the next to join this unique project? What does the Science Traineeship look like? The Science Traineeship is a full-time program for 12 months, dependent on the requirements for your Master thesis. During this period, you work on your thesis research for 3 days a week. On the other 2 days, you get the opportunity to work on one of Rewire’s AI Business projects in a regular project team. In the first half of the traineeship (depending on your study’s timelines), your research focuses on completing your thesis and achieving successful graduation. After graduation, you have the opportunity to further develop your work together with your UMCG supervisor, with the aim of bringing it to the next level. This potentially involves preparing it for scientific publication. This offers the possibility to translate your thesis into tangible societal impact, although publication cannot be guaranteed within the traineeship period. The research will focus on applying state-of-the-art AI techniques in a medical setting. With this research you will make a vital contribution to the clinical field. You will work together with a group of leading academics in their field. As Science Trainee, you are part of the Applied Quantitative AI team within Rewire. Being part of this team, you join all team meetings, outings and experience what working as a Data Scientist at Rewire entails. At Rewire, you’ll be part of a dynamic working environment, both literally and figuratively. For your research, you can work from the Rewire office alongside many like-minded and ambitious colleagues. During your business project, you may travel to the client’s office or collaborate with your team from one of our offices. We offer flexibility in where you work, always in alignment with your project team, while encouraging time in the office or in Groningen at the UMCG to foster connection, collaboration, and strong guidance. On Fridays, most Rewire colleagues come together at the Amsterdam office to catch up, hold team meetings, and kick off the weekend with Friday afternoon drinks. What do we offer? A unique opportunity to graduate, while employing your analytical skills to make a societal contribution. Flexibility in the duration of the program, depending on the number of ECTS and requirements for your Master thesis. Intensive personal guidance from a Rewire coach and supervisor, and UMCG biological experts and researchers. The opportunity to contribute to AI solutions or scalable skill-building within companies, while doing impactful academic research. Chance to explore working at Rewire as a Trainee both in our internal as well as client-facing teams. An above-average thesis salary, 25 holiday days and possibility for a performance-based bonus. A laptop and all other necessities for your work. Regular team building events and weekly Friday afternoon drinks. REQUIREMENTS What do we ask? Currently pursuing a Master's degree in Econometrics, Mathematics, Artificial Intelligence, or another quantitative field. A medical background is not required. Top-class academic performance, honour program and other extracurricular activities are highly valued. Strong focus on personal development, eager to learn and collaborate in a multidisciplinary team. Highly ambitious and impact-driven. Curious, pragmatic and persuasive. Excellent command of analytical programming language (like Python, R) and fluent in English. Experience with bioinformatics software is not expected. Full-time availability for a program for 12 months (depending on the requirements for your Master thesis), aiming to start in January ’27. Ready to kick-start your career, while having a lot of fun! About Rewire Rewire is an AI company with offices in Amsterdam and Heidelberg. From these offices, we drive AI …

items.desc: About FoodLabs FoodLabs is Europe's leading early-stage VC and venture studio, backing founders who are shaping the future of the food, health, and climate value chains. We build companies from zero, putting capital, our own team, and hands-on operating time behind a founding team before there's a product or even a name. The studio's work spans wherever a market and the data or infrastructure underneath it are broken enough to justify building the fix from scratch. About The General Data Corporation General Data is the infrastructure for licensing proprietary data: The platform runs the whole deal from request to delivery, with privacy checks, rights evidence and contracts built in. The vision is to become the system of record between AI and the world’s private data, the data that has never been published but that the next generation of AI depends on. On one side are enterprises, AI labs and robotics teams that need real-world data, and on the other are companies whose operations generate it. General Data is the data infrastructure for the modern economy, connecting every party so that data can be licensed safely, transparently and at scale. Why this is a unique opportunity AI has absorbed the public internet, and its next gains will come from private, real-world data, yet today these deals still run on email, WhatsApp and brokers, with no visibility into what was checked, who holds the rights, or whether personal data was removed. Labs are already paying for this data, and regulation like GDPR and the EU Data Act makes a trusted, verifiable layer a necessity. General Data is VC-backed and looking for its technical co-founder. Together with Founder & CEO Louai Allani , you will own the product and architecture, shape the company’s direction as an equal partner and build the team from the ground up. About the role Supplier intake: Build connectors for where companies actually keep their data: Databases, document stores, ticketing systems, machine logs, and sensor and video archives. Transaction layer: Own the pipeline, rights evidence, contracts, permissions, audit trail and delivery API. ML and data quality: Build anonymisation across text, tables, images and video, plus re-identification checks, deduplication, quality scoring and tooling that turns raw records into training-ready data. Delivery and compute: Decide whether data is processed in our cloud or inside the supplier’s environment. Build secure delivery, recurring updates and our GPU infrastructure. Technical direction: Own the architecture and roadmap. Work directly with labs, suppliers and researchers to understand what the system needs to become. What you need to succeed Data infrastructure at scale: You have built pipelines for large unstructured datasets, such as video, images, sensor logs or documents, at terabyte scale or more. Physical-world data: You have worked with documents, logs, video or sensor streams, ideally in robotics, industrial or autonomous systems and know what embodied AI teams need from data and where it breaks. Sensitive data: You know how to handle personal and confidential data safely. Experience with regulated data is a plus. Technical leadership: You make architectural decisions, explain them clearly and raise the engineering bar as the team grows. Hands-on Builder: You have taken a product, platform or open-source project from 0 to 1 that others relied on, and you still write code and own the critical paths. Founder mindset: You care about the outcome, not the title. You form strong views, test them quickly and are comfortable owning technical, product and operational problems. Location: Paris preferred. English required; French is a plus. Please note: As a co-founder, you take a real stake in what we build. The compensation is a founder salary, and your upside grows with the company through your equity. Come build the infrastructure between AI and the world's data with us!

Hands-on experience integrating multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics) to answer key scientific questions and advance disease understanding. Industry experience working with clinical data and ensuring its responsible handling. Hands-on experience applying AI and machine learning methods to scientific or R&D datasets. Experience using AI tools, including large language models (LLMs) and agentic workflows, to accelerate analysis and decision-making. Team-oriented mindset with a practical, problem-solving approach. Desirable Requirements Experience working with or fine-tuning foundation models in biology, chemistry, or clinical data. items.desc: The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee. Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to make a real difference. The role This is a Data Scientist role aimed at supporting the data collection and analysis of an exciting InnovateUK funded project in association with Aviasenze Ltd, the Pirbright Institute and Hay Farms. The project is focused on monitoring health and early warnings of ill health in poultry flocks through Aviasenze' novel acoustic monitoring technology. There may be opportunity for contract extension subject to satisfactory performance and funding, The role is offered on a hybrid basis with significant on site presence required and cannot be offered as a fully remote role. The role may be undertaken as either a full time or part-time position. About You Previous experience with data collection,storage, analysis and data governance is essential for this role, ideally in a farming or bird wildlife context. You will be involved in data reporting to multiple stakeholders with varied information needs in addition to some software development including front and back end applications. You will also have experience working with crop cards, avian data and ideally on-farm experience. Experience with Excel macros, python and pytorch is also desirable. How To Apply To apply please submit a CV and cover letter. You will also be asked to answer some brief questions to help us assess your suitability for the position. We value authentic, human-written insights, so please refrain from using generative AI tools when applying. Further Information If you require further information on this position, please contact Prof. Kevin Wells k.wells@surrey.ac.uk The University of Surrey is committed to providing an inclusive environment that offers equal opportunities for all. We place great value on diversity and are seeking to increase the diversity within our community. Therefore we particularly encourage applications from under-represented groups, such as people from Black, Asian and minority ethnic groups and people with disabilities.

items.desc:
Job Title
Clinical Application Specialist – Cardiovascular & Radiology Informatics 
 Job Description
 Clinical Application Specialist – Cardiovascular & Radiology Informatics 
 As a Clinical Application Specialist, you will contribute to the research and development of Philips’ IntelliSpace Cardiovascular reporting and diagnostic software by translating clinical cardiology workflows and customer insights into innovative informatics solutions. You will also support the Radiology Informatics portfolio, collaborating with clinical experts and R&D teams to enhance imaging workflows and improve patient care.
 Your role: 
 You will help shape clinical features that enhance cardiology reporting, diagnosis and workflow efficiency for IntelliSpace Cardiovascular customers globally, contributing to informatics solutions used by more than 5,000 customers worldwide. You will serve as a clinical expert across the Cardiology and Radiology Informatics product portfolio, working with global R&D teams to define, refine and validate clinical requirements.
 You are part of the Cardiovascular Informatics Clinical Excellence team within Philips’ Enterprise Informatics business group in Eindhoven, working closely with global ISCV customers, clinical application specialists, and R&D teams based in Eindhoven, Bangalore and Blumenau. You will represent the voice of the clinician throughout the product development lifecycle and build strong relationships with customers, validation sites and key clinical stakeholders.
 This role gives you the opportunity to collaborate with customers and multi-disciplinary teams, co-create innovative clinical informatics applications, lead clinical validation and testing activities, train field specialists and customers, and stay connected to the latest developments in cardiology imaging and healthcare IT. You will also provide clinical guidance across radiology imaging and informatics workflows.
 You will translate customer, product management and marketing needs into clear clinical requirements that guide software development, verification and product releases.
 You will lead and support clinical validation, expert testing, defect classification, risk assessments, complaint analysis and product quality initiatives.
 You will support the Clinical Affairs/Medical Office in planning and executing clinical collaborations and studies, including protocol development, data collection and analysis, while ensuring robust scientific methodologies.
 You're the right fit if: 
 You hold a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Radiology, Echocardiography, Cardiac Care Technology, Biomedical Engineering, Ultrasound, or a comparable discipline, or a Medical Degree with a radiology or cardiology specialization.
 You bring 7+ years of hands-on experience in radiology, with strong knowledge of cardiovascular imaging workflows and clinical practice.
 You can understand, convey and teach clinical workflows in cardiology specialties, translate clinical requirements from customers, product management and marketing into technical input for engineering teams, and confidently bridge clinical and technical conversations. You also have experience translating clinical requirements into product requirements, conducting clinical validation and defect assessment, collaborating with customers, and working across multidisciplinary software development teams.
 You have a strong understanding of radiology, particularly cardiology specialties, and diagnostic modalities such as echocardiography, X-ray angiography, electrocardiography (ECG), computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or related cardiovascular workflows.
 You are customer-centric, highly flexible and self-driven, and thrive in a collaborative international environment.
 You possess excellent communication skills and the ability to build strong internal and external relationships.
 You are fluent in English (verbal and written).
 You have the willingness to travel globally up to 15% of your time.
 Preferred: 
 Experience with Philips solutions such as IntelliSpace Radiology/ISPACS, Vue PACS, IntelliSpace Cardiovascular, Xcelera, Cardiovascular Information System (CVIS), XperIM, or Philips Ultrasound Workspace.
 Familiarity with Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS), Vendor Neutral Archive (VNA), Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM), Health Level Seven (HL7), Healthcare Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) standards, and Agile software development methodologies is preferred.
 Experience participating in or managing clinical studies or serving as an author or co-author of related documentation and publications, is preferred.

Location: Bristol, UK
 Start date: September 2027 
 Application deadline: Midnight, 29th November 2026 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 
 The Graduate Programme at Graphcore 
 Join Graphcore in a permanent role and start your career with two years of hands-on learning. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, share your ideas and help shape what we’re creating. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are. 
 What you’ll work on 
 Turn the models you’ve studied into AI systems that run at scale. 
 In Applied AI, you’ll help implement, train and optimise advanced models on Graphcore’s next generation hardware, connecting research ideas with systems running across thousands of accelerators. 
 You’ll benchmark models, use profiling to find performance bottlenecks, design experiments and contribute fixes across models, software and accelerator systems. 
 Working with Research, Software and Product teams, you’ll test ideas that could inform future hardware. Your experiments will help us understand what makes a model accurate, efficient and ready to scale. 
 Your team and support 
 The Applied AI team acts as a proxy for Graphcore’s customers. We understand current AI models, applications and software, then make sure Graphcore technology works at scale. You’ll work alongside people who write low-level kernels, train large language models and enjoy figuring out challenging AI problems together. 
 Work spans low-level kernel optimisation through to implementing research-level algorithms for new AI models. Engineers move between experiments, profiling, code reviews and technical debate – giving you a view of how different parts of an AI system fit together. 
 Decisions are driven by evidence, performance data and clear engineering judgement. You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and share ideas for making things better. Take responsibility for your work and speak up when you spot a problem or need support. 
 How you’ll learn and grow 
 During the two-year programme, you’ll build technical range through hands-on work across AI models and accelerator systems. 
 With visibility across the full stack – from novel accelerator hardware and its software stack to state-of-the-art AI applications – you’ll identify opportunities to innovate and differentiate Graphcore’s technology. 
 What we’re looking for 
 Bachelor/Master's degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Maths, Data Science, or related field 
 Software development skills and proficiency with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX 
 An understanding of deep learning architectures, optimisation, evaluation and scaling, with the ability to design, run and explain ML experiments 
 A collaborative approach and willingness to work through unfamiliar technical problems, ask questions and take responsibility 
 You can demonstrate these skills through coursework, a dissertation, personal or team projects, research, or other relevant experience. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned. 
 Benefits
 Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
 Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
 Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
 Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
 Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones
 Electric Vehicle Scheme: Choose an electric vehicle and lease it through salary sacrifice
 Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover
 Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.
 Sponsorship
 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.
 Introduction to Graphcore
 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: from semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds …

 What you’ll work on 
 Put your software skills to work testing how AI and machine learning workloads run on Graphcore accelerator hardware. 
 As a Graduate Software Engineer in AI/ML Test Systems, you’ll create representative machine learning workloads and analyse their numerical accuracy and performance. You’ll design tests and help improve testing strategies and infrastructure across simulated and physical hardware. 
 You’ll also build continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, investigate difficult problems and turn your findings into measurable improvements. Your work will connect machine learning frameworks and models with the hardware beneath them, helping improve software quality and customer experience. 
 Your team and support 
 The Software QA team combines software engineering, automation and data analysis to improve product quality and customer experience. We work extensively with industry-standard machine learning frameworks and models, including contributions to upstream open-source projects. 
 Our team works in small squads, each with ownership of a particular area of software quality. As a graduate, you’ll have the opportunity to explore the breadth of our work, gain practical experience across different areas and discover what interests you before settling into a squad. 
 You’ll work alongside engineers who investigate problems, share findings and collaborate closely with development teams to improve quality, security and maintainability. Test results, performance data and the needs of the wider software organisation guide our decisions. 
 You’ll have a buddy to help you find your feet and a manager who will support your development, explore your career goals with you and help make time for learning. You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and take initiative, with experienced colleagues to turn to for guidance as you build confidence and take ownership of your work.

 Creating workloads and analysing results will help you understand how software behaves on accelerator hardware. Debugging issues will develop your problem-solving skills and help you connect numerical accuracy and performance to the systems running a model. 
 Work on test infrastructure and CI/CD will show you how automated checks support software development across simulated and physical platforms. Sharing findings with development teams will help you explain technical problems clearly and turn evidence into improvements.

items.desc:
Overview 
 Microsoft AI is looking for Researchers and Research Engineers to join our Pre-training Data team and help train the world’s most capable AI frontier models, pushing the boundaries of scale, performance and product deployment. The Pre-Training team at Microsoft AI tackles some of the most challenging problems in deep learning at scale. As a team, we will deliver one of the best foundation models in the world, forming the foundation of many initiatives across Microsoft AI.
In this role, you’ll work at the intersection of data and innovation, collaborating with scientists, engineers, and annotators to curate, analyze, and evaluate diverse and large-scale data sources critical to model development. You will lead efforts to:
 Design and curate high-quality datasets to power frontier AI models.
 Develop novel data collection strategies.
 Improve dataset quality and integrity.
 Understand data-driven model behaviors.
 Align datasets with ethical and societal values.
 This is a cross-disciplinary, high-impact role ideal for engineers who want to push the boundaries of what AI can learn from data. Our focus is on research and engineering that improves the models and products we ship. Academic publishing is not a priority for this role.
 Responsibilities 
 Create high-quality datasets for training and evaluation; run experiments on new datasets (data ablations) to assess their impact and determine the most effective data.
 Develop and maintain scalable data pipelines for ingestion, processing, filtering, and annotation.
 Analyze real-world datasets to assess quality, diversity, relevance, and identify areas for improvement.
 Build lightweight tools and workflows for dataset auditing, visualization, and versioning.
 Collaborate with Safety, Ethics, and Governance teams to ensure datasets meet standards for quality, privacy, and responsible AI practices. 
 Qualifications 
 Required Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's Degree in AI, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, or related technical discipline AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, Python and common data libraries (Pandas, NumPy, etc.)
 OR equivalent experience.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's Degree in AI, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, or related technical discipline AND 10+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, Python and common data libraries (Pandas, NumPy, etc.)
 OR Master's Degree in AI, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, or related technical discipline AND 8+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, Python and common data libraries (Pandas, NumPy, etc.)
 OR equivalent experience.
 2+ years of experience in data analysis or data engineering, including work with large-scale datasets that are unstructured or semi-structured.
 Proficiency in statistics and exploratory data analysis methods.
 Familiarity with data processing frameworks such as Spark, Ray, or Apache Beam.
 Ability to communicate technical findings clearly to research and product teams.
