items.desc: Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? The department of clinical science and education, Södersjukhuset (KI SÖS), is characterized by medical research that is closely integrated with clinical practice. Our location at one of Stockholm's major emergency hospitals provides excellent opportunities to investigate clinically relevant research questions through collaboration between researchers and healthcare professionals. The department is now looking for a statistician to join Gianluigi Savarese’s research group. Here, you will have the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary academic environment, develop your expertise, and contribute to research that has the potential to improve healthcare. Your mission As a statistician, you will be part of the heart failure and arrhythmia research group. The group focuses on heart failure, arrhythmias, and related cardiovascular diseases. We use large clinical registries, linked national health data registries, electronic health records, and clinical trials to study patient outcomes, treatment effectiveness, the implementation of evidence-based care, and the epidemiology of these diseases. Working closely with clinical researchers, doctoral students, and international collaborators, you will contribute to the entire research process, from study design to scientific publication. Your responsibilities will include: Develop study designs and statistical analysis plans in collaboration with the research group. Apply for access to data from quality registries and administrative registers. Process, manage, and validate large datasets, including data from the Swedish heart failure registry (RiksSvikt/SwedeHF) linked to other national registers. Independently conduct statistical analyses, including survival analysis, longitudinal modelling, competing risk analysis, propensity score methods, methods for handling missing data, machine learning and AI, as well as target trial emulation using the clone-censor-weight approach. Contribute to scientific manuscripts and research grant applications. Provide statistical guidance and support to doctoral students and other researchers, and ensure well-documented and reproducible analytical workflows. Serve as the point of contact between the research group and KI's IT department to coordinate the management and resolution of IT-related issues concerning research servers, virtual machines, and associated IT infrastructure. Participate in all activities of the research group. Additional responsibilities may be assigned depending on the development of the research group and your expertise. Your profile We are looking for a candidate with a master's degree in statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology, or a related quantitative field. You have extensive and documented experience in applying for access to data from quality registries and administrative registers, as well as in extracting, managing, and analyzing large registry-based datasets and data from electronic health records. Your expertise includes pharmacoepidemiology, studies of treatment effectiveness and safety, survival analysis, longitudinal analyses, and the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence. A good understanding of the Swedish healthcare system is required to ensure the correct interpretation of extracted data. Furthermore, you have good proficiency in both R and Stata. As a person, you are structured and detail-oriented, with the ability to work independently. You enjoy sharing your expertise and are able to provide guidance and support to doctoral students and other researchers in a clear and pedagogical manner. You have strong collaboration skills, are flexible, and are able to adapt to varying needs and priorities within a large international research group. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment with wide-ranging expertise and interests. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. Karolinska Institutet is also a state university, which entitles you to several good benefits through our collective agreement. And you get to practice freely in our modern wellness facilities, where trained staff are on site. items.desc: Are you ready to shape the future of neurodegenerative disease therapeutics? Our mission is to discover and develop a novel class of disease-modifying small molecule and RNAi therapeutics using the latest in artificial intelligence, deep learning, and multiomics technologies. What You’ll Do Be part of a team discovering, validating and optimising next-generation therapeutics, enabling real-world impact on drug discovery for Alzheimer's and other neurodegenerative conditions. Collaborate daily with top drug discovery and AI specialists: brainstorm, troubleshoot, and innovate together. Present findings and shape our scientific direction in regular internal and external meetings. Champion data integrity, safety, and operational excellence in our dynamic laboratory setting. About You You’re passionate, driven, and hardworking, and would thrive in a dynamic startup environment at the intersection of science and technology. PhD (or Master’s plus experience) in biochemistry, cell biology, or a related discipline, with optional postdoctoral or pharma/biotech/startup laboratory experience. Ready to work independently and in collaborative multidisciplinary teams, sharing results and ideas with confidence. items.desc: What we are building We are a local-first desktop application that understands what happens on a screen. It observes real work as it unfolds, including the tools, the actions, and the sequence, and turns raw screen and video into structured, machine-readable representations of the underlying process. The payoff is broad. Once a system can reliably parse arbitrary on-screen activity, that understanding feeds anything downstream: documentation, automation, analytics, and AI agents that can finally act on workflows no one ever wrote down. We are building the layer that makes screens legible. (We are early and still mostly heads-down, so our page here is intentionally sparse. The full picture, meaning team, traction, and product, we are glad to share directly.) The technical problem The hard part is vision, and it is genuinely hard. Every environment runs on a different, messy stack of interfaces, so there is no clean API to integrate against. The only universal signal is the pixels themselves. That means learning to understand and segment what happens on screens and in video directly: parsing layout and state, detecting and segmenting the relevant regions and objects, recognizing actions and intent, and reasoning over long, noisy temporal sequences to find where one meaningful step ends and the next begins. Generic OCR and brittle per-app scripts fall apart here. Visual Language Models, combined with strong segmentation and temporal grounding, are the path forward. Building that layer well, meaning accurate, fast, and privacy-preserving on the user’s own device, is the core technical bet of the company. We have a working proof of concept and real users in sight. Your job is to take the vision core from there to production, and to own it as it scales. What you’ll do Own the CV/VLM core end to end, from raw screen and video capture to a semantic understanding of what is happening and why Build, fine-tune, and evaluate VLM and segmentation pipelines: spatial grounding, action and intent recognition, and temporal segmentation over long, noisy interaction sequences Make it run where it matters: on-device inference under real latency and resource constraints, built privacy-by-design and GDPR-native from the ground up. This is a hard constraint, and shaping the right approach to it is part of the role Define how we measure quality, including the benchmarks, failure cases, and standards that keep the vision layer honest as we scale Set the technical direction for vision and help shape the engineering team and roadmap as we grow Who we’re looking for Senior or staff level computer vision engineer or researcher with genuine VLM and multimodal depth, from research or production Hands-on experience across the vision stack: segmentation, detection, video understanding, and modern VLM architectures You have shipped models into real products, not just notebooks, and you care about what happens after the demo: evaluation, edge cases, inference cost, maintainability You think in systems, not tickets. You want to own architecture, set the bar, and make the hard calls early You want the weight and the upside of a founding role, and you are ready to build in Munich (EU) Why now, why us This is a true founding seat. The founding team brings experience from SAP, Celonis, Tacto, and Enpal, so we know enterprise software, process intelligence, and how to go to market, and we are building at exactly the moment VLMs are becoming good enough to make this possible. We are backed and supported by one of the most renowned labs for software and AI, which gives us the technical network, infrastructure, and credibility of an institution most startups never get access to at this stage. Your salary is secured through state startup funding, so you get founding-level ownership and meaningful equity with real runway behind it, rather than a race against the next raise. Concrete numbers we are happy to discuss early and openly. We strongly encourage everyone to apply, especially women and underrepresented candidates, even if you do not meet every requirement on this list. This is the vision core of the company, and we are hiring the person who will own it. If that is the kind of problem you want to spend the next years on, we would love to talk.

It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries. Look At The BSC Experience BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic research engineer to join the Atmospheric Composition (AC) group within the Earth Sciences department at the BSC-CNS. The AC group is currently composed of about 50 people among researchers, engineers and students of different nationalities. It aims at better understanding and predicting the spatio-temporal variations of atmospheric pollutants along with their effects upon air quality, weather and climate. This is addressed through the continuous development and application of numerical models over multiple scales, from weather to climate and from global to urban scales. The AC group develops and maintains its own forecast model MONARCH, which is a coupled meteorological-chemistry model that can be run at global and regional scales to simulate gaseous chemistry and aerosols plus their feedbacks on radiation. MONARCH is also coupled to a data assimilation scheme for gases and aerosols that is used to initialize forecasts or produce reanalyses of the atmospheric composition. The AC group operates several operational forecasting systems in the framework of the World Meteorological Organization Sand and Dust Storm Advisory System (SDS-WAS, ), the Copernicus atmospheric monitoring services (CAMS, ), the Spanish air quality forecasting system CALIOPE (), and the International Cooperative for Aerosols Predictions (ICAP). The successful candidate will join the Data Assimilation Forecasting and Application team of the AC group and will play a key coordinating role in the production and continuous improvement of the team's operational forecasting and reanalysis systems. The activities will be carried out mainly in the framework of the Copernicus CAMS2_40bis international project, with contributions to the CAMS2_82bis project and to the activities of the Barcelona Dust Regional Center (BDRC). The candidate will work in a highly collaborative environment, with tight links with researchers and engineers in the AC group. The candidate will have the opportunity to follow multiple training activities, including those aimed at improving coding and data analysis, project writing abilities, or project management. All this will be implemented via the formal courses organized by the Education and Training team and Human Resources, and the participation in the regular seminars organized by the department. Coordinate the preparation and timely delivery of project deliverables, and represent the team in international project meetings. Coordinate the upgrades of the production systems: define and evaluate target model configurations, organize the e-suite experiments, and ensure successful operational deployments. items.desc: 20.10.2026, Academic staff The Chair of Complex Soft Matter at the TUM School of Life Sciences is seeking to appoint a Research Associate – Multivalent Colloid Science (E13, with the opportunity to pursue a doctorate) at the earliest possible date. The position addresses challenges in medicine/diagnostics, focusing on the design of supramolecular architectures, their advanced physicochemical characterization and relative biological activity. About Us: The Technical University of Munich (TUM) is one of Europe’s leading academic institutions. At the TUM School of Life Sciences, Prof. Stefan Guldin recently established the Chair of Complex Soft Matter. We deploy molecular self-assembly to create bio-inspired, bio-derived and bio-integrated materials for life science applications. Our research focuses on understanding and controlling the formation and interactions of soft materials at the nanoscale, using building blocks including polymers, biomolecules, vesicles and nanoparticles to engineer colloidal systems and interfaces with targeted functionality and selective molecular recognition. We combine synthesis and advanced characterisation with automated experimentation and data-driven materials design. Current activities include multivalent nanoparticles for selective recognition of biological targets, nanostructured biosensing interfaces for extracellular vesicle detection, and the investigation of protein interactions at functional biointerfaces. Your Responsibilities: Contribute to the recently awarded ERC Consolidator Grant project “Engineering Multivalency for Superselective Recognition of Pathogen Targets” (EngToTarget), combining experimental chemistry with automated experimentation and data-driven materials design for life science applications”. Conducts research on the synthesis, surface functionalisation and characterisation of colloidal nanoparticles and their interactions with biological targets, including in complex biological environments. The aim is to understand how self-assembly and consequent molecular architecture govern multivalent interactions and selective biomolecular recognition. Perform high-throughput, automated synthesis, surface functionalization, and characterization of multivalent colloidal nanoparticles. Investigate interactions with biological targets, including selective binding, competitive interactions and nonspecific adsorption in complex biological environments Establish relationships between molecular architecture, ligand organisation and biomolecular recognition Develop reproducible experimental workflows and contribute to automated experimentation and data-driven optimization Analyse and interpret experimental data and document protocols and research findings Collaborate with researchers across chemistry, materials science, life sciences and computational disciplines Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations and dissemination activities Contribute to teaching and practical courses and support the supervision of bachelor’s and master’s research projects Your Profile: Master’s degree or equivalent in chemistry, materials science, nanoscience, chemical engineering, or a related discipline Experimental research experience in synthetic chemistry, colloid science, soft matter, or functional nanomaterials Experience with ligand synthesis, nanoparticle synthesis or surface functionalisation is advantageous Familiarity with relevant characterisation techniques, such as NMR, mass spectrometry, light scattering, UV-vis or fluorescence spectroscopy, is beneficial Interest in multivalent interactions, molecular self-assembly and selective recognition of biological targets Enthusiasm for automated experimentation and data-driven materials design; experience with quantitative data analysis or scientific programming is advantageous Strong problem-solving abilities, careful experimental practice and motivation to pursue a doctorate in an interdisciplinary research environment Ability to work independently and collaboratively within an international team Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English What We Offer: The opportunity to pursue a doctorate at the Technical University of Munich, one of Europe’s leading universities, within an ERC-funded project on multivalent colloid science and selective biomolecular recognition Participation in an interdisciplinary research programme combining synthetic chemistry, molecular self-assembly, biointerfaces, automated experimentation and data-driven materials design Access to state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure and advanced characterisation platforms Scientific freedom to develop ideas and shape your doctoral research, supported by close mentoring from the principal investigator and principal scientist Opportunities to publish your research, present at international conferences and collaborate with leading research groups A collaborative and supportive international team, with opportunities for teaching …

items.desc: Overview CHIMES² — the Centre for Heterogeneous Integrated MicroElectronic and Semiconductor Systems — is one of the UK’s national semiconductor research-translation programmes, a £16.3M Innovation and Knowledge Centre led by the University of Sheffield. We are appointing a Research and Innovation Fellow in Manufacturing Pathways, Test and Supply Chain to its CTO Office. This is not a conventional postdoctoral research post. Its core is landscape analysis and roadmap intelligence — reading the international state of the art in packaging, test and supply chain, identifying the gaps the UK must close, and turning that into the knowledge infrastructure a national programme runs on. A research theme of your own is developed alongside that work, not instead of it. This post focuses on the ‘ physical’ layer of heterogeneous integration — the realisation of system architecture into physical package configurations, assembly processes and manufacturable implementations. This spans back-end physical implementation (place-and-route, physical verification, DRC/LVS across heterogeneous stacks, timing closure under packaging parasitics), advanced packaging architecture selection (2.5D, 3D, hybrid bonding, fan-out), manufacturing pathway management, known-good-die test strategy, and the UK and global supply chain for heterogeneous integration. We are advertising two paired CTO Office posts in parallel: this post in Manufacturing Pathways, Test and Supply Chain (the physical layer) and a companion post in Systems Architecture and Design (the logical layer). The logical-to-physical handoff — where system partitioning decisions are handed from architectural intent to physical realisation — is the primary interface between the two posts, and both post holders are expected to develop working familiarity with each other’s domain. Candidates whose interests span both layers are welcome to apply for both; please indicate this in your cover letter. You will join the Microelectronics and Integrated Semiconductor Systems Team within the Quantum and Semiconductor Systems (QSS) Group — one of the UK’s largest and most successful semiconductor research environments. The Team hosts Sheffield’s leadership role for CHIMES², which brings together partner universities including Cambridge, Oxford, Edinburgh, Manchester, Newcastle, Strathclyde, Queen’s University Belfast and King’s College London, alongside the Science and Technology Facilities Council. Industrial partners include, among others, Imec, Arm, Pragmatic, Cadence, Synopsys and Siemens EDA. The CTO Office sits at the centre of the programme’s technical intelligence function; you will collaborate closely with the newly established CHIMES² engineering cohort, though the CTO Office and the engineering team are distinct functions. Why this role is distinctive. It is a national-programme intelligence role. You will lead landscape and roadmap work that directly shapes CHIMES² research priorities, demonstrator projects, and the Design Commons — work with reach across the UK ecosystem, not confined to a single lab. It is a deliberate platform to launch from. The post is designed to let you build a visible, fundable independent research identity and the track record to launch it — whether toward a research fellowship (RAEng, UKRI FLF, MSCA, ERC Starting), a first permanent academic appointment, or a senior role in the national semiconductor ecosystem. The four-year term gives genuine room to figure out which of those is right for you and to become competitive for it. You will be a named representative of CHIMES² externally — at IMAPS, IEEE ECTC, TechWorks DESN and equivalent forums — and a named author on Design Commons white papers, capability maps and policy briefings produced from your work. Areas Of Particular Interest For This Post Include: Advanced packaging architectures — 2.5D silicon interposer, 3D hybrid bonding, fan-out WLP/PLP, glass interposers — and their physical-design implications. Back-end EDA and physical implementation for multi-die stacks — place-and-route, cross-die DRC/LVS, packaging parasitics extraction, packaging-aware timing and signal/power-integrity sign-off. Known-good-die test methodology and its relationship to physical implementation; reliability, qualification and manufacturing yield. The UK and global supply chain for HI — OSAT and foundry pathways, compound-semiconductor assembly and its interface with silicon back-end processes. Sustainability, lifecycle assessment and embodied-carbon modelling applied to packaging and assembly. All four cross-cutting constraints — design-for-test (DfT), design-for-power-delivery (DfP), design-for-security (DfS) and design-for-thermal-extraction (DfTh) — span the logical-physical boundary, and both post holders are expected to develop working familiarity with them regardless of primary domain. No candidate need span all areas. Strong credibility in one area of advanced packaging, semiconductor test, back-end physical …

items.desc: Inżynier Danych (Data Engineer) Inżynier Danych będzie odgrywać kluczową rolę w tworzeniu i rozwoju fundamentów danych, mocy obliczeniowej oraz rozwiązań inżynieryjnych dla naszych platform opartych na dużych modelach językowych (LLM). Kluczowe obowiązki Wspieranie działań z zakresu inżynierii danych dla inicjatyw związanych z LLM, w tym wdrażanie i transformacja dużych zbiorów danych medycznych na potrzeby trenowania i oceny modeli. Projektowanie, ocena i rozwój procesów transformacji danych w środowiskach Snowflake i AWS, w tym analiza wydajności istniejących procesów badawczych pod kątem wdrożenia na skalę produkcyjną. Zapewnianie dostępności danych oraz migracji do wysokowydajnych środowisk obliczeniowych, gwarantując łatwy dostęp do danych, ich wysoką wydajność oraz kontrolę wersji dla zespołów modelowania. Wdrażanie mechanizmów śledzenia pochodzenia danych (data lineage), wersjonowania oraz zarządzania referencjami do zbiorów danych w celu zapewnienia powtarzalności i identyfikowalności procesów trenowania oraz oceny modeli. Współpraca z zespołami modelowania, MLOps i infrastruktury w zakresie wspierania cyklu życia modeli, w tym integracji z procesami ewaluacji i rejestrami modeli. Praktyczna znajomość Snowflake/Snowpark, usług danych AWS oraz pracy z dużymi zbiorami danych. Doświadczenie we wspieraniu środowisk ML/AI, w tym budowie i utrzymaniu potoków danych wykorzystywanych do trenowania i oceny modeli. Dlaczego warto do nas dołączyć? items.desc: Introductie Help jij ons om complexe machine learning modellen naar productie te brengen en op schaal te laten draaien voor ruim 5 miljoen ANWB-leden? Als Machine Learning Engineer werk je aan innovatieve data-gedreven oplossingen die direct bijdragen aan onze marketing- en klantinteractieprocessen. Denk hierbij aan personalisatie, next-best-action modellen, klantsegmentatie, churn voorspelling en campagne-optimalisatie. In deze rol ligt de focus vooral op het ontwikkelen, implementeren en operationaliseren van concrete ML-use cases, terwijl je daarnaast een bijdrage levert aan de verdere ontwikkeling van ons machine learning platform. Jouw rol Waar ga je aan werken? Als Machine Learning Engineer ben je verantwoordelijk voor het vertalen van data science oplossingen naar robuuste, schaalbare systemen die in productie kunnen draaien. Je speelt een cruciale rol in het overbruggen van de kloof tussen experimentele modellen en waardevolle bedrijfsoplossingen. Wat ga je doen: Modellen productiewaardig maken Bouwen van schaalbare ML-pijplijnen Reviewen van code en ondersteunen bij het omzetten van experimentele oplossingen naar productiewaardige, geteste en onderhoudbare software Implementeren van monitoring, logging en alerting voor modellen in productie Zorgen voor efficiënte model serving strategieën samenwerken met data Scientists Adviseren over best practices voor reproduceerbare en productiegerichte code Meedenken over model-architectuur vanuit een engineering perspectief Gezamenlijk oplossen van technische uitdagingen MLOps platform ontwikkelen Bijdragen aan de verbetering van ons MLOps platform Automatiseren van herhalende processen in de ML lifecycle Ons aanbod Wat bieden wij? Miljoenen gebruikers, geweldige werkcultuur, ruimte voor persoonlijke groei, en..... Een maandsalaris tussen de € 4.136,- en € 6.667,- op basis van 38 uur en een eindejaarsuitkering van 5,58%; Volledige vergoeding van de kosten voor woon-werkverkeer met het openbaar vervoer; ANWB-lidmaatschap en Wegenwacht-abonnement in Nederland voor auto of fiets; 25 vakantiedagen en 13 dagen kortere werktijdenregeling (ADV) bij een voltijds contract 40 uur); Uitgebreide opleidings-, trainings- en persoonlijke ontwikkelingsmogelijkheden via onze ANWB Academy; Diverse optionele collectieve regelingen met spannende kortingen op en arrangementen op alle ANWB producten en diensten; Goede voorzieningen voor thuiswerken en een thuiswerktoeslag van € 2,45 euro per dag (onbelast) – ANWB bevordert hybride werken; Persoonlijk ontwikkelingsbudget van € 700,- per jaar ter bevordering van jouw vitaliteit, vaardigheden, carrière, betrokkenheid en balans tussen werk en privé. Ons team Waar werk je in de organisatie? Waar denk jij aan als je aan ANWB denkt? Grote kans dat je aan de Wegenwacht denkt. Dat klopt! Toch doen we veel meer. Wij zijn een vereniging die ook producten verkoopt in onze winkels, maatschappelijk relevante projecten realiseert, verzekeringen biedt, reizen voor onze leden organiseert, energieleverancier en nog veel meer. Dat maakt ANWB een veelzijdige werkgever met verschillende expertises onder één dak en waarbij maatschappelijke impact vooropstaat. Al deze producten en diensten genereren veel data die we binnen het Marketing Data Science (MDS) gebruiken om zo relevant mogelijk voor onze leden te zijn en onze marketingactiviteiten te optimaliseren. Jij wordt onderdeel van dit team. Je werkt in een team van Data Scientists en Machine Learning Engineers. Als Machine Learning Engineer vorm je de brug tussen Data Science en productie, waarbij je nauw samenwerkt met zowel Data Scientists, Data Engineers en MLOps Engineers. Je zorgt ervoor dat modellen schaalbaar, betrouwbaar en reproduceerbaar in productie worden gebracht en draagt actief bij aan de doorontwikkeling van ons MLOps-platform. Als achtergrond neem jij mee Hebben wij een match? Je bent een technisch talent met passie voor het bouwen van robuuste ML-systemen! Je combineert software engineering expertise met kennis van machine learning en maakt graag de vertaalslag van experiment naar productie. Als achtergrond neem je verder mee: Afgeronde WO opleiding in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science of vergelijkbare richting 2-5 jaar ervaring met het bouwen van production-grade machine learning systemen Uitstekende programmeervaardigheden in Python, inclusief ervaring met software development best practices zoals testing, versioning en code reviews Grondige kennis van ML frameworks (zoals TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn) en begrip van fundamentele ML-concepten Ervaring met een groot cloud platform (wij werken met AWS) Bekend met containerization (Docker) Ervaring met CI/CD pipelines en MLOps principes Basiskennis van data engineering-concepten (data pipelines, ETL processen) Goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal

Role Overview ONVO is looking for a highly skilled AI Visualization & Video Design Specialist to push the boundaries of automotive design visualization through advanced AI technologies, cinematic storytelling, and high-quality video production. Based in the ONVO Munich Design Studio, The ideal candidate combines a strong automotive design sensibility with exceptional visualization skills, an experimental mindset, and deep expertise in AI-powered image and video generation. items.desc:
Scientific Assistant – Biomedical Data Science & Spinal Cord Injury Research 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Scientific Assistant – Biomedical Data Science & Spinal Cord Injury Research
 80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The Biomedical Data Science Lab investigates data-driven solutions for healthcare applications with a focus on neurological conditions and systemic infections such as sepsis. At the core of our research is the collaboration across disciplines spanning expertise in medicine, biology, computer, and data science. We seek a motivated scientific assistant to join this growing team and contribute to interdisciplinary research partnerships. 
 Project background
 The Biomedical Data Science Lab at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Scientific Assistant to support our data-intensive projects in biomedical imaging and clinical research. This position offers an excellent opportunity to work at the forefront of biomedical data science, contributing to key projects including data curation, image segmentation, and tool development for clinical research applications. The scientific assistant will support the Biomedical Data Science Team for a range of application projects, with a particular focus on our work in pediatric sepsis, lower back pain, and pediatric neurooncology.
 Job description
 We are looking for a Scientific Assistant with a strong background in statistics, machine learning, and biomedical data science to support our research using the European Multicenter Study about Spinal Cord Injury (EMSCI) and related SCI databases.
 The position combines hands-on data analysis and scientific project support with the coordination of scientific activities within our research network. The successful candidate will work closely with researchers, clinicians, and international collaborators to analyse large-scale longitudinal SCI datasets and contribute to scientific publications and meetings.
 Your key responsibilities will include:
 Conduct statistical and machine-learning analyses using EMSCI and related SCI datasets.
 Develop and validate predictive models of neurological recovery and functional outcomes after SCI.
 Perform data preprocessing, quality control, harmonisation, feature engineering, and exploratory data analysis.
 Apply appropriate statistical methods, including regression, longitudinal data analysis, survival analysis, and machine-learning approaches.
 Develop reproducible analytical workflows in R and/or Python.
 Contribute to scientific publications, reports, presentations, and grant applications.
 Collaborate with clinicians, neuroscientists, statisticians, and data scientists across participating SCI centres.
 Support the organisation and coordination of scientific meetings, workshops, consortium meetings, and other research activities, including scheduling, preparation of agendas and materials, communication with participants, and follow-up.
 Assist with the coordination of ongoing collaborative projects and follow-up of scientific activities and deliverables.
 Profile
 MSc or equivalent degree in statistics, biostatistics, data science, biomedical engineering, computer science, epidemiology, neuroscience, or a related discipline.
 Strong background in statistics and/or machine learning.
 Experience working with longitudinal and/or clinical datasets.
 Strong programming skills in R and/or Python.
 Experience with statistical modelling, data visualisation, and reproducible research.
 Familiarity with machine-learning methods such as random forests, gradient boosting, neural networks, or related approaches.
 Previous experience working with EMSCI data or other large SCI databases is highly desirable.
 Knowledge of SCI-specific clinical and neurological outcome measures (e.g., ISNCSCI/ASIA, SCIM) is an advantage.
 Experience working with multicentre clinical datasets is an advantage.
 Fluent in English and proficient in German, both written and spoken.
 Excellent organisational and communication skills.
 Ability to work independently and reliably while collaborating effectively in a multidisciplinary and international research environment.
 Interest in SCI research and the application of data science to clinical research.
 Workplace
 Workplace
 We offer
 An 80–100% position within the Biomedical Data Science Lab at ETH Zurich.
 The opportunity to work with EMSCI, one of the major longitudinal SCI research databases, and related international datasets.
 A highly interdisciplinary environment at the interface of clinical neuroscience, statistics, machine learning, and biomedical data science.
 Close interaction with leading SCI researchers and clinical centres in Switzerland and internationally.
 The opportunity to contribute to high-quality scientific publications and international collaborative projects.
 A varied role combining hands-on quantitative research with scientific coordination and project management.

items.desc: Service de statistique (STAT) Le STAT constitue le pôle cantonal en matière de science des données et d'intelligence artificielle. Ses principales missions consistent notamment à fournir aux autorités cantonales et communales ainsi qu'à la collectivité des informations statistiques pertinentes, significatives, fiables et cohérentes. Il collecte, produit, traite, analyse et stocke des données à but statistique sur la base de principes scientifiques choisis en toute indépendance, dans le respect de la charte de la statistique publique suisse. Vos missions En tant qu'expert·e IA, vous collaborez étroitement avec la déléguée cantonale à l'IA et êtes en charge de projets liés à l’intelligence artificielle et à la science des données. Dans ce cadre, vous réalisez des analyses avancées dans divers domaines (santé publique, finance, marché du travail, etc.). Vous développez et mettez en œuvre des solutions innovantes en matière de machine learning, deep learning et d'IA générative pour valoriser les données statistiques et soutenir la prise de décision. De plus, vous assurez la préparation et l’exploitation de grandes bases de données, tout en participant à la création et à la diffusion de formations relatives à l’IA au sein de l’administration cantonale et de ses partenaires. Dans l'exercice de vos missions, vous collaborez activement avec les services de l’État, les communes et le système statistique suisse. Enfin, vous documentez vos travaux, proposez des pistes d’amélioration et contribuez à la valorisation et à la diffusion des données statistiques du canton. Votre profil Titulaire d’un master universitaire ou d’un diplôme jugé équivalent en intelligence artificielle, science des données, mathématiques, physique ou informatique, vous justifiez d’une expérience professionnelle de 3 ans minimum dans les domaines de l’IA et de la science des données. Un doctorat dans l'un de ces domaines constitue un atout. Vous disposez de solides compétences en planification et gestion de projets complexes et multidisciplinaires. Sur le plan technique, vous maîtrisez parfaitement les langages (Python, R) et outils (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn) liés au machine learning, à l’analyse de données (Pandas, NumPy, RStudio, Tableau+) et aux bases de données (PostgreSQL, SQL Server). À cela s'ajoute, une maîtrise de la mise en place de RAGs et l'implémentation d'agents IA. Vous attestez également de bonnes connaissances du fonctionnement des institutions politiques et administratives ainsi que des missions de la statistique publique. Par ailleurs, vous possédez de bonnes connaissances en anglais et allemand. Enfin, votre profil se distingue par un esprit d’initiative, une grande rigueur organisationnelle, une réelle aisance relationnelle et un respect absolu de la confidentialité. Nous vous offrons pour ce poste D’intégrer une équipe dynamique, accueillante et bienveillante. Un poste à responsabilités, varié et motivant, dans un cadre prônant l'innovation. Une organisation de travail flexible dans un environnement moderne et ouvert aux nouvelles idées. Lieu de travail : Neuchâtel Début d’activité : 1er janvier 2027 ou à convenir Délai de postulation : 25 octobre 2026 Salaire : Classe 11 Renseignements complémentaires : M. Olivier Berthoud, chef de service adjoint, tél. 032 889 46 28 Les postulations féminines sont vivement encouragées pour les fonctions supérieures. Nous défendons l’égalité des chances et l’inclusion, les candidatures de personnes de tous horizons et vivant avec un handicap sont les bienvenues.

Présenter et vulgariser les résultats des analyses auprès des différentes parties prenantes afin de faciliter la prise de décision. items.desc: Introduction At Burberry, we believe creativity opens spaces. Our purpose is to unlock the power of imagination to push boundaries and open new possibilities for our people, our customers and our communities. This is the core belief that has guided Burberry since it was founded in 1856 and is central to how we operate as a company today. We aim to provide an environment for creative minds from different backgrounds to thrive, bringing a wide range of skills and experiences to everything we do. As a purposeful, values-driven brand, we are committed to being a force for good in the world as well, creating the next generation of sustainable luxury for customers, driving industry change and championing our communities. Job Purpose The Customer Data Science team at Burberry is looking for an early-career Data Scientist to help create more relevant and personalised experiences across every customer touchpoint. This role is well suited to someone with master's-level knowledge or approximately one year of relevant experience who is ready to apply statistical modelling, machine learning and emerging AI techniques to meaningful business challenges. Working with data scientists, engineers and cross-functional stakeholders, you will build scalable solutions that deepen our understanding of customer behaviour, preferences, purchase intent and response to marketing activity. Your work will contribute to areas including propensity and causal modelling, product recommendations, discovery algorithms and client relationship intelligence. Responsibilities Develop robust statistical models, machine learning solutions and data-driven tools that support customer and business objectives. Explore and prepare new data sources, assess data quality and create relevant features for modelling and analysis. Apply techniques including propensity modelling, causal inference and experimentation to understand customer behaviour and measure the impact of customer outreach. Contribute to product recommendation, discovery and client relationship solutions that create more relevant customer experiences. Collaborate with data scientists and engineers to build scalable, reliable and production-ready solutions. Monitor and evaluate models in production, using technical and business measures to identify opportunities for improvement. Optimise existing models and analytics solutions through a structured test-and-learn approach. Translate business questions into clear analytical frameworks, methodologies and practical solutions. Generate reliable insights and recommendations that inform strategic and operational decisions. Present analytical methods, findings and limitations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Identify opportunities to improve models, processes and ways of working across the team. Explore relevant developments in data science and AI, applying new technologies where they can deliver meaningful value. Personal Profile A master's degree or PhD in a quantitative discipline, such as Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Physics or Engineering, or equivalent technical knowledge. Master's-level project, placement or internship experience, or approximately one year of relevant experience in data science or a closely related role. Experience applying statistical analysis, machine learning or data science techniques to practical problems in an academic or commercial setting. A sound understanding of mathematics, statistics, experimental design and model evaluation. Practical experience developing, testing and interpreting statistical or machine learning models. Exposure to one or more specialist areas, such as time series, recommendation systems, customer journey modelling, causal inference, deep learning or large language models. A solid programming foundation, with practical experience using Python and SQL. Familiarity with relevant libraries and technologies such as Pandas or PySpark would be advantageous. An understanding of collaborative development practices, including version control tools such as Git. Exposure to Python packaging tools such as Poetry would be welcomed but is not essential. A logical and considered approach to problem-solving, with the curiosity to explore new analytical methods. The ability to translate business requirements into structured analytical questions and practical approaches. A collaborative working style and the ability to contribute effectively across technical and business teams. Clear communication skills, with the ability to explain complex analysis to different audiences. A commitment to learning and keeping informed about developments in data science, machine learning and AI. Burberry is an Equal Opportunities Employer and as such, treats all applications equally and recruits purely on the basis of skills and experience.

items.title: Signal Processing & Data Engineer
items.card: What You'll Do Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer. Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour.
items.desc: Who We Are Limatica measures what batteries whisper. We turn the tiny voltage noise of battery cells into a quality verdict, far faster than conventional tests, and help cell manufacturers cut scrap. We are a team of twelve in Chemnitz and Munich, spanning data, ML, HPC, hardware and industrialization. Early adopters across Europe and Asia already use our technology. In 2026 we move from pilots to production lines, and our data grows faster than our team. What You'll Do Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer. Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour. Make throughput a design decision: Build modular, parameterizable nodes for our distributed processing pipeline and help bring them into our Rust-based production environment. Ship modules, not scripts: Automate evaluations end to end, from raw data to reports for our engineering team and our customers. Own customer projects technically: Assess requirements, communicate interim results and findings, and turn feedback into improvements. What You Bring Measurement experience: A degree in electrical engineering (or comparable) and 3+ years with real-world measurement data. Sampling, noise, filtering and artifacts you know from practice, not just lectures. Physical intuition: You can explain why a feature makes sense, and you prefer a simple, well-understood method over a model nobody can explain. Data at scale: You think in throughput: data formats, intermediate results, distributed and cached processing. Clean engineering: Python, Git, tests and CI/CD as a matter of course. No Rust expertise needed, but the will to learn it. Customer confidence: Fluent German and English, written and spoken. You explain results clearly to engineers and managers alike. Why Limatica Real ownership: Your own part of the pipeline and your first customer project within months. As we grow, this role can grow into technical lead. Learn what few get to learn: Electrochemistry, Rust in production and data engineering at scale, with real cells and international manufacturers. Share the upside: Salary package including virtual stock options. Invest in yourself: Additional holiday for personal learning Flexibility & wellbeing: Flexible hours, hybrid work, further benefits via Guud Card and free beverages What it's like here: You get a lot of trust and a lot of room to shape things. We look for people who stay with a problem until it's solved and who enjoy the moments when a customer launch needs the whole team. Those are the moments where people here grow fastest. This role is intentionally a towards-senior position. You will take on increasing responsibility for pipeline modules and customer projects. Those who help shape the architecture and lead projects independently grow into a senior role with us. Ready to find the signal in the noise? Let's build the future of battery diagnostics together. ⚡

The Amazon Robotics team is seeking an experienced Applied Scientist to join our team. In this role you will apply the latest trends in research to solve real-world problems in robotics and AI. You will collaborate with a team of scientists and engineers building these applications. We holistically design, build, and deliver end-to-end robotic systems. Our team is also responsible for core infrastructure and tools that serve as the backbone of our robotic applications, enabling roboticists, machine learning scientists, software engineers, and hardware engineers to collaborate and deploy systems in the field.
Key job responsibilities
• Research, design, develop, and evaluate complex perception, motion planning, and decision making algorithms integrating across multiple disciplines and leveraging machine learning.
• Create experiments and prototype implementations of new learning algorithms and prediction techniques.
• Work closely with software engineering team members to drive scalable, real-time implementations.
• Collaborate with machine learning and robotic controls experts to implement and deploy algorithms, such as machine learning models.
• Collaborate closely with hardware engineering team members on developing systems from prototyping to production level.
• Represent Amazon in academia community through publications and scientific presentations.
• Work with stakeholders across hardware, science, and operations teams to iterate on systems design and implementation.

items.desc:
Apple's Camera Algorithm team is looking for extraordinary engineers and researchers interested in developing next generation of image capture, processing and rendering algorithms to be used across all Apple product cameras! As part of the team you will research and develop novel ways to improve the image and video quality of Apple’s camera systems. In order to reduce the computational complexity of your methods you are encouraged to take advantage of Apple silicon technologies such as the Image Signal Processor (ISP) or the Apple Neural Engine (ANE). The Camera Algorithm Tone Mapping team works at the intersection of software and hardware, developing real time algorithms required for camera operation, and has major impact on the final image and video quality! The team has a history of delivering solutions running on Apple products, for example Smart HDR, HDR video tone mapping or Apple Log encoding. This interdisciplinary team works closely with many other groups including silicon design, camera hardware and camera software teams to deliver industry leading consumer imaging devices. The work environment champions innovation, rapid iteration and awards independence and creativity in solving engineering problems.
As an algorithm developer you will be responsible for crafting the creative look of videos captured with Apple cameras by developing capture side tone mapping algorithms. You will drive algorithm development across all stages of the cycle; from the initial idea and proof of concept work through on-device implementation all the way to field testing, validation and finally surprising and delighting our customers.
MS and a minimum of 10 years relevant industry experience.
Track record of developing image processing algorithms for example: auto white balance, tone mapping, auto exposure and high dynamic range capture.
Validated coding skills in Python or MATLAB.
Familiarity with a digital camera image processing pipeline and the Image Signal Processor (ISP).
Understanding of image quality metrics and subjective evaluations.
Proven knowledge of HDR encoding standards.
Prior experience with professional video content postproduction and color grading workflows.
Curiosity about vision science and/or color science.
Programming skills in C/C++.
Exposure to machine learning algorithms.
Passion for photography and videography.

Job Description: 
 Join us to be part of the new Airbus UpNext strategic demonstrator paving the future of Aircraft Connectivity. 
This demonstrator will accelerate the development of new technologies to bring tangible learnings to the business.
 Designed as a talent incubator, Airbus UpNext is a place where you can act and think like a startup while building on the strong expertise of Airbus, a place where you are empowered to challenge and test new processes and ways of working.
 This position comes with a limited contract (CDI-C) linked to the deliverable of the demo (estimated end date - end of February 2028), starting ASAP. 
 Mission: 
 As the Computer Vision & Video Analytics Engineer, you will be working with the senior AI engineer to develop vision based solutions on our different test/integration benches. 
 There are several industrial benches to be managed in this scope: ground / air / road benches, it is key to ensure the consistency between them. 
 This position is based in Toulouse, and we will collaborate with teams across Europe and an international partnership landscape. 
 Your main tasks and responsibilities will include: 
 Build and maintain annotated datasets: frame extraction, labelling, quality checks and train/validation splits. 
 Train, fine-tune and evaluate models, and report results with clear metrics. 
 Implement and test new algorithms from the research literature in the existing Python codebase. 
 Write unit and regression tests and keep the documentation up to date. 
 Help to integrate the pipeline on the target hardware: running and benchmarking models, and diagnosing issues in video input and camera setup. 
 Help evaluate new sensors by recording data, checking quality and writing integration prototypes.
 Your Boarding Pass 
 What you bring: 
 Master's degree, engineering degree or equivalent in computer vision, machine learning, robotics or a related field (or a comparable portfolio). 
 Good Python and some experience with PyTorch and OpenCV. 
 Knowledge of the basics of computer vision: object detection, tracking, camera geometry, evaluation metrics. 
 Comfortable with Git and the Linux command line. 
 Curious, rigorous and able to document your work clearly. 
 Passion about technology, science. 
 Autonomy, Adaptability, Availability, Accountability. 
 Eagerness in working in an international, diverse and geographically located team. 
 Values of transparency, courage, humility, empathy. 
 English at negotiation level is mandatory. 
 Willingness to have fun.
 What you get: 
 Pivotal Role in a Strategic Mission: play a key part in a project and participate in the Aviation Connectivity revolution. 
 Build Something that Last: Your work will create a high-value asset 💎 and learning contribution for Airbus’s future. 
 Develop Critical Competences: Acquire and develop a sound background in connectivity technologies, a field essential for the future of aerospace. This experience can provide a unique career development opportunity within Airbus. 
 Agile and Empowering Environment: Thrive in a work culture that empowers you to act and think like a start-up while being supported by the strong expertise of Airbus. 💪🏻 We value an eagerness to take initiative and propose efficient ways of working. 
 A Great Team and Culture: Be part of a high-achieving, experienced and fun team in a shared open-space office with highly skilled colleagues. We are guided by the “Care for Each Other” value. 
 Flexibility & Fun: Enjoy the ability to craft your calendar 🗓️ with flexible hours and the opportunity to work remotely, alongside regular UpNext community bonding events. And yes, we have complimentary freshly ground coffe ☕ and beverages 🧃 
 The responsibilities and the technical scope of the job might evolve according to the agile working environment of the project, so being flexible is important.
 About us 
 Founded in 2017, Airbus UpNext is actively shaping the future of aerospace by using demonstrators to evaluate, mature and validate new products and services. Our purpose is to pioneer game-changing technologies with Airbus.
 In this role, you will embody the core Airbus UpNext values: 
 Care for Each Other : Ensuring a supportive and inclusive environment. 
 Be Simple : Finding the most efficient path to success. 
 Be Audacious : Challenging the status quo to make the unthinkable real. 
 Be Open: Collaborative solution-finding across diverse teams. 
 Speed of Execution : Moving at the speed of a startup.

items.desc:
OWN YOUR INTELLIGENCE

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

You will own applied RL programs from the first ambiguous customer problem through a deployed improvement loop. You will understand the workflow and business stakes, decide what can be measured and learned, build the environment and evaluation, run post-training experiments, deploy the result, and determine what should generalize into Prime's shared stack. The majority of your work will be organized around external programs. You will work directly with customer researchers, engineers, and leaders, and you will be accountable for both the research result and its practical impact.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Role scope

We have active programs across technology, science, engineering, regulated industries, and the public sector.

Representative early problems

 - Turn a partially documented workflow and business goal into an environment, baseline, and evaluation that the customer team agrees measures the right outcome.

 - Improve a domain agent through RL or another post-training method while separating model limitations from task, harness, inference, and integration failures.

 - Carry a successful experiment into deployment, measure its effect on the customer outcome, and convert the recurring parts into reusable environments, recipes, data loops, or platform capabilities.

What you will own

 - Technical and business discovery that produces a clear research plan, success measure, environment, and baseline.

 - RL, distillation, and other post-training experiments tied to deployment outcomes.

 - Agent systems that handle tool use, memory, recovery, long horizons, and human oversight.

 - Deployment and adoption decisions, plus reusable artifacts carried back to Prime's research, engineering, and product teams.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Relevant experience: customer-embedded technical work, research engineering, technical founding experience, applied ML consulting with real build ownership, or end-to-end post-training programs.

 - You should be comfortable with senior external teams and able to connect experimental evidence to business decisions without lowering the research bar.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

 - Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

 - Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

 - Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your …

Your experiments will track skill acquisition, transfer, forgetting, and loss of plasticity over long sequences of tasks.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Role scope

Control update cadence, policy lag, task drift, and exploration, and evaluate each checkpoint on earlier skills, unseen tasks, and general capabilities. Build task-generation and training pipelines with reproducible data and harness versions, so regressions can be traced to a specific change and rolled back. You will work directly with the external collaborators whose deployments drive the research.

Representative early problems

 - Select high-value production traces and interventions, convert them into training signal, and establish regression gates before a change reaches deployment.

 - Determine which adaptation belongs in model weights, harness state, memory, tools, or data, then measure the tradeoffs across a sequence of tasks.

 - Build evaluations that distinguish retained learning and transfer from memorization, context accumulation, or measurement drift.

What you will own

items.desc: The AIT Austrian Institute of Technology is Austria’s largest Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . We aim to transform scientific excellence into innovation with impact. Together with our partners, we develop technologies and solutions for a sustainable, resilient, and digitalised future, strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and technological sovereignty. Our international teams combine cutting-edge research with strong implementation expertise to create measurable value for industry and society. Our Center for Digital Safety and Security is looking for new Ingenious Partners for our location in Vienna (Giefinggasse, 1210). In the Reliable Wireless Communication and Sensing research team , we develop energy efficient solutions for reliable wireless 5G/6G communication and sensing. We are enthusiastically researching integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) methods in mobile indoor and outdoor scenarios using 5G/6G physical layer technologies. Scientists (f/m/d) for Advanced Algorithms in 5G/6G Wireless Networks CENTER FOR DIGITAL SAFETY & SECURITY You will investigate cooperative positioning and advanced localisation algorithms for wireless communication networks in complex outdoor scenarios, using AIT’s Radio-Frequency lab and an optical tracking system to obtain accurate ground-truth position measurements. You will validate the algorithms through numerical simulations and empirical measurements , while contributing to the development and deployment of a distributed wireless network using state-of-the-art hardware and software-defined radio (SDR) technology. You will publish your research results at conferences and in international journals. You will gain expertise in a research field with a wide range of applications , spanning construction, logistics, aviation, railways, agriculture, robotics, and defence. You will work alongside an international team of scientists and expand your professional network through European-wide research projects . Your qualifications as an Ingenious Partner: Completed technical studies (Master’s degree or PhD) related to Telecommunications, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering Experience in at least one of the following profiles: 1. Distributed localisation in wireless networks 2. Positioning and sensing in 5G/6G networks Please describe in the cover letter how your CV and expertise match with at least one of the technological areas above (explicitly referring to 1.– 2.) Applications that do not address this point may not be considered further. Excellent knowledge in the field of statistical signal processing and numerical simulation software development (Python or MATLAB) Sound knowledge of radio propagation modeling and data analysis, machine learning, algorithm design and validation Experience in performing lab measurements and collecting datasets for validation of developed algorithms Good understanding of algorithms in the field of wireless communications (beamforming, channel estimation, signaling, …) Interest in reading and writing scientific publications and motivation for solving application-oriented challenges from industry High level of commitment and ability to work in a team Good language skills in English (spoken & written). German language skills are an advantage. What to expect: The minimum gross annual salary on a full-time basis (38,5 h / week) according to the collective agreement is EUR 56.784, -. The actual salary will be determined individually, based on your qualifications and experience. In case of interest, we offer the opportunity to pursue a PhD at TU Wien alongside your full-time employment as a Scientist. Highlights of our employee benefits include a canteen and meal allowance, organic coffee, tea and fruit baskets, preventive healthcare benefits and company doctor, pension fund, additional days off for various life events, family benefits (including two weeks of paid paternity leave “Papa-Weeks” and leisure subsidies), voucher programme, sports, cultural and socialising events and many more, as well as flexitime models (incl. up to 50% home office), travel support for conferences and networking, and individual training and career development opportunities. At AIT, we create an inclusive and family-friendly working environment that promotes equal opportunities and actively strengthens diversity across our workforce and in leadership positions. Among other initiatives, we are committed to increasing the proportion of women in our company and therefore particularly welcome applications from female applicants. Please submit your complete application documents online, consisting of your CV, a cover letter, relevant certificates (transcript of records), as well as a proof of identity. Would you like to get to know our team & how it feels like working at AIT? Join us live! When: Thursday, 22.10.2026 | 5 pm (CET) Topic: PhDs and other career opportunities at AIT: Research the 6G networks of tomorrow Please subscribe here ! …

items.desc: Informations Générales Nom Chargé de contrôle des coûts, du plan de charge et de l’IA Junior F/H Ref # 16854 Date de publication Lundi, octobre 19, 2026 Pays France Region Île-de-France Ville Châtillon Business Unit (BU) ADF Type de Contrat CDI Date de début souhaitée 01-12-2026 Horaire de travail Horaire Normal Télétravail Télétravail possible Métier G - GESTION DE PROJET Métier Orano Projets 023 - Contrôle des Coûts Description Description Depuis plus de 50 ans, Orano recycle sur le site de La Hague les combustibles usés issus des centrales nucléaires. Aujourd'hui, avec le projet Aval du Futur, Orano relève un nouveau défi : concevoir et construire les installations industrielles qui accompagneront la filière jusqu'à l'horizon 2120, dans une perspective de performance durable, de sûreté renforcée et d'excellence technologique. Par son ampleur financière (40 à 50 milliards d'euros), sa technicité et son intensité, le projet Aval du Futur (AdF) figure parmi les plus grands programmes industriels d'Europe. Rejoignez-nous en tant que Chargé de contrôle des coûts, du plan de charge et de l'IA ! Au sein de la Direction Performance et Contrôle de Projet (DPCP) du Projet Aval du Futur (AdF), vous contribuez : Au processus de contrôle des coûts et au pilotage financier du projet (consolidation budgétaire, reporting mensuel des coûts et fiabilisation des coûts à terminaison) A l'élaboration et au suivi du plan de charge du Projet A la transformation digitale et au déploiement d'outils d'intelligence artificielle (IA) En appui aux responsables « Contrôle des coûts » et « Outils, données et méthodes » de l'équipe Cost Control de la DPCP, vos missions principales seront : 1. Élaboration et suivi du plan de charge Contribuer à la structuration du plan de charge et à la consolidation des données de l'ensemble du Projet en appui aux exercices semestriels d'analyse capacitaire des métiers de l'ingénierie Collecter les hypothèses et en assurer la traçabilité Assurer le suivi et l'analyse des écarts par rapport aux prévisions Contribuer à l'amélioration et au développement d'outils intégrés pour le suivi du plan de charge, des transferts de ressources et du plan de recrutement 2. Appui au contrôle des coûts Consolider les données et analyser les écarts par rapport aux prévisions concernant la répartition des ressources et la part de sous-traitance des études Réaliser des contrôles trimestriels des pointages afin de vérifier leur cohérence avec le plan prévisionnel de transfert des ressources 3. Reporting, Power BI et déploiement de l'IA Contribuer à l'intégration des données entre ECOSYS et Power BI, ainsi qu'au développement de tableaux de bord Power BI intégrés à ECOSYS Contribuer à l'identification, au test et au déploiement de cas d'usage de l'IA sur les activités de contrôle des coûts du Projet Profil souhaité Profil recherché : Formation supérieure Bac+5 (école d'ingénieurs ou université) en contrôle de gestion, finance, gestion de projet, gestion des données ou dans un domaine technique pertinent pour l'ingénierie industrielle. items.desc: Share page Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology : Chair of Learning Technical Systems In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date , we are looking for a Research associate (m/f/x) The group conducts core research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, with a primary focus on online decision-making under uncertainty. Our work spans areas such as (inverse, deep, and causal) reinforcement learning, multiarmed bandits, and learning in multi-agent systems involving cooperation, competition, and coordination. We are particularly interested in how intelligent systems can adapt across changing domains and recover from suboptimal or biased decisions through principled approaches to domain adaptation and algorithmic recourse. While our methods are generic and applicable across diverse fields—including medicine, education, and finance—we primarily apply them to engineering and technical systems, such as the Internet of Things, nextgeneration communication networks, and robotics. The researcher will work on the development of robust and efficient collective algorithmic recourse methods to enhance the resilience of mission-critical networked systems. The project lies at the intersection of machine learning, optimization, and multi-agent systems, addressing challenges arising from resource volatility and uncertainty in dynamic environments. The work will include both theoretical analysis—covering efficiency, scalability, and convergence—as well as the application of the proposed methods to optimize networked systems. Scope: full-time Duration: fixed-term, 36 months Start: at the earliest possible date Apply by: 2026-11-02 Your tasks: The main task is to conduct high-quality and independent research in the area of collective algorithmic recourse, with a particular focus on its application to networked systems, and to publish the results in leading scientific venues. Your profile: An excellent, recently completed Ph.D. or M.Sc. degree with a strong publication record in Computer Science (Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence), Mathematics (pure or applied, including Operations Research), Electrical Engineering (Signal Processing, Information Theory), or related fields such as Theoretical Physics. A solid mathematical background. Strong programming skills. Excellent command of English, both written and spoken. We offer: We offer a cooperative and friendly working environment that encourages collaboration, creativity, and professional growth. The position is part of a DFG Priority Programme (SPP) , which provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and networking . The successful candidate will have the chance to participate in project meetings, workshops, and joint events within the programme to further develop their expertise and build research connections. If the personal and collective agreement requirements are met, the employee will receive pay grade E13 TV-L TV-L. Further information can be found at (in German). items.desc: Junior Machine Learning Engineer Entra nel team di Amaris Consulting come Junior Machine Learning Engineer e inizia un nuovo percorso professionale in un ambiente internazionale, tecnico e orientato alla crescita. items.desc: Turn complex energy questions into clear, data-driven decisions Are you analytical, curious and motivated by solving challenging problems? Join Axpo Polska as a Junior Data Scientist and help turn commercial and trading questions from the Polish energy and gas business into robust analyses, models and data products. You’ll work with colleagues across the business to strengthen decision-making through high-quality data science. You bring critical thinking, a constructive, questioning mindset and the determination to work through complex issues—not just produce numbers, but understand what they mean and communicate the insight clearly. What you’ll do Develop, maintain and improve predictive machine-learning models, including time-series, regression and classification models. Translate commercial and trading questions into analyses, models and practical data products. Work with large-scale data and use tools such as SQL, Python, GCP and Snowflake to deliver reliable analytical solutions. Explore and visualise results, including with Power BI, and explain findings to technical and business stakeholders. Check data quality, validate analytical outputs and critically review code and model results. Document your work clearly so that analyses and models can be understood, maintained and handed over effectively. Contribute to improving processes, performance and efficiency across the business. What you’ll bring A bachelor’s degree in data science, mathematics, IT, economics, finance, energy or a related field. At least one year of experience in data science or a similar analytical role. Strong SQL skills, including practical knowledge of query optimisation. Practical Python skills and a sound understanding of data science and machine-learning concepts, such as model evaluation, clustering and common model types. An analytical approach, strong critical-thinking skills and confidence working through complex, ambiguous problems. A challenging mindset: you question assumptions, investigate root causes and look for better ways to solve problems. A proactive, self-sufficient and entrepreneurial approach, with a can-do attitude and the ability to work well with multiple stakeholders. Good spoken and written English. Polish is relevant for the local business context; knowledge of the Polish energy and gas industry is an advantage. What we offer Full-time employment contract. Development in an international company that is shaping the face of the energy market. A progressive medical care package that takes care of your health and well-being. Co-financing of the Multisport card, enabling the use of various forms of physical activity. Foreign language classes during working hours. Flexible working hours and the possibility to work in hybrid mode. An office with a beautiful view, located in the city center. A motivated team, ready to guide you through your daily challenges. Details about the salary range for this position and other components of the compensation package will be provided in the following stages of the recruitment process. Ready to put your analytical mindset to work on complex energy challenges? We look forward to hearing from you. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome applications regardless of race and ethnicity, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, as well as socioeconomic, cultural, and religious background. We are committed to ensuring a respectful and inclusive recruiting process and workplace for everyone.
