Responsibilities: 1. Project Management : Define research programs aligned with new product and service objectives. Organize and execute laboratory-scale R&D
items.desc: Role The Research Engineer will contribute to driving R&D initiatives within a dynamic industrial setting, focusing on the development of new products, services, and basic knowledge of steel casting fluxes (mold powder for continuous casting of steel) and raw materials. The role encompasses applications in continuous casting of steel. This position bridges laboratory research and plant operations, emphasizing sustainable solutions, process efficiencies, and delivering high-quality results for industrial clients worldwide. Responsibilities: 1. Project Management : Define research programs aligned with new product and service objectives. Organize and execute laboratory-scale R&D projects. Performs tasks/projects and takes the responsibility for assuring quality, cost effectiveness & timeliness for those projects Develop materials and processes while supporting related projects. Maintain regular reporting on project progress and outcomes. Supervise customer sample preparation and optimize products based on feedback. Monitor technical advancements in the market, including patents and scientific publications. Consolidate fundamental knowledge on steel casting fluxes and associated raw materials. 2. Laboratory Research and Data Management : Plan research activities, including experiments, characterization, and analytics Manage, process, analyze, and document data from lab activities. Maximize data collection value from R&D, production, and quality assurance. Develop project reviews, technical reports, and presentations with clarity and precision. Document knowledge and findings in technical memos and share them with stakeholders. Utilize project management tools (e.g., Vantage) for deliverables and resource planning. Organize stage-gate meetings and prioritize multiple projects. 3. External Collaboration and Scientific Contributions : Prepare papers, proposals, and presentations for conferences, congresses, and seminars. Build external collaborations and networks to share and extend expertise. Address intellectual property topics, support evaluations, and assist in patent filings. Requirements: PhD or master’s degree in Materials Science, Metallurgy, Mineralogy, or a related engineering discipline, preferably with a focus on casting fluxes (mold powders), glass chemistry, and/or interactions between slag and liquid steel. Minimum of 5 years of experience in R&D, project management, or product development, ideally within or for a steel plant environment. Comprehensive knowledge of continuous steel casting processes, mineralogy, and ceramic raw materials for casting fluxes, including their melting and solidification mechanisms under high-temperature conditions. Strong expertise in thermodynamics and reaction kinetics, with proficiency in thermodynamic calculation tools (e.g., FactSage®). Hands-on experience with advanced analytical techniques, such as high-temperature viscometry, hot-stage microscopy, TG/DTA, XRD, and Rietveld refinement. Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities, with demonstrated experience in data analysis and interpretation. Strong technical writing and presentation skills, including the ability to clearly summarize research outcomes and present results during stage-gate or project review meetings. Motivated, adaptable, and innovative, with a proactive approach to challenges and a strong drive for continuous improvement. Collaborative mindset, with the ability to work effectively in an international environment and partner across R&D and plant operations. Fluency in German and English, both written and spoken. As a global organisation operating across multiple countries, compensation for this role may vary depending on location, local market benchmarks, and experience. In line with our commitment to pay transparency, a salary range relevant to your location will be shared with you during the early stages of the recruitment process, before any interview is scheduled.

items.desc: À propos de l’entreprise Kalray est une entreprise technologique spécialisée dans les semi-conducteurs et le calcul haute performance au service de l’intelligence artificielle. Forte de plus de quinze ans d’expertise en architectures de calcul parallèle, en conception de processeurs et en systèmes de calcul haute performance, Kalray est une entreprise technologique française et un acteur européen de premier plan dans des domaines devenus essentiels aux infrastructures d’intelligence artificielle. Avec plus de 120 collaborateurs en France et en Roumanie, Kalray développe et licencie des technologies matérielles et logicielles stratégiques pour les nouvelles générations de semi-conducteurs dédiées aux infrastructures d’IA et, plus largement, aux applications nécessitant le traitement de volumes massifs de données. Ces technologies permettent de traiter, de faire circuler et d’orchestrer efficacement les données entre les différentes ressources de calcul, afin d’optimiser les performances, la consommation énergétique et la sécurité. Kalray accompagne ses clients à travers la concession de licences sur ses technologies matérielles et logicielles (IP), complétée par des projets de développement sur mesure. De la définition d’architectures complexes jusqu’à leur intégration dans de nouvelles générations de semi-conducteurs, Kalray associe ses technologies propriétaires à une solide expertise des systèmes, de la conception des puces en silicium et du développement de systèmes complets. Rejoindre Kalray, c’est intégrer une entreprise technologique européenne pionnière, qui conçoit des solutions innovantes à la croisée des semi-conducteurs, de l’intelligence artificielle et du calcul haute performance. Vous travaillerez aux côtés d’ingénieurs et d’experts technologiques reconnus, sur des projets de pointe qui contribuent à façonner l’avenir des infrastructures d’IA. Nous offrons un environnement de travail stimulant, collaboratif et inclusif, où les professionnels expérimentés comme les nouveaux talents peuvent développer leurs compétences, évoluer et contribuer concrètement à des projets ambitieux. Le tout dans un cadre de vie privilégié, au cœur des paysages inspirants des Alpes ou de la Côte d’Azur. Envie de contribuer avec nous à façonner l’avenir des infrastructures d’intelligence artificielle ? Rejoignez l’aventure Kalray ! Kalray est cotée sur Euronext Growth Paris (ALKAL). Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur notre site internet et suivez-nous sur LinkedIn. Voir la fiche de l'entreprise Description Des Activités Significatives De L'emploi Rejoignez l’équipe IA de Kalray, à la pointe de l’innovation, pour développer des solutions d’IA autonomes dédiées à la conception de puces de bout en bout, depuis la définition des exigences initiales et l’exploration architecturale jusqu’à la génération du RTL, à la vérification et à l’implémentation physique. Notre ambition est de repenser la manière dont les puces sont conçues en développant des systèmes agentiques capables de planifier des activités d’ingénierie complexes, de coordonner les outils de conception et d’itérer sur les résultats en s’appuyant sur des mécanismes de validation fiables. Cette approche doit ouvrir une nouvelle ère pour les architectures de puces, en permettant d’explorer des possibilités de conception difficiles à envisager avec les méthodes conventionnelles. Vous contribuerez directement à cette ambition en développant des solutions combinant des grands modèles de langage (LLM) de dernière génération, des agents d’IA et des outils de conception de semi-conducteurs. Dans un premier temps, vos travaux associeront une collaboration étroite avec les ingénieurs de Kalray, un accompagnement opérationnel à l’adoption de l’IA et le développement de prototypes fonctionnels. À mesure que vous vous familiariserez avec nos pratiques d’ingénierie et nos contraintes de conception, vous évoluerez vers le développement de processus autonomes de plus en plus ambitieux, avec pour objectif de transformer les premières expérimentations en solutions robustes capables de prendre en charge des projets complets de conception de puces. Vos Principales Responsabilités Appliquer l’IA à des problématiques concrètes de nos activités techniques, développer des processus de travail efficaces et partager les approches qui ont fait leurs preuves. Concevoir des prototypes d’agents capables de planifier des tâches, d’utiliser des outils d’ingénierie, d’évaluer les résultats et d’itérer pour atteindre un objectif de conception défini. Explorer des processus couvrant l’exploration architecturale, la génération du RTL, la vérification et l’implémentation, en collaboration avec les experts en conception de puces. Connecter les modèles et les agents aux outils de conception via des API, des interfaces en ligne de commande et des scripts. Évaluer le degré d’autonomie, la fiabilité, la qualité de conception et l’efficacité des solutions développées par rapport aux processus …

items.desc: ¡Hola! Somos OGA Nos ilusiona que estés considerando esta oportunidad de empleo. Somos una compañía pionera en la hibridación de la Inteligencia Artificial y la Investigación Operativa, con sede en Sevilla. Nuestro objetivo es transformar la industria a través de soluciones innovadoras y de alto impacto para nuestros clientes, líderes en sectores como el logístico, supply chain, industrial o el químico. Esto lo conseguimos gracias al talento de nuestro equipo, que incluye a matemáticos/as, estadísticos/as o desarrolladores/as de software, entre otros, y a la confianza de grandes clientes. Además, mantenemos una estrecha colaboración con la Universidad a través de nuestro Consejo Asesor Tecnológico, Grupo CÁTEDRA, compuesto por 14 catedráticos de renombre nacional e internacional, especializados en Investigación Operativa y ciencia de datos, y con el que reforzamos nuestra propuesta y valor científico. Sobre la posición. Buscamos un/a Data Scientist con experiencia en la investigación, análisis y modelado de datos para identificar patrones y tendencias clave, impulsando la toma de decisiones estratégicas en la organización, para unirse a nuestro equipo. ¿Qué harás? Análisis de datos y desarrollo de aplicaciones de optimización de procesos complejos con técnicas tanto de Inteligencia Artificial como de Investigación Operativa, utilizando entre otros, lenguajes de programación como Python, Java, JavaScript o C++. Analizar, depurar, transformar, visualizar, etc. los datos disponibles para proyectos de IA, utilizando las herramientas y tecnologías necesarias en cada caso concreto. Realizar el EDA (Exploratory Data Analysis) de los datos para proporcionar un buen conjunto de datos a los modelos de IA. Utilización de diferentes modelos de Machine Learning y Deep Learning, los cuales serán entrenados, validados y testados en función de los objetivos de cada proyecto. Tuning de modelos ML/DL. Investigación e implementación de algoritmos y herramientas de ML/DL. Implementación del pipeline completo de un modelo de ML/DL (Datasource, Limpieza datos, Ingeniería de Variables, Entrenamientos, Validación, Puesta en producción y Monitorización/Operación). Analizarás bases de datos utilizando técnicas de análisis estadístico avanzado. Desarrollarás soluciones y modelos avanzados de Inteligencia Artificial. Elaborarás documentación técnica relacionada con los proyectos. Timing de primeras semanas en OGA Desde tu primer día, estarás acompañado/a por todo el equipo. El área de People organizará una serie de reuniones de Onboarding en tres niveles con distintos responsables de OGA: aspectos generales y sistemas internos, el propósito de la compañía y las tecnologías que utilizamos. También conocerás a tu Buddy, quien te guiará, especialmente en tu primer mes, durante todo el proceso de integración. Junto a tu Buddy, tendrás reuniones programadas para abordar cualquier tema que facilite tu adaptación. ¿Qué requerimos? Titulación en Máster en Matemáticas / Estadística / Ingeniería / Ciencias de la Computación o área relacionada (valorable Doctorado). Experiencia de 3 a 5 años en el sector de Inteligencia Artificial, incluyendo al menos 2 años como consultor liderando proyectos complejos y horizontales con exposición al negocio, con experiencia en tratamiento de datos (captura, almacenamiento, normalización, limpieza, visualización, ETLs y modelos de datos) e implementación de soluciones de IA utilizando Machine Learning y Deep Learning, aplicando algoritmos supervisados, no supervisados y auto-explicativos, como RandomForest, CatBoost, XGBoost, CNN y RNN. Conocimiento y dominio experto en Python (valorable experiencia en otras plataformas y lenguajes), conocimientos recomendables en bases de datos como Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL y MS SQL/SQL Azure, así como experiencia en el entorno de desarrollo de Microsoft Azure. Nivel Alto de inglés. ¿Qué valoramos? Airflow, Hadoop, Spark, MongoDB. Interés por el desarrollo de una carrera técnica y vocación por la especiación tecnológica. Pasión por la tecnología y por la creación de valor para el cliente. Capacidad de relación con equipos de negocio y funcionales, visión holística del problema de negocio a resolver. Orientación a resultados, proactividad, trabajo en equipo. Disponibilidad para viajar a nivel nacional e internacional de manera esporádica. ¿Qué te ofrecemos? Un entorno de trabajo dinámico y flexible, con proyectos y clientes tecnológicamente retadores en nuestra oficina de Sevilla. Formar parte de un equipo apasionado por los datos y la innovación tecnológica, con perfiles senior y junior, de las áreas de las matemáticas, estadística, ciencia de datos o desarrollo de software, entre otras. Colaboración permanente con el Grupo CÁTEDRA, el Consejo Asesor Tecnológico de OGA, compuesto por 14 catedráticos de renombre nacional e internacional especializados en Investigación Operativa y ciencia de datos. Acceso a diversas herramientas de IA Generativa, que nos ayudan a acelerar …

items.desc: APPLICATION BY EMAIL according to the application rules hereunder (not via LinkedIn). Please attach all the documents asked. CONTEXT We are seeking a full-time research scientist or engineer with a master’s degree in physics, photonics, optical engineering or a related engineering discipline to join the ‘PESLAPOD’ project. The position combines laser and optical system modelling, experimental measurements, and the integration and testing of technologies for laser power transfer and optical communication with drones. The Royal Military Academy is a recognised university conducting academic and applied research funded by Belgian Defence and external organisations. We value diversity and equal opportunities. Whether you are a man, a woman or X, or come from any background, we firmly believe that diversity enriches our community, and we encourage all qualified candidates to apply. PROJECT PESLAPOD (Persistent Eye in the Sky from Laser Powered Drones) is a three-year research project managed by the European Defence Agency. It investigates long-range laser power transfer to extend the endurance of small electric drones, with the longer-term ambition of enabling continuous airborne operation. The project also addresses secure, reliable communication with drones and resilient navigation in environments with jamming or unavailable satellite navigation signals (GNSS). Alongside other international partners, Belgium has committed to contributing to this research project through research activities at the Royal Military Academy. You will work within the Royal Military Academy’s Department of Communication, Information, Systems, and Sensors (CISS), specifically in the Laser & Optronics research unit (https://optro.rma.ac.be), in close collaboration with scientists and engineers from other consortium partners. MAIN TASKS Model and evaluate laser beam propagation and optical link performance for drone power transfer and communication, taking atmospheric conditions and operational constraints into account. Develop and conduct laboratory measurements to characterise relevant laser and optical components, including beam properties, optical power and receiver performance. Contribute to the integration and experimental validation of laser power transfer and optical communication systems. Prepare for and participate in field trials, analyse measurement data, and compare experimental results with model predictions. Assess laser safety requirements and develop appropriate operating procedures and protective measures for the applications under study. Review current approaches (state of the art) to high-power laser safety and contribute to the assessment of safety requirements, operating procedures and protective measures for laboratory and field activities. Contribute to the concept study for long-distance optical power transfer to high-altitude pseudo-satellites. Prepare technical reports and scientific publications, and present results at consortium meetings, conferences and stakeholder meetings. SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: Applicants should hold a master’s degree in physics, photonics, optical engineering, electrical engineering or a related discipline, with relevant knowledge of lasers and optical systems. Applications are welcome from recent graduates to candidates with research and/or industrial experience. “MUST HAVE” skills A sound understanding of lasers, optics and beam propagation. Practical experience with optical experiments or instrumentation, gained through academic projects, a thesis, an internship or employment. Ability to analyse experimental data and interpret results using physical principles. Ability to prepare clear technical and scientific documents. Good spoken and written English is essential. “NICE-TO-HAVE” skills Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage: Optical alignment, beam profiling and laser power measurements. Free-space optical communications or optical power transfer. Atmospheric propagation modelling or measurements. Photodetectors, optical receivers and data acquisition. Python, MATLAB or LabVIEW for modelling, instrument control or data analysis. Training or experience in the use of high-energy lasers. Laser safety, particularly for high-power laser systems, would be an asset Personal skills You work carefully and systematically, with attention to experimental quality and safety. You take initiative and progressively develop independence, with guidance from experienced researchers. You collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary and international team. You communicate methods and results clearly. You respect confidentiality requirements when handling consortium information and intellectual property. Knowledge of Dutch and/or French is an added value. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS The position may involve access to classified information. items.card: About The Role You'll build out the data science layer of Adaptyv's foundry — the work that turns tens of thousands of raw, messy experimental readouts into clean, trustworthy, structured data that our customers, our models, and our own scientists can rely on. items.desc: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About The Role You'll build out the data science layer of Adaptyv's foundry — the work that turns tens of thousands of raw, messy experimental readouts into clean, trustworthy, structured data that our customers, our models, and our own scientists can rely on. Binding (BLI/SPR), developability, biophysical, and functional assays all produce data at scale; your job is to make that data correct, comparable, and useful. This sits at the intersection of three things: data quality (is this number real, or an artifact?), bioinformatics (linking experimental results back to sequence, structure, and protein design), and dataset building (turning foundry output into the kind of high-quality, benchmarkable data that frontier AI labs actually want). You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with the lab scientists who run the assays, the software team who own the pipelines, and the customers who train models on what we produce. This is a hands-on build role, not a management one. What You'll Do Own the scientific logic of data quality across the foundry: define what "good data" looks like for each assay type — expected signal ranges, control thresholds, failure modes, edge cases — and turn it into automated checks. Build anomaly detection and QC models that catch bad data the eye would miss: assay drift, instrument variability, plate effects, false passes and false fails — and distinguish real signal from noise statistically. Work with the software and ML teams to specify, review, and improve the automated data pipelines that process instrument outputs, feeding back precise requirements for what to flag, auto-reject, or route to human review. Connect experimental results back to the protein side — sequence, structure, and design — so wet-lab data and computational models reinforce each other. Turn foundry output into structured, documented, benchmark-grade datasets that are a genuine asset for our customers and for training and evaluating protein-design models. Apply real statistical rigor to multi-condition data at scale — thousands of samples across hundreds of simultaneous experiments — and make the results interpretable and comparable across runs. What We're Looking For Strong data science / bioinformatics background — you're fluent in Python (pandas, numpy, the scientific stack) and comfortable owning messy, real-world experimental data end to end. Genuine biology grounding — you understand proteins, assays, and sequence/structure/function well enough to know what the data means, not just how to process it. You don't need to be a bench scientist, but you can't be biology-blind. Statistical maturity — process control, anomaly detection, handling variability and batch effects; you can tell drift from noise and defend the call. Prolific builder with the receipts to prove it. You've shipped a lot — pipelines, tools, models, datasets — and can point to concrete things you built end to end and put into real use, not prototypes that died in a notebook. You move fast, systematize what works, and have no patience for babysitting a fixed dashboard. AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce. Interdisciplinary by instinct. You're energized working across the lab bench, software, and ML, and you treat automation and data infrastructure as part of your job. Bonus: experience with protein/sequence-structure data (bioinformatics tooling, structural data), ML on experimental data, or building datasets for model training and benchmarking. Details Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site) Type: Full time Start date: ASAP Application deadline We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

items.desc: Vous souhaitez mettre votre expertise en cybersécurité et en analyse de données au service de la lutte contre la fraude ? Rejoignez-nous ! Nous recherchons un(e) Expert(e) sécurité et cybersécurité du SI F/H – Expert(e) cyber IA data science en CDI, sur notre site de Sophia-Antipolis ou de Rennes. Qui sommes-nous ? La CNAF (Caisse Nationale des Allocations Familiales), tête de réseau des 101 CAF, représente la branche Famille de la Sécurité sociale et a pour mission de piloter la politique familiale et l’aide aux populations en situation de précarité ainsi que la politique d’action sociale. Votre futur service : Au sein de la la Direction des Systèmes d’Informations (DSI) de la Cnaf, la Direction du Contrôle Interne et de la Sécurité Numérique (DCISN) mobilise, au sein d’une même Direction, l’ensemble des acteurs œuvrant pour la sécurité numérique afin de faire face à l’augmentation incessante du niveau de menace, en apportant de l’agilité dans la mise en place des postures de sécurisation des SI, de détection des tentatives de compromission, de contrôle de l’application des politiques et processus. Rattaché(e) au département Cyber défense de la DCISN, vous intégrerez plus précisément le pôle SOC (8 collaborateurs) qui participe au dispositif de détection des activités malveillantes ayant trait à la fraude sur le système d’information de la DSI de la CNAF. Concrètement votre futur quotidien ? Votre mission consistera à transformer de grands volumes de données en systèmes intelligents de prévention et de détection de la fraude, directement exploitables par les équipes métiers ! Pour ce faire, vous vous appuierez sur votre expertise cyber et sur l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle, en combinant Data Science avancée, Machine Learning, analyse comportementale et expertise fraude. Vous prendrez en charge les missions suivantes : Analyser les traces cyber et investiguer les comportements frauduleux Analyser les journaux de sécurité, les événements applicatifs et les traces d’utilisation des services web et des API pour identifier des activités suspectes ; Reconstituer les enchaînements d’événements et caractériser les modes opératoires associés aux compromissions de comptes, aux usurpations d’identité, aux usages automatisés abusifs et aux détournements de services numériques à des fins frauduleuses ; Conduire les investigations techniques en croisant les sources disponibles, distinguer les comportements légitimes des anomalies et des indices de fraude. Concevoir et faire évoluer la collecte et la corrélation des données Enrichir la détection par la CTI et les informations de compromission Exploiter les outils et sources de CTI afin d’identifier les menaces, les indicateurs de compromission et les modes opératoires susceptibles d’alimenter des scénarios de fraude sur les services numériques. Développer des capacités de détection combinant expertise cyber, analyse de données et IA Construire des variables pertinentes à partir des traces cyber et des parcours d’utilisation des services. Développer des approches supervisées et non supervisées : classification, détection d’anomalies, regroupement de comportements et calcul de scores de risque. Identifier les signaux faibles, les comportements coordonnés et les relations entre différentes entités. Industrialiser les dispositifs et améliorer leurs performances Intégrer les règles, traitements et modèles dans les outils de détection et d’investigation. Automatiser les opérations répétitives de collecte, d’enrichissement et de préqualification. Définir les méthodes de validation et d’évaluation à partir des données historiques et des cas confirmés. Proposer des améliorations sur les outils et processus utilisés lors de la détection et qualification des cas de fraude. Apporter une expertise opérationnelle et garantir la maîtrise des usages Collaborer avec les équipes cybersécurité, lutte contre la fraude, métiers, données et développement pour comprendre les usages légitimes, qualifier les risques et définir les priorités de détection. Produire des restitutions claires et exploitables : synthèses d’investigation, descriptions de scénarios, documentation des règles et des modèles, recommandations d’amélioration des dispositifs de surveillance et de sécurisation. Garantir l’explicabilité des résultats et documenter les sources. Des déplacements sur les autres sites de la CNAF sont possibles. Etes-vous notre prochain(e) collaborateur(trice) ? Par ailleurs, vous vous reconnaissez dans les compétences suivantes : Cybersécurité Maîtrise d’un SIEM, notamment Splunk et du langage SPL Sécurité des applications web et des API : savoir interpréter les méthodes HTTP, les codes de réponse, les en-têtes, les cookies et les identifiants de session Capacité de comprendre et d’exploiter des données CTI, IOC, données issues de fuites de données Analyse de données Python pour l’analyse de données SQL avancé : écrire des requêtes comprenant des jointures, des agrégations, des …

items.title: Applied AI Engineer
items.card: The Role Reporting to the AI & Innovation Lead, the Applied AI Engineer builds and improves AI-enabled products and workflows. The role focuses on agents, model and tool selection, prompt and context engineering, retrieval, MCP, evaluation, token economics and the practical skills needed to make AI useful in legal and business work. The role will work closely with the Product Manager, Automation & AI Engineer,
items.desc: The Department Our Technology team continues to go from strength to strength, playing a vital role in firm-wide innovation and strategy. Far from being a support function, Technology is integral to the firm's growth agenda, backed by strong leadership engagement and sustained investment. The Team The AI and Engineering team develops practical AI, automation and integration capability for legal practice and business operations. It works closely with Product, Data, Architecture, Security and operational teams to turn valuable ideas into secure, maintainable services, while retaining space for controlled experimentation and rapid learning. The Role Reporting to the AI & Innovation Lead, the Applied AI Engineer builds and improves AI-enabled products and workflows. The role focuses on agents, model and tool selection, prompt and context engineering, retrieval, MCP, evaluation, token economics and the practical skills needed to make AI useful in legal and business work. The role will work closely with the Product Manager, Automation & AI Engineer, lawyers, business teams, Data, Architecture, Security and vendors. It will move use cases from rapid experiment and proof of concept into tested services, with clear evidence of quality, safety, adoption and value. Duties And Responsibilities Applied AI delivery Work against the prioritised AI and innovation roadmap, with the Product Manager accountable for product priorities and outcomes and the AI & Innovation Lead accountable for innovation direction and team capability. Build AI-enabled applications, agents and workflow components using Python, TypeScript, Azure and approved model services. Develop prompts, system instructions, tool definitions, retrieval approaches and context strategies suited to real legal and operational tasks. Design and evaluate retrieval pipelines, including document preparation, chunking, metadata, permissions-aware access, source attribution and retrieval quality. Build MCP integrations and other APIs that allow agents to use approved data and tools through controlled interfaces. Use AI-assisted software development to accelerate prototyping, while reviewing, testing and hardening generated code before release. Evaluation, quality and token economics Create representative evaluation sets from real use cases and define acceptance thresholds before wider release. Evaluate end-to-end outcomes and intermediate agent behaviour, including tool selection, task adherence, groundedness, safety and failure modes. Measure token consumption, latency and cost; compare models and architectures and recommend the simplest approach that meets the need. Use telemetry and user feedback to improve prompts, retrieval, skills, agents and model configuration after release. Track task-success rate, output quality, human correction or override, latency, unit cost, adoption and time or capacity created. Experimentation and productionisation Work with Product to turn opportunities into clear hypotheses, technical spikes, PoCs and controlled pilots. Document experiment design, limitations, decisions and results so learning can be reused across the roadmap. Retain engineering ownership as successful prototypes move into secure, monitored and supportable production services, working with the Automation & AI Engineer on architecture, integration and production standards. Contribute reusable components, evaluation harnesses, prompt patterns and engineering guidance. Responsible delivery Protect confidential and personal data through appropriate access, retention and environment controls. Design human review, fallback and escalation into AI workflows where quality or consequence requires it. Explain model limitations and uncertainty clearly, avoiding the presentation of experimental capability as production-ready. Monitor production AI services for quality, cost, latency, tool failures and unexpected behaviour; investigate incidents and maintain appropriate runbooks, rollback arrangements and operational guidance. Essential Skills and Experience Strong software engineering fundamentals, including version control, testing, code review, documentation and secure development. Experience working with APIs, integrations, cloud services and event-driven or workflow-based solutions. Ability to move from an unclear problem to a working prototype, then improve it using evidence and user feedback. Confidence working with Product, Data, Architecture, Security and business specialists in a multidisciplinary environment. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders. A pragmatic approach to experimentation, with good judgement about what is safe to test and what is ready to operate. Use of approved identity, secrets-management and service-connection patterns, avoiding embedded credentials and unmanaged service accounts. Commitment to accessible and usable user-facing applications and workflow interfaces. …

The team waiting for you: Our Engineering team manages a powerful data platform that has unlocked a growing backlog of applied ML work. items.desc: We’re looking for data scientists who turn ambiguous business questions into models and analyses that actually get used. You’ll frame the problem, wrangle the data, build and validate models, and — just as importantly — explain what the numbers mean to people who don’t speak Python. Your day-to-day will revolve around the classic Python data stack: pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. You’ll also work on modern enterprise data platforms — running notebooks and lakehouse workloads in Microsoft Fabric, building pipelines and operational applications in Palantir Foundry, and deploying analytics on Azure, AWS, or GCP. The science matters, but so does making it work inside a real organization’s data ecosystem. What We Offer AI Grant — Stop talking about AI and start building it. Our AI Grant gives you dedicated budget and resources to turn your wildest AI idea into a working project, backed by two paid weeks to focus on nothing else. AI Center of Excellence — Work alongside specialists in agentic AI, sovereign AI, generative and discriminative AI. This isn’t a siloed team — it’s the people you’ll learn from and build with daily. Your tools, your choice — Full access to AI-powered development tools including Claude, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Pick what works best for you. Real project variety — From generative AI for legal document compliance through agentic systems in manufacturing environments to enterprise-scale AI platforms, computer vision, and autonomous driving. You won’t get bored. Conference and speaking support — Want to attend conferences? We’ll back you. Want to speak at them? Even better — we’ll support you with dedicated preparation time and bonuses. Your tasks Translate business problems into analytical solutions: define hypotheses, choose metrics, and select the right modeling approach for the question at hand Explore, clean, and prepare data using Python (pandas, NumPy), working with structured and semi-structured sources of varying quality Build, validate, and tune machine learning models for classification, regression, forecasting, segmentation, and recommendation using scikit-learn, XGBoost, and statsmodels Design and analyze experiments: A/B tests, statistical hypothesis testing, and causal analysis that hold up to scrutiny Work hands-on with enterprise data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric (lakehouses, notebooks, semantic models) and Palantir Foundry (pipelines, ontology, operational workflows) Communicate findings through clear visualizations, dashboards, and narratives tailored to technical and non-technical stakeholders alike Collaborate with data engineers on data availability and quality, and with ML/AI engineers to move models from notebook to production Monitor deployed models for drift and degradation, and own the retraining and improvement cycle Requirements At least 4 years in data science or applied analytics, with models and analyses that made it past the prototype stage Strong Python skills across the standard data stack (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn) Solid statistical foundations: hypothesis testing, regression, experimental design, and knowing when a result is real versus noise Knowledge of at least one cloud/data platform and its data science components — Azure (Microsoft Fabric, Azure Machine Learning), AWS (SageMaker), GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery ML), Snowflake (Snowpark ML, Cortex), Databricks (MLflow, Mosaic AI), or Palantir (Foundry Code Workspaces, Foundry ML, AIP) items.desc: We’re looking for data scientists who turn ambiguous business questions into models and analyses that actually get used. You’ll frame the problem, wrangle the data, build and validate models, and — just as importantly — explain what the numbers mean to people who don’t speak Python. Your day-to-day will revolve around the classic Python data stack: pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. You’ll also work on modern enterprise data platforms — running notebooks and lakehouse workloads in Microsoft Fabric, building pipelines and operational applications in Palantir Foundry, and deploying analytics on Azure, AWS, or GCP. The science matters, but so does making it work inside a real organization’s data ecosystem. What We Offer AI Grant — Stop talking about AI and start building it. Our AI Grant gives you dedicated budget and resources to turn your wildest AI idea into a working project, backed by two paid weeks to focus on nothing else. AI Center of Excellence — Work alongside specialists in agentic AI, sovereign AI, generative and discriminative AI. This isn’t a siloed team — it’s the people you’ll learn from and build with daily. Your tools, your choice — Full access to AI-powered development tools including Claude, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Pick what works best for you. Real project variety — From generative AI for legal document compliance through agentic systems in manufacturing environments to enterprise-scale AI platforms, computer vision, and autonomous driving. You won’t get bored. Conference and speaking support — Want to attend conferences? We’ll back you. Want to speak at them? Even better — we’ll support you with dedicated preparation time and bonuses. Your tasks Translate business problems into analytical solutions: define hypotheses, choose metrics, and select the right modeling approach for the question at hand Explore, clean, and prepare data using Python (pandas, NumPy), working with structured and semi-structured sources of varying quality Build, validate, and tune machine learning models for classification, regression, forecasting, segmentation, and recommendation using scikit-learn, XGBoost, and statsmodels Design and analyze experiments: A/B tests, statistical hypothesis testing, and causal analysis that hold up to scrutiny Work hands-on with enterprise data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric (lakehouses, notebooks, semantic models) and Palantir Foundry (pipelines, ontology, operational workflows) Communicate findings through clear visualizations, dashboards, and narratives tailored to technical and non-technical stakeholders alike Collaborate with data engineers on data availability and quality, and with ML/AI engineers to move models from notebook to production Monitor deployed models for drift and degradation, and own the retraining and improvement cycle Requirements At least 4 years in data science or applied analytics, with models and analyses that made it past the prototype stage Strong Python skills across the standard data stack (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn) Solid statistical foundations: hypothesis testing, regression, experimental design, and knowing when a result is real versus noise Knowledge of at least one cloud/data platform and its data science components — Azure (Microsoft Fabric, Azure Machine Learning), AWS (SageMaker), GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery ML), Snowflake (Snowpark ML, Cortex), Databricks (MLflow, Mosaic AI), or Palantir (Foundry Code Workspaces, Foundry ML, AIP) items.desc: The Role The Rosalind Franklin Institute (the Franklin) is a technology institute established by the UK Government as a unique centre committed to advancing tools that are needed to transform healthcare in the future. The Institute brings together researchers in life and physical sciences, and engineering, to develop a spectrum of tools which we will use to image, interpret and intervene in biological systems. These insights will speed up the discovery of new medicines, help find new diagnostics and contribute to a deeper understanding of human health and disease. Our Science Strategy seeks to focus the Franklin’s research and unite our researchers around our Technology Innovation Challenges and Life Science Challenges. For more information on the Franklin’s Challenges click here . The Grange group is developing tools that can image the 3-dimensional organisation of macromolecular complexes within brain tissues. This utilises fast vitrification of surgical biopsies and in-situ structural biology methods (cryo-focused ion beam milling, cryo lift out, electron tomography). We are seeking a motivated postdoctoral research associate who will be able to develop methods to investigate content-rich data taken from human tissue resections and reconstruct the molecular make-up of supramolecular complexes utilising quantitative approaches. The project will focus on cytoskeletal and mitochondrial changes during aging and disease. As part of this post, you will drive a project aimed at the computational reconstruction of macromolecular structures from in-situ data, pushing integration of workflows to enable the molecular sociology of cytoskeletal and mitochondrial processes to be examined in the context of aging and neurodegeneration. As part of the team, you will work with partners at Imperial, University College London and the University of Oxford to coordinate the procurement of specimens, work towards the acquisition of high-quality cryo-electron tomography data and develop structure determination pipelines capable of delivering a comprehensive overview of macromolecular organisation and diversity. Key Responsibilities As a Research Associate at the Franklin, you will bring scientific knowledge and skills to deliver a specific research project and/or you will bring independent, creative science, or specific skills to a team delivering a project or program. Through this work, you will build scientific independence, develop new science and leadership skills, and establish a growing reputation externally. You will also: Develop and streamline computational approaches to in-situ structure determination methods from tissue sources that enable an assessment of macromolecular diversity. Demonstrate leadership as part of a team working with clinicians to prepare tissues for cryo-electron tomography. Plan and conduct experiments, analyse and interpret results and supervised delivery of outputs (e.g. research reports, patent applications) in a scientific/technology area of interest. Work within a project team, contributing to wider projects around key Franklin's Challenges. Lead major contributions to research outputs including papers, patents and both internal and external presentations. Support and develop others including day-to-day supervision of students or visitors in areas related to your own research. Have supervised, staged progression to first stages of scientific independence with opportunities to further develop science and skills/experience. Enhance your research through collaboration with other researchers and make active contributions to exchange of ideas through your own network. Be able to understand, interpret, create and communicate appropriately within a research context. Develop search and discovery skills and techniques. Be supervised by a Scientist/Senior Scientist in delivery of research outputs, either in the context of a project or Franklin's Challenge or as an early career development fellow. Before submitting your application please ensure you read the Job Information Pack for full details of this role. This can be found in the careers section on the Franklin's website. This job description sets out the skills and experience we believe are needed to be able to do this job but, research also tells us women are much more likely than men to take this list of requirements as absolute and self-select out of the process. If you think you can deliver this role then we want to hear from you, regardless of the boxes you did not tick. Whilst the role requires candidates to hold a PhD/DPhil (or equivalent), we may consider candidates who have submitted their PhD/DPhil thesis, in which case the initial appointment will be made at £38,500 per annum (to be increased on completion of the PhD/DPhil qualification). items.desc: About the role The Product Intelligence Platform is a generative AI-driven system that transforms how Tesco handles product data at scale. The platform leverages multi-agent generative AI systems to automate product categorisation, enrichment and matching across a vast number of products every week, processing over 1 million events weekly on an event-driven Kafka architecture. This role sits closest to our generative AI work: prompt engineering, LLM orchestration, embeddings, scoring and evaluation. You will work alongside our Java/Spring Boot platform engineers but will spend most of your time in Python, on the services and pipelines that sit nearest to the models. A lot of this work starts as ambiguous, research-shaped problems — “is this even feasible?” — before becoming production services. You'll run feasibility studies and proofs of concept, then carry the strongest ideas through to production, working closely with product managers, data stewards and engineering peers along the way. You will be responsible for Leading generative AI feasibility studies and proofs of concept for new product intelligence capabilities (for example, image-based accuracy scoring or dynamic attribute handling), and turning promising results into production designs. Designing and building generative AI solutions that integrate large language models (Azure OpenAI GPT-4) through our GenAI Service facade, including prompt design, evaluation and iteration. Building and maintaining embedding-based similarity and scoring pipelines using PostgreSQL with pgvector. Contributing to LLM observability and evaluation practices (e.g. with Langfuse), including regression testing and drift detection as prompts and models change. Supporting Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) tooling that helps data stewards review and validate generative AI output efficiently — 100% HITL review before publication is a core control on this platform. Contributing to responsible Gen AI governance activities, including audit support and structured release criteria for prompt and model changes. Building event-driven services in Python for high-volume data processing on Kafka. Collaborating with product managers, data stewards and other engineers to translate ambiguous business problems into clear technical designs. Sharing generative AI knowledge with the wider team and contributing to upskilling. Optionally representing the team's generative AI work externally, such as at conferences or in the tech community. You will need Mandatory skills Solid, recent experience building production backend services in Python with a modern framework (FastAPI, Django, Flask or similar). Practical, hands-on experience with LLMs and prompt engineering in a production or near-production setting, not only experimentation. Experience with embeddings and vector similarity (pgvector or an equivalent vector database). Good understanding of event-driven architectures and Apache Kafka. Comfort working on ambiguous, research-shaped problems — running feasibility studies or PoCs — and then carrying them through to a shipped solution. Experience with cloud platforms, preferably Azure. Understanding of software engineering best practices, including CI/CD, testing and code review. Strong stakeholder communication skills: able to navigate ambiguity and translate it into clear requirements and implementation plans. Nice-to-have skills Experience with LLM observability and evaluation tooling (Langfuse or similar). Experience working with multi-agent systems. Familiarity with Java/Spring Boot, since the wider platform is polyglot Java/Python. Experience with Kubernetes (Azure Kubernetes Service) for container orchestration. Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform). Knowledge of the retail or e-commerce domain. Understanding of data quality and governance principles. Experience mentoring or upskilling others in applied generative AI, or involvement in hiring. Whats in it for you? Salary UoP 20 000 - 25 000 PLN gross/month Hybrid working We know life looks a little different for each of us. That’s why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about different flexible working options. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a career, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support. This role requires you to be based in or near Kraków, as you will spend 60% (3 days) of your week collaborating with colleagues at our office locations or local sites and the rest remotely. Benefits Tesco is a diverse and exciting employer, dedicated to being #aplacetogeton, providing career-defining opportunities to all of our colleagues. If you choose to join our business, we will provide you with (for all): Up to 20% yearly salary bonus – based on both individual and business performance Permanent contract from the go – as a sign of our trust in your …

items.desc: Vacatureomschrijving Een klant helpen een passende outfit te kiezen. Informatie uit documenten begrijpen. Een toepassing gecontroleerd acties laten uitvoeren in onze systemen. Als AI Engineer bij Omoda Brands bouw je de AI-functionaliteit die dit mogelijk maakt. Je zorgt dat die in productie betrouwbaar doet wat ze moet doen. Wat een AI Engineer bij ons is Jouw expertise zit in de AI ín de toepassing. Je kiest en combineert bestaande modellen en bouwt de retrieval, context, tool use en controles eromheen. Je begrijpt hoe die keuzes doorwerken in kwaliteit, snelheid, betrouwbaarheid en kosten. Je ontwikkelt vooral met bestaande taal- en beeldmodellen. Waar gerichte fine-tuning waarde toevoegt, werk je samen met het datateam. Je werkt aan klantgerichte toepassingen, zoals onze AI Stylist en aan AI die interne processen ondersteunt of taken uitvoert. Wat je doet Je bouwt AI-functionaliteit die informatie begrijpt, antwoorden of content genereert en gecontroleerd acties uitvoert. Je combineert modellen, bedrijfsdata, retrieval en tools tot werkende toepassingen. Je ontwikkelt, deployt en beheert de services en API’s achter die toepassingen. Je zet evaluaties op en behandelt prompts en configuraties als geversioneerde, geteste onderdelen. Je bouwt logging, monitoring, foutafhandeling en terugvalopties vanaf het begin in. Je zorgt voor duidelijke grenzen aan wat een toepassing zelfstandig mag doen en wanneer menselijke beoordeling nodig is. Je bewaakt en verbetert kwaliteit, betrouwbaarheid, snelheid en kosten in productie. Je bouwt mee aan gedeelde AI-voorzieningen die het team kan hergebruiken. Functie-eisen Je bent een medior of senior software-engineer en hebt AI- of LLM-toepassingen in productie gebracht. Je kunt betrouwbare backendservices en API’s bouwen, deployen en beheren. Je hebt praktische ervaring met bijvoorbeeld retrieval, tool use, agents of multimodale modellen. Je begrijpt embeddings, contextmanagement en de afwegingen rond fine-tuning. Je weet hoe je systemen test waarvan de uitkomst niet iedere keer identiek is. Je werkt met Python of een vergelijkbare backendtaal en hebt ervaring met een cloudplatform. Je gebruikt coding agents en beoordeelt hun output kritisch. Je kunt technische keuzes helder uitleggen. Voor deze functie is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal vereist. Je hoeft niet ieder model of framework te kennen. Sterke software-engineering, productie-ervaring en het vermogen om nieuwe technologie te doorgronden vinden we belangrijker. Aanvullende informatie Je team Je werkt in het AI-team, samen met AI Product Builders en AI Specialists, en werkt intensief samen met IT en data. AI Product Builders bouwen interne software met behulp van coding agents. AI Specialists passen AI toe binnen hun vakgebied en helpen de inhoudelijke kwaliteit beoordelen. Jij brengt de engineeringexpertise voor de AI-functionaliteit en de technische werking daarvan in productie. Security, privacy en verantwoord datagebruik zijn gezamenlijke verantwoordelijkheden. Over Omoda Brands Omoda Brands is het huis achter Assem, Omoda, Wehkamp en Kleertjes.com. Vier merken, ruim 2.000 collega’s en meer dan 3 miljoen klanten per jaar. Onze ambitie is de meest persoonlijke boutique op schaal. Een winkelervaring waarin we klanten helpen kiezen op basis van hun smaak, wensen en situatie. Daar werken we al aan. Onze AI Stylist stelt outfits samen in een gesprek, we maken productbeelden met AI en onze webchat handelt een deel van de klantvragen af. Ook intern bouwen collega’s toepassingen voor campagnes, content en planning. Wat je bij ons vindt Flexibel werken vanuit Zierikzee, Amsterdam of Zwolle. We komen gemiddeld 1 à 2 dagen per week samen op één van deze locaties. 32–38 uur per week, afhankelijk van jouw voorkeur. Een passend salaris op basis van jouw kennis, ervaring en de waarde die je meebrengt. Concrete AI-toepassingen waarop je kunt voortbouwen. Technisch eigenaarschap, van ontwerp tot werking in productie. Ruimte voor technische keuzes en verdieping. De schaal van vier merken en direct contact met de collega’s die jouw werk gebruiken. Een rol die we op medior- of seniorniveau kunnen invullen. Interesse? Laat ons zien of vertel wat je hebt gebouwd en vooral hoe je daartoe kwam. Welk probleem loste je op, wat was jouw eigen bijdrage en welke technische keuzes maakte je? Hoe controleerde je of de AI goed werkte, en wat leerde je nadat de toepassing live ging? Hoe je dit deelt is aan jou: een korte beschrijving, link, screenshots of demo. Een beknopt voorbeeld is voldoende voor je sollicitatie; in het gesprek gaan we er samen dieper op in. Vertrouwelijke code of bedrijfsinformatie hoef je niet te delen.

items.desc: Are you looking for a new challenge? Fancy helping us shape the future of motor insurance? Prima could be the place for you. Since 2015, we’ve been using our love of data and tech to rethink motor insurance and bring drivers a great experience at a great price. Our story began in Italy, where we’ve quickly become the number one online motor insurance provider. In fact, we’re trusted by over 5 million drivers. And now we’re expanding to help millions more drivers in the UK and Spain. To help fuel that growth, we need a Data Scientist to join our Anti Fraud Team. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to tackle fraud, one of the most impactful and fast-evolving challenges in insurance. You will do this from a global perspective. In fact, the team is responsible for detecting fraudulent claims across all Prima markets: the UK, Spain and Italy. You’ll collaborate with engineers, claims handlers and business leaders to improve the detection of fraud, directly influencing real-world fraud decisions with impact on the company’s bottom line measured in millions. This is a highly practical area of work where strong business judgment is just as important as technical expertise. Excited to make an impact? Here are the details What You’ll Do Design and improve fraud detection systems that prioritize high-risk claims, optimizing the trade-off between detection accuracy and operational efficiency Collaborate across teams and functions, working closely with fraud analysts, engineers, and product managers Develop deep expertise in fraud dynamics, identifying emerging fraud patterns, understanding how they evolve across the insurance lifecycle, and translating these insights into effective detection and prevention strategies, for example identifying suspicious networks of related claims, synthetic entities, or anomalous behavioral patterns What We’re Looking For Extensive experience (3+ years) in data science or applied machine learning, leading end-to-end initiatives in complex technical domains and delivering measurable business impact Strong analytical and quantitative mindset able to translate data into insights, assess model performance, and guide decision-making with evidence and clarity Structured problem solver skilled at framing ambiguous challenges, defining success metrics, and communicating results to both technical and non-technical audiences Strong Python programming skills, especially in the data domain, and fluent use of Git Knowledge of Spark, SQL or any other data-oriented programming language and proficiency with standard data wrangling and modeling libraries (Pandas, Sklearn, Keras, XGBoost, LightGBM, etc.) Nice-to-Have Experience in analytical fraud detection in the Insurance, Finance or Law Enforcement domain In-depth knowledge of graph databases (Neo4j, AWS Neptune) and analytics (NetworkX, GNN) or explainability applied to anomaly detection Knowledge of BI tools (Tableau or similar) €45,000 - €65,000 a year Why you’ll love it here We want to make Prima a happy and empowering place to work. So if you decide to join us, you can expect plenty of perks. 💵 Competitive compensation: We offer a performance-based bonus of up to 5% of the fixed salary for this position. 🤸 Work Your Way: Enjoy hybrid working, with a mix of home and office days. Plus, for up to 30 days per year, work from anywhere. 🏁 Grow with us: We may move fast at Prima, but we move together. Get access to learning resources, mentorship and a growth plan tailored to you. 🌈 Thrive and perform: Your best work begins when you feel your best. Enjoy private healthcare, gym discounts, wellbeing programs and mental health support. Think you’re a match? Apply now. At Prima, we celebrate uniqueness. If you don’t meet every requirement but are passionate about this role, we still want to hear from you. Innovation thrives on diverse perspectives. Prima is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Need accommodations during the process? Email us at accessible.recruiting@prima.it. Let’s build the future of insurance, together.

items.desc: Data Science Graduate Contract type: Permanent Location: Hatfield (Hybrid working – 3 days in the office) Working hours per week: 40 hours Level: Entry level – Graduate Starting Salary: £32,000 Application Closing Date: Sunday 1st November 2026 Scheme commences: September 2027 About Us Our mission is to deliver joy in every shop, through unbeatable choice, unrivalled service, and reassuringly good value. We’re Ocado Retail , a market-leading joint venture between Ocado Group and M&S, and the world’s largest dedicated online supermarket, ocado.com . Not only is Ocado.com the only place to shop a full range of M&S food online, it’s also the home to the widest online supermarket range in the UK and champion of small, independent brands. We’re also the brains behind Zoom by Ocado , our same-day grocery delivery service. About The Team And The Role Data is core to our decision making, and we have one of the richest datasets in the industry. The Data Science team develops models which turn our data into actionable insights. It is our mission to leverage data to give the best value and experience to our customers and suppliers whilst increasing profitability and growth for Ocado Retail. The Data Science team is responsible for understanding the complexities in the data, generating appropriate models to answer business questions, and delivering the outputs of these models to stakeholders in diverse areas of the business. It is our responsibility to work across functions to productionise these models so they are available to the right people, any time they need them. This could be in the form of a data table with the outputs of the model, or developing an interface to allow users to interact with the data in a way that allows them to leverage models for their specific needs. We also develop multi-agent AI systems to solve for complicated workflows. This means that we have to truly understand the business users, their needs and the goals they are trying to achieve in order to create AI systems that can deliver value for those users. To do this we have to understand the art of the possible with AI, and have to keep up with an ever changing AI technology space. Our remit is to apply statistics, machine learning and artificial intelligence to our data at scale. To do this we use Python, SQL, and the Google Cloud Platform (GCP). We are cross-functional by design, working with stakeholders across the business with varying degrees of technical expertise, meaning communicating complex ideas is core to the success of the Data Science team. What You’ll Do This scheme is about learning how we apply data science in Ocado Retail. The majority of your time will be spent in the Data Science team, owning projects from start to finish with responsibility for managing stakeholders and delivery of data science solutions with support from the wider team. This will allow you to continue to develop your Python and SQL skills to answer business questions. There will be opportunities to rotate into other areas of the business and explore analytics, insight and data engineering with Ocado Retail. You will be given support and guidance from the Data Science team in scoping out data science projects, developing novel solutions and delivering these to key stakeholders. A typical project involves researching a business question within the context of scientific literature, identifying relevant data sources, developing models that provide an answer to the question, and delivering this to our internal stakeholders. Throughout this process there is clear communication of progress of the project to the wider team, alongside our stakeholders. You will be taught our coding standards, and will be producing production-ready code by the end of the programme. At the end of the programme you will have a rounded knowledge base of how data is used in the organisation, and how to apply statistical approaches to improve our service for customers and suppliers. Placements in other teams will be aimed at broadening your awareness of what goes into data driven decision making. They may involve: Working in an analyst team within insight for 6 months in either Marketing, Category, Operations, Forecasting, Customer Research, Web Merchandising, or Trading (Range, Pricing, and Promotions). Delivery of key analytic projects for the designated team and the wider business. Build relationships with analyst colleagues and understand different data needs throughout the business. Working with Data Engineering for an expanded understanding of how data is processed, prepared and used in the wider business. In addition to your core scheme, you will have the opportunity for cross-functional rotations to gain broader business exposure outside of your primary discipline. Skilled in logical …

items.title: Research Associate In Translational Radiobiology
items.card: You will support a Prostate Cancer UK funded project investigating extracellular matrix remodelling in prostate cancer radioresistance and the development of non-invasive urinary biomarkers to monitor treatment response. You will be responsible for: Conduct individual and collaborative research projects. Develop research objectives and proposals for own or joint research, with the assistance of a mentor if required.
items.desc: We are seeking a motivated and collaborative individual to join our team as a Research Associate in Translational Radiobiology. This is an outstanding opportunity to work within the Translational Radiobiology group under the supervision of Professor Ananya Choudhury at Manchester Cancer Research Centre. You will support a Prostate Cancer UK funded project investigating extracellular matrix remodelling in prostate cancer radioresistance and the development of non-invasive urinary biomarkers to monitor treatment response. You will be responsible for: Conduct individual and collaborative research projects. Develop research objectives and proposals for own or joint research, with the assistance of a mentor if required. Use creativity to analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes. Prepare proposals and applications to external bodies, e.g. for funding and contractual purposes. Plan and manage own research activity in collaboration with others. We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work. About You We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate: Essential Criteria Have, or be about to obtain, a relevant PhD (or equivalent) Specialist knowledge in the discipline oncology, radiobiology or radiotherapy Experience in research methods and techniques in molecular biology assays, specifically RNA/DNA extraction and real time PCR assay, Western blots, Immunofluorescence Experience of working on clinical research projects involving collection and processing of human liquid and tissue samples Experience in cell culture and excellent aseptic techniques Desirable Criteria Experience of undergraduate or masters project supervision Experience working in research related to prostate cancer Experience working on clinical research projects Specialist knowledge in the field of radiotherapy Experience in RNAseq, Genomics and/or proteomics (such as Mass Spectrometry) We value transferable skills and real-world experience as much as formal qualifications. Our benefits include: Generous employer contribution pension 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure Ride to work and EV car scheme available For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here. We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy. Enquiries About The Role, Shortlisting And Interviews Name: Professor Ananya Choudhury / Dr Luisa Vanesa Biolatti Email Address: ananya.choudhury@manchester.ac.uk / luisa.biolatti@manchester.ac.uk General enquiries and administrative support recruitmentservices.people@manchester.ac.uk Technical and job portal support https://jobseekersupport.jobtrain.co.uk/support/home Applications close at midnight on the closing date. items.desc: Job title: Machine Learning Engineer Locations: Manchester or Haywards Heath (hybrid working) Role Overview Markerstudy Group are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help take leading-edge and novel insurance risk modelling and pricing techniques and participate in creating fully automated machine learning pipelines. Markerstudy is a leading provider of private insurance in the UK, insuring around 5% of the private cars on the UK roads, 20% of commercial vehicles and over 30% of motorcycles in total premium levels of circa £1 billion. Most of Markerstudy’s business is written as the insurance pricing provider behind household names such as Tesco, Sainsbury’s, O2, Halifax, AA, Saga and Lloyds Bank to list a few. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will use your skills to: Tune machine learning methods to best leverage our state-of-the-art processing capabilities Deploy and maintain machine learning methods in a DevOps / MLOps based machine learning environment Create robust high-quality code using test-driven development (TDD) techniques and adhering to the SOLID coding standards Your work will enable sustained improvements to products, prices and processes giving Markerstudy a critical advantage in the increasingly competitive insurance market by minimizing the development to deployment and monitoring stages of the ML lifecycle through automation. You will also be responsible for refining, tuning, deploying and maintaining machine learning methods in our machine learning pipeline by using robust test-driven development (TDD) approaches to maximise performance and robustness, and improve company performance and our customer-centric offerings across Motor, Home and Commercial Lines businesses. The successful candidate will also enjoy opportunities for leading, coaching, and mentoring more junior ML Engineers. Key Responsibilities: Report and communicate with Senior Stakeholders, such as the Head of Data Science and Machine Learning and Director of Technical Underwriting Propose, proof-of-concept, develop, and deliver novel machine learning processes that automate current manual processes, and leverage DevOps and MLOps software. Work in a collaborative environment with data science to help deploy machine learning methods that are state-of-the-art, robust, and future extensible. Tune machine learning methods for optimal performance. Deploy and maintain machine learning methods in our machine learning pipeline using robust test-driven development (TDD) coding approaches, using the SOLID software development principles. Actively contribute to creating a culture of coding and data excellence Implement efficient solutions across a range of markets, including Private Motor, Commercial Vehicle, Bike, Taxi, and Home Lead and mentor junior machine learning engineers and share best practices Key Skills and Experience: Previous experience in tuning and deploying machine learning methods Experience with some of the following predictive modelling techniques; Logistic Regression, GBMs, Elastic Net GLMs, GAMs, Decision Trees, Random Forests, Neural Nets and Clustering Experience in DevOps and Azure ML, or other MLOps and ML Lifecycle technology stacks, such as AWS, Databricks, Google Cloud, etc. Experience with deploying services in Docker and Kubernetes Experience in creating production grade coding and SOLID programming principles, including test-driven development (TDD) approaches Experience in programming languages (e.g. Python, PySpark, R, SAS, SQL) Experience in source-control software, e.g., GitHub Proficient at communicating results in a concise manner both verbally and written Experience in data and model monitoring is a plus Behaviours: A high level of professional/academic excellence, educated to at least a master’s level in a STEM-based or DS / ML / AI / or mathematical discipline Collaborative and team player Logical thinker with a professional and positive attitude Passion to innovate and improve processes

items.desc: We’re looking for data scientists who turn ambiguous business questions into models and analyses that actually get used. You’ll frame the problem, wrangle the data, build and validate models, and — just as importantly — explain what the numbers mean to people who don’t speak Python. Your day-to-day will revolve around the classic Python data stack: pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. You’ll also work on modern enterprise data platforms — running notebooks and lakehouse workloads in Microsoft Fabric, building pipelines and operational applications in Palantir Foundry, and deploying analytics on Azure, AWS, or GCP. The science matters, but so does making it work inside a real organization’s data ecosystem. What We Offer AI Grant — Stop talking about AI and start building it. Our AI Grant gives you dedicated budget and resources to turn your wildest AI idea into a working project, backed by two paid weeks to focus on nothing else. AI Center of Excellence — Work alongside specialists in agentic AI, sovereign AI, generative and discriminative AI. This isn’t a siloed team — it’s the people you’ll learn from and build with daily. Your tools, your choice — Full access to AI-powered development tools including Claude, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Pick what works best for you. Real project variety — From generative AI for legal document compliance through agentic systems in manufacturing environments to enterprise-scale AI platforms, computer vision, and autonomous driving. You won’t get bored. Conference and speaking support — Want to attend conferences? We’ll back you. Want to speak at them? Even better — we’ll support you with dedicated preparation time and bonuses. Your tasks Translate business problems into analytical solutions: define hypotheses, choose metrics, and select the right modeling approach for the question at hand Explore, clean, and prepare data using Python (pandas, NumPy), working with structured and semi-structured sources of varying quality Build, validate, and tune machine learning models for classification, regression, forecasting, segmentation, and recommendation using scikit-learn, XGBoost, and statsmodels Design and analyze experiments: A/B tests, statistical hypothesis testing, and causal analysis that hold up to scrutiny Work hands-on with enterprise data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric (lakehouses, notebooks, semantic models) and Palantir Foundry (pipelines, ontology, operational workflows) Communicate findings through clear visualizations, dashboards, and narratives tailored to technical and non-technical stakeholders alike Collaborate with data engineers on data availability and quality, and with ML/AI engineers to move models from notebook to production Monitor deployed models for drift and degradation, and own the retraining and improvement cycle Requirements At least 4 years in data science or applied analytics, with models and analyses that made it past the prototype stage Strong Python skills across the standard data stack (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn) Solid statistical foundations: hypothesis testing, regression, experimental design, and knowing when a result is real versus noise Knowledge of at least one cloud/data platform and its data science components — Azure (Microsoft Fabric, Azure Machine Learning), AWS (SageMaker), GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery ML), Snowflake (Snowpark ML, Cortex), Databricks (MLflow, Mosaic AI), or Palantir (Foundry Code Workspaces, Foundry ML, AIP) Ability to communicate analytical results clearly to business stakeholders and influence decisions with data Familiarity with working autonomously while collaborating effectively with data engineers, architects, and product teams Fluent English, both written and spoken Fluent Polish required Residing in Poland required Nice to have Production experience with Microsoft Fabric or Palantir Foundry certification (Foundry Data Engineer / Data Scientist tracks) Experience with time series forecasting, NLP, recommender systems, or exposure to LLM-based workflows Familiarity with MLOps practices: MLflow, experiment tracking, model versioning, and CI/CD for ML Experience with Power BI or other BI tools, and distributed processing with Spark/PySpark Job no.
