Are you interested in applying scientific research to real-world challenges in CO₂ transport, storage, and emissions measurement?
 In this role, you will investigate chemical processes relevant to CO₂ systems and the measurement of methane, hydrogen, and CO₂ emissions. Working alongside scientists, engineers, and consultants, you will turn experimental research into practical insights that can support the development of industry standards, measurement methodologies, and new technologies for a lower-carbon future.
 What you’ll do 
 Lead and carry out experimental research on chemical reactions in CO₂ systems.
 Plan and conduct measurement activities related to methane, hydrogen and CO₂ emissions.
 Design experiments and develop new test and measurement methods.
 Analyse and interpret complex experimental datasets.
 Translate scientific findings into practical recommendations and technical solutions.
 Prepare clear technical reports, scientific publications and presentations.
 Present research findings at conferences and other technical forums.
 Collaborate with scientists, engineers, consultants and customers on multidisciplinary projects.
 Contribute your technical expertise to the development of new projects and future work.
What we offer: 
 You will benefit from the support that comes from being part of a large and experienced community of auditors,
 Wide range of benefits: flexible working hours, pension scheme, profit share bonus,
 Calibration workshops for auditors,
 Very varied working weeks – your workday is never the same,
DNV is an Equal Opportunity Employer and gives consideration for employment to qualified applicants without regard to gender, religion, race, national or ethnic origin, cultural background, social group, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age or political opinion. Diversity is fundamental to our culture and we invite you to be part of this diversity.
About you 
 We are looking for someone who brings:
 Doctoral-level qualification or equivalent specialist expertise in emissions measurement, chemical sciences, or a closely related field.
 Experience working with CO₂ composition, CO₂ systems, or emissions measurement.
 Experience designing experiments and interpreting complex scientific or technical data.
 Ability to communicate technical findings clearly through reports, publications, or presentations.
 Experience working collaboratively in multidisciplinary technical or scientific environments.
 Experience working with customers or other external stakeholders.
 Experience contributing to technical project development or new project opportunities.

items.desc: Are you interested in semiconductor fabrication and 3D integration and looking for a new job opportunity in the field? Would you like to develop innovative technology with superb colleagues who are top experts in their field? Do you want to build an excellent science career and work at the interface of academy and industry? VTT is one of the leading applied research organisations in Europe. What unites us are curiosity, a passion for learning and a purpose: to solve the biggest challenges of our time and turn them into sustainable growth and well-being. Our cross-disciplinary community of over 2300 brilliant minds is focused on creating impact through science-based innovation. Get to know us further by exploring VTT's tech & infra . We are now looking for Research Scientist or Research Engineer for 3D integration with a strong background in semiconductor device fabrication or process integration. You identify and solve problems independently and creatively, while working closely and flexibly with a team of experts. You focus on the design and fabrication aspects of developing processes for 3D integration of CMOS and semiconductor devices. You understand the big picture and participate in the concept development. Our team develops advanced semiconductor components focused on more than Moore applications such as CMOS integrated 2D sensors, in-memory analog computing, and post-CMOS 3D integration. The developments are made in close collaboration with our academic partners along the lines agreed with our industrial partners. Your responsibilities as Research Scientist / Research Engineer: Development and characterization of processes for monolithic and heterogeneous integration for post-CMOS integration Solving complex fabrication challenges Communicating and solving the problems in tight collaboration with others at VTT Who we are looking for: Experience in semiconductor process integration and 3D technologies You have a MSc or PhD in physics, electronics, or closely similar field. You have experience in cleanroom fabrication Excellent communications skills in English are required. As a person, we hope that you are: You have strong communication and collaboration skills. You are able to efficiently interact with your colleagues and with people from different fields. An enthusiastic outside-the-box thinker. You enjoy challenges and learning new things and have a strong passion for science and research and development A further benefit is knowledge about the interactions between research and business With VTT, you’ll enjoy: / What we offer you: Visionary work in technology. We offer positions at the cutting-edge of technology and engineering from next generation microelectronics and quantum technology to automation and robotics, energy systems and more. Our research agenda is dedicated to creating sustainable growth by solving systemic and technological challenges, so your work will go towards creating real, positive impact. Read more about our strategy – the path of exponential hope. Fascinating projects, excellent research environment. Our researchers get to work on a combination of cutting-edge academic research and applied customer projects, both locally and internationally. At VTT, you’ll have state-of-the-art research facilities at your disposal, such as Micronova, the Finnish research infrastructure for micro-, nano- and quantum technologies. Great career opportunities, superb colleagues. At VTT, excellence in research is a strategic priority. We offer long-term positions and stable career paths in top-level research. People tend to stay with us over 10 years since there are always new roles and responsibilities to grow into. Collaborating in a cross-disciplinary community with superb colleagues is a source of learning, inspiration, and fun. Read more about our organisational culture as the builder of the world's most meaningful place to work. Support for your well-being. Our people are our main asset, so we take good care of them. We aim to nurture great team spirit and leadership and offer versatile well-being services to enable a good work–life balance. On top of 6 weeks of paid holidays, we offer exercise and culture benefits, hobby clubs, and voluntary well-being services such as meditation programmes and trainings on cognitive ergonomics. Apply now and join our community of brilliant minds! Please send your CV with your salary request via our recruitment system as soon as possible but at the latest by 15 November 2026 Interested and want to hear more? For further information, please contact Research Team Leader Olli-Pekka Kilpi by email (olli-pekka.kilpi@vtt.fi). We look forward to hearing from you! items.desc: #StormYourCareer Rejoins STORM GROUP et construis ta carrière avec nous ! Détecte les menaces invisibles et révolutionne l?analyse comportementale du SOCAu sein du Security Operations Center (SOC) d?un grand compte, nous recherchons un(e) Data Scientist Cybersécurité / SOC. Ton rôle consistera à renforcer les capacités de détection des cybermenaces par l?exploitation avancée des données de sécurité, en concevant des modèles prédictifs et d?analyse comportementale pour isoler les signaux faibles et optimiser la réponse aux incidents. Ton futur environnementTu évolueras au c?ur du Security Operations Center d?une infrastructure d?envergure. En interface directe avec les analystes SOC, les ingénieurs SIEM et les spécialistes de la Threat Intelligence, tu interviendras sur des flux massifs de journaux d?événements. C?est le cadre idéal pour appliquer le Machine Learning et la Data Science à la lutte contre les cyberattaques, tout en industrialisant des modèles au sein d?architectures de données distribuées. Tes missions clésModélisation & Détection Avancée des Menaces (Mode DATA & IA) : Concevoir, développer et entraîner des modèles de détection d?anomalies sur des volumétries massives de journaux de sécurité (logs réseau, système, identité et applicatifs). Développer et déployer des algorithmes d?analyse comportementale des utilisateurs et des entités (UEBA) pour identifier les compromissions de comptes et les mouvements latéraux. Mettre en ?uvre des modèles de scoring et de priorisation dynamique des alertes afin de réduire le bruit et le taux de faux positifs pour les analystes. Réaliser l?ingénierie des caractéristiques (feature engineering) sur des jeux de données complexes et fortement déséquilibrés. Évaluer rigoureusement les performances des modèles à l?aide de métriques adaptées à la détection d?intrusions (précision, rappel, ROC-AUC, taux de faux positifs). Industrialisation & Collaboration SOC (Mode RUN & MLOps) : Assurer l?industrialisation, le déploiement et le monitoring continu des modèles en production (MLflow, Docker, Kubernetes). Collaborer au quotidien avec les analystes SOC et les équipes d?investigation pour qualifier les détections et réinjecter les retours terrain dans l?entraînement des algorithmes. Mener une veille active sur les nouvelles techniques d?attaque répertoriées dans le cadre de référence MITRE ATT&CK. Ton profilFormation : Diplôme d?Ingénieur ou Bac+5 en Data Science, statistiques, informatique décisionnelle ou cybersécurité. Expérience : Tu justifies d?une expérience de 3 à 5 ans en Data Science et Machine Learning, idéalement appliquée aux cas d?usage de la cybersécurité ou de la détection de fraude. Expertise Data Science & IA Impérative : Maîtrise des algorithmes de détection d?anomalies (Isolation Forest, autoencodeurs, One-Class SVM) et de l?apprentissage sur données déséquilibrées. Pratique confirmée de l?écosystème Python Data Science (Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch, pandas, numpy). Culture Cybersécurité & Données Massives : Bonne compréhension du fonctionnement d?un SOC, des typologies de menaces et de la matrice MITRE ATT&CK. Connaissance des architectures distribuées et des outils volumétriques (SQL, Spark, Kafka). Familiarité avec les solutions SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Microsoft Sentinel) et le suivi de cycle de vie ML (MLflow). Langues : Anglais professionnel opérationnel. Tes atoutsEsprit d?Analyse et Goût pour l?Investigation : Curiosité intellectuelle pour traquer les anomalies statistiques au sein de flux de données brutes. Rigueur Méthodologique : Précision scientifique indispensable dans la validation des métriques de détection et la gestion des faux positifs. Sens du Travail d?Équipe : Aisance relationnelle pour vulgariser les choix algorithmiques auprès des analystes sécurité opérationnels. Nos avantagesRemboursement des titres de transport à hauteur de 75%. Tickets restaurant pris en charge par STORM GROUP à hauteur de 50% (10,5? / jour). Accès Gymlib / Wellpass (sport et bien-être). Contrat Santé / Prévoyance mis en place auprès de la compagnie Alan. Formation continue : Accès à Udemy Business. Prime de cooptation, prime d?intéressement et de participation. Deux à trois jours de télétravail par semaine. 5 raisons de nous rejoindreParcours sur mesure : Co-construis une trajectoire professionnelle unique, adaptée à tes ambitions. Missions Stratégiques : Interviens sur des projets d?envergure, en parfaite cohérence avec ton expertise. Suivi Dédié : Bénéficie d?un pilotage annuel structuré pour garantir ta progression continue. Excellence Continue : Développe tes compétences au quotidien au sein d?un écosystème exigeant. Performance Durable : Évolue dans un cadre où l?exigence métier respecte ton équilibre de vie.

items.title: Ingénieur·e de recherche en IA et data science pour la R&D et l’industrie F/H
items.card: vos missions seront les suivantes : Identifier, cadrer et mener des projets de recherche appliquée en IA et data science. Concevoir, développer et évaluer des agents IA experts et des architectures agentiques capables de mobiliser des connaissances scientifiques, de raisonner sur des problématiques métier et d’utiliser des outils, des modèles et des sources de données pour assister les workflows de recherche :
items.desc: Pourquoi a-t-on besoin de vous ? Au sein de la R&D de Saint-Gobain, l’équipe de Data Science développe et déploie des approches d’intelligence artificielle au service des activités scientifiques et industrielles du Groupe. L’équipe combine des compétences en analyse de données, statistiques, machine learning, IA générative, systèmes agentiques et graphes de connaissances pour accélérer la compréhension des phénomènes, la capitalisation des connaissances, la conception des matériaux et des procédés, ainsi que la transformation des pratiques de R&D. Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront les suivantes : Identifier, cadrer et mener des projets de recherche appliquée en IA et data science. Concevoir, développer et évaluer des agents IA experts et des architectures agentiques capables de mobiliser des connaissances scientifiques, de raisonner sur des problématiques métier et d’utiliser des outils, des modèles et des sources de données pour assister les workflows de recherche : recherche bibliographique, génération d’hypothèses, expérimentation, simulation, aide à la décision et production de livrables. Développer des méthodes d’analyse de données et de machine learning adaptées aux données scientifiques et industrielles : statistiques, apprentissage supervisé et non supervisé, modèles probabilistes, optimisation, séries temporelles, traitement d’images ou de signaux. Développer des prototypes robustes et sécurisés avec les équipes scientifiques et IT, en intégrant les usages afin de favoriser leur adoption et la transformation IA de la R&D. Assurer une veille scientifique et technologique, valoriser les résultats et développer des collaborations avec les équipes du Groupe et des partenaires académiques. Des déplacements ponctuels de courte durée sont à prévoir en France et à l’étranger (visites d’usines, conférences, formations…). *** Within Saint-Gobain’s R&D division, the Data Science team develops and deploys artificial intelligence approaches to support the Group’s scientific and industrial activities. The team combines expertise in data analysis, statistics, machine learning, generative AI, agentic systems, and knowledge graphs to accelerate the understanding of phenomena, knowledge capitalization, the design of materials and processes, and the transformation of R&D practices. In this role, your responsibilities will include : Identifying, scoping, and leading applied research projects in AI and data science. Designing, developing, and evaluating expert AI agents and agentic architectures capable of leveraging scientific knowledge, reasoning through business challenges, and utilizing tools, models, and data sources to support research workflows—such as literature reviews, hypothesis generation, experimentation, simulation, decision support, and the production of deliverables. Developing data analysis and machine learning methods tailored to scientific and industrial data, including statistics, supervised and unsupervised learning, probabilistic models, optimization, time-series analysis, and image or signal processing. Developing robust, secure prototypes in collaboration with scientific and IT teams, incorporating user needs to foster adoption and drive the AI transformation of R&D. Monitoring scientific and technological trends, showcasing results, and developing collaborations with Group teams and academic partners. Occasional short-term travel within France and abroad is to be expected (e.g., for plant visits, conferences, or training). Ce poste est-il fait pour vous ? Doctorat dans une discipline scientifique avec une forte composante en machine learning / IA, ou doctorat en ML/IA appliqué à des données et problématiques scientifiques ou industrielles. Les candidatures présentant un autre parcours, avec une expérience significative en recherche appliquée, seront également étudiées. Vous avez une bonne compréhension des modèles de langage et de leurs usages. Une première expérience du développement d’agents IA, de systèmes multi-agents ou de l’évaluation de LLM est appréciée, sans être indispensable. Vous maîtrisez Python et les bonnes pratiques de développement ; une familiarité avec le cloud Azure est un plus. Vous êtes à l’aise pour contribuer à plusieurs projets, travailler avec autonomie, proposer des orientations et communiquer clairement avec des interlocutrices et interlocuteurs scientifiques, techniques ou non spécialistes. L’entraide, l’écoute et la coopération font partie de votre manière de travailler. Atouts supplémentaires : une connaissance ou un intérêt pour les graphes de connaissances, le product management et l’expérience utilisateur. Vous maîtrisez le français et l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. Nous savons qu’une candidature ne correspond pas toujours à 100 % des critères. items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle Le centre Inria de Lyon est le 9ème centre de recherche Inria. Créé en janvier 2022, il regroupe environ 410 personnes au sein de 20 équipes de recherche et des services supports à la recherche. Ses équipes sont localisées à Villeurbanne, à Lyon Gerland, Lyon Bron ainsi qu’à Saint-Etienne. Le centre de Lyon est présent dans les domaines du logiciel, du calcul distribué et haute performance, des systèmes embarqués, du calcul quantique et de respect de la vie privée dans le monde numérique, mais aussi de la santé et de la biologie numériques. Contexte et atouts du poste Dans le cadre d’un partenariat : collaboration entre le programme Inria Startup Studio (centre Inria de Lyon) et le projet de startup Camly AI. L’objectif est de développer et évaluer des modèles vision-langage et un prototype de surveillance fonctionnant sur les caméras existantes , plus particulièrement dédiés à la détection de situations à risque qui persistent dans les entrepôts logistiques (issues de secours encombrées, allées obstruées, équipements de sécurité rendus inaccessibles), sans reconnaissance faciale ni suivi des personnes . Déplacements : des déplacements ponctuels sont prévus vers les sites pilotes de la région lyonnaise et pour présenter les travaux en conférence. Les frais de déplacement seront pris en charge dans la limite du barème en vigueur. Mission confiée Missions : Avec l’aide du fondateur de Camly AI (Oussama MESSAI, docteur en vision par ordinateur), la personne recrutée sera amenée à construire un protocole d’évaluation des modèles vision-langage (VLM) sur des tâches de surveillance de sécurité, et à constituer des jeux de données publics et réels d’entrepôts conformes au RGPD. Collaboration : La personne recrutée sera en lien avec le fondateur de Camly AI, qui définit la feuille de route produit et les besoins des clients, pour transformer les résultats de recherche en améliorations concrètes du produit. Elle travaillera aussi avec les sites pilotes, qui fournissent les conditions réelles d’usage, pour valider le système sur de vraies images de vidéosurveillance. L’équipe d’Inria Startup Studio accompagne le projet, et la CPPI d’Inria est consultée pour la propriété intellectuelle. Responsabilités : La personne recrutée a la charge du banc d’évaluation des VLM (tâches de référence, métriques, comparaison des modèles), du fine-tuning des modèles open-weight et de la qualité des jeux de données. Le cas échéant, elle encadrera aussi des stagiaires. Recenser, sélectionner et ré-annoter des jeux de données publics de vidéosurveillance, puis constituer un jeu de données réel d’entrepôts conforme au RGPD. items.desc: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. AI is a key investment area for Kraken Technologies. You’ll join Autonomous Agents , the team building AI-powered customer service for the energy industry. We connect conversational AI to Kraken’s customer platform so agents can do more than answer questions: they can use account information and approved tools to resolve real customer needs, like understanding a bill or submitting a meter reading, and hand over to a person, with full context, when it matters. We’re launching autonomous agents with our utilities clients and the demand is growing quickly. The team is moving from initial trials to long-term production use, and we’re scaling from client-specific builds to a reusable product that can serve many clients. We’re growing the team to make that happen. Where you'll fit in: You’ll join a cross-functional team of around 10 engineers, alongside product and machine learning specialists, working closely with Kraken platform teams. The work spans two connected areas, and you’ll contribute to both: Build: the reusable core of the product. This covers client-agnostic agent journeys and tooling, MCP interfaces into Kraken, email, messaging and voice capabilities, and the observability, feature toggles and guardrails that let us roll out safely. Implementation: taking that core to individual clients. You’ll work with client teams to understand their customer journeys, configure and extend what we’ve built, and feed what you learn back into the shared product. This is a hands-on engineering role. You’ll work alongside senior engineers and leads who will support your growth, while owning meaningful pieces of work from the first few months. What you'll own: Connect the dots: Investigate customer support queries, get to grips with regulatory and business processes, and turn them into clear technical plans. Bring agents to life: Build integrations between Kraken, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces and our AI agent setup, using Python on the Kraken side and TypeScript on the agent side. Build once, reuse everywhere: Spot patterns across customer journeys and client needs, and turn them into reusable, client-agnostic components rather than one-off fixes. Make it safe and reliable: Build authentication, permissions, validation and human handoff into the design, and help us test and monitor behaviour that is less predictable than traditional software. Roll out with confidence: Ship features behind toggles, tested and documented, so they can be introduced gradually across clients and teams. Work with clients and teammates: Take part in client conversations, explain technical details clearly, document decisions and keep your commitments on track. Operate what you build: Contribute to dashboards, monitoring and runbooks so the services you ship are observable and supportable in production. What you bring to the party: Solid software engineering: You have shipped and supported production software, and you’re comfortable with testing, code review and working in a team codebase. Python and TypeScript: You write clean, maintainable code in both and are happy moving between tools and environments. Problem-first thinking: You take time to understand the problem before jumping to the first solution. Curiosity about AI: You’re interested in LLMs, autonomous agents and MCP, and in how to give agents the right context and tools. Hands-on experience is great, but you don’t need to have all the answers. Customer and client awareness: You’re comfortable talking to non-engineers, asking good questions and translating messy real-world processes into software. Reliable delivery: You’re organised, write clear documentation and follow through on what you take on. Learning agility: You welcome feedback, ask questions when things are ambiguous and enjoy learning alongside others in a field that changes fast. What success looks like: Delivery: You ship well-scoped features and integrations that make it into production and are used by real clients. Reusability: Your work strengthens the shared product, so the next client is easier to onboard than the last. Trust: Agents you help build behave safely, resolve customer needs correctly and hand over to people when they should. Growth: You take on increasing ownership and become a go-to person for part of the platform. ️ Bonus points: AI engineering: Building with LLMs, agent …

items.desc: Invest in Values. Produce in Freedom. Boost Europe. Europe's plants run on gas, power, heat and steam – and all of them are being rebuilt at the same time. The hard part isn't ambition, it's arithmetic: which asset to buy, when to run it, what to hedge. Europe's largest companies (~2% of total energy demand) answer these questions with our Energy OS: a digital twin of the site, an optimizer that plans it, and agents that operate it. The optimizer is yours. Twenty-year investment decisions, quarter-hourly dispatch, real tariffs, real market rules. You report directly to the CTO – and nobody stands between your model and the plant it runs on. Tasks Optimization Models End-to-End: Own capacity expansion planning over multi-year horizons, dispatch at quarter-hour resolution, and MIP production scheduling with sequence-dependent setup times. Model Physics & Contracts: Storage, thermal networks, transmission, flexibility, self-consumption, minimum part loads, start-up costs – formulate what reality actually demands. Make It Solve: Tighten big-Ms, scale models cleanly, decide where decomposition earns its complexity – and where it doesn't. Smart Data Reduction: Time series clustering, extreme periods, segmentation and aggregation – without accuracy quietly disappearing. Regulation into Constraints: Model grid fees, levies, tariffs, balancing power and intraday trading per country, and understand what they do to the objective function. Prove It's Right: Test cases on real customer systems, fixtures that catch regressions, and infeasibility output an engineer can actually diagnose. Interface & Production: Define inputs and outputs with the Product Engineers; own the runs on Kubernetes – solve time, memory and cost are your numbers. Explain to the Customer: When a customer questions a schedule, you're the one who can say why the model chose it. Requirements Education & Background: Degree in mathematics, operations research, computer science, physics, energy systems engineering, business mathematics or a comparable STEM qualification. Optimization: Deep familiarity with LP and MILP and the craft around it – formulation strength, relaxations, warm starts, solver behavior. Practice over Papers: You've taken a model from formulation to production that others depended on. Code & Solvers: Strong Julia – or strong Python/C++ and a real appetite to learn Julia (JuMP) fast. Hands-on with Gurobi or HiGHS, including reading logs and knowing when to reformulate instead of tuning. Data Sense & Engineering: Comfortable with long time series, unit and sign conventions; tests, version control, code review and CI are second nature. AI-Native: Claude Code, agents and subagents are part of your daily loop – a requirement, not a plus. High Ownership, Low Ceremony: You take on the unclear. Energy domain knowledge helps but isn't required. Nice to have: Stochastic or robust optimization, Benders or column generation, unit commitment, energy market modeling. Benefits Share in the Success: Competitive base salary plus equity – we set your level during the process, not based on your CV. Top-Tier Venture Capital Network: Direct access to the Point 9 and Earlybird networks – including formats for sparring, mentoring and further education. Unforgettable Team Offsites (Workation): Once a year, the whole team goes on a workation. Including exclusive exchanges with our Visionary Voices (e.g. Robert Habeck, Kitty Mayo, James Vincent). Corporate Health: Full flexibility for your fitness and health with Urban Sports Club. Out to the Plant: Seeing the boiler you modeled changes how you build the product. Our stack: Julia with JuMP on Gurobi and HiGHS, forecasting in Python, the product in TypeScript (Vue, Node, PostgreSQL), Google Cloud with Kubernetes for optimization jobs, GitLab CI, agents on LangGraph. Small team, no layers between you and the decision. A model change that lands on Tuesday is in front of the customer on Thursday. In-person onboarding, then hybrid from Munich, Düsseldorf or Münster. Not a research position without deployment – and not a place where solve time is someone else's problem.

items.desc: About CommonAI CommonAI CIC is a non-profit organisation built around collaborative engineering and is backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. Our Scaling Inference Lab (SIL) is developing simulation grounded in real measurements to help the UK invest in promising AI infrastructure. We connect proposed hardware designs to realistic workloads, helping investors and engineers understand their potential, their limitations and the next experiment worth doing. The Opportunity Build the workloads and benchmarks that reveal how AI infrastructure performs on useful applications. You will develop reproducible LLM serving workloads, connecting application behaviour and requirements to physical measurements and SIL's simulation platform. The initial focus includes long-context inference and agentic workloads. You will investigate how request patterns, context lengths, caching, repeated model calls and interactions with tools shape the demands placed on a system. Your benchmarks will make performance comparisons meaningful by specifying the work being done and the quality and service requirements it must meet. Working with measurement and simulation engineers and our partners, you will help preserve the workload behaviour that matters when moving between real systems and models. Your work will help engineers and investors understand which infrastructure choices suit particular applications, and how conclusions change when the workload changes. What you will do Build and maintain reproducible LLM serving workloads, serving configurations and benchmark tools, including long-context and agentic workloads, using suitable existing software. Characterise relevant behaviour such as request arrivals, prompt and output lengths, caching, batching, tool interactions and dependencies between requests. Define performance measures alongside application-quality and service requirements, so comparisons reflect useful work under stated conditions. Work with measurement engineers to reproduce workloads on physical systems, and with simulator engineers to develop workload representations that preserve the behaviour and dependencies that matter. Investigate how changes in workloads and serving configurations affect conclusions, and keep the benchmark suite relevant as inference technology and workloads evolve. Document datasets, model and software versions, configurations, provenance and permitted use so other engineers can reproduce and extend the work. An example early project would be to build a reproducible agentic workload and work with measurement colleagues to compare its performance across two systems, under agreed application-quality and service requirements. Requirements Experience building or evaluating ML systems, inference services, performance benchmarks or comparable workload-driven systems. Strong practical software skills for constructing reliable benchmark tools, analysing results and debugging interactions between applications and infrastructure. Understanding of LLM inference and an interest in how serving choices affect performance and output quality. items.desc: Catalytic conversion of the soluble starch into platform molecules Réf ABG-140677 Stage master 2 / Ingénieur Durée 6 mois Salaire net mensuel Grattification de stage aux droits français ( 22/10/2026 Institut Mines Telecom - Mines Albi Lieu de travail Albi Occitanie France Champs scientifiques Chimie Sciences de l’ingénieur Mots clés Starch; Sugar; catalysis; valorization Date limite de candidature 10/01/2027 Établissement recruteur Site web : https://www.imt-mines-albi.fr/en Located in the heart of South West France, IMT Mines Albi has embodied academic excellence in engineering since 1993. As a renowned general engineering school, it trains future engineers to manage large-scale projects, giving them the means to develop a meaningful career focused on a positive environmental and social impact. With a rich history and a world-class research cluster, IMT Mines Albi offers high-level training to prepare students for the complex challenges of the real world. IMT Mines Albi is a school of the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industry, and is part of Institut Mines-Télécom, a French federal institute of technological universities of science and management. As an associate member of the EPE University of Toulouse, it is authorized by the Commission des titres d'ingénieur (CTI) to award engineering degrees. Positioned at the forefront of industrial and academic issues both in France and internationally, IMT Mines Albi drives scientific and economic progress by integrating its four missions into an innovative virtuous circle: training committed engineers cutting-edge research and innovation local and national economic development dissemination of scientific and technical culture Description Location: RAPSODEE Research Centre, IMT Mines Albi, France Level: Master 2 or equivalent Period: Feb 2027 – Aug 2027 Duration: 6 months The transition towards increased use of biomass in a bioreffinery approach is a major issue in the current energetic and environmental context. In this sense, the valorization of biowaste through a bioreffinery approach considering all mass and energy streams is the logical approach for industrial processes to become greener. In the sector of paper and cardboard recycling, there is a potential of production of high-added value molecules from the compounds present in the recycling process effluents. Namely, during recycling, part of the additives present in cardboard is lost, in particular starch, which is found in the process water, favorizing the growth of microorganisms and fermentation reactions and contributing to the effluent’s chemical oxygen demand. Starch is initially used in cardboad either as dry-strength agent to improve burst and bending properties of packaging papers, or as adhesive in the converting process. When dealing with recycling carboard, starch could be extracted by physico-chemical treatment during carboard pulping and chemical, enzymatic and catalytic thermo-chemical processes, which could be efficient to convert the extracted starch into added value molecules. In the framework of the PAPERS & CARDBOARDS - PAC3R project (PEPR recyclage), the work carried out on the present internship is dedicated to the valorization of soluble starch from residual cardboard recycling process effluents into valuable platform molecules by the catalytic conversion. In fact, during the recycling of carboard and paper wastes, a fraction rich in starch can be obtained. If the quality of starch, separated from physico-chemical processes, is not good enough to be recycled as additive in the production of cardboard, it will be submitted to the valorization into high added-value chemicals such as sugars (glucose, fructose etc.), furfurals, humins, levulinic acid etc., via catalytic transformations using water as green solvent, and highly-performing catalysts developed by RAPSODEE partner. For that, original multifunctional solid catalysts will be developed such as hydroxyapatite-based catalysts, natural clay-based catalysts, carbon-based catalysts etc., using non-critical metals (e.g. Fe, Ni, Co) under the form of well-divided species (nanoparticles, nanocluster, or isolated single atoms) as catalytically active phases. One-step transformation process will be targeted in order to optimize cost and minimize environment impact. Profil Master 2 or equivalent. Student in the final year of engineering studies with a specialty in energy, chemistry, materials or processes. Aptitude for work in the laboratory or on a pilot scale and chemical analysis and desire to discover applied research. Comfortable with reading and writing in French and English. Prise de fonction 01/02/2027

items.desc: Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé Réf ABG-140678 Sujet de Thèse 22/10/2026 Autre financement public Laboratoire Génie de Production - Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées Lieu de travail Tarbes - Occitanie - France Intitulé du sujet Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé Champs scientifiques Sciences de l’ingénieur Psychologie, neurosciences Mots clés territoire de santé; hôpital du futur; technologies; acceptabilité; mesure de performance; analyse multicritère; évaluation multiéchelle Description du sujet Description du sujet Le projet de thèse vise à mieux comprendre les risques associés à l’introduction des technologies innovantes et à mesurer leur impact dans un environnement sanitaire. Dans ce contexte, l’ingénieur aura en charge la mission de concevoir et tester un modèle permettant l’identification des déterminants (territoires, acteurs, activités et technologies) à l’œuvre dans la perception des risques dans le secteur hospitalier et leurs impacts à différents niveaux de l’organisation. Le travail à accomplir consistera à réaliser une modélisation multiéchelle des territoires de santé et des processus temporels de soin, en portant une attention particulière aux activités, aux acteurs et aux technologies impliqués. Cette modélisation s’appuiera sur les connaissances des spécialistes disciplinaires du Living Lab de l’Hospitalité, qui sera sollicité pour valider les scénarios représentatifs et les processus sous-jacents. Une cartographie des technologies sera établie et mise en regard de leur positionnement sur les processus de soin. Cette cartographie sera validée au sein du Living Lab pour garantir sa pertinence auprès de tous les acteurs identifiés. A partir de là une méthodologie de quantification d’un indicateur d’acceptabilité établi par agrégation des critères objectifs et subjectifs, aux niveaux individuels et collectifs et sur les différentes strates et échelles du territoire de santé permettra de sous peser les facteurs en faveur ou défaveur de l’intégration de la technologie. Le Living Lab participera dans le cadre de ce Work Package à l’établissement des principes de construction des seuils d’acceptabilité, de pondération des facteurs et de choix de méthodes d’agrégation en vue d’arbitrer sur l’intérêt technique mais aussi l’impact économique, écologique et sociale de l’introduction d’une technologie. Prise de fonction : 01/12/2026 Nature du financement Autre financement public Précisions sur le financement Projet ANR PRC ACACIA Présentation établissement et labo d'accueil Laboratoire Génie de Production - Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées L’ Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées (UTTOP) est un établissement public d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche spécialisé dans les sciences et technologies de l’ingénieur. Située à Tarbes, au cœur du sud-ouest européen et à proximité immédiate de l’Espagne, l’université développe des activités de recherche reconnues dans les domaines des systèmes complexes, du génie industriel, de l’intelligence artificielle, de la science des données, de l’énergie, de la mécanique et de la gestion des risques. L’UTTOP entretient des relations étroites avec les acteurs industriels, institutionnels et territoriaux et participe à de nombreux projets nationaux et européens. Son positionnement transfrontalier constitue un atout particulier pour le développement de collaborations scientifiques à l’échelle des Pyrénées et de l’espace européen. Le doctorant sera accueilli au sein du Laboratoire Génie de Production (LGP), unité de recherche de l’UTTOP. Le laboratoire développe des recherches en génie industriel et en ingénierie des systèmes complexes, avec des compétences reconnues dans les domaines de l’aide à la décision, de l’optimisation, de la fiabilité, de la transformation numérique, de l’intelligence artificielle, de la science des données et de la gestion des risques. Le LGP rassemble enseignants-chercheurs, doctorants et partenaires académiques ou industriels autour d’une approche systémique des problématiques d’ingénierie. Ses travaux portent aussi bien sur les systèmes industriels que sur les systèmes territoriaux, environnementaux ou socio-techniques. La thèse sera réalisée au sein du département scientifique « Systèmes » , dont les activités concernent notamment la modélisation, l’évaluation et l’aide à la décision pour les systèmes complexes. Les recherches menées mobilisent des approches avancées telles que les réseaux bayésiens, les jumeaux numériques, l’intelligence artificielle explicable, les méthodes probabilistes et l’analyse de données massives. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet européen Interreg POCTEFA RISKRAPID consacré au développement de systèmes de prévision, d’alerte et de prévention des risques naturels à déclenchement rapide dans les petits bassins versants de montagne. items.desc: Company Description Statkraft has been making clean energy possible for over a century. That's what we offer: 125 years of unrivalled expertise in supplying the world with what it needs most. Because in the fight against climate change, we don't see renewable energy as part of the solution, we believe it must be the solution. With us, you'll shape a career that is truly forward-facing, with many amazing opportunities and offerings to match. But there's more work to be done. That's why we need you to join us. Job Description The Global Software Development team is a specialist software development team in Statkraft that delivers leading software for all business areas in Statkraft, ranging from Energy management to robotic trading systems. Custom software development is essential for Statkraft to remain a market leader in renewable energy production and market access services. What to expect As a Python Developer you will closely engage with the business by developing customized systems in our back-office processes, giving Statkraft a competitive edge in the power market. The following tasks are mainly part of your area of responsibility: Design, develop, test and deploy solutions based on Python and AKS. Support the team to build and extend its knowledge base. Work closely with the business to understand the business process and needs; refine and design the technical concept. Develop high quality software in all its aspects. This includes design, developing code, debugging and unit testing. Technical specifications, design documents, functional designs and requirements are required. Knowledge of estimation processes is required. Contribute to the further development of software development within Statkraft and our business in Spain Qualifications Four or more years of experience in software development, with a passion for your craft Experience using AI assisted software development You have used Python extensively throughout your working experience Knowledge of the Fast API framework, PostgreSQL, Oracle and knowledge of AKS are important to this role as well Experience with working with financial & time series data and systems supporting business or industrial processes Proficiency in written and spoken English Additional Information At Statkraft, you’ll shape a career that is truly forward-facing with many amazing opportunities and offerings to match. This includes (non-exclusive): The chance to grow your career alongside a truly global network of experts, leaders, specialists and graduates from different countries and backgrounds The opportunity to work somewhere with pride, and to be able to honestly say “My work is contributing to saving the planet” A work culture that puts emphasis on the individual, offering flexible working solutions, and work life balance principles A focus on fun outside of work, supported by various activity groups such as soccer, yoga, sailing, climbing, boxing, cabin rentals, and much more Being part of a company proudly certified as a ‘Great Place to Work’ Our vision is to renew the way the world is powered. To navigate the complex journey ahead, we need every voice at the table. We enable leading apps, agencies, media buyers, and brands to run programmatic customer acquisition, retargeting, and brand performance campaigns through our self-serve and managed service options. Built on the three core pillars of performance, transparency, and control, Kayzen powers the world's best mobile marketing teams with bespoke solutions that fuel business growth and deliver a competitive advantage. The goal of the team is to deliver on the client's objectives through established or new trading best practices and communicate account status regularly and effectively with their CSM counterparts. Why this role This is a hands-on trading role where you'll manage mobile programmatic campaigns across verticals like gaming, fintech, and betting, optimizing toward CPA/ROAS targets while learning to scale efficiently. Learn to leverage LLMs (GPT/Claude) for recurring analyses, data briefs, and performance diagnostics, this is a core part of how our team works. Support the creation and maintenance of dashboards and reporting tools used by the trading team. Develop your analytical instincts: learn to ask the right questions, understand what's driving performance, and use available tools (SQL, AI, BI tools) to find answers. Cross-functional impact Work with CSMs to understand client goals and communicate campaign status clearly. Support QBR preparation and client-facing deliverables alongside senior growth analysts. For optimal overlap with customers' time zones and internal teams your main working location should preferably be close to the CET time zone. Analytical mindset; SQL ability or a demonstrated willingness to learn quickly. OTHER DETAILS Ref. num. 2026-CR_ADM-ADM-358 Infraestructure technical assistant IMDEA Materials Institute is a public research organization founded in 2007 by Madrid’s regional government to carry out research of excellence in Material Science and Engineering by attracting talent from all over the world to work in an international and multidisciplinary environment. IMDEA Materials has grown rapidly since its foundation and currently includes more than 120 researchers from 22 nationalities and has become one of the leading research centers in materials in Europe which has received the María de Maeztu seal of excellence from the Spanish government. The research activities have been focused on the areas of materials for transport, energy, and health care and the Institute has state-of-the-art facilities for processing, characterization and simulation of advanced materials. Support the operational follow-up of maintenance, cleaning, security, reception/concierge, gardening, waste, industrial-gas and laboratory-furniture services. Collect consumption data for electricity, water and gas and prepare routine monitoring information. Support documentation, filing, purchase requests, cost follow-up and administrative preparation for maintenance and minor works. Support events, moves and routine adaptation of spaces within established instructions. Apply safety and contractor-coordination procedures relevant to assigned tasks and promptly report risks or incidents. Provide general operational support to the Infrastructure Technician and Infrastructure Manager. Desirable experience : Experience in research, university, laboratory, healthcare or industrial environments. Using CMMS or ERP systems. Maintaining energy-consumption records. items.desc: Company Description As a world market leader in crop protection, we help farmers to counter these threats and ensure enough safe, nutritious, affordable food for all – while minimizing the use of land and other agricultural inputs. Syngenta Crop Protection keeps plants safe from planting to harvesting. From the moment a seed is planted through to harvest, crops need to be protected from weeds, insects and diseases as well as droughts and floods, heat and cold. Syngenta Crop Protection is headquartered in Switzerland. Health Promotion Switzerland recognizes Syngenta's commitment to the health and well-being of its employees and awards the "Friendly Work Space" label to all its Swiss sites. At Syngenta, employee health and well-being are key to the company Job Description Purpose of the role Provide scientific leadership for computational and systems-level disease-control biology, accelerating discovery and development of fungicide, biological and integrated crop-protection solutions. Integrate pathogen, host, crop, environmental, agronomic and multi-omics evidence with AI/ML, bioinformatics and digital phenotyping to generate robust, decision-ready insight from Discovery through Product Support. items.desc: We are seeking a Medical Statistician/Statistical Programmer to join the Cancer Epidemiology Unit (CEU), within the Nuffield Department of Population Health at the University of Oxford. You will work closely with statisticians, epidemiologists and other colleagues on large prospective cohort studies investigating lifestyle, dietary, hormonal, molecular and genetic factors in relation to cancer and other common non-communicable diseases. The post focuses on linking and managing large epidemiological datasets, preparing data for analysis, and carrying out statistical analyses. You will work particularly with the EPIC study and EPIC-Oxford, which links cohort data with NHS records of cancer registrations, deaths and hospital admissions. You will also support EPIC-Oxford 2, a new study building on the cohort. Your work will include managing research databases; incorporating electronic health records, questionnaire data and laboratory results; deriving disease outcomes from coded health data; and preparing datasets for cohort and nested case-control studies. You will analyse data, mainly using survival and logistic regression, and prepare tables, figures and reports for research projects and publications. There may also be opportunities to work with biomarker and omics data. You will hold a graduate degree, or have equivalent experience, in medical statistics, statistics, health data science or another quantitative subject, with training in statistical analysis and epidemiological study design. You will have experience working with routinely collected electronic health records and preparing epidemiological data for analysis, including survival analysis and logistic regression. You will also be proficient in Stata and/or R, and have experience using SQL and a relational database system to manage large datasets. Excellent attention to detail, clear and well-documented coding, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively are essential, as are strong communication and organisational skills. An understanding of epidemiological concepts and study designs, experience working with NHS-linked data under information governance requirements, or experience with biobank, sample-tracking, biomarker, dietary or omics data would be an advantage. Experience contributing to peer-reviewed publications and designing databases would also be beneficial. The post is full-time (although part-time is considered) and fixed term for 2 years. The closing date for applications is noon on 16 November 2026. You will be required to upload a CV and a cover letter as part of your online application. The cover letter should clearly describe how you meet each of the selection criteria listed in the job description.

items.desc: About CommonAI CommonAI CIC is a non-profit organisation built around collaborative engineering and is backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. Our Scaling Inference Lab (SIL) is developing simulation grounded in real measurements to help the UK invest in promising AI infrastructure. We connect proposed hardware designs to realistic workloads, helping investors and engineers understand their potential, their limitations and the next experiment worth doing. The Opportunity Build the workloads and benchmarks that reveal how AI infrastructure performs on useful applications. You will develop reproducible LLM serving workloads, connecting application behaviour and requirements to physical measurements and SIL's simulation platform. The initial focus includes long-context inference and agentic workloads. You will investigate how request patterns, context lengths, caching, repeated model calls and interactions with tools shape the demands placed on a system. Your benchmarks will make performance comparisons meaningful by specifying the work being done and the quality and service requirements it must meet. Working with measurement and simulation engineers and our partners, you will help preserve the workload behaviour that matters when moving between real systems and models. Your work will help engineers and investors understand which infrastructure choices suit particular applications, and how conclusions change when the workload changes. What You Will Do Build and maintain reproducible LLM serving workloads, serving configurations and benchmark tools, including long-context and agentic workloads, using suitable existing software Characterise relevant behaviour such as request arrivals, prompt and output lengths, caching, batching, tool interactions and dependencies between requests Define performance measures alongside application-quality and service requirements, so comparisons reflect useful work under stated conditions Work with measurement engineers to reproduce workloads on physical systems, and with simulator engineers to develop workload representations that preserve the behaviour and dependencies that matter Investigate how changes in workloads and serving configurations affect conclusions, and keep the benchmark suite relevant as inference technology and workloads evolve Document datasets, model and software versions, configurations, provenance and permitted use so other engineers can reproduce and extend the work An example early project would be to build a reproducible agentic workload and work with measurement colleagues to compare its performance across two systems, under agreed application-quality and service requirements. Requirements Experience building or evaluating ML systems, inference services, performance benchmarks or comparable workload-driven systems Strong practical software skills for constructing reliable benchmark tools, analysing results and debugging interactions between applications and infrastructure Understanding of LLM inference and an interest in how serving choices affect performance and output quality Care in designing reproducible comparisons and interpreting results against stated application requirements Practical experience using AI coding agents, with the judgement to validate generated code, data transformations and evaluations Experience with vLLM, SGLang or similar serving software, long-context workloads, agentic applications, trace analysis or quality evaluation would be valuable. Depth in a subset is sufficient. The initial remit is LLM serving; other forms of inference are possible later extensions. Why join us Help build UK AI capability and improve how investment and compute serve the public good Build a network spanning UK hardware SMEs, major technology companies, venture and public investors, and leading universities Shape a growing team with startup pace and close academic links Use frontier models and coding agents with a substantial tooling budget Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package, including pension and benefits Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential figures from across the tech sector and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes' walk away from Cambridge train station Working with us Hybrid, with Cambridge attendance agreed individually around collaboration and the work; applicants across the UK are welcome. We are open to permanent employment, part-time arrangements and consultancy. We would like you to start as soon as practical and can be flexible for the right person. We particularly welcome experienced engineers and can also consider earlier-career candidates with strong evidence of ability. Relevant postgraduate study is useful, but qualifications are secondary to experience and the quality of your work. …

items.desc: Bij RH Marine realiseren wij de systeemintegratie van elektrische- en automatiseringssystemen aan boord van marineschepen, onderzeeboten en superjachten. Een complex, maar fascinerend werkgebied vol innovaties. Ieder schip is maatwerk voor de klant en na de doop blijven wij verantwoordelijk voor het onderhoud en upgrades. Het blijft dus de hele life cycle ‘ons kindje’. Binnen RH Marine gebruiken wij AI om slimmer en efficiënter te werken. We zien volop mogelijkheden om AI nog breder in te zetten en verder te integreren in onze dagelijkse processen. Daarom zoeken we een AI Specialist die ons helpt deze ontwikkeling verder vorm te geven. Je ontwikkelt slimme AI-toepassingen, copilots en automatiseringen en helpt collega's om AI effectief in hun werk te gebruiken. Een veelzijdige functie waarin je technische kennis, innovatie en samenwerking combineert. Functie Als AI Specialist werk je nauw samen met verschillende afdelingen binnen RH Marine om kansen voor AI te ontdekken en ideeën om te zetten in concrete oplossingen. Je onderzoekt wat er technisch mogelijk is, ontwikkelt prototypes en proof-of-concepts en begeleidt de implementatie van nieuwe toepassingen. Daarbij zorg je dat oplossingen niet alleen technisch goed werken, maar ook aansluiten bij de behoeften van gebruikers en daadwerkelijk iets toevoegen aan de dagelijkse praktijk. Je concrete taken: Ontwikkelen van AI-toepassingen, copilots en slimme automatiseringen; Ontwerpen en realiseren van prototypes en proof-of-concepts; Integreren van AI-oplossingen in bestaande systemen en werkprocessen; Signaleren van kansen om bedrijfsprocessen met AI te verbeteren; Begeleiden van collega's bij het toepassen van AI en organiseren van workshops en kennissessies; Opbouwen van een intern AI-kennisnetwerk en delen van best practices; Samenwerken met onze Information Security Officer aan richtlijnen voor veilig en verantwoord AI-gebruik; Volgen van nieuwe AI-ontwikkelingen en vertalen daarvan naar praktische toepassingen binnen RH Marine. Functie-eisen We zoeken iemand met een technische achtergrond die enthousiast wordt van de mogelijkheden van AI en vooral graag zelf aan de slag gaat. Je hoeft nog geen jarenlange ervaring als AI-specialist te hebben, maar je hebt wel voldoende technische basis om ideeën om te zetten naar werkende oplossingen. Je vindt het leuk om zelfstandig nieuwe mogelijkheden te onderzoeken, maar zoekt ook actief de samenwerking met collega's. Je kunt technische oplossingen ontwikkelen én anderen enthousiast maken om ermee te werken. Verder vragen wij: Een afgeronde hbo-opleiding in bijvoorbeeld Informatica, Software Engineering of een vergelijkbare technische richting; Bij voorkeur minimaal 2 jaar relevante werkervaring in softwareontwikkeling, automatisering of AI; Ervaring met generatieve AI-tools zoals ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot of Claude; Kennis van prompt engineering en affiniteit met het ontwikkelen van AI-toepassingen; Bij voorkeur programmeerervaring, bijvoorbeeld met Python, en kennis van API's en systeemintegraties; Bereidheid een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) en/of Verklaring van Geen Bezwaar (VGB) aan te vragen; Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal. Aanbod Een geweldig bedrijf om voor te werken met een rijke historie en een mooie toekomst, met veel aandacht voor innovatie. De collegialiteit is groot; een goede sfeer en samenwerking is onmisbaar om ons complexe werk succesvol uit te voeren. Geen project is hetzelfde en ieder project is bijzonder. Het eindresultaat is altijd een prachtig varend schip waarop alles werkt. Werk waar we trots op zijn! Een veelzijdige functie waarin je de vrijheid krijgt om nieuwe ideeën uit te werken en een belangrijke bijdrage levert aan de verdere ontwikkeling van AI binnen onze organisatie. De arbeidsvoorwaarden zijn als volgt: Een salaris tussen de € 4.290,- en € 6.274,- bruto per maand, afhankelijk van kennis en ervaring; 8% vakantiegeld; Een variabele winstdeling; 25 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV dagen; Een laptop en smartphone van de zaak; Flexibele werktijden en hybride werken; Een goede pensioenregeling via PMT. Solliciteren Direct reageren kan via de button. Ben je geïnteresseerd, maar heb je toch een vraag? Neem dan contact op met Natasja Dokter via 06 -11010122 of natasja.dokter@rhmarine.com. items.desc: Are you our new Data Scientist – Panels & Survey Methodology? AudienceProject is looking for a Data Scientist – Panels & Survey Methodology for our Copenhagen office to support our continued growth. — Are you a quantitative researcher who enjoys working with data about people? And are you interested in how panels and surveys can make audience measurement more reliable? Then, we have an opportunity for a career in a fast-growing scale-up with 100+ employees that collaborates directly with companies such as Heineken, L’Oréal, LVMH, Omnicom Media, Publicis Media, WPP Media, Amazon, Google, Netflix, RTL and Warner Bros. Discovery. AudienceProject is a leader in independent cross-media measurement, enabling advertisers, media owners and the industry to trust, prove, and improve advertising outcomes through a scalable SaaS platform. Our platform provides advertisers with a unified view of campaign performance, enabling confident omnichannel investment decisions, and provides media owners with comparable, third-party validation to demonstrate the value of their inventory. After more than 15 years of leading cross-media measurement, we are now looking for a motivated Data Scientist – Panels & Survey Methodology to join our Data Science Research team. Joining AudienceProject will give you a front-row seat in the rapidly evolving advertising industry and an opportunity to work within a respected business, delivering insights about audiences across the world's largest media channels to top-tier clients. What you will do You will join our Data Science Research pod, led by Jacob Daniel Kirstejn Hansen, and help turn panel and survey data into reliable audience measurement. Our panelists are recruited through several panel partners. They contribute passive measurement data through integrations and take part in surveys that help calibrate our models. You will work with 10 other data scientists and engineers, bringing together a range of academic and professional backgrounds. Your focus will be quantitative analysis, panel quality and statistical methodology. You will use Python to investigate data and develop reproducible analyses, working closely with researchers and engineers to improve the inputs and methods behind our measurement. We actively explore and apply AI in our internal work, production systems and products, combining experimentation with sound analytical judgement. You will help evaluate promising approaches with data scientists and developers and turn useful ideas into practical improvements. Your key responsibilities will include: Analyse panel composition and coverage across partners, identifying differences, gaps and potential sources of bias. Assess the completeness, consistency and plausibility of passive measurement data, and investigate unexpected changes. Design and analyse surveys that describe panelists and their behaviour and provide data for model calibration. Contribute to the development and evaluation of weighting, calibration, and statistical modelling approaches, testing how methodological choices affect audience estimates. Identify survey-response quality issues and assess the trade-off between stricter quality rules and retaining a representative sample. Clean, combine, and analyse panel and survey datasets in Python, with clear documentation of assumptions, methods and limitations. Work with panel-partner colleagues, data scientists, and engineers to turn findings into practical data-quality improvements and evaluate their effect. Who you are You combine strong quantitative skills with curiosity about how people are represented in data. You enjoy tracing an unexpected result back to its source, questioning assumptions and explaining what the evidence supports. Your background may be in statistics, quantitative social science, economics, psychology, data science or another relevant field. You bring: Strong skills in quantitative analysis and applied statistics, including regression, sampling, uncertainty and model validation. Hands-on Python skills to clean, explore and analyse real-world data independently and make your work reproducible. An understanding of panels and surveys, including representativeness, selection bias, non-response and measurement error. A careful approach to data quality and the ability to judge how data issues affect an analysis or model. The ability to explain methods and findings clearly to both technical and non-technical colleagues. A relevant quantitative education or equivalent applied research experience. Useful additional experience includes weighting, calibration or passive behavioural data. We value thoughtful analysis, openness to different perspectives and colleagues who share what they learn. You ask questions, test assumptions and explain your conclusions clearly. What we offer You will join a curious, collaborative and energetic environment where data scientists and developers share ideas and learn from one another. Different perspectives help us …

items.desc: The Role Work directly with the founding team to define and build the technical foundation behind our AI Workers. These systems operate inside live logistics workflows across email, telephony, and enterprise software, where reliability matters and edge cases are the product. You will own the hard parts underneath the features: agent architecture, context and state, evaluations, observability, execution reliability, data flows, and the platform other engineers build on. This is a hands-on role. You will write production code every day, but your job is bigger than shipping a backlog. You will decide which abstractions survive, where we need rigor, what we build next, and how the engineering team operates as we grow. This is not a research-only role, and it is not an architecture role where you stop coding. You build, ship, measure, fix, and keep raising the bar. What You'll Do Own the architecture and evolution of the core AI Worker platform across backend services, agent workflows, integrations, data, and infrastructure. Build reliable, long-running AI workflows that make decisions and take action across inboxes, phone calls, TMS, ERP, EDI, SFTP, APIs, and event queues. Develop the systems that make agents dependable in production: evaluations, tracing, feedback loops, guardrails, retries, fallbacks, and human escalation. Work through the difficult parts of applied AI: ambiguous inputs, changing context, tool use, state management, latency, cost, and failure recovery. Turn patterns from customer deployments into reusable product capabilities instead of one-off fixes. Make deliberate technical tradeoffs between speed and durability. Ship the simple version first, then know when the system needs to be rebuilt properly. Shape product and technical direction with the founders. Challenge assumptions, propose better approaches, and own decisions through production. Help set the engineering standard for the company, from system design and code quality to how we use AI tools to build faster. Help hire and develop the engineering team as we grow. Who You Are You take ownership of unclear, important problems. You do not wait for a ticket, a complete spec, or someone else to define the path. You have strong technical judgment. You can simplify a system without being careless, and add structure without slowing everyone down. You think like a product builder, not only an engineer. You care whether the system solves the real operational problem, not whether the implementation looks clever. You move fast and iterate constantly, but you do not hide behind prototypes when customers depend on the system. You build with AI, not just around it. AI-native development is how you think and work. You are low ego and direct. You can disagree clearly, change your mind quickly, and make the best argument win. You are comfortable being close to customers, production incidents, and the messy details of logistics operations. You want to be in the room. Munich office, in person. This is not a remote role or a 9-to-5. What You Bring Strong software engineering fundamentals: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, SQL, REST APIs, data modeling, and system design. Experience owning production systems across architecture, implementation, deployment, and operations. Hands-on experience with LLM systems in production: agent workflows, tool use, prompt engineering, structured outputs, context management, evaluations, and observability. Strong understanding of distributed and asynchronous systems, including queues, retries, idempotency, concurrency, background jobs, and failure handling. Experience with Docker, CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, monitoring, and production incident debugging. A track record of shipping products or systems that real users depend on. Bonus: experience with enterprise integrations, voice systems, email automation, logistics, supply chain, or freight. Process We move fast. Expect a decision within one week. Application. Send your CV and the one thing we care about most: an AI coding session. A transcript or log from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or whatever tool you build with. It can be .md, .txt, several sessions, or a hosted link. We want to see how you actually work. Online interview. One conversation covering technical depth, product judgment, ownership, and team fit. No multi-round gauntlet. Technical session (60 min). Build a small service from scratch with an AI assistant that we provide. We watch how you work, then you walk us through your decisions. Founder session. A direct conversation about how you think, what you want to build, and the level of ownership you want to take. Decision. Feedback and a potential start within one week.

items.desc: About Ensemble IP Ensemble IP is a U.S.-based patent search and software company founded by veterans of the professional patent search industry. Our team of experienced patent analysts delivers patentability, freedom-to-operate, invalidity, and landscape searches to law firms, in-house IP teams, R&D organizations, and inventors who rely on accurate prior art to make high-stakes decisions. We pair that domain expertise with our own software. Quartet, our AI-enabled patent search platform, integrates AI and Boolean search techniques to help professionals find better prior art, faster. Duet extends that platform into agentic AI. Because our analysts use these tools every day, engineers work side by side with the people who know the problem best. We have a small development team in Barcelona and offer both remote and co-working options. Our co-work location is in Gracia. About Our Products Duet is an agentic AI application for anyone needing to find, understand, or interact with patent data. Users ask natural-language questions about inventions, prior art, portfolios, and claims. Duet searches a proprietary patent corpus, reads documents, and returns grounded, actionable answers. Duet sits in the Ensemble IP ecosystem alongside our traditional patent search platform Quartet. Duet implements a cutting-edge agent harness to use the resources made available by Quartet via tools, skills, and expert subagents. This is applied AI engineering in production, not model training or demos. The role We're looking for an AI Product Engineer who efficiently ships outcomes. You'll receive a user problem, a rough capability, or a direction like “expose this through MCP”, not necessarily accompanied with a full interface design. Your job is to chart a path to the end-state, sequence the unknowns so you're never blocked on a single big bet, and put working functionality in the users’ hands at every stage. We innovate and move fast. The focus is on thin vertical slices that compound to produce impressive features. Concretely, that means extending Duet's agent harness: integrating new data sources, building MCP access to Duet functionality, and authoring curated prompts and skills. The AI Product Engineer needs to bring their expertise to these processes to implement robust and cutting-edge solutions with incremental wins along the way. How We Expect You To Work Start from outcomes, not design requirements. We are obsessed with delivering value to our customers. You translate user needs into solutions with a staged delivery plan that brings value to the user in each sprint. Be curious and engaged. We are a small company that values the voice of every team member. We expect every engineer to become familiar with the world of intellectual property and to bring your ideas and talents to the table so that we can create the best possible solutions for our customers. Collaborate, challenge, and support your team members. We live the spirit of agile – we are radically transparent, we take introspection seriously, and we constantly adapt and improve. You will be joining a highly collaborative team that thrives on exchanging ideas, challenging each other, and learning from each other. What You'll Work On MCP server access Design and implement our approach to expose Duet's capabilities via MCP. Rapid data integration Add new data sources by writing thin TypeScript connectors and wiring them into the agent as composable tools. You'll often get “we need source X in the agent” before every field and failure mode is defined. Take the lead to understand the data source and find the most efficient way to incorporate it into Duet. Curated prompts & skills Author and iterate on system prompts, tool designs, skill definitions, and the architecture that links these resources together. Agent platform work Extend and improve our production agent loop. You’ll work with client teams to understand their customer journeys, configure and extend what we’ve built, and feed what you learn back into the shared product. This is a hands-on engineering role. Bring agents to life: Build integrations between Kraken, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces and our AI agent setup, using Python on the Kraken side and TypeScript on the agent side. items.desc: Accurate software sizing using Function Point Analysis or Easy Functional Sizing remains a manual, expert-driven process. This thesis explores how Large Language Models can automate this task by translating common project artefacts into traceable size estimates. You’ll investigate which artefacts are essential, assess LLM accuracy versus expert judgment, and design an end-to-end framework that links early project bids to delivery metrics. Today, accurate Function Point Analysis (FPA) or Easy Functional Sizing (EFS) counts rely on experts interpreting heterogeneous artefacts (user stories, APIs, diagrams, code) and aligning their understanding. It is unclear which minimal set and quality of artefacts are required for reliable counting, and how consistently a Large Language Model (LLM) can translate those artefacts into FPA/EFS elements. Additionally, there is no standard workflow connecting early bidding to realised throughput in Function Points. This thesis addresses these gaps. The Assignment Investigate how to automate and operationalise FPA/EFS within Info Support’s Way of Working using AI. Deliver a Proof of Concept (PoC) that ingests typical project artefacts and produces traceable FPA/EFS counts, along with a framework to integrate this process from bid to delivery metrics. Evaluate accuracy, consistency and lead time against a human baseline on multiple cases. Documentation readiness for FPA/EFS – Analyse which artefacts (and quality criteria) must be present pre‑bid and per delivery phase for accurate counting (e.g., backlog items, acceptance criteria, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, entity models, sequence diagrams, code). Produce a readiness checklist and examples. LLM‑based translation to FPA/EFS – Design and implement a pipeline that maps artefacts to FPA/EFS elements (EI, EO, EQ, ILF, EIF) and/or an EFS estimate with explanations and traceability (why each element was counted). Compare prompting vs. structured extraction, few‑shot exemplars, and rule‑assisted post‑processing. Integration framework in the Way of Working – Define how this fits Info Support’s standard process: from bid (initial sizing and pricing), through project start (baseline), to tracking (FP delivered per sprint/context) and retro (variance analysis). Provide reference integrations (e.g., Azure DevOps/Jira for backlog; OpenAPI; dashboards). Example Research questions What is the minimal viable artefact set (and quality level) needed for accurate and reproducible FPA/EFS counts? How accurate and consistent are LLM-assisted counts compared to expert counts across domains and artefact types? How can we operationalise FP metrics in our Way of Working to improve bidding and delivery predictability? About Info Support Info Support specializes in custom software, data/AI solutions, management, and training and is active in the Finance, Industry, Agriculture, Food & Retail, Mobility & Public, and Healthcare sectors. We provide solid and innovative solutions for complex and critical software issues. Our headquarters are located in Veenendaal (NL) and Mechelen (BE). At present, approximately 500 employees are employed by Info Support. Info Support’s working method is characterized by a number of core values: solidity, integrity, craftsmanship, and passion. These core values are intertwined in our work and the way we interact with each other. To ensure that all employees are always up to date with the latest developments, Info Support has an in-house IT Academy that eagerly satisfies the hunger for more or different knowledge and skills. B2 language proficiency in Dutch is required.
