items.desc:
We are seeking an experienced Front-End Developer to join the Literature Services team at the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI), based at the Wellcome Genome Campus near Cambridge, UK. 
 About the Team 
 The Literature Services team develops and operates Europe PMC , a major open research infrastructure providing access to biomedical and life sciences literature. Europe PMC contains over 47 million publications, including more than 12 million full-text articles, and connects the scientific literature with research data, grants, citations, persistent identifiers and text-mined biological information. The service supports millions of users and large-scale programmatic access to the scientific literature. 
 What you will do 
 You will have a key role in developing the user-facing Europe PMC service, creating fast, accessible and intuitive interfaces that enable researchers to search, navigate and understand a large and increasingly interconnected scientific literature corpus. 
 Working closely with UX and product colleagues, back-end developers, data scientists and other members of the Literature Services team, you will translate user needs and designs into robust, reusable and maintainable front-end applications and components. 
 You will contribute to the ongoing evolution of Europe PMC's web architecture, helping us improve performance, accessibility, maintainability. 
 Your key responsibilities will include: 
 Designing, developing and maintaining responsive, accessible and high-quality web interfaces for Europe PMC. 
 Building reusable front-end components and contribute to a consistent design system across the service. 
 Translating UX designs, prototypes and user requirements into production-quality interfaces. 
 Developing interfaces for complex, data-rich functionality including literature search, filtering, article pages and research workflows. 
 Integrating front-end applications with APIs and other web services using structured data such as JSON. 
 Optimising front-end performance, including page loading, rendering and efficient delivery of web assets. 
 Developing automated tests and contributing to continuous integration and deployment practices. 
 Ensuring interfaces meet appropriate accessibility, usability and web standards. 
 Working collaboratively with software developers, UX/product specialists, data scientists and scientific colleagues as part of cross functional teams 
 Participating in code review, technical design and architectural discussions. 
 Contributing to Agile development processes and the continuous improvement of Europe PMC. 
 You will have: 
 Strong knowledge of HTML, CSS and JavaScript and modern web development standards. 
 Experience developing responsive, cross-browser web applications using a modern front-end framework such as React, Vue or equivalent. 
 Experience building reusable components and maintainable front-end architectures. 
 Experience integrating web applications with REST APIs and working with structured data such as JSON. 
 A good understanding of web performance and experience diagnosing and improving front-end performance. 
 Experience with automated testing and modern front-end testing frameworks. 
 Experience using source control, particularly Git, and collaborative software development practices. 
 Good understanding of web accessibility, usability and responsive design. 
 An understanding of interaction and visual design, with the ability to work effectively with UX specialists and translate designs into high-quality interfaces. 
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively with complex requirements and large, data-driven applications. 
 Fluency with AI-assisted coding and development tools as part of standard working practice 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills 
 It would be advantageous to have additional experience in: 
 Developing high-traffic or large-scale public web services. 
 Design systems and component libraries. 
 Front-end performance monitoring and optimisation. 
 Search and discovery interfaces or other complex data-intensive applications. 
 Agile development methodologies such as Scrum or Kanban. 
 Bioinformatics, scientific information services, scholarly publishing or open research infrastructure. 
 Working Pattern: This role offers a hybrid working arrangement, with 1-2 days per week on site, including one designated team day to support collaboration and connection. 
 Contract length: Grant-funded, 3-year fixed-term Staff Member contract.

About the job 
 Help make Graphcore hardware feel native inside the ML frameworks engineers use every day.
 As a Software Engineer in our PyTorch team, you will help build the software that connects Graphcore accelerators with state-of-the-art machine learning frameworks. You will design, implement, optimise and support features across PyTorch, Triton and related technologies.
 Your work will help ML engineers and researchers get more from Graphcore hardware, without changing how they want to build. That means better compatibility, stronger performance and cleaner developer experiences.
 You will contribute to upstream PyTorch, support our hybrid Python and C++ extension, and help integrate compiler backend capabilities with torch.compile. You will learn fast, solve real engineering problems and build expertise in a large open-source ecosystem.
 The team and culture 
 You will join the PyTorch team within Frameworks, working in a SCRUM team that ships features, reviews code, writes documentation and supports users. Work happens through clear ownership, practical decisions and close communication across software, AI/ML, research and hardware teams.
 The team values maintainable code, thoughtful design and curiosity about unfamiliar systems. Engineers are trusted to investigate, speak up and improve the codebase as they learn.
 This is a team for people who like open-source communities, complex technical problems and visible impact. You will move quickly, but with care for users and long-term quality.
 What we're looking for 
 · Strong core software engineering skills and a collaborative team mindset
· Experience developing Python libraries
· Experience building performant C++ applications in a commercial setting
· Understanding of linear algebra, floating-point arithmetic or numerical analysis
· Confident using Git and reviewing code in a commercial team setting
· Willingness to explore large, unfamiliar open-source codebases independently and with others
 Benefits 
 · Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
· Generous leave: Take time to rest, recharge and enjoy life outside of work
· Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
· Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
· Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
· Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones
· Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover
· Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.
 Join the team at Graphcore 
 Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.
 As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.
 Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore brings together deep expertise to solve complex problems and deliver meaningful progress in AI compute.
 If you want to help shape how PyTorch runs on Graphcore hardware, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now to be part of the journey.

Bist du bereit, mit dem Besten zu rechnen ? 
 Bei Zurich leben wir Versicherung neu. Um die Wünsche unserer Kunden noch besser zu erfüllen, gehen wir neue Wege, denken kreativ, arbeiten agil. Unsere Unternehmenskultur schenkt dir in jeder Hinsicht mehr Flexibilität – und viel Freiraum, dich optimal zu entfalten. Think big – und gerne auch international! Denn deine Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten kennen bei uns keine Grenzen. Bereit, die Zukunft in die Hand zu nehmen? 
 Das erwartet dich 
 Du unterstützt unser Team am Standort Köln bei der technischen Weiterentwicklung der Input-Management-Plattform für die automatisierte Dokumentenverarbeitung und erhältst umfassende Einblicke in unsere Infrastruktur und End-to-End-Prozesse 
 In deiner Rolle gestaltest du die nächste Generation unserer Input-Management-Plattform und entwickelst, trainierst sowie optimierst Deep-Learning-Modelle zur automatisierten Klassifikation von Kundenanliegen und Dokumenten 
 Mit deinem Know-how führst du Benchmarks, Modellvergleiche und Qualitätsanalysen durch und stellst die kontinuierliche Verbesserung unserer KI-Modelle sicher 
 Dein Fokus liegt auf der Evaluation und Integration neuer Technologien aus den Bereichen Deep Learning, Generative AI und Agentic AI sowie auf dem Einsatz moderner KI-Verfahren 
 Im agilen Umfeld arbeitest du eigenverantwortlich mit Spezialist:innen, IT, Dienstleistern, Fachbereichen, Architekt:innen, Entwickler:innen und Prozessverantwortlichen zusammen 
 Du überführst fachliche Anforderungen in produktive KI-Lösungen und unterstützt stabile sowie nachvollziehbare Datenflüsse und Transformationen mit XML, JSON und CSV 
 Das bringst du mit 
 Zielstrebigkeit, hohe Eigeninitiative, analytisches Denkvermögen sowie eine organisierte, strukturierte und gewissenhafte Arbeitsweise 
 Freude daran, innovative Lösungen eigenständig zu entwickeln, produktiv einzusetzen und das eigene Arbeitspensum zuverlässig zu steuern 
 Fundierte Kenntnisse in Machine Learning und Deep Learning sowie Erfahrung mit Python, PyTorch oder TensorFlow 
 Kenntnisse in NLP, Document AI und der Verarbeitung unstrukturierter Daten, 
 Idealerweise Erfahrung mit Dokumentenklassifikation, OCR, Information Extraction, Intelligent Document Processing sowie LLMs, Azure OpenAI, Open-Source-LLMs, Prompt Engineering oder Retrieval-Technologien 
 Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift 
 Abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik oder Wirtschaftsinformatik bzw. eine vergleichbare Ausbildung 
 Das bieten wir dir 
 Flexible Arbeitsformen für eine optimale Balance zwischen Arbeiten am Arbeitsplatz und von zu Hause aus 
 Zahlreiche Trainings- und Lernangebote, um fit für den Arbeitsalltag zu bleiben und eine individuelle Weiterentwicklung zu ermöglichen 
 Unterstützung bei deiner Karriereplanung - von der Potenzialanalyse bis hin zur individuellen Förderung 
 Eine moderne, offene und transparente Arbeitsumgebung, die Kreativität und teamübergreifende Zusammenarbeit fördert 
 Ob Fitness in der Gruppe vor Ort oder virtuelles Achtsamkeitstraining von zu Hause: Unser vielfältiges Sport- und Gesundheitsangebot der FIT@ZURICH Betriebssportgemeinschaft unterstützt eine gesunde Work ‑ Life ‑ Balance 
 Bikeleasing, vergünstigtes Deutschlandticket, vermögenswirksame Leistungen, ein Mitarbeitenden ‑ Aktienprogramm und weitere tolle Benefits 
 Z usätzliche Informationen 
 Die Zurich Gruppe Deutschland unterstützt in Abhängigkeit zur individuellen Stellenanforderung und der persönlichen Eignung grundsätzlich sowohl flexible als auch Teilzeit-Arbeitsformen. Wenn du Interesse an dieser Stelle hast und deine persönliche Situation nicht ganz mit dem angegebenen Pensum (Voll- und Teilzeit) zusammenpasst, wende dich gerne an uns ( marisa.schell@zurich.com ), um die potenziellen Möglichkeiten zu besprechen. 
 Arbeitsort: Köln 
 Teilzeit oder Vollzeit: Vollzeit 
 Marisa Schell freut sich auf deine Bewerbungsunterlagen mit Angabe deiner Gehaltsvorstellungen und des möglichen Starttermins über das Karriereportal (“Jetzt Bewerben”-Button). Leider können wir Bewerbungen per E-Mail nicht berücksichtigen. 
 Willkommen in deiner Zukunft 
 55.000 Kolleginnen und Kollegen in 215 Ländern und Gebieten. Gemeinsam auf dem Weg, Versicherung jeden Tag neu zu denken – und die Zukunft für alle zu gestalten. Willkommen in einer starken Gemeinschaft, in der du von Anfang an etwas bewegst. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir uns weiter!

items.desc:
Location 
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy 
 Description 
 Earth Observation Security Applications Engineer in the Industrial Competitiveness Section, Green Solutions Division, Science Applications and Climate Department, Directorate of Earth Observation Programmes.
 Duties 
 You will be responsible for building up the increased use of civilian EO capabilities, in line with the ESA Convention, in all security and resilience domains in the framework of the ERS programme. This will include law enforcement (environmental crime, crimes against humanity, proliferation, organised crime and terrorism), intelligence analysis, actions addressing fragility, conflict and violence, hybrid threats and civil/military cooperation in Earth observation.
 Your responsibilities will include:
 engaging key stakeholders from the law enforcement/security community, identifying opportunities for strategic collaboration at international and national level;
 building awareness and acceptance of civilian EO capabilities among law enforcement/security-sector stakeholders to foster longer-term adoption, consolidating their information requirements;
 identifying and addressing structural impediments to the uptake of civilian EO-based products and services in the law enforcement/security domain;
 defining and implementing innovative projects to foster the use of civilian EO, in particular private sector systems, in this domain;
 defining and implementing innovative projects to combine EO data with non-EO datasets, new architectures (e.g. edge processing) and advanced processing methods (including AI) to address emerging needs from security stakeholders;
 assessing EO science and applications developments (data analytics, artificial intelligence, etc.) regarding the exploitation potential for the law enforcement/security domain;
 cooperating with other ESA teams involved in industrial innovation to address evolving priorities in this domain;
 liaising with the other divisions and departments involved with the ERS-EO Element 1 activities and the ERS-EO Element 2 Clusters where appropriate;
 contributing to ESA communication efforts promoting EO results, mission achievements and EO benefits for society;
 supervising and supporting the work of Young Graduate Trainees, National Trainees and Research Fellows.
 Technical competencies 
 Experience in the application of satellite/airborne EO with stakeholders from the security domain in Europe and worldwide
 Knowledge of European and Global law enforcement/security environments
 Experience in setting up and implementing projects involving exploitation of Earth observation data
 Behavioural competencies 
 Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking
For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

 A master's degree in engineering, Earth science, computer science, applied physics or data science is required for this post together with, in principle, six years of relevant professional experience.

 Specialist experience of working in the one of the following areas would be an advantage: law enforcement, fragile states, civil-military cooperation
Strong problem-solving skills to deal with day-to-day operational challenges

items.desc:
Location 
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands 
 Description 
 You will be assigned as a Product Assurance and Safety (PA&S) Engineer to the Exploration and Science PA&S Section, Product Assurance Management Division, Quality Department, Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality.
 The Exploration and Science PA&S Section provides PA&S management and coordination for the missions and activities of the Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration and the Directorate of Science.
 Upon joining the Exploration and Science PA&S Section, you will assume the role of PA&S Engineer for the LISA Project and become part of the related Project Core Team. As such, while reporting hierarchically to the Head of the Exploration and Science PA&S Section, you will report functionally to the LISA Project.
 Duties 
 Your tasks and responsibilities will include supporting the Project PA&S Managers in:
 establishing and maintaining the PA&S requirements baseline in compliance with ESA policies;
 ensuring the implementation of the PA&S requirements by industry and other suppliers (e.g. CFI providers), supporting milestone reviews and participating in the process of verifying compliance with requirements;
 monitoring the implementation of approved plans and specifications from industry and other suppliers (e.g. CFI providers), ensuring that adequate resources are deployed for the implementation of the PA&S programme;
 coordinating the technical aspects of relevant service support and acting as the primary point of contact between service functions and project teams;
 planning, coordinating and monitoring the support provided by the assigned PA&S workforce;
 participating in the boards for the disposition of deviations from the requirements baseline (CCB), and changes to the agreed design;
 representing ESA in the boards established for the disposition of non-conformances and anomalies, and the definition and monitoring of relevant corrective and preventive actions (NRB), failure investigations, and project technical reviews (e.g. MRR, TRR, PTR or TRB);
 ensuring the implementation of the reliability, availability, maintainability and safety (RAMS) programme and the software assurance programme, including their support for design trade-off decisions and verification of requirements;
 monitoring the selection, procurement and use of electrical, electronic and electromechanical (EEE) components, and materials, mechanical parts and processes (MMPP);
 monitoring manufacturing, assembly, integration and test activities through mandatory and key inspection points, test witnessing, quality assurance checks, etc.;
 conducting the acceptance reviews of all contractually deliverable items;
 reviewing the safety data packages from industry and other suppliers (e.g. CFI providers) as needed, ensuring that they are made available on time to the corresponding safety authorities, and supporting safety reviews and other key events for ground and launch safety;
 supervising PA&S activities during the launch campaign;
 performing any other PA&S tasks necessary to ensure a safe and successful mission.
 In carrying out tasks for the Project, you will receive support from experts of the ESA Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality. 
 In addition to your Project responsibilities, you will support the Head of the Exploration and Science PA & Safety Section in improvement activities and cross-project coordination.

 Experience in PA&S management for space projects (for example as PA&S Manager or PA&S Engineer)
 Knowledge of individual PA&S disciplines (quality assurance, RAMS, materials and processes, EEE components and/or software product assurance)

 Understanding of space systems engineering

Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking
For more information, please refer to the ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook. 
 Education and professional experience 
 A master’s degree in a relevant field is required for this position, together with at least four years of relevant professional experience. Alternatively, candidates with a bachelor’s degree and an additional four years of relevant professional experience may be considered.

 The ability to manage complex decision-making processes, especially under pressure and in the presence of conflicting positions or priorities.

 Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal.

Are you ready to use your business intelligence skills to help key energy stakeholders develop an actionable path to a safe, reliable, equitable, and carbon-free electric grid?
 DNV - Energy Systems' Analytics and Digitalization group is seeking a Business Intelligence Developer to join our team, based out of our Gdynia, Poland office.
 This role is suited to a BI professional who already has practical experience delivering Power BI solutions and can handle standard development assignments with a good degree of independence. The person should understand the full reporting lifecycle, from requirements and source data through transformation and modelling to visualization, deployment and support.

 The role is part of an international environment, with close collaboration across global teams, particularly in the US. It offers a high degree of autonomy and ownership, as well as opportunities to build strong partnerships across different locations and time zones. Occasional business travel to the US or other locations for meetings, conferences and similar business events may be part of the role, providing valuable opportunities for in-person collaboration and relationship building.

 Strong working knowledge of Power BI Desktop.
 Ability to design intuitive dashboards, effective visualizations and meaningful KPIs.

 Working knowledge of Power BI Service, including publishing, refresh and content management.
 Experience implementing and managing Row Level Security (RLS).
 Knowledge of UX/UI principles applicable to dashboard and report design.

 Experience analyzing and transforming data from different source types.
 Experience developing or maintaining ETL/ELT processes.
 Good working knowledge of Power Query and the M language.
 Ability to identify data anomalies, investigate root causes and resolve reporting errors.
 Ability to document transformation logic, business rules and technical decisions clearly.
 Experience using Tabular Editor for semantic model development and maintenance.
 Working knowledge of Git and Azure DevOps practices for version control and team collaboration.
 Experience working with Azure Analysis Services or comparable tabular semantic models.
 Demonstrates foundational AI literacy by using approved AI tools for routine analytical and communication tasks, writing clear prompts, recognizing tool limits, staying curious and flexible as tools evolve.
 Take ownership for the quality and reliability of AI-assisted work by reviewing outputs for accuracy, bias, and fit before using them.
 Task Management 
 Ability to work independently and take ownership of assigned tasks and deliverables.
 Ability to gather, challenge and refine requirements with business stakeholders.
 Ability to collaborate with Data Engineers, Analysts, Product Owners and other BI professionals.
 A solution-oriented mindset, with the ability to recommend improvements rather than only implement instructions.
 Behavior and Communication 
 Clear and professional communication with end users and client stakeholders.
 Strong attention to quality, accuracy and detail.
 Ability to work effectively in an Agile environment.
 Fluent spoken and written English, suitable for daily work with international teams and English-speaking clients.

 You will design and maintain scalable data pipelines, manage secure data environments, and prepare data for AI-driven systems while collaborating with cross-functional teams and clients. You’ll tackle real-world challenges by contributing to the development of next-generation AI systems and grow as a technologist by working alongside diverse experts across industries.

You’ll assess data landscapes, apply data quality fundamentals, and prepare data for AI solutions. Additionally, you’ll learn to translate simple hypotheses into engineered features, manage secure data environments, and contribute to R&D initiatives focused on innovating and scaling next-generation AI capabilities.
 Your work will help solve some of the most complex and high-impact challenges facing clients across industries.  Your work offers a unique opportunity to grow at the forefront of AI, data engineering, and emerging agentic technologies. You’ll develop expertise at the intersection of technology and business by tackling diverse challenges in the evolving AI landscape. Working alongside multidisciplinary teams, you’ll gain a holistic understanding of how data engineering enables advanced AI while collaborating with several leading AI and data experts in the industry.

 Exceptional time management in a complex and largely autonomous work environment

 Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, in English

items.desc: Description du poste Domaine Mathématiques, information scientifique, logiciel Contrat Stage Intitulé de l'offre Intership Agentic Multimodal AI for Understanding and Reasoning over Complex Technical Documents-H/F Sujet de stage The internship aims to develop multimodal agentic AI for understanding and reasoning over complex technical documents containing text, tables, figures, diagrams, and equations distributed across multiple pages. The work will focus on evaluating recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs), designing an agentic architecture capable of decomposing complex queries, planning multi-step reasoning, and dynamically selecting relevant pages, tools, and models, and combining information across multiple modalities. A dedicated benchmark may also be developed, and the proposed approach will be evaluated against direct VLM and multimodal RAG baselines. Durée du contrat (en mois) 6 mois Description de l'offre As an intern at the CEA, you will have the opportunity to work within a world-renowned research environment. Our teams consist of passionate and dedicated experts, providing an ideal setting for learning and collaboration. You will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and top-tier research resources to carry out your assignments. The work conducted may potentially lead to a scientific publication. Context : Complex technical documents combine heterogeneous information such as text, tables, diagrams, figures and equations, often distributed across multiple pages. They include technical manuals, maintenance procedures, user guides, datasheets, product specifications, engineering documents, and technical or scientific reports. Understanding such documents raises several challenges: retrieving relevant information across long documents, jointly interpreting heterogeneous modalities, linking information distributed over multiple pages, and performing multi-step reasoning. This internship aims to develop multimodal agentic AI capable of planning and orchestrating specialized models and tools for complex document understanding and reasoning. What do we expect from you? To address these challenges, the internship will investigate the following research directions: Review existing benchmarks and, if necessary, develop a benchmark covering a fine-grained taxonomy of technical documents and multimodal reasoning tasks. Evaluate recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for technical document understanding. Design an agentic architecture able to decompose complex queries and plan multi-step reasoning. Dynamically retrieve relevant pages and select appropriate tools or models. Combine and reason over information from text, tables, figures, diagrams and equations across multiple pages. Evaluate the proposed approach against direct VLM and multimodal RAG baselines. # Cea-List Profil du candidat Students in their 4th or 5th year of studies (M1, M2 or gap year) Strong interest for Multimodal Generative AI Knowledge of LLMs, Vision-Language Models (VLMs), Transformers, RAG and agentic systems Computer vision skills Machine learning skills (deep learning, perception models, generative AI…) Python proficiency in a deep learning framework (especially TensorFlow or PyTorch) Localisation du poste Site Saclay Localisation du poste France, Ile-de-France, Essonne (91) Ville Saclay Critères candidat Langues Français (Courant) Anglais (Courant) Diplôme préparé Bac+5 - Diplôme École d'ingénieurs Formation recommandée Apprentissage automatique et IA Possibilité de poursuite en thèse Oui Informations générales Entité de rattachement Le CEA est un acteur majeur de la recherche, au service des citoyens, de l'économie et de l'Etat. Le CEA s'engage depuis plus de 75 ans au service de la souveraineté scientifique, technologique et industrielle de la France et de l'Europe pour un présent et un avenir mieux maîtrisés et plus sûrs. Implanté au cœur des territoires équipés de très grandes infrastructures de recherche, le CEA dispose d'un large éventail de partenaires académiques et industriels en France, en Europe et à l'international. items.desc: Aghanim is an integrated commerce, liveops automation, community engagement, and payments platform for video games. Mobile games have traditionally depended on app stores for distribution, payments, and player relationships. We believe there is a better way. Aghanim helps game studios build direct relationships with players, sell directly, and build their future on their own terms. Today, more than 100 games worldwide are already building this future with Aghanim. Our team brings together people across Los Angeles, New York, Seoul, Beijing, London, Lisbon, Belgrade and other locations around the globe, with deep expertise in gaming, fintech and technology. We move quickly, keep communication direct, and focus on getting things done. We believe the best people thrive when they have autonomy, ownership, and a stake in the company's success. We’re looking for a Founding ML Engineer at Senior or Principal level to lead the transition of Newton , Aghanim’s AI product for partners, from proprietary model APIs to models we control. Newton already runs in production on frontier models. You’ll own the model layer end to end: data collection, evaluation, post-training, serving, and rollout. The goal is to preserve the quality partners rely on while reducing cost, improving speed, and keeping partner data within our infrastructure. You’ll work closely with the product to understand its behavior and partner expectations, then independently define the technical approach and priorities. Decisions about training, routing, and model replacement should be backed by production data and evaluations. Key Responsibilities Build production data pipelines that capture versioned instructions, tool calls, outputs, costs, and outcomes, with anonymization, partner-level deletion, and expert corrections. Develop benchmarks, regression tests, and code-based and LLM-judge evaluators using real Newton runs to measure factual accuracy, tool use, answer quality, cost, and latency. Compare frontier and open-weight models, route tasks to suitable models, and identify where prompting, distillation, or post-training delivers the best results. Train and adapt models using distillation, SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, and DPO on accepted trajectories and expert feedback; use RL where simpler approaches fall short. Deploy models behind Newton’s existing interface, validate them through shadow runs, and manage rollout based on quality benchmarks and serving economics. Tech stack: Python, TypeScript, SQL, self-hosted Langfuse, TRL / Unsloth / Axolotl or managed training platforms, vLLM, serverless GPUs, GCP / Modal; open-weight models including Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, and GLM. Required Qualifications Hands-on experience post-training LLMs and shipping them to production using SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, and distillation. Experience building evaluation systems from production data, including offline benchmarks, regression and behavior tests, and code-based and LLM-judge evaluators. Understanding of agentic systems, including tool calling, multi-step trajectories, structured outputs, and the impact of changing the underlying model. Practical experience serving models with vLLM or similar tools, quantization, and GPU deployment, including latency, cold-start, and cost tradeoffs. Strong production Python and SQL skills, with enough TypeScript proficiency to modify product code and instrumentation independently. Ability to understand product behavior and user expectations, translate them into measurable quality requirements, and decide when training is justified. Experience independently owning a technical area, setting priorities, and working across an unfamiliar codebase and its design documents. Regular use of AI coding agents, with a clear approach to verifying their output. Preferred Qualifications Experience migrating a production product from proprietary model APIs to self-hosted or open-weight models. Experience with RL for LLMs, particularly GRPO with automatic verifiers. Familiarity with Langfuse, Braintrust, or similar tracing and evaluation tools. Experience with GCP, including Vertex AI, Cloud Run GPU, and BigQuery. Interest in game monetization and analytics. Why Join Us World-class team – work alongside experienced professionals from around the globe who have built products used by millions of players High growth, high impact – be part of a fast-growing company where ideas turn into products and reach customers in days, not months Autonomy and ownership – we trust people to make decisions, take initiative, and drive results Modern tools and technology – use AI, automation, and modern tools as part of your everyday work Equity – participate in the company's growth and long-term success

items.desc: Description We are seeking an AI Data & Integration Engineer to connect Plessey’s data and systems to AI. The company operates an advanced compound semiconductor fab and develops complex MicroLED display and optical interconnect technologies. This role will give AI agents secure, efficient and reliable access to data from across the business, including manufacturing, engineering, quality and business systems, so they can deliver real outcomes. The successful candidate will combine strong data and software engineering skills with a deep understanding of how AI agents use tools and data. They will build the connections, shape the data so agents use it well, and prove through testing that agents can complete real work with it. Success in this role will be demonstrated by AI agents that answer questions and complete tasks accurately and efficiently using Plessey’s data. This will include clear evidence of faster access to information, less time spent gathering and analysing data, and measurable productivity gains across fab operations, engineering and business functions. The role reports to the Lead AI Solutions Engineer and works closely with IT, data owners and teams across the business. As AI agents take on longer-running and more complex work, this role will make sure Plessey’s data is ready for them: secure, well structured and efficient to use. Key Responsibilities Map Plessey’s data sources with their owners: structure, quality, sensitivity and who should see what. Build pipelines that turn raw fab data into agent-ready data: tool logs, recipes, statistical process control, metrology, test and inspection data. Build and own the connectors that give AI agents access to company data and systems, using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). These include the Manufacturing Execution System (MES) data warehouse, Microsoft 365, engineering file shares, tool and process data, and business systems. Design connections that agents can use effectively and efficiently: easy to find and understand, economical with tokens and cost, and ready for longer-running, multi-step and event-driven work. Prove every connection works by testing it with real agents on real Plessey tasks, measuring accuracy and cost, and monitoring it in production without degrading source systems. Secure every connection so people only reach data they’re already entitled to. Protect personal, commercially sensitive and IP data, guard against AI-specific risks such as prompt injection, and keep full audit trails. Work with production, engineering, quality and business teams, IT, data owners and vendors to turn real needs into documented connections that deliver measurable gains. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Fully committed to AI: uses AI tools every day, keeps pace with the latest models and agent capabilities, and believes in a future where AI is part of everything we do. items.desc: Chirurgie Voll- und Teilzeit befristet Stellen-Nr.: 26_10_019 Ismaninger Straße (TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar) We are looking for an ambitious Bioinformatician / Computational Scientist to become a central part of our research program in Cancer Neuroscience and Translational Oncology . Our laboratory studies how neural, immune, stromal and malignant cell populations interact within tumors and how these interactions influence tumor evolution, invasion, metastasis and therapeutic resistance. A major focus of our work is the systematic characterization of the neural ecosystem of cancer using single-cell, spatial and multimodal datasets and the development of computational approaches capable of uncovering previously unrecognized cellular states and intercellular communication programs. The group is supported by highly competitive funding including the European Research Council (ERC), Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), Deutsche Krebshilfe and Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung and operates within a strong international cancer neuroscience network. Our ambition is to establish computational cancer neuroscience as a defining component of the emerging field and to generate datasets and concepts with international visibility. Aufgaben You will work closely with experimental scientists, clinician scientists, pathologists and international collaborators and will take responsibility for the computational analysis of complex translational datasets. Key areas include: single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, high-plex spatial imaging and transcriptomic platforms, bulk RNA sequencing, multimodal datasets, tumor microenvironment analysis, cell-state and trajectory analysis, ligand–receptor and cell–cell communication analyses, neural–tumor–immune interaction networks, integration of experimental and clinical datasets Depending on your interests and expertise, projects may also involve: development of novel computational approaches for identifying neural-associated tumor states, spatial neighborhood and tissue architecture analyses, integration of transcriptomic, genomic and epigenomic datasets, comparative analyses across cancer entities, machine-learning-based patient or phenotype stratification, analysis of large public cancer datasets, generation of publication-quality computational frameworks and visualizations A particular scientific opportunity will be the development of computational strategies to identify and characterize neural-like, neuroplastic and neuron-interacting cancer cell states and their spatial relationship with nerves, immune cells and stromal populations. Profil We are looking for a candidate with a background in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Systems Biology, Biostatistics, Data Science or Computational Genomics strong expertise in several of the following areas: R and/or Python, single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, RNA-seq analysis, statistical analysis of high-dimensional biological data, data visualization, reproducible computational workflows, integration of heterogeneous biological datasets Experience in cancer biology, neuroscience, immunology or spatial biology is particularly welcome but is not mandatory if there is a strong interest in learning the underlying biology. We value candidates who do not see bioinformatics merely as a service function, but who want to formulate biological hypotheses, develop computational concepts and actively shape scientific projects . Benefits You will become a core member of a highly interdisciplinary research group combining: Cancer Biology, Neuroscience, Immunology, Spatial Biology, Computational Science An extension beyond the initial funding period is explicitly envisaged, depending on scientific performance, project development and future funding. access to unique and deeply characterized human and experimental datasets and close interaction with experimental scientists and clinician scientists highly competitive ERC-, DFG-, Deutsche Krebshilfe- and foundation-funded projects opportunities for first- and co-authorship on high-impact publications as well assubstantial freedom to develop computational projects and methodological approaches participation in an international network at the forefront of Cancer Neuroscience the possibility to establish an independent computational profile within this rapidly developing field EGYM well pass, corporate benefits and discounts (e.g. Käfer), cafeteria, sports and cultural offers, company bike Working in the heart of Munich at Max-Weber-Platz with very good accessibility by public transport such as the subway, S-Bahn or tram Company pension plan through the Federal and State Pension Institute (VBL) Kontakt Sarah Mößmer Klinik und Poliklinik für Chirurgie 089 4140 2044 Weitere Informationen If the candidates’ suitability for the position in question is equal, severely disabled applicants shall be given preference. items.desc: Who we are At Frontiers, we are on a mission to make science open. Most research today sits behind paywalls, meaning only people at well-funded universities or those who can pay get to read it. Open access flips that: every article we publish is peer-reviewed and made available online to anyone, anywhere at no cost. As one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access publishers, we’ve seen Frontiers research cited 16 million times, and viewed and downloaded more than 5.3 billion times, proof of what science without barriers can do. About the role Do you have an academic or professional background in biology, microbiology, biotechnology, environmental science, agriculture, food science or a related discipline? Looking for an alternative career path where you can stay connected to research while developing commercial, business development and relationship-management skills? As a Publishing Development Specialist at Frontiers, you will combine subject-area understanding with proactive outreach, consultative conversations and data-informed journal development. You will work with researchers, editors and academic communities worldwide to identify opportunities, build strong relationships and generate high-quality submissions for Frontiers journals. What you'll do Reach out directly to researchers and editors to spark new collaborations, launch dedicated article collections, recruit into the Editorial Board, commission manuscripts, and liaise with Chief Editors at a journal section level. Manage a dynamic sales pipeline, taking opportunities from first contact through to successful publication. Use AI tools daily to research prospects, personalize outreach, and manage your pipeline more efficiently. Cultivate trust and build long-term professional relationships with editors and authors. Present research findings at national and international scientific meetings and conferences. Contribute to scientific publications, research grant applications and collaborative research proposals. items.desc: DESCRIPCIóN ¿Disfrutas investigando, desarrollando y poniendo a prueba nuevas metodologías de teledetección? De los datos al modelo y del modelo a su validación: combina tu base científica con la programación y el análisis geoespacial en proyectos de I+D aplicados a agricultura, recursos hídricos y medio ambiente. Para ello, buscamos una persona especialista en teledetección, con una buena base científica y experiencia en programación y análisis geoespacial. ¿QUÉ HARÁS Y EN QUÉ PROYECTOS PARTICIPARÁS? Te incorporarás al desarrollo de soluciones de teledetección y observación de la Tierra, participando en el diseño, implementación y validación de metodologías que transformen datos satelitales, meteorológicos y otras fuentes geoespaciales en productos, indicadores y modelos. EN TU DÍA A DÍA… Desarrollarás flujos de adquisición, preparación y procesamiento de datos, integrando distintas fuentes y trabajando con grandes volúmenes de información geoespacial. Analizarás imágenes satelitales y series temporales, aplicando técnicas de análisis espectral y multiespectral. Desarrollarás y validarás modelos físicos, estadísticos y de Machine Learning para tareas de estimación, clasificación, segmentación, detección de objetos, cambios y anomalías. Evaluarás los resultados de las metodologías y los modelos, mediante métricas estadísticas y procedimientos de validación adecuados para cada aplicación. Participarás en proyectos de I+D, contribuyendo a generar soluciones robustas, reproducibles y escalables. Tus desarrollos podrán aplicarse a ámbitos como agricultura y vegetación, recursos hídricos, medio ambiente, atmósfera y clima, territorio e infraestructuras, riesgos naturales y gestión de emergencias. ¿QUÉ CONOCIMIENTOS Y EXPERIENCIA NECESITAS? Teledetección: tienes una buena base científica y una comprensión global de la disciplina, incluidos sus fundamentos físicos, los principios de adquisición y procesamiento de datos, las características de los sensores y la interpretación de la información obtenida mediante observación de la Tierra. Sensores satelitales: cuentas con experiencia con Sentinel-2 y Landsat . También se valorarán tus conocimientos de Sentinel-1 (SAR), Sentinel-3 y otros sensores . Programación Python: manejas Python a nivel intermedio y tienes experiencia con NumPy, Pandas, PySTAC, Xarray, Rasterio, GeoPandas y GDAL . Procesamiento geoespacial: sabes realizar reproyecciones, remuestreos, máscaras y mosaicos, y trabajar con sistemas de coordenadas y datos ráster y vectoriales. Análisis espectral: tienes conocimientos de cálculo de índices de vegetación, análisis multiespectral y tratamiento de series temporales. Fuentes de datos y repositorios abiertos: conoces las principales plataformas, repositorios y datasets de acceso libre de observación de la Tierra y sabes localizar, consultar, seleccionar y obtener datos adecuados para diferentes aplicaciones. Machine Learning: tienes conocimientos de regresión, clasificación, Random Forest, XGBoost y validación de modelos mediante métricas estadísticas. Herramientas de desarrollo: cuentas con experiencia con QGIS, Git y entornos de desarrollo Python . items.desc: Who we are At Frontiers, we are on a mission to make science open. Most research today sits behind paywalls, meaning only people at well-funded universities or those who can pay get to read it. Open access flips that: every article we publish is peer-reviewed and made available online to anyone, anywhere at no cost. As one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access publishers, we’ve seen Frontiers research cited 16 million times, and viewed and downloaded more than 5.3 billion times, proof of what science without barriers can do. About the role Do you have an academic or professional background in biology, microbiology, biotechnology, environmental science, agriculture, food science or a related discipline? Looking for an alternative career path where you can stay connected to research while developing commercial, business development and relationship-management skills? As a Publishing Development Specialist at Frontiers, you will combine subject-area understanding with proactive outreach, consultative conversations and data-informed journal development. You will work with researchers, editors and academic communities worldwide to identify opportunities, build strong relationships and generate high-quality submissions for Frontiers journals. What you'll do Reach out directly to researchers and editors to spark new collaborations, launch dedicated article collections, recruit into the Editorial Board, commission manuscripts, and liaise with Chief Editors at a journal section level. Manage a dynamic sales pipeline, taking opportunities from first contact through to successful publication. Use AI tools daily to research prospects, personalize outreach, and manage your pipeline more efficiently. Cultivate trust and build long-term professional relationships with editors and authors. Represent our journals at scientific conferences, webinars, and online events to increase their market footprint. Requirements About You You bring experience in sales, outreach, or business development with a proven track record of hitting targets. You enjoy fast-paced environments, handle multiple projects with ease, and know how to prioritize your day. You have a strong grasp of AI-based tools in a business operations context. Experience using AI in sales or outreach workflows is a plus. You are a natural communicator who is persuasive, personable, and loves building professional relationships and your English is fluent, both spoken and written, as you will be communicating with global researchers and international teams every day. You have an entrepreneurial mindset, always looking for opportunities and taking the initiative to make things happen. This opportunity may be particularly relevant if your background includes microbiology, cellular and infection microbiology, bioengineering, biotechnology, agronomy, soil science, environmental science, environmental chemistry, water research, food science, food technology or related life-science fields. Recruitment is free from discrimination – including based on race, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or sexual orientation. With employees from more than 50 different nations, our diversity creates vibrant teams and constantly challenges us to appreciate multiple perspectives. items.desc: We are seeking an exceptional Consultant Clinical Scientist to provide scientific, strategic and managerial leadership within the Proton Beam Therapy Physics service at UCLH. This is a rare opportunity to lead a key specialist area of a national proton therapy service, driving innovation, research and service development while ensuring the highest standards of patient safety and clinical excellence. Working within a highly experienced multidisciplinary team, you will play a key role in developing advanced proton therapy techniques, leading complex projects and influencing the future direction of radiotherapy physics locally, nationally and internationally. You will lead a key area of the Proton Beam Therapy Physics service, with responsibility for clinical service delivery, scientific leadership, treatment planning or dosimetry & quality assurance activities, and the implementation of new technologies and techniques. Acting as a Medical Physics Expert, you will provide highly specialised advice on complex clinical and technical issues, oversee commissioning and quality assurance programmes, and ensure compliance with all relevant legislation and professional standards. You will manage and develop staff, lead service improvement and research initiatives, contribute to strategic planning, and work closely with clinicians, radiographers, physicists, engineers, academic and industrial partners to deliver world-class proton therapy services. You will also support education and training programmes and contribute to the national and international profile of UCLH through research, innovation and publication. University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research. We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites: University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing) National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals University College Hospital Grafton Way Building Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centre The Hospital for Tropical Diseases University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women’s health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology. We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040. For the full Person Specification and more information regarding the main responsibilities of this role, please refer to the attached Job Description. Come and be a part of the best NHS trust in England to work for, according to our staff* UCLH top trust to work at in England - In the most recent NHS staff survey UCLH had the highest percentage of staff who said they would recommend us as a place to work, out of all general acute or acute/community NHS trusts in England – for the third year in a row. items.desc: Vacancy ID: 50294 Role overview: Site Reliability Engineer Waterloo - Hybrid Working Full Time Permanent Grade 4 At Currys we’re united by one passion: to help everyone enjoy amazing technology. As one of the best-known retailers of tech, we’re proud of the service our customers receive – and it’s all down to our team of caring and committed colleagues. Join us and you’ll work in a great team where you can be yourself and bring your personality. Working as one team, we learn and grow together, celebrating the big and small moments that make every day amazing. As a Site Reliability Engineer you will apply software engineering practices to operations, owning the end-to-end availability, performance and resilience of our customer-facing and core trading services. You will work as part of a centralised SRE squad, embedding with product engineering teams to design reliability in from the start: defining service level objectives, automating away operational toil, and continuously improving how we build, deploy, observe and operate software at scale. A core focus of this role is the design and build of our central AIOps platform: a shared capability that ingests telemetry, events and change data from across the estate and applies machine learning and AI-assisted automation to detect anomalies earlier, correlate and suppress alert noise, predict capacity and performance issues before they impact customers, and drive automated diagnosis and remediation of common failure modes. You will help shift Currys from reactive incident response towards predictive, self-healing operations. This is an operations role first and foremost. However you will write production-quality code, treat infrastructure and operational tooling as software, and bring rigour to incident response, root cause analysis and the systematic elimination of repeat failures. Role overview: Reliability Engineering: Define, implement and report on SLIs, SLOs and error budgets with product squads, and use them to drive engineering prioritisation and release decisions. AIOps platform: Design, build and operate Currys’ central AIOps platform, covering telemetry ingestion and event correlation, ML-based anomaly detection and predictive alerting, intelligent alert routing and noise reduction, and automated runbook execution and remediation, integrated with our ITSM, incident and on-call tooling. Observability: Build and evolve a modern observability stack (metrics, logs, traces and events) using open standards such as OpenTelemetry, ensuring services are instrumented, debuggable and measurable by default. Automation: Eliminate operational toil through software: infrastructure as code, self-service tooling, CI/CD pipeline improvements and automated reliability testing, including chaos and resilience experiments. Incident Response: Act as an escalation point for major incidents, lead blameless post-incident reviews, and drive root cause analysis through to permanent fixes, increasingly augmented by AI-assisted diagnosis from the AIOps platform. Design for reliability: Review and challenge architecture and designs (HLD/LLD) to embed reliability, scalability, security and operability principles; set direction on strategic tooling and reduce duplication and technical debt. Peak Readiness: Lead capacity planning and performance engineering for peak trading events (e.g. Black Friday), using predictive modelling from platform telemetry. Engineering Culture: Coach product engineering teams in SRE and operational best practice, raising production standards across internal and third-party engineering functions, and participate in a 24x7 on-call rota. Required Skills & Experience: The successful candidate will have a strong software engineering background and be able to demonstrate sound judgement operating complex, high-traffic production systems. You will collaborate with engineers, product owners, service management and third-party partners in the UK and overseas, so clear communication and strong stakeholder skills are essential. Experience in retail, e-commerce, consumer goods or finance is valued. Essential: Strong software engineering skills: proficiency in at least one modern language (e.g. Python, Go, PHP or Java), with experience writing, reviewing and operating production code. Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (Azure preferred; AWS/GCP valued), containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and Linux/Windows environments. Deep observability and monitoring experience (e.g. OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, New Relic, Azure Monitor, PagerDuty), including designing SLIs/SLOs and alerting strategies. Experience with AIOps capabilities such as anomaly detection, event correlation, predictive alerting or automated remediation, either building them or applying platforms. Solid incident management experience in complex, fast-paced IT environments, including post-incident review and root cause analysis. Desirable: Applied ML/data engineering for operations: …

items.desc: The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic. The Department of Psychiatry is based on the Warneford Hospital site in Oxford – a friendly, welcoming place of work with an international reputation for excellence. The Department has a substantial research programme, with major funding from Medical Research Council (MRC), Wellcome Trust and National Institute for Health Research (NIHR) and provides highly rated medical training in psychiatry. The Head of Department is Professor Belinda Lennox. Reporting to the Dr Chloe Yap, the post holder is a member of the Immuno-Metabolism & Severe Mental Illness research group with responsibility for the provision of research support for a project investigating the role of accelerated biological aging in psychosis. What We Offer As an employer, we genuinely care about our employees’ wellbeing and this is reflected in the range of benefits that we offer including: An excellent contributory pension scheme 38 days annual leave A comprehensive range of childcare services Family leave schemes Cycle loan scheme Discounted bus travel and Season Ticket travel loans Membership to a variety of social and sports clubs This role also offers the opportunity for hybrid working About the Role The post is a part-time, 7.5 hours per week (20.13%FTE), funded to 31 January 2028, and based in the Department of Psychiatry at the Warneford Hospital. You will analyse large multi-modal datasets relevant to psychosis, including proteomic, metabolomic, neuroimaging and genomic data, and generate and apply biological ageing clocks across a range of omics modalities. You will select, adapt and develop appropriate analytical methodologies, as well as review and synthesise literature on biological ageing and undertake systematic literature reviews. You will contribute to research publications and conference presentations and support wider project planning and day-to-day project administration. About You You will hold a first degree, for example in biomedical sciences, psychology or psychiatry, and/or have relevant experience, and be working towards a doctorate in psychosis. You will have experience using command line tools for reproducible data analysis, alongside skills in statistics, machine learning, data cleaning and analysis pipelines. You will also have experience working with large multi-modal datasets relevant to psychiatry and sufficient specialist knowledge of biological ageing to work within established research programmes. You will be able to communicate research findings clearly, including writing for publication, presenting data at conferences and representing the research group at meetings. Experience of contributing to research publications and working collaboratively within a research team, including contributing ideas for new research projects, would be desirable. Diversity Committed to equality and valuing diversity Our active Psychiatry People and Culture teams and initiatives including our values and behaviours framework, work to make the Department of Psychiatry as supportive, welcoming and inclusive as possible. Please see the University pages on the application process at https://www.jobs.ox.ac.uk/application-process The closing date for applications is 28 October 2026.

Most research today sits behind paywalls, meaning only people at well-funded universities or those who can pay get to read it. Open access flips that: every article we publish is peer-reviewed and made available online to anyone, anywhere at no cost. As one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access publishers, we’ve seen Frontiers research cited 16 million times, and viewed and downloaded more than 5.3 billion times, proof of what science without barriers can do. items.desc: Department: Data & AI Location: UK - London Description Insurance isn’t the first industry most data scientists think of when they imagine cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) work, but the incredibly rich data and nature of the business make it a great place to put cutting-edge AI to use. CFC's Data & AI team is building production agentic and ML systems that automate and inform complex underwriting decisions that drive real business outcomes - not demos, not proof-of-concepts sitting on a shelf. The team includes ML engineers and software engineers shipping production services, and this role sits alongside them as an analytical counterpart: running experiments, stress-testing assumptions, and generating the evidence that shapes what gets built and how it improves over time. We are looking for a mid-level Data Scientist to join the team that owns business-critical, live solutions utilising Large Language Models (LLMs), such as an email ingestion/extraction solution and underwriting agents. This is not a pure research or offline-modelling role - when research is carried out and potential opportunities identified it is expected that you will work closely with ML engineers and software engineers to build this into a live system, where quality, reliability, and evaluation rigor directly affects the business. We expect that a successful candidate will be able to own the data science side of a production LLM system end-to-end: partnering with stakeholders to build early prototypes, designing evaluation frameworks, measuring agent quality, and turning ambiguous "is this good?" questions into repeatable, defensible metrics - while working closely with engineers to understand what it takes to take that work from prototype to live system. About the role Explore complex, high dimensional, real-world datasets to uncover insights that meaningfully improve underwriting decisions and system performance at scale. Partner directly with underwriting and business stakeholders to scope problems, assess feasibility, and build early prototypes (e.g. PoC agents, rapid evaluation of an LLM approach) before committing engineering investment. Stay involved from prototype through to production, working with ML/software engineers to harden, scale, and maintain what you've built as a key contributor to the codebase. Design and run evaluation frameworks for LLM-powered agent behaviour, including offline (golden datasets, regression suites) and online (production monitoring, A/B testing) evaluation. Build and maintain analytical pipelines — prompt design, calibration against human labels, bias/consistency checks, LLM-as-a-judge, and ongoing validation that the judge stays trustworthy as the underlying models change. Partner with ML engineers to design system nodes/components, translating data science findings into concrete engineering requirements. Define quality metrics for agent outputs (accuracy, hallucination rate, task completion, groundedness, latency/cost trade-offs) and track them over time. Work with software engineers on productionising evaluation and monitoring code: CI/CD integration, release gating, and operational readiness (alerting, dashboards, on-call awareness). Actively explore cutting-edge developments in AI and machine learning — with the space and support to experiment, prototype, and bring new techniques into production where they add value. Investigate how agentic systems behave in production — identifying edge cases, failure modes, and opportunities to make systems more robust and reliable. Prototype and iterate on features for AI/ML pipelines, taking ideas from early exploration through to measurable impact in production services. Document experiments, findings, and methodologies clearly so that insights are reproducible and decisions are traceable. items.desc: About the job The prompt is the easy part. Maybe this is your situation. You got a Claude Code or Copilot license at work this year. Everyone did. But you aren’t satisfied with simply using it to complete your tasks faster. You want to do more. You compare harnesses. You try a new model the day it is released. You build a loop of agents, then a graph of them. You put a workflow behind an endpoint, try a vector database just to see how it behaves, build a semantic index over your own notes, ship a small app nobody asked for. You want this to be your real job, but you have to take that next ticket anyway. Or maybe it is this. You are past that. You have the Max accounts and the API keys. Your AI bill is in the tens of thousands of kronor a month and you think it is cheap. You are building the foundations, pushing what an autonomous model can actually do, and you are good at it. The problem is that you are alone. Nobody at work does what you do, and when you figure something out there is no one to argue with about it. If either of these is you, keep reading. If you have been both, a year apart, we should talk today. What we do Prompting stopped being the hard part a while ago. Everyone does it now. The hard part is the step after: building the structure that lets autonomous models like Claude Fable and GPT-6 plan, build, test, deploy and ship a complete application, with no human writing code, and with code, architecture and tests of a quality no developer sustains by hand. That is TokenTek's whole job. We have migrated millions of lines of legacy code this way, fully autonomously. Independent external code reviews have given the code and architecture our structures produce their highest rating, and we will show you the reports in the first interview. Nobody here writes code by hand. When something is manual, we build the workflow that does it. The tools change with the client. The way we work does not. We have shipped apps with a millions of downloads and a banking app with a million users. Our systems run inside companies in finance, automotive and shipping. You would work forward deployed: inside the client's team, with their management, from first idea to running system. What you would do here You design the checks the model cannot game: the specification, the evals, property and differential tests, and the gates between build, deploy and release. When the model writes both the code and the tests, your job is to make sure the tests mean something. You decide what each model is for, what goes in its context and what it retrieves, and you read the traces when a run goes wrong. You run legacy migrations at the scale of millions of lines, autonomously, and you prove the result is correct. You build the data layer: retrieval, embeddings, vector search and knowledge graphs, exposed as tools and endpoints the client's systems can call, with evals that show it works. You are responsible for quality. What you ship is built to pass an external review, not just a demo. You sit with the client's team, understand the actual problem, and take it from vision to production. If you like teaching, there is room for that too. Together with Hubbau we run a twelve-month AI engineering program for M.Sc. graduates, with our engineers as coaches. What we need from you M.Sc. in computer science, systems architecture, informatics or similar. At least two or three years of building production software, preferably also with experience from data integrations or ML models. There is no upper limit. Being able to present something you built with AI where the model did the work and you built the structure. A repo, a demo, a workflow. Preferably something with real users. Opinions. You know how the models and harnesses differ, and you can argue for your choices. Judgment. Models will hand you working code all day. You know the difference between working code and good architecture, and you insist on the second. Swedish and English, spoken and written. Several of our clients require both. What you get This work, all day, on the company's account instead of your own. Colleagues who read the same release notes you do and are passionate about AI. Exciting projects where you can grow your skills in a small specialized team. Generous vacation, pension and insurance benefits, plus team trips worth closing your laptop for. Practicalities Full-time, based at our office in Göteborg. We work mostly from the office, with flexibility when you need it. How to apply: Send your CV and a link to the thing you built to hello@tokentek.ai, with "AI Engineer" in the subject line. We read every application ourselves.

Ett exempel på vad man redan vet är att man skulle kunna använda en separat agent som testar kod som har skrivits av en annan agent. En sådan lösning flyttar dock bara problemet från vad en agent gör till vad en annan agent gör och man har egentligen inte löst någonting eller väldigt lite. Osäkerheten finns där fortfarande. Detta gäller framför allt verktygsstöd. Själva processen (den manuella) spelar visserligen en roll, men i slutändan vill man kunna automatisera tester så långt det går. Processen har då en underordnad roll och det viktiga blir tekniska lösningar för att säkerställa säkerhet, robusthet, prestandakrav, minska eller eliminera externa beroenden, ha en möjlighet att kunna underhålla koden och drifta den osv. Du kommer utföra arbetet på sektionen för Data & AI. Du får en handledare. Personer som aktivt jobbar med dessa frågor kommer kunna ge feedback på ditt arbete allt eftersom det fortskrider. Din profil Arbetet är lämpligt för två studenter med intresse för AI, forskning och utveckling. Du/ni är i slutet av en master-utbildning inom datavetenskap (CS), datateknik (CE) eller motsvarande och ska påbörja ett examensarbete om 30 HP. Du måste ha erfarenhet av programmering så att du är väl bevandrad i olika problemställningar som kan uppstå vad gäller kodstruktur, algoritmanalys (ordo-komplexitet), integration mot andra system via API:er osv. Vi ger dig det stöd och den vägledning du behöver för att omsätta dina teoretiska kunskaper i praktiska lösningar. Bli en drivande kraft bakom Saabs tekniska framsteg! Befattningen kräver att du genomgår och godkänns enligt vid var tid gällande bestämmelser för säkerhetsskydd. För befattningar där Saab har krav på säkerhetsklassinplacering kan, i förekommande fall, medföra krav på visst medborgarskap. Vänligen observera att vi arbetar med löpande urval och tjänsten kan komma att tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdatum har gått ut. Kontaktperson och tentativ handledare Mikael Hillborg, Chef Data & AI e-post: mikael.hillborg@saabgroup.com +46 (0)72 970 2648 Vad du blir en del av Upptäck oändliga möjligheter. Anta utmaningar, skapa smarta innovationer och uppgradera dina förmågor. Det här är en plats för kluriga tänkare, modiga pionjärer och alla däremellan. Tillsammans uppnår vi det extraordinära, var och en tar med sitt unika perspektiv. Varje bidrag räknas. Med 28 000 talangfulla medarbetare utvecklar Saab teknik och lösningar för en säkrare och mer hållbar värld. Saab utvecklar, tillverkar och underhåller avancerade system inom flygteknik, vapen, ledningssystem, sensorer och undervattenssystem. items.card: You will be part of a team building Bain’s integrated suite of agentic decisioning tools that gives large organizations always-on intelligence across their most important growth decisions. The role sits at an intersection few organizations can offer: the analytical depth and client access of a top-tier consultancy, the technical ambition of a product company, and engineering work at the frontier of applied AI. You
items.desc: What Makes Us a Great Place to Work We are proud to be consistently recognized as one of the world’s best places to work. We are currently the top ranked consulting firm on Glassdoor’s Best Places to Work list and have earned the #1 overall spot a record seven times. Extraordinary teams are at the heart of our business strategy, but these don’t happen by chance. They require intentional focus on bringing together a broad set of backgrounds, cultures, experiences, perspectives, and skills in a supportive and inclusive work environment. We hire people with exceptional talent and create an environment in which every individual can thrive professionally and personally. Who You’ll Work With You will be part of a team building Bain’s integrated suite of agentic decisioning tools that gives large organizations always-on intelligence across their most important growth decisions. The role sits at an intersection few organizations can offer: the analytical depth and client access of a top-tier consultancy, the technical ambition of a product company, and engineering work at the frontier of applied AI. You will work inside Bain’s standing product team, building software that helps the world’s largest companies answer the questions that drive their business: where to invest, where to focus, and how to win. The impact of what you build is direct and immediate, and the platform compounds in value with every release. The platform has two layers working together: an agentic core and a set of decision modules, each solving a distinct commercial problem. The build lifecycle is connected to the real world: as case teams work alongside clients across industries and geographies, that feedback flows straight back to engineering and into the product. Every client engagement makes the platform smarter, broader, and more resilient. This is a startup inside an established company. You get genuine early-stage ownership and real influence over architecture and product direction, backed by Bain’s global scale, client relationships, and leadership commitment; the pace of a startup with the runway of a global firm. We are looking for engineers who see how to make the platform’s evaluations sharper and bring that instinct to every sprint without being asked, and who are comfortable with problems that do not have a known answer. The work involves evaluation frameworks for LLM-based and agentic systems, integration testing, and data problems with no off-the-shelf answer. Experience with agentic systems matters: tool and context protocols such as MCP, evaluation harnesses, and entity resolution across messy enterprise data. This is applied AI in production, at scale, with real users depending on what you build. The field is moving quickly and the team is built to move with it, so the willingness to keep learning counts for as much as what you already know: real-time decision engines, cloud-native infrastructure, and data challenges without off-the-shelf answers. This is applied AI in production, at scale, with real users depending on what you build. Native AI fluency matters here, and so does the drive to keep learning: because the field is moving fast and this team is built to move with it. Where You’ll Fit Within the Team The AI Engineer, Evals and Systems Integration works directly under the AI Engineering Lead, Evals and Systems Integration, contributing to the evaluation framework and integration testing infrastructure across the Growth AI Performance System platform. This is a hands-on implementation role: you will build and run the test suites, evaluation pipelines, and data quality checks that the evaluation framework depends on, working across the data ontology, Agentic Core, and platform and security layers under the direction of the Evals Lead. You will develop broad exposure to the full Growth AI Performance System stack: from the knowledge graph and semantic layer through agentic orchestration and retrieval pipelines to the product module outputs that clients see. This cross-cutting view makes it an excellent role for an engineer who wants to develop deep expertise in how complex AI systems fail, how to measure quality systematically, and what it takes to make a production AI platform reliable enough for enterprise clients to depend on. You will work across the platform and product modules focused on marketing ROI, brand, and pricing strategy, building the evaluation datasets, regression tests, and integration checks that validate quality at each layer and across the integration points between them. The role has developing client proximity. As you grow into the position, you will engage with consulting teams to understand where system outputs fell short in live engagements, and contribute to the structured feedback loops that translate client experience into evaluation improvements. What You’ll Do Building evaluation infrastructure Build and maintain automated test suites and evaluation pipelines for components of the Growth AI …
