items.desc: Placeringsort Luleå Diarienummer FK 2026/031951 Varje år fattar Försäkringskassan 21 miljoner beslut som påverkar människors liv och hela samhället. Vi betalar ut cirka 260 miljarder kronor varje år. Det är allas skattepengar vi har hand om. Det är ett stort ansvar. Därför tänker vi nytt och använder den senaste tekniken för att förenkla och förbättra, utveckla och leverera it-tjänsterna för den svenska socialförsäkringen. Välkommen till en av Sveriges största IT-avdelningar. It-utvecklingsenheterna i Luleå och Kalix befinner sig i en spännande utvecklingsfas och utökar nu verksamheten. Här utvecklar och förvaltar vi samhällsviktiga IT-lösningar inom bland annat arbetsmarknadsstöd, pension, externt informationsutbyte och datahantering. På våra kontor arbetar drygt 100 medarbetare, varav majoriteten är systemutvecklare. Du får arbeta med komplexa system i nära samarbete med erfarna kollegor i agila team. Tekniskt ansvar, kvalitet, säkerhet och automatisering är centrala delar av vardagen och du får möjlighet att påverka lösningar som används av stora delar av samhället varje dag. Systemutveckling, Java, backend, testare och systemanalytiker Vi söker nu fler kollegor till våra agila DevOps-team. Vårt uppdrag är att utveckla och förvalta samhällsviktiga system som ska vara tillförlitliga, säkra och användbara. För att lyckas med detta behöver vi stärka upp med flera kompetenser. Som systemutvecklare hos oss arbetar du med hela kedjan från kravanalys och utveckling till test, förvaltning och observerbarhet. Samtidigt finns möjlighet att fördjupa sig inom särskilda områden där vi har särskilt behov. Nedan kan du läsa mer om de kompetenser vi nu söker: Systemutveckling i Java: Vi söker systemutvecklare med tyngdpunkt inom backend och Java. Du arbetar med utveckling och förvaltning av komplexa system och är delaktig från analys och design till implementation, test och driftsättning. Vi ser gärna att du har förståelse för hela utvecklingskedjan och kan se hur kod, test, integration, infrastruktur och drift hänger ihop. Arbetet innebär att utveckla och förvalta system med höga krav på prestanda och robusthet. Teknisk test: Vi söker erfaren tekniska testare som kan ta ansvar för kvalitetssäkring av komplexa system. Du planerar, genomför och utvecklar tester och bidrar till att identifiera risker och fel tidigt i utvecklingsprocessen. Arbetet omfattar både automatiserade och manuella tester. Du har god teknisk förståelse och kan bedöma hur olika delar av ett system samverkar. Erfarenhet av testautomation och utveckling av testmetoder är värdefullt. Systemanalytiker: Vi söker erfaren systemanalytiker som kan analysera komplexa behov och problem och omsätta dem till tydliga krav och tekniska lösningar. Du arbetar nära verksamhet och IT och skapar struktur och förståelse mellan olika perspektiv. Rollen innebär att analysera behov och krav, förstå komplexa system och ta fram lösningsunderlag som kan omsättas av DevOps-teamen. Du samarbetar nära systemutvecklare, testare och andra kompetenser i den agila utvecklingsmiljön. Tjänsten innebär att du hanterar sekretessbelagda uppgifter vilket ställer höga krav på rätt hantering. Därför är det viktigt att du som ska arbeta hos oss har högt säkerhetsmedvetande. Det är ett jobb för dig som vill vara med och ta ansvar. Vi söker dig som har högskoleexamen eller erfarenheter och kvalifikationer som kan prövas likvärdiga har specialistkompetens inom systemutveckling inom Java, test, systemanalys agerar på eget initiativ och tar ansvar för att nå goda resultat samarbetar effektivt med andra för att nå gemensamma mål har ett systematiskt och noggrant arbetssätt kan förstå och analysera komplexa frågor har god kommunikativ förmåga, i tal och skrift har goda kunskaper i svenska, i tal och skrift. Det är meriterande om du har har erfarenhet av DevOps, Confluence, Bitbucket, Gitea, SQL, Linux har erfarenhet av microtjänstlösningar i OpenShift och Kubernetes har erfarenhet av agilt arbetssätt har erfarenhet av arbete i stor it-organisation har erfarenhet av arbete inom offentlig verksamhet. Vi lägger stor vikt vid dina personliga egenskaper. Övrigt Ett flertal tjänster, tillsvidare heltid, med tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Provanställning kan bli aktuellt. Vissa anställningar hos oss innebär deltagande i säkerhetskänslig verksamhet. För att bli anställd i en sådan tjänst krävs godkänd säkerhetsprövning enligt säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585). I enlighet med Försäkringskassans riktlinje för säkerhet genomförs bakgrundskontroller i denna rekrytering. Möjlighet till distansarbete finns om arbetet tillåter. I den här rekryteringen kan arbetspsykologiska test användas som en del i urvalsarbetet. Placeringsort: Luleå. Vill du veta mer om Försäkringskassan som arbetsgivare? items.desc: Due to internal promotion, we are now looking for a Medical Advisor to join our team! Bring your scientific expertise to a role where your insights, relationships, and ideas can help shape oncology care in Sweden. As a trusted scientific partner to healthcare professionals, you will focus on solid tumours, particularly gynaecological oncology, with the potential to expand into other tumour areas as our pipeline evolves. You will connect emerging evidence with clinical needs, turn insights into medical strategy, and collaborate with internal teams and external experts to advance patient care. If you are curious, collaborative, and motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is an opportunity to grow your expertise while uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. We create a place where people can grow, be their best, be safe, and feel welcome, valued and included. Discover more about our company wide benefits and life at GSK on our webpage Life at GSK | GSK In this role you will Build and strengthen trusted, peer-to-peer scientific relationships with oncology healthcare professionals and key stakeholders in solid tumours, with a particular focus on gynaecological oncology. Lead balanced, evidence-based scientific exchange, translating complex and emerging data into clear discussions that support informed clinical decisions and patient care. Identify unmet clinical needs, gather and document actionable insights, and translate them into recommendations for medical strategy. Contribute to clinical development by identifying and qualifying potential investigators and clinical sites. Represent GSK at scientific meetings, congresses, and expert forums, fostering scientific dialogue and bringing relevant knowledge back to the organisation. Partner with cross-functional colleagues on approved scientific education, medical projects and initiatives that address clinical needs. Why you? Basic Qualifications & Skills: We are looking for professionals with these required skills to achieve our goals: Advanced degree in medicine, pharmacy, life sciences or a related field, such as MD, PhD, PharmD or equivalent. Pharmaceutical-industry experience in Medical Affairs, Medical Science Liaison or a related scientific role. Strong knowledge of solid-tumour oncology clinical practice, treatment options and the evolving treatment landscape. Ability to make complex scientific information clear, relevant, and engaging for healthcare professionals. Demonstrated experience in building trusted, peer-to-peer relationships with oncology experts and healthcare teams. Ability to work independently, take initiative, and organise priorities effectively while complying with relevant regulations and standards. Fluent in Swedish and English both written and spoken. Preferred Qualifications & Skills: Please note the following skills are not necessary, just preferred, if you do not have them, please still apply: Clinical experience in oncology or direct patient care environments related to solid tumours, preferably gynecological cancer. Experience supporting clinical trials, investigator-initiated studies, or real-world evidence projects. Familiarity with the Swedish healthcare system, including hospitals and reimbursement processes. Strong presentation and facilitation skills that encourage meaningful scientific discussion and learning. Proven ability to identify and engage key opinion leaders and academic experts in oncology. A collaborative mindset, enthusiasm for continuous learning, and a commitment to contributing within cross-functional teams. Work model and travel This role is based in Sweden with hybrid working flexibility, combining remote work with regular, in-person engagement with healthcare professionals across your assigned territory. Travel within the region is expected, at 50% of your time. Ready to turn scientific expertise into meaningful impact? Bring your curiosity, ideas, and passion for oncology to a role where you can contribute to patient care today and develop your expertise as our pipeline evolves. We value your growth, your contribution, and the power of inclusion. Apply today and help advance care for people living with solid tumours in Sweden. Together, we can unite science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease. Closing Date for Applications – 30th October (COB) Please take a copy of the Job Description, as this will not be available post closure of the advert. When applying for this role, please use the ‘cover letter’ of the online application or your CV to describe how you meet the competencies for this role, as outlined in the job requirements above. The information that you have provided in your cover letter and CV will be used to assess your application. items.desc: Studies show that women and underrepresented groups often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. At Stegra, we’re building an impact-driven, sustainable company - and we need a diverse, inclusive team to make it happen. If you share our passion but don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the perfect fit for this role, or another as we grow. At Stegra, we’re not just building a plant, we’re proving that sustainable industry is possible. And to do that, we need people like you. Join a team where safety comes first. Where we support each other, learn as we go, and make space for everyone to grow and contribute. This is your chance to be part of something big - while being closer to nature and leading a balanced, purposeful life. What you’ll do Right now, we are looking for a Digital Workplace Technician for our Digital Workplace team . This is a temporary 12-month assignment. As a Digital Workplace Technician at Stegra, you’ll help colleagues with everyday digital workplace questions and issues. This is a one-year contract where you’ll provide on-site and remote support, follow established processes, and build your experience with workplace tools and user support. Specific to this role, the day-to-day tasks will include the following, but as we are a growing company with few silos between teams, other tasks may be included as well. Provide in-person and remote support through Digi Bars (onsite support points), Slack, and ticketing systems. Help troubleshoot common issues with Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Windows, macOS, devices, and user access, escalating issues when needed. Support onboarding and offboarding tasks, such as preparing devices and setting up user accounts. Follow existing support processes and help keep user guides, FAQs, and other support materials up to date. Contribute to self-service materials and simple workflow improvements with guidance from the team. Identify recurring support questions and share them with the team. Help prepare and share short digital tips or walkthroughs for colleagues. Learn about AI capabilities relevant to digital workplace support and share potential use cases with the team. What you’ll bring You’re curious and believe that real progress happens when we work together. You’re not afraid to challenge old ways of thinking - and you treat others with respect while doing it. At Stegra, we value people who take initiative, build trust, and help create a workplace where everyone can do their best. Who we think you are You have an interest in IT support, workplace technology, and helping people solve everyday problems. You communicate clearly and patiently, and enjoy working with colleagues. You’re comfortable providing direct support on-site as well as remotely. You have some familiarity with tools such as Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Windows, or macOS. You’re organized, willing to follow established processes, and know when to ask for help or escalate an issue. You’re curious and willing to learn new tools and ways of working. It’s a bonus if you have Experience in a service or support role, or through a student project. An interest in writing clear instructions or maintaining user documentation. Basic familiarity with scripting, automation, or no-code tools. Benefits at Stegra At Stegra, you’ll join a company where your work has real impact on the climate, the industry, and future generations. We’re building a culture rooted in safety, trust, and inclusion, where people feel supported to grow and thrive. You’ll receive fair, competitive compensation aligned with collective agreements, along with benefits like up to 30 days of paid vacation, occupational pension, parental benefits, and insurance. If you need support with relocation or immigration, our relocation department will help guide you through the process, whether it’s permits, housing or other practical matters. You can also enjoy perks like subsidized gym memberships and bike leases, plus the everyday benefits of life closer to nature. Read more about Benefits at Stegra here. This is Stegra Stegra is on a mission to change the global steel industry by producing green hydrogen, iron, and steel - with the goal of eliminating CO₂ emissions. Instead of coal, we use green hydrogen and fossil-free electricity, meaning our primary emissions will be water and heat. By 2030, our ambition is to produce 5 million tonnes of green steel annually in our fully integrated, digitized, and sustainable plant in Boden, Northern Sweden - currently under construction. But this is just the beginning. Our expertise in green hydrogen will enable us to decarbonize industries beyond steel, paving the way for a cleaner future. Our Boden Site Our Boden site is located just west of Boden City, right in the heart of a growing green industrial hub in Northern Sweden. It’s where we’re building one of the world’s most modern, sustainable steel plants—designed with safety, efficiency, and …

items.desc: Applications are invited for this fixed term, full time role as Medical Laboratory Assistant (MLA) in the specimen reception section for the South East Haematological Malignancy Diagnostic Service (SE-HMDS) at King’s College Hospital. The reception is integral to the SE-HMDS, acting as a central sample receipt point for the four key laboratories that make up the SE-HMDS plus the clinically lead morphology service. The most important part of the role will be sample handling and electronic logging of the samples received. The SE-HMDS reception also contribute to the preparation, maintenance, operation and quality assurance of laboratory equipment. Training and development is a key focus at Synnovis and this is an excellent opportunity to enhance skills and knowledge in a specialist department environment. There is also a keen interest in Research & Development within the departments that is supported by various funds and collaborators as we endeavour to provide a leading and fit-for-purpose service to our patients. There is culture of continuous quality improvement that applies to both staff and departmental development. This is a great opportunity to work amongst a team of dedicated and patient focused individuals and enhance administrative, communication and data/sample handling skills. The successful candidate will be a team player and will be working closely with the laboratories, scientific and clinical staff. They must have excellent attention to detail and be able to accurately and efficiently transfer data on to electronic systems. Effective communication skills with all levels of staff, internal and external users is essential. There is a variety of laboratory information management systems (LIMS) in use within the laboratories, candidates must have good IT skills, and prior experience of various forms of LIMS is beneficial. The role largely involves accurate transfer of clinical information and specimen prioritisation with the requirement for good medical/scientific literacy skills. Working knowledge of the Health & Safety requirements of handling biological materials is desirable and experience in the preparation of blood and bone marrow slides would be of additional benefit. The SE-HMDS is a regional centre for diagnostic services, providing UKAS accredited Immunophenotyping, Morphology, Cytogenetic, Molecular Diagnostic and Histopathology services covering most of Southeast England. There has been a steady rise in referrals to the SE-HMDS, from clinicians who require increasingly sophisticated and accurate haematological investigations, for diagnosis and disease monitoring. As a member of the SE-HMDS reception, you are the essential first and last points of contact for patient specimens and results, with service quality, a key focus throughout. As an essential part of the SE-HMDS, the reception team also have access to a number of developmental activities including clinical presentations, webinars and integrated departmental training sessions for haematological malignancies. Here you can learn more about the various departments, investigations and the patients that we serve. The SE-HMDS reception area acts as a central location for receipt of samples, performing pre and post analytical procedures and other support for the five areas that make up SE-HMDS: Immunophenotyping, Morphology, Cytogenetics, Laboratory Molecular Haemato-Oncology and Histopathology. The post holder will work as a member of the support staff to assist SE-HMDS in the appropriate handling, receipt and distribution of specimens. The main responsibility of the post holder will be to perform the electronic receipt, data management and quality assurance of specimens, as well as preparation, maintenance, operation and quality assurance of laboratory slide staining equipment. Concentration, attention to detail and accurate transcription of data are essential skills to these processes and form the greater part of the working day. Good IT and typing skills are required to perform this role and training will be provided for the use of the various and bespoke LIMS. The post holder will offer a helpful and professional service to all visitors and enquiries from a broad spectrum of service users under the direction of qualified laboratory staff and where appropriate will assist in the collection and compilation of data for management purposes. It will be essential that the post hold can follow written and verbal instructions as directed by the supervisor, senior scientists, operational and quality leads or head or section. Prioritisation and time management skills are required for time sensitive tests and urgency of clinical investigations within a busy environment. Once competence in tasks is achieved members of the team are also required to assist in the training of others whilst maintaining and promoting safe working practises. items.desc: Job number NAT02293 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Chemistry Salary or Salary range £48,246 - £58,318 per annum Location/campus White City Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 18 Nov 2026 About the role We are seeking a talented technician to join the team in the group of Professor Ed Tate at Imperial College London. This role will support the production and characterisation of recombinant proteins for molecular glue discovery. The position is available full time, starting in January 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter, with flexibility to start earlier). Molecular glues are an emerging class of small molecules which induce or stabilise protein-protein interactions, creating new opportunities to modulate biological processes and tackle ‘undruggable’ targets through induced proximity. Despite growing interest in the field, there remain limited approaches for the systematic discovery of molecular glues. As a result, there is a need for scalable and generalisable molecular glue discovery platforms that enable target proteins and compound libraries to be screened across the proteome. To support these efforts, we are establishing workflows for the production and characterisation of recombinant proteins for use in proteomic, biochemical, biophysical and cell-based assays. The successful candidate will play a central role in generating high-quality protein reagents and supporting downstream studies that underpin molecular glue discovery. What you would be doing Your role will focus on the expression, purification and characterisation of recombinant proteins using mammalian cell expression to support molecular glue discovery projects. You may also contribute to the development of biochemical or biophysical assays using these proteins. You will be contributing to a dynamic and ambitious research programme, working in a multidisciplinary team spanning chemical biology, proteomics and medicinal chemistry. In addition to your core activities, you will support the day-to-day running of the laboratory. This includes maintaining equipment, purchasing and organising consumables, disposal of biohazard and chemical waste, participating in laboratory duty rotas, and providing introductory training for new users. The Tate group is culturally diverse and highly multidisciplinary, with project teams encompassing scientists at all levels of experience and from a variety of backgrounds (chemical biology, cell biology, proteomics, cancer biology, drug discovery, etc.). Technicians are expected to engage in the various projects across the Tate group and offer support on an ad-hoc basis as required outside of their core projects. We are looking for candidates who can thrive in this dynamic and creative environment and take optimal advantage of the many training opportunities it provides. What we are looking for Essential criteria for the role include: A minimum of a BSc and/or MSc qualification in biochemistry, chemical biology, biotechnology, or a closely related field, or an equivalent level of professional qualifications and experience. Experience with mammalian cell culture, protein purification and characterisation Knowledge of, data analysis, and safe laboratory working practices. Desirable experience for this role includes one or more of the following: experience with HEK293, Expi293 or related mammalian expression systems; biochemical or biophysical assay development; experience with plate-based assays; experience of ternary-complex formation assays; relevant laboratory management; knowledge of the molecular glue field. What we can offer you Working within the Tate group would give you the opportunity to work with >60 scientists at all levels from undergraduates to postdoctoral researchers with our state-of-the-art labs in West London, including the Agilent Measurement Suite and Imperial Drug Discovery Hub. You will be joining a team with an excellent track record in the areas of molecular glues and induced proximity mechanisms (https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c12299; https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c01420; The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: Gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year and generous pension schemes). items.desc: Job Introduction Scientist Analytical Chemistry Hoddesdon Pharmaron is a global CRO helping pharma and biotech companies bring new therapies to life. With over 25,000 employees worldwide across 23 locations in the US, UK and China, we support drug discovery through to manufacturing with fully integrated, high-quality services. We’re proud of the impact we make and just last year, we supported over 780 discovery projects, 1,000+ CMC programmes, and 1,000+ clinical trials across all phases. Our teams are involved in everything from small molecules to biologics and gene therapies, and we work with more than 3,000 global customers. To learn more, visit www.pharmaron.com. Is this you? Do you love getting hands-on with HPLC and seeing your results move a project forward? Are you keen to build your analytical skills in a fast-paced, GMP environment alongside experienced scientists? If so, we’d love to hear from you. We’re looking for a Scientist in Analytical Chemistry with solid HPLC experience, ideally alongside GC, SFC, NMR or other techniques used to characterise APIs. You’ll support our chemistry projects, help develop and validate analytical methods, contribute to the characterisation of Starting Materials, Intermediates and APIs, and work closely with our Process Chemistry colleagues. What’s in it for you at Pharmaron A vibrant, dynamic place to work: we’re a highly specialised, growing company in a critical sector of the economy. Our future is strong and exciting, and you can be part of it. Room to grow: our rapid growth means more opportunities for you to learn, develop and progress faster. A team that has your back: we support each other and enjoy what we do. After all, you spend about a third of your time here! What you’ll bring A BSc (Hons) or MSc in Analytical Chemistry or Chemistry Relevant experience in an Analytical Chemistry laboratory Significant expertise in HPLC and/or UPLC methods Hands-on experience and up-to-date knowledge of other analytical methodologies Experience working to GLP and GMP What you’ll be doing Analysing APIs, Intermediates, Starting Materials and Raw Materials using HPLC and other analytical methods Delivering your assigned tasks to tight deadlines Stepping in to learn new techniques whenever a project needs it Solving scientific problems as they arise Working effectively in a GMP laboratory Who we are “We are a dynamic, fast-growing company, with an enviable reputation for leading edge science, offering contract research services to some of the world’s leading pharmaceutical companies, solving what were believed to be unsolvable scientific challenges.” We relentlessly push the boundaries of scientific excellence to deliver solutions for our clients, always ethically and with integrity. We take pride in our professionalism and in giving our very best every time. Where you’ll work Picture yourself on our Hoddesdon campus in Hertfordshire: several purpose-built scientific and administrative buildings, a dedicated conference area and more than 5,000 m² of premier R&D space. It’s home to established Process Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Product Development and Drug Discovery teams, with state-of-the-art GMP facilities for API development, Oral Solid Dose manufacture, formulation development and process chemistry. It’s a highly supportive, team-focused environment where you can develop and fulfil your true potential. Your team Our Analytical Chemistry team supports other chemistry functions and our science partners with advanced analytical solutions that help move medicines to market. Here you’ll: Gain exposure to a wide range of modern techniques, including UHPLC, NMR and GC-MS Experience both early- and late-phase pharmaceutical development Apply your problem-solving skills across a wide variety of R&D projects Contribute to the development and validation of modern methods for testing raw materials, intermediates, APIs and material characterisation Explore further opportunities in polymorph screening, crystallisation optimisation and pre-formulation development What we offer A competitive salary and a progressive, comprehensive benefits package A state-of-the-art working environment on site Real growth and development, including funding for relevant training programmes Salary Competitive Frequency Annual Job Reference ukpharmaron/TP/141/781 Contract Type Permanent Contract Closing Date No expiry date Job Category Scientific (Analytical Chemistry) Division Process Chemistry Location Hoddesdon, United Kingdom Posted on 15 October, 2026

items.desc: Job Description Vertex is a global biotechnology company that aims to discover, develop and commercialize innovative new medicines so people with serious diseases can lead better lives. Founded in 1989 in Cambridge, MA, Vertex today has research and development sites and commercial offices around the world in the United States, Canada, Europe and Australia. We are recruiting for an Industrial placement student in the Structural Biology & Biophysics (SBB) Department, at our research facility in Oxfordshire, as part of our wider intern intake for the year. During your Industrial Placement you will get the opportunity to learn about our industry from a hands-on perspective. You will be working closely with and learning from some of the brightest people in the industry. Students can expect to be challenged by their work, connect with other students, and feel valued by the Vertex community. Main Duties & Objectives We are seeking an enthusiastic Biology Industrial Placement Student to join a collaborative project at the interface of Structural Biology & Biophysics (SBB) and Biology. This laboratory-based placement will provide hands-on experience in studying membrane proteins using complementary biochemical, biophysical and functional approaches. You will work alongside scientists across both departments, contributing to activities that support protein preparation and reconstitution into model membrane systems, followed by functional characterisation using electrophysiology-based methods. Through the placement, you will gain exposure to how multidisciplinary teams combine structural, biophysical and cellular/functional data to build understanding of biologically important targets and support drug discovery. items.desc: We are looking to recruit an experienced Cardiac Physiologist/Clinical Scientist in Echocardiography. The post is a fixed term 22-month contract funded as part of a research study funded through commercial partnership with Edwards. The successful candidate will assist in the development and delivery of an electronic fast track referral pathway across Cheshire and Merseyside for patients with severe aortic stenosis. The candidate will assist in the Standardisation of diagnostic and triage protocols for suspected AS to support the implementation of the pathway and enhance the identification of symptomatic and asymptomatic patients with severe AS by strengthening regional collaboration across NHS partners. The cardiac physiologist will be based at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital and will be expected to provide hands on echocardiography support and educational support across multiple hospital sites; there will be an innovative element to this post. Main duties of the job Provide specialised technical expertise to the area of echocardiography. Provide specialised technical expertise in diagnosis of valvular heart disease, particularly aortic stenosis Provide independent outreach Provide direct point of communication and liaison between regional echo services and LHCH structural valve service Provide close collaboration with TAVI specialist nurses and medical teams. Demonstrates empathy when dealing with patients in distressing conditions. Independently interprets results and provides factual reports for highly specialised diagnostic cardiac investigations Communicates effectively and advises both clinical and non-clinical staff regarding outcomes of diagnostic investigations. Undertakes supervision & training for Clinical staff, Trainee Cardiac Physiologists and other allied health professionals. Within their designated area assists the lead physiologist in implementing departmental strategies to ensure continuing development of patient-focused services in line with activity targets and the requirements of the Directorate. Assists lead physiologist in monitoring and maintaining quality of services within designated section. Ensures that individual own level of practice is kept up to date. Demonstrates active participation in clinical audit, and R&D activities. Has awareness of future implications for development of current Cardiology As the largest single site specialist heart and chest hospital in the UK, we, at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital, have a clear vision 'to be the best cardiothoracic integrated healthcare organisation'. We provide specialist services in cardiothoracic surgery, cardiology, respiratory medicine both in the hospital and out in the community. We serve a catchment area of 2.8 million people, spanning Merseyside, Cheshire, North Wales and the Isle of Man, and increasingly we receive referrals from outside these areas for highly specialised services such as aortics. Our reputation for strong performance is important in delivering the best care for our patients and high quality clinical services. This is underpinned by a culture of research and innovation, delivered in modern estate and our encouragement of flexible working in a variety of forms. Please visit our website - https://www.lhch.nhs.uk/ Please follow this link for a tour of our site - https://bit.ly/36ylsoq For full job description and personal specification please see attached files for main responsibilities of the post.

items.desc: Salary - Grade GBP £57,180 to £59,394 57180 - PO5 Contract Type Fixed Term / Secondment Contract Length 24 months Contracted Hours Full Time - 36 hours per week DBS Required Yes Department Adults, Health & Integration Service Adult Social Care Closing date 08/11/2026 Hackney is one of the most dynamic and progressive local authorities in the UK. We are a resilient, vibrant, and creative borough in the heart of London, with strong, diverse communities and a powerful set of shared values. Over the past twenty years, the Council has built up first-class services, outstanding public infrastructure, and a reputation for excellence, innovation, and ambition. We are leading the way on essential work such as our fight for equity in Hackney with a particular focus on becoming an actively anti-racist borough. But the work doesn’t stop there, we are proactive in our approach to bringing fairness to all aspects of life including gender, neurodiversity and across the poverty divide. Our Adult Social Care vision is that “We want you to achieve what matters to you, in partnership with our communities in Hackney. Where you need support, together we can find a solution that keeps you safe, well and independent.” We have an ambition to make a step-change in how we prevent, reduce and delay the development of social care needs, working collaboratively across the council, and with our partners in health, and the voluntary, community and faith sector in order to achieve this. Our Public Health Service plays a vital role in this mission. Together, we’re passionate about improving the health and wellbeing of our communities in Hackney. We work collaboratively and creatively to address health inequalities and create a healthier future for all. You can find out more about how we work in Adult Social Care, and how it is changing, by reading our annual report and three year plan at https://www.hackney.gov.uk/health-and-social-care/adult-social-care/adult-social-care-annual-reports-and-strategies. If you would like to find out more information about public health in the City and Hackney, please visit the Hackney and City of London Health and Wellbeing Profiles website at https://cityhackneyhealth.org.uk/ and the services recruitment page at https://recruitment.hackney.gov.uk/the-public-health-team/. As a Public Health Analyst working within our Adult Social Care transformation programme, you will play a critical role in applying analytical skills to prevent, reduce, and delay the development of social care needs, address health inequalities, and build good health in all of Hackney’s communities. This role will join the team on a fixed term contract for 2 years and will be focussed exclusively on the Adult Social Care “Understanding demand and maximising prevention” programme. The programme covers a range of different initiatives that cut across the whole health and social care system; including changes to how we provide holistic support to people approaching social care for the first time, how we ensure people remain stable while waiting for an assessment or a review, and how we support those with the most complex needs to keep them well. As well as delivering partnership projects, the programme supports culture change within individual teams, ensuring all staff have the capability, motivation and opportunity to work preventatively on a day to day basis. The role will sit within the Public Health Intelligence Team (PHIT), which supports strategic planning and service development across Hackney and the City of London. This ensures the postholder will have appropriate analytical line management, professional support, and quality assurance, while maintaining clear accountability to the Adult Social Care prevention programme for delivery of the agreed project objectives. In this role you will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of analytical projects that help the department to understand and model social care demand, and embed a population health management approach within Adult Social Care. You will transform complex datasets into actionable insight using tools such as Tableau, Python, and Google Workspace. This will include analysing demographic, health and service data, delivering all stages of the evaluation cycle, analysing quantitative and qualitative data and preparing reports for a range of stakeholders, use of machine learning and development of predictive models, and developing a longer term model of demand for Adult Social Care. You will also provide expert analytical advice, contribute to evidence-based planning and evaluation and help build data and insight capability across the wider ASC Transformation service. You will lead on specific work areas and collaborate with colleagues across and beyond the organisation to make best use of analytical and data resources, ensuring insight is co-produced, ethical, secure and impactful. You may also work directly with residents and service users to ensure their lived …

items.desc: Start Your Career in AI & CRM Development at Amore Group At Amore, we do things differently. Our Group brings together Mortgages, Life Insurance and Renewable Energy. As a growing business at an early stage of developing our internal systems, we are looking for someone to help us introduce straightforward CRM improvements, practical automations and useful AI tools. We're looking for an enthusiastic AI & CRM Developer to help build and improve the systems that support our teams and customers. This opportunity would be ideal for a recent graduate or someone at the beginning of their career in technology, AI or CRM development. You do not need years of industry experience. Our initial requirements are relatively basic, and we are looking for someone with the right aptitude, curiosity and willingness to learn as the role develops. You'll work with managers and colleagues to turn ideas into simple, reliable CRM features, automations and AI-enabled tools, with the opportunity to take on more complex projects as the business grows. What You'll Be Doing You will support Amore Mortgages, Amore Life and Amore Renewables by helping to set up, configure and gradually improve CRM functionality and straightforward automated workflows. You will understand how teams work, identify repetitive tasks and design practical technical solutions that improve lead management, reporting, customer journeys and internal efficiency. You will help test, implement and refine solutions, with appropriate support and guidance, ensuring they are practical, secure and easy for colleagues to use. Your responsibilities will include: · Building, configuring and enhancing CRM systems to meet operational requirements. · Designing AI-powered tools, assistants and workflow automations for internal use. · Connecting CRMs with other platforms through APIs, webhooks and integrations. · Developing lead allocation, follow-up and customer journey automations. · Creating dashboards, reports and data workflows to improve visibility and decision-making. · Working with teams across Mortgages, Life and Renewables to gather requirements. · Testing, troubleshooting and improving system reliability and performance. · Maintaining accurate data flows, access permissions and appropriate safeguards. · Documenting developments and providing clear guidance to system users. · Evaluating emerging AI tools and recommending practical applications. · Taking ownership of development priorities and delivering agreed improvements. items.desc: About Us Flok Jobs is on a mission to fix hospitality hiring for good. We're building the UK's first direct, real time platform connecting hospitality venues with verified, flexible staff. No agencies, no fees, no nonsense. Founded on more than 25 years of hands on hospitality and recruitment industry experience, Flok is solving a problem that touches a multi billion pound industry and has never been properly solved. We're not just an idea on a slide deck. We already have real traction, an active investment pipeline, and a founding technical team with over 30 years of combined development experience between them, including a CTO with more than 20 years of enterprise technology leadership. We're small right now, but we're going big. As we head towards launch with genuine momentum behind us, there's real room for the right person to step in, make their mark, and grow with us as the business scales. This role could suit someone fresh out of university looking for their first real opportunity to make an impact, or a more experienced developer looking for genuine ownership and influence at an early stage company. What matters most to us is attitude, curiosity and the willingness to learn and grow. Experience level is secondary to that. Important. Please Read Before Applying This role has two distinct stages, and because we're building Flok the right way, with honesty and respect for the people who join us, we want to be completely upfront about both before you apply. Stage 1 (unpaid, up to 4 to 6 weeks) An initial period working directly with our Director, CTO and wider team, including one of our existing developers, to help get Flok ready for launch. You'll be involved in real discussions, technical decisions and product priorities alongside a team that already brings decades of hospitality, recruitment and software development experience to the table. Stage 2 (paid and/or equity, ongoing) At the end of Stage 1, we'll have an honest conversation about where the business is at and what we can offer. We know unpaid stages can raise legitimate concerns, so here's what we commit to. You'll work directly with the Director, CTO and team, not sit on the sidelines, as your contribution and input will matter from day one. At the end of Stage 1, we'll give you a clear, honest answer about what we can offer, with real feedback either way. We won't ask for more time or scope than we agree upfront. No unpaid overtime, no scope creep. If we're not able to offer a wage or equity at that point, we'll tell you clearly, rather than leaving it vague. This arrangement will only suit candidates who are able to take on unpaid work for this initial period. If that doesn't work for your circumstances, we completely understand, and we'd encourage you to look at paid roles elsewhere with no hard feelings. Why Now Is a Great Time to Join This isn't a startup starting from zero. It's a business built on more than 25 years of hospitality and recruitment expertise, backed by a technical team with over 30 years of development experience between them, and with real momentum and investment interest already in motion. Joining now means getting in ahead of the crowd, while the business is still small enough that every person genuinely shapes what Flok becomes. Whether you're a graduate looking to prove yourself on a real product from day one, or a more established developer who wants meaningful ownership instead of being one voice among many, this is a chance to be part of decisions that actually matter, not just execute someone else's roadmap. Working Arrangement We're based out of our Loughborough office. Hybrid working is available, as some of our existing team already work this way. items.desc: Specialism Software Engineering, AI/ML, Data Job type Permanent Location London Salary £100,000 - £140,000 per annum There are a lot of AI startups out there right now, all claiming they're doing something different. But how many are actually building technology that businesses genuinely need? This company is taking an interesting approach to that. They're focused on industries where people are still spending ridiculous amounts of time working through documents, managing spreadsheets, processing emails and dealing with admin that really shouldn't need so much human involvement. The aim is to change that by building AI powered systems that take on the repetitive work and make these processes far more efficient. And that's where you come in. They're looking for a Founding Forward Deployed Engineer to join a small engineering team and help turn some pretty complicated business problems into working software. You will be getting close to the problems themselves, understanding how things currently work and figuring out where AI can actually make a difference. It's a hands on engineering role, where you'll be working across AI, backend systems, integrations, data and whatever else is needed to get something working. There won't always be a clear brief or someone telling you exactly how to approach a problem, so you'll need to be comfortable figuring things out for yourself. The good thing is, you'll actually get to see what happens when your work goes live. You're not spending months building something without knowing whether it's going to be useful. It's still early days, but there's a clear plan for where they want to take the business, along with the investment and backing to make it happen. The engineering team is small, which means you'll be working closely with senior technical leadership, having a say in how things are built and taking on far more responsibility than you would in a larger company. There's also meaningful equity on offer, so you'll have a stake in what you're helping to create. It's not going to suit everyone. There's a lot to figure out, things will change quickly and some weeks will be pretty demanding. But if you like the idea of joining something early, getting stuck into difficult engineering problems and having the freedom to build things your way, there's a lot to like here. What are they looking for? A strong software engineer who's comfortable working across the stack and isn't restricted to one language. Someone who's already built and shipped AI applications into production. Experience working in environments where you've had to take ownership and figure things out without much hand nholding. An interest in building products from scratch and solving problems that don't always have an obvious answer. You don't need to have 'Forward Deployed Engineer' on your CV. What's more important is that you enjoy getting close to the problem, working out what needs building and then actually building it. If this sounds like something you'd be interested in hearing more about, apply below. Leah Smith Talent Consultant 07527938219

items.desc: Overview Stats Perform is the market leader in sports tech. We provide the most trusted sports data to some of the world's biggest organizations, across sports, media, and broadcasting. Through the latest AI technologies and machine learning, we combine decades' worth of data with the latest in-game happenings. We then offer coaches, teams, professional bodies, and media channels around the world, access to the very best data, content, and insights. In turn, improving how sports fans interact with their favourite sports teams and competitions. How do we add value? Media outlets add a little magic to their coverage with our stats and graphics packages. Sportsbooks can offer better predictions and more accurate odds. The world's top coaches are known to use our data to make critical team decisions. Sports commentators can engage with fans on a deeper level, using our stories and insights. Anywhere you find sport, Stats Perform is there. However, data and tech are only half of the package. We need great people to fuel the engine. We succeeded thanks to a team of amazing people. They spend their days collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data from a wide range of live sporting events. If you combine this real-time data with our 40-year-old archives, elite journalists, camera operators, copywriters, the latest in AI wizardry, and a host of 'behind the scenes' support staff, you've got all the ingredients to make it a magical experience! Responsibilities: We are looking for a motivated and hands-on Network & Security Engineer to join our network team. In this role, you will be responsible for supporting day-to-day network operations (BAU) as well as executing device implementations, rollouts, and maintenance across our enterprise and data center environments. Working in close collaboration with senior engineers, you will contribute to technical designs, maintain perimeter security and traffic management, and assist with network automation initiatives. Technical Design & Documentation: Collaborate with more senior engineers to analyze technical requirements; contribute to design discussions and produce detailed Low-Level Designs (LLDs), network diagrams, and standard technical documentation. Continuous Improvement & Business Continuity: Review existing network topologies continuously, identify single points of failure, and design and integrate resilient solutions upon business approval. Implementations & Operations: Deliver end-to-end hands-on execution across the full network lifecycle—from day-to-day BAU operational support, configuration changes, and maintenance to hardware provisioning, rack-and-stack, commissioning, and migrations, both remotely and on-site at local offices and data center facilities. Automation: Contribute to and maintain the team's network automation and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) frameworks. Incident & Problem Management: Provide tier-3 troubleshooting and packet analysis for critical issues; participate in the team's on-call rota adhering to ITIL standards. Team Collaboration: Work closely with engineering peers, systems administrators, and business stakeholders. Required Qualifications: Routing & Switching: Solid hands-on experience with routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, PBR, VRF) and switching architectures (VPC, STP, 802.1Q). Strong proficiency with Cisco Nexus switches. Multicast: Solid understanding and operational experience with Multicast protocols ( PIM , IGMP ). Network Security & VPNs: Hands-on experience configuring and managing Fortinet (FortiGate) firewalls and enterprise VPN technologies (IPsec site-to-site, remote access). Load Balancing / ADC: Practical hands-on experience with Application Delivery Controllers such as F5 BIG-IP , A10 Networks , or Radware Alteon . Automation & Version Control: Experience working with automation frameworks ( Ansible , Terraform ) and version control ( Git ). Monitoring & Diagnostics: Proven troubleshooting capabilities, including packet capture and traffic analysis. Experience with Network Monitoring Systems (NMS) such as Zabbix or SolarWinds Desired Qualifications: Growth Mindset & Learning Drive: Strong desire to learn, acquire new technical competencies, and grow professionally within the role. Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to articulate technical details clearly. Work Ethic: Self-managing, proactive, and a committed team player. Process Orientation: Familiarity with ITIL service management processes (incident, change, and problem management). Operational Flexibility: Availability to participate in an on-call rotation . Travel: Willingness to travel abroad sporadically if business needs arise. Cloud Networking: Experience in public cloud environments ( e.g. AWS ). Scripting: Practical scripting skills in Python or Bash for task automation and API integrations. Network Access Control (NAC): Experience with enterprise NAC solutions (e.g., HPE Aruba ClearPass or 802.1X policy frameworks). …

items.desc: Overview We are seeking a dynamic and innovative Full-Stack Mobile & Python Developer to join our vibrant tech team. In this role, you will drive the development of cutting-edge mobile applications across multiple platforms, leveraging your expertise in Android and iOS development, while also building robust backend solutions using Python. Your contributions will directly impact user experience, application performance, and overall product success. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define application requirements and translate them into functional features with intuitive UI/UX design. Build and optimize backend services using Python, ensuring efficient data processing and integration with frontend components through RESTful APIs. Implement APIs to connect mobile apps with backend systems securely and reliably. We value innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning—empowering you to grow your skills while making a meaningful impact through your work. As a Platform Engineer, you’ll play a vital role in designing, automating and optimising secure, cloud-native platforms that enable critical operations. You’ll take ownership of complex engineering challenges, apply creative thinking to improve performance and resilience, and collaborate with talented teams to deliver solutions that make a real difference. Working in an agile, supportive environment, you’ll have the opportunity to develop your expertise, influence technical decisions and contribute to high-impact programmes that help protect the UK’s digital future. CGI was recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and has been named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We offer a competitive salary, excellent pension, private healthcare, plus a share scheme (3.5% + 3.5% matching) which makes you a CGI Partner not just an employee. Due to the secure nature of the programme, you will need to hold UK Security Clearance or be eligible to go through this clearance. This is a hybrid position based out of our CGI Reading office. Your future duties and responsibilities In this role, you will build and maintain secure, scalable cloud-native platforms that underpin critical Big Data and cyber defence capabilities. With Kubernetes at the heart of your work, you’ll take ownership of platform engineering, automation and container orchestration, ensuring applications operate reliably and efficiently in complex environments. You’ll have the freedom to explore innovative approaches, optimise infrastructure and enhance development workflows while delivering solutions that meet demanding security and performance requirements. Working collaboratively within an agile, multidisciplinary team, you’ll contribute to the full engineering lifecycle, from solution design and implementation through to deployment, monitoring and continuous improvement. You’ll be supported by experienced colleagues while having the opportunity to influence technical decisions, solve complex challenges and develop your expertise in modern platform technologies. Automate & Optimise: Develop automation solutions and improve CI/CD pipelines to accelerate delivery, reduce manual intervention and enhance reliability. Operate & Troubleshoot: Monitor platform health, investigate complex technical issues and implement improvements to availability, performance and resilience. Engineer & Integrate: Develop and configure infrastructure, networking and Linux-based systems, ensuring seamless integration across platform components. Innovate & Improve: Apply modern DevOps practices, infrastructure automation and cloud-native technologies to continuously enhance engineering capabilities. Collaborate & Contribute: Work closely with software engineers, architects and delivery teams in an agile environment, sharing knowledge and contributing to technical decisions. Required qualifications to be successful in this role To succeed in this role, you should have strong hands-on experience in Kubernetes and platform engineering, combined with a practical understanding of DevOps, automation and cloud-native technologies. You'll be comfortable working with Linux-based infrastructure, diagnosing complex technical challenges and contributing to secure, resilient solutions. We’re looking for someone who takes ownership, approaches problems creatively and thrives in a collaborative engineering environment where continuous learning and improvement are encouraged. Essential skills and experience: Kubernetes: Strong hands-on experience deploying, managing, troubleshooting and optimising Kubernetes clusters and containerised workloads. This is a key requirement. Platform Engineering: Proven experience designing, building and supporting reliable, scalable cloud-native platforms. DevOps & CI/CD: Practical experience with GitLab, CI/CD pipelines and modern DevOps tooling. Linux & Infrastructure: Strong understanding of Linux systems, infrastructure configuration and operational troubleshooting. items.desc: Description About Bright Software Group At Bright, we are powering the digital practice of tomorrow – today. We deliver products that help accountants, payroll bureaus, and businesses across the UK and Ireland work smarter and win more. Our innovative solutions and outstanding customer experiences enable our customers to run their businesses efficiently and serve their customers brilliantly. We believe understanding is the difference between working and winning. The Role We are looking for a proactive Software Engineer to strengthen the backend of the TimeKeeper platform. The role is Python-led, covering the services, APIs and data layer behind our web and mobile applications, and working closely with engineers across the stack. It suits an engineer who enjoys solving problems across a varied technology stack and picks up new tools quickly. Proficiency in every technology listed below is not expected; being proactive and keen to learn is what matters most. What You'll Do Design, build and maintain backend services in Python (Flask) that power the TimeKeeper platform Develop and improve APIs, data models and Postgres queries, with a focus on reliability and performance Shape features based on customer and team feedback, and deliver them alongside the web and mobile teams Write automated tests, investigate issues and fix bugs Review pull requests and share knowledge with the wider team Contribute to infrastructure and deployment work across AWS, Terraform and Redis Prioritise and manage multiple tasks, delivering on time and picking up new topics as needed Build strong working relationships and contribute positively to the team What We're Looking For Essential Minimum 4 years of professional experience as a Software Engineer, with a strong backend focus Professional experience building and maintaining backend services and APIs in Python Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases Experience writing automated tests and reviewing code Comfortable working alongside AI tools; curious about how technology can make you better at your job Nice to Have Experience with Python frameworks and libraries such as Flask, Django or SQLAlchemy Relevant AWS infrastructure experience, including Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) Experience with Postgres and Redis in production Familiarity with React or React Native, enough to work effectively with front-end colleagues Bachelor's or higher degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field The Technology Stack • Python (Flask) – Backend services • Postgres – Database • Redis – Application cache layer • AWS – Infrastructure • Terraform – Infrastructure as Code • React – Web application • React Native – Mobile application Don’t worry if you aren’t proficient in all of these, the main thing is you are proactive and able to pick new things up. Working At Bright Bright builds software that genuinely makes people's working lives easier. That matters — and you'll never have to apologise for what you're selling. But honestly, the first thing people mention is the culture. It's collaborative, it's human, and we're not a small company anymore, but it still feels like one — in the best way. People are genuinely looked after here — that's not just something we say. You get real autonomy to learn, grow, and make an impact. And right now is a genuinely exciting time to join. We're growing fast, investing heavily in AI, and that creates real opportunity — for the business and for the people in it. It's a place where curious people thrive. About Bright Software Group Bright is built around brilliant people doing brilliant work, and we invest in making sure the environment matches that ambition. You’ll have genuine flexibility in how you work, backed by modern practices that adapt to how work actually gets done today. We recognise and celebrate strong performance, support your wellbeing, and give you real opportunities to grow, not just in role, but in career. We’re proud of the culture we’ve built. It’s high-trust, high-expectation, and focused on doing great work. That’s Bright

We welcome applications from all backgrounds and particularly encourage interest from women, underrepresented groups, and neurodivergent candidates. We offer reasonable adjustments throughout the hiring process and are dedicated to creating a supportive, accessible environment for everyone. Technical Security Architect Location: Hampshire (5 days per week onsite) Due to the nature of the work and the customers we support, the successful candidate must be eligible to meet UK Government and contractual personnel security requirements, including the applicable residency requirements for the role, and have the right to work in the United Kingdom. Some roles may also be subject to nationality requirements where these are necessary to meet UK Government or contractual security obligations. The Technical Security Architect is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining technical security architectures that protect the organisation's information systems, data, and infrastructure. Embedded within the Technical team, this role leads the tech refresh and evergreening of security toolsets - ensuring the security technology estate remains current, supported, effective, and aligned with evolving threat landscapes, client policies, and cross-domain architectural patterns. This is a hands-on architecture role, not a governance-only position. The Technical Security Architect is expected to produce detailed technical designs, evaluate and select security technologies, define integration patterns, and guide implementation teams through delivery. The role requires deep technical expertise across cloud security, identity and access management, boundary and perimeter security, secure platform architectures, and security tooling ecosystems. Key Responsibilities Design and deliver security architectures across cloud, on-premise, hybrid and air-gapped environments. Produce technical designs including HLDs, LLDs, architecture patterns and data-flow diagrams. Lead the refresh and evergreening of security technologies, including IAM, PAM, firewalls, EDR/XDR, SIEM, vulnerability management and cloud security. Evaluate new technologies through PoCs/PoVs and make clear, evidence-based recommendations. Design and review cloud, identity, network, perimeter and platform security solutions. Apply Zero Trust, defence-in-depth and threat-informed design principles. Ensure security architectures align with NIST, ISO 27001, CIS, NCSC and client security requirements. Act as a security design authority, providing technical guidance and architectural decisions. Work closely with enterprise, infrastructure, network and application architects to embed security across the technology landscape. Support security accreditation, risk assessments and client security reviews. Keep pace with emerging threats and technologies and identify opportunities to improve and simplify the security estate. What you'll bring Significant experience as a Technical Security Architect, Security Architect or Senior Security Engineer. Strong technical expertise across multiple security domains, particularly IAM, network security, cloud security, endpoint security and secure platforms. Proven experience delivering security technology refresh, migration or modernisation programmes. Strong experience with AWS, Azure and/or GCP security architecture. Experience producing detailed technical architecture documentation. Strong understanding of threat modelling, risk and security architecture principles. Experience working within complex, regulated or formally accredited environments. Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence both technical and senior stakeholders. CISSP (or equivalent) and TOGAF and/or SABSA. Desirable: Zero Trust, DevSecOps, MITRE ATT&CK, SIEM, PAM, Kubernetes/container security, PKI and security automation experience. At DXC Technology, we believe strong connections and community are key to our success. Our work model prioritizes in-person collaboration while offering flexibility to support wellbeing, productivity, individual work styles, and life circumstances. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. These emails may request recipients to provide personal information or to make payments as part of their illegitimate recruiting process. DXC does not make offers of employment via social media networks and DXC never asks for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process, nor ask a job seeker to purchase IT or other equipment on our behalf. To include the planning and implementation of effective care plans, regular review meetings, timely referral to external agencies, within the framework of the CPA, to ensure effective pre-release planning. To communicate effectively with all relevant internal departments and external agencies regarding clients, within the restrictions of a prison environment. To offer a range of evidence based interventions and proactive risk management approaches to help the patient reduce and manage symptoms, high risk behaviour and other disabling effects of their conditions and enable, as far as possible, full and sustained recovery. items.desc: About Union Maritime Union Maritime Limited is a London-based shipowner and operator. Its core business is the product tanker market, focused on MR2 and larger vessels, alongside a presence in the dry bulk sector. The company is also investing in its future fleet, with newbuild hulls at Wuhu Shipyard in China. Decisions on when to buy, sell and build are central to the business, and the S&P / Strategy team sits at the heart of that work. Role Purpose The Junior Analyst will support the S&P / Strategy team in tracking the secondhand, newbuilding and demolition markets, analysing potential acquisitions and identifying areas for investment across tanker and dry bulk. Working closely with Guy Blunden, the Senior Associates and the Analyst, you will turn market data and broker intelligence into clear analysis, practical tools and well-reasoned recommendations. Key Responsibilities Market Monitoring & Intelligence Monitor vessel sales, asset values, newbuilding orders and contracting, and demolition activity on a daily and weekly basis across the tanker and dry bulk markets. Review broker reports and market intelligence, track comparable sales, and flag notable transactions, price movements and emerging trends to the team. Asset Screening & Acquisition Analysis Screen and evaluate secondhand and newbuild acquisition candidates, reviewing vessel specifications, age, building yard, and inspection and class information. Assess valuations against recent comparables and model earnings potential to test the investment case for each candidate. Prepare clear, well-supported acquisition recommendations for review by the Head of Strategy and senior team members. Prepare and maintain candidate vessel lists, target and watch lists, owner lists and sales candidate lists. Investment Research Research segments, vessel types and market trends to identify areas for investment and support the company's investment strategy. Analyse the drivers of asset values, such as fleet age profiles, the orderbook, demolition and regulatory change, and summarise the implications for the business. Tools, Models & Databases Build and refine models and analytical tools for vessel valuation, fleet analysis and market analysis, primarily in Excel and, ideally, using Python or Power BI. Maintain and develop the vessel sales register, asset value database, and fleet and market databases, taking ownership of data quality. Reporting Compile the weekly S&P market round-up, presenting tanker and dry bulk separately for asset values, sales and newbuildings. Consolidate broker reports into concise internal summaries, and prepare analysis, charts and slides for internal management presentations. Development Path This role is designed for someone who wants to build a long-term career in shipping. It begins with a strong analytical foundation and offers a clear opportunity to grow into a more commercial position over time. As your knowledge and judgement develop, you will gain increasing exposure to brokers and counterparties, take part in deal negotiations and support transaction execution alongside senior colleagues. Requirements Essential A strong degree in a numerate discipline such as economics, finance, engineering, maritime/shipping or similar. Advanced Excel skills, including building and maintaining models. Analytical rigour, close attention to detail, and clear, concise written communication. A genuine interest in shipping and the markets that drive it. Desirable 2 years' experience in shipping S&P, chartering, ship finance or broking. Working knowledge of Python, SQL or Power BI, and familiarity with data sources such as Clarksons, VesselsValue or IHS. An MSc in Shipping, or ICS (Institute of Chartered Shipbrokers) qualifications completed or in progress. Personal Attributes Curious and proactive, with the initiative to dig into data and ask the right questions. Organised and reliable, taking ownership of tasks and balancing recurring deadlines with ad hoc requests. Commercially minded, with the confidence to form a view and support it with evidence. Discreet and professional when handling commercially sensitive information. Benefits Salary: [Competitive – to be confirmed], with [bonus arrangements to be confirmed]. Benefits: [Benefits package to be confirmed, e.g. pension, private medical cover, holiday entitlement]. Direct exposure to senior decision-makers and to live S&P and newbuilding activity. [Training and professional development support to be confirmed].

This role is critical in identifying and addressing software defects through the design and execution of robust testing. Through collaboration with software developers, product managers, and other stakeholders, the QA Engineer will produce clear testing objectives and comprehensive test plans, with the goal being to prevent significant bugs or usability issues, thereby safeguarding the user experience and the Unily’s reputation. items.desc: What’s Yonder? “It's as if Time Out, Amex and Monzo had a baby” - Will T, Yonder Member We’re building the financial membership of the future. One that works for how you live now. Not how your parents banked in the ‘90s. Yonder combines credit or debit in one membership, designed to be fair, flexible, and actually enjoyable to use. No confusing terms. No dusty points system. Just rewards that actually feel rewarding - from bao to beer to a boarding pass. Sounds cool. What’s my part in this? Over the last year we've added a debit card, a free membership tier, hundreds of new independent partners around the country, countless product improvements and our personal favourite, Yonder Flights, a new way to use Yonder points on any flight with any airline globally. We've maintained a 4.5 TrustPilot rating and our customers really love us (and we love them back... hi!). Over the last 24 months, we’ve grown from just an idea to a beautiful, fully regulated financial product that our members absolutely love. Why design matters at Yonder Design isn’t just making something look good. It’s how a new member decides they can trust us with their money. It’s how we take something as complex as a credit account and make it simple, clear and fun. It’s how we turn rewards into something you actually look forward to using, rather than just a bunch of useless points you never touch. That’s why design sits right at the centre here. You’ll work on some of the most important problems we have, alongside people who’ll help you crack them. The expectation is that you care deeply about the quality and detail of your work, as much as the larger ambition driving everything we do. About the role You’ll join a small team where design carries real weight, as the designer in a lean squad with a senior product manager and two engineers. Your PM sets the direction for the squad, and you’ll own the design that brings it to life, taking work from early concepts to something in members’ hands. You won’t be doing it alone. Our designers work closely across squads, with product and design crits every week, and you’ll have a lot of support from Craig, our VP of Design, and our senior designers as you grow into the role. What you’ll be doing: Turning complex problems into simple experiences. Working closely with your PM, you’ll take complex problems and design the flows and prototypes that make them feel simple and effortless for members. Crafting experiences people love using. Yonder feels different from other finance apps because of how much we obsess over the craft. You'll design beautiful, enjoyable products that feel premium and worth coming back to. This is where we expect you to shine. Running research. Designers here don’t sit at arm’s length from members. You’ll run research alongside your PM, testing concepts and running usability sessions, and build up to leading your own research projects. If this is newer to you, we’ll help you get there. Working shoulder to shoulder with your squad. You'll work in the open with your PM and engineers from the first sketch, solving problems together so the final product feels like it was built by one team. Balancing speed with polish. Some weeks you’ll put scrappy ideas in front of members just to learn. Other times you'll slow right down to get the details right. Knowing which a problem needs takes judgement, and we’ll help you build it. Contributing to our design system. You’ll add to it and refine it, so it helps the whole team move fast without losing consistency or quality. You're a great fit if... Your craft is the strongest thing about your work. Typography, layout, colour, spacing, hierarchy, motion. Visual execution is where you stand out, and you can’t leave the details alone until they’re right. You have a few years of experience, including some in product. You’ve been designing for a few years, and for at least the last couple you’ve been working on digital products and shipping work people use. You might have started out in brand or marketing design and moved across, and now you want an in-house product role where you can learn how great products get made. You care about how things feel on a phone. Yonder lives on a smartphone. Ideally you’ve shipped native mobile experiences, but if not, you’ve designed digital interfaces and you’re keen to treat mobile as its own craft. You want to be involved end to end. You might have a specialism, but you want to be part of every stage, from talking to members and shaping ideas to sweating the final details. We don’t have researchers, content designers or copywriters, so you’ll get to grow across all of it, with support. You want feedback. You ask for it, take it well and act on it. You’ll get a lot of it here, and the people who grow fastest are the ones who go looking for it. You communicate openly and often. You share early, bring people into your process and see engineers and PMs as creative partners. You care about impact, not output. You believe …

items.desc: Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH) | £75,000 Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology. Our products, Street.co.uk and Spectre form a powerful duo, working harmoniously together to transform an agent's job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK. How we work in 2026 Engineering at Street Group has changed. Most of us don't write code by hand day-to-day anymore - agents do; we direct. For our mobile team, that shifts where the value is: when AI handles more of the code, what matters most is how the app looks, how it feels, what it does for the user and the ideas you bring to it. Understanding the product and the people using it sits at the heart of the role: we expect engineers to know why they're building something, not just how.
